I rolled over in bed, listening to the sound of my pager going off. It couldn’t have been more than 15 minutes since I had dropped into bed from my last admission. I looked at the number on the pager. Yes, it was the Emergency Department again.

I attempted to rub the sleep out of my eyes and stir my still sleepy brain to wakefulness. I picked up the phone and dialed the ER. “Hey,” the ER doctor said. “I’ve got two admissions for you.”

“Oh,” I said sleepily.

“You sound tired,” he said, jokingly.

I was tired. After graduating from Medical School, doctors go through an intense training period called residency. The first two years of that training period involved overnight calls in the hospital. It wasn’t unusual to put in one hundred hours at the hospital in a week’s time.

Even when we weren’t on call, the days started early and went late. I often fought sleep as I was driving home from the hospital. I certainly learned a lot during that time, but I am also glad that those days are behind me.

Fatigue is part of the human condition. Everyone has had times when they struggled with tiredness. Maybe it was due to a job that needed to get done, a long trip, or sleepless nights due to a new baby in the family—whatever the difficulty, we determinedly push ourselves to make it through these challenging times.

From our childhood days we are taught that work is important. We need to be responsible and take care of the tasks that are set for us to do.

Work is ordained by God. In Genesis Chapter 2, God gave Adam the task of caring for the Garden of Eden. Later, in Deuteronomy 5:13, the Israelites were commanded to do all their work in six days and then rest the seventh day.

The New Testament gives a couple of more reasons to work. We are to work so we can provide for our families (see II Thessalonians 3:10). In addition, we are to work so we can give to others who are in need (see Ephesians 4:28).

God expects us to work and that we do it in a way that will glorify Him. However, we also have need of rest, which God made provision for as well.

God Exemplified Rest in the Creation

And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made –Genesis 2:2-3.

When God created the universe, including the earth and all it contains, it took Him just six days. Since God is God, we can be certain that He wasn’t tired at the end of this work. Yet, despite that fact, He took a day of rest and set it apart. He did it as an example for us.

Even though the law of the Sabbath would not be instituted for at least two thousand years, the precedent was set in Creation… Rest one day a week.

God Mandated Rest in the Law

Perhaps the thing that comes to mind first is the Sabbath Day laws that were given in Exodus 20:8-11. It was specifically commanded that the people were not to work on the Sabbath. And further, they were not to cause other people to work either.

Another law which seemed very much focused on the need for rest was the Year of Jubilee. In Leviticus 25, this law mandated that every seven years the land was to lie fallow for the whole year, slaves were to be released, land was to revert to its original family’s ownership, and debts were to be cancelled.

Within the Jubilee commands were certain promises. There was the promise of freedom—no matter how bad things had been the previous six years there would be a reset. It was a promise of inheritance—the things that had been lost and sold would be reclaimed. It was a promise of abundance—And if ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase: Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years –Leviticus 25:20-21. Most of all, it was a promise of rest from labor—for the people and the land.

These commands were not put on the people to afflict them. Rather, God gave them knowing that without them His people would not rest enough and would not take enough time to focus on Him, their Creator.

Each one of us needs times of rest, but we need to understand that keeping the Sabbath is not simply about abstinence from work. Our efforts at keeping the Sabbath must include both rest and worship and it must be emphasized with the presence of God in our lives, without distraction.

The New Testament did not Change the Need for Rest

One of the verses that comes to my mind when I think about rest, is a promise that Jesus gave. Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light –Matthew 11:28-30.

The biblical book of Hebrews also speaks of the importance of rest and of our entering into God’s rest. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrews 4:9-11.

It is important to see that the New Testament concept of rest is more than simply time off from work. True biblical peace is intrinsically intertwined with the concept of peace, even in the midst of a chaotic world. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. Jesus gave peace to His followers that allowed them to be at rest, even when they were dealing with high levels of stress.

This is a blessing, for it is not enough simply to take time off from our normal work. We need to have that peace and calm which a connection with Jesus offers. Without …the peace of God, which passeth all understanding… –Philippians 4:7, our time off will be just as unrestful as our time at work.

It is clear that God wants us to rest. He knows that we need it, not just for spiritual reasons, but also for our physical health.

******************************

The folks in charge of the French Revolution made an attempt to eliminate all the institutions of the past. It was a particularly godless endeavor and among other things, the new government decided to “reform” the calendar.

In 1793, they established a ten-day work week. Each month would have three weeks with one rest day in each of these ten-day weeks. Their goal, among other things, was to eliminate all religious holidays and the celebration of Sunday as a day of rest. They believed that more work would be done by having fewer days of rest each month.

This created a huge headache for watchmakers. They needed to somehow make watches that would support the details of these new decrees—each day would be ten hours long, each hour would contain one hundred minutes, and each minute would be 100 seconds long.

It turned out to be a disaster. The people hated the changes and productivity dropped considerably across France. Finally, in 1806, Napoleon abolished it and went back to the old calendar and the system of Sunday days of rest. This scientific “experiment” was over. It turns out that people need times of rest and recharging and that a seven-day week with one day off to rest is not just a Christian concept, it is something that is necessary for health and wellbeing.

The Soviet Union, under Joseph Stalin, also tried a similar experiment of eliminating Sunday rest, with similar results.

******************************

The week, as God created it, (with one day in seven for rest) is necessary for us to remain productive.

Rest Reduces Inflammation

Part of the problem that modern people face is that they deal with high levels stress hormones, like adrenaline and cortisol. These hormones increase blood pressure and pulse rates. They also increase levels of inflammation in our bodies.

Chronic inflammation is not healthy, but fortunately, rest really seems to help bring those hormone levels down a lot. A good night of sleep is essential for healing, precisely because it turns down these hormones and allows healing of overworked nerves and tissues.

Autoimmune diseases and pain levels improve when people get adequate levels of sleep. Blood pressure and heart conditions also benefit when a person gets adequate amounts of restorative sleep.

Rest Allows for Healing

Exercise is a good thing. Doctors recommend doing regular cardiovascular exercise because it is healthy for our hearts, minds, and overall wellbeing.

It is not wise to exercise every day. It too, raises stress hormone levels and does not give our bodies adequate times to heal. People who exercise too frequently and with too much intensity are much more likely to end up with nagging injuries, joint and muscle pain, and fatigue. One study found that it takes 72 hours after doing weight training for muscles to fully recover.

People who exercise ideally need one to two days off a week to let their bodies recover from the activity. The harder you are training, the more you need those times of rest. Even someone who is training intensively for something like a marathon needs to take periodic days with no running or they will injure themselves.

Rest Decreases Pain Levels

There have been many studies that looked at people’s reports of sleep and looked at things like chronic pain and tension headaches. At least 50 percent of people with insomnia also have chronic pain. Of course, it could simply be that people with chronic pain don’t sleep as well as people who don’t have that.

There have been several studies that looked at people’s pain tolerance after sleep deprivation. They found that even a single night of sleep deprivation was enough to make people feel pain more acutely.

Rest Improves Our Immune Systems

There have been several studies that looked at function of different parts of our immune systems and found that they work better when study participants have adequate levels of sleep. Probably the fact that inflammation levels are higher when we don’t rest, increases the risks of infection.

When we push ourselves too hard without rest it is hard on our immune systems. On the other hand, the best way to recover is to make certain that we get sufficient rest.

There are many other things that rest does. It helps improve mood. It can help with academic performance and memory tasks.

As with all things, moderation is key. Someone who does nothing but rest and sleep, is not going to have any better function than someone who sleeps well for seven hours a night, nor will they be very productive.

There are some basic rules that can help us with times of rest.

Rest Regularly

The message of the Sabbath is that we need to take regular, short periods of time to rest. The Jubilee Years tell us that we need less frequent, longer times to recharge. It takes effort and scheduling to make certain that these times are truly restful.

Maybe it is a bit like a car. You can only drive so far on a tank of gas. If you always wait until the warning light turns on to fill up that tank, eventually you will have this happen when you are too far from a gas station to fill up before you run out of gas. There is never a good time to run out of gas. In the same way, we need to periodically recharge our spiritual, emotional, and physical batteries. There is no reason to wait until warning signs show up that we desperately need to take a break.

Rest Takes Preparation

The story of the gift of manna in Exodus 16 tells us that manna came every day. The people could not keep it for a second day because it would spoil. However, on Fridays, they were to gather extra since the next day was a day of rest and no manna came on the Sabbath. Those who had not gathered extra the day before went hungry.

In the same way, it takes preparation to have these sorts of times. It won’t be easy, but it is important.

Do Healthy Things With Your Rest

There is a tendency when people are under stress to eat unhealthy things. When people are exhausted, they don’t usually feel like exercising or taking walks. These are the sorts of things that can really help recharge us, both physically and emotionally.

Once again, this takes some effort, but choosing healthy options is important for our well-being.

Focus on God

I have left this till the last, but it is the most important aspect of rest. True rest grows, not out of medication or even multiple vacations, but out of a heart that is filled with peace. The peace which passes understanding comes from a heart that is focused on God.

Our times of prayer and Bible reading should be times of rest. If we can eliminate distractions and the challenges of our work and home life and train our gaze on the One who matters most, we will receive a real blessing and the recharging that our spirits need.

I am afraid that many people struggle to find rest because they are not truly at peace. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrew 4:11. The rest here is one that is promised to those who persevere and receive God’s peace.

Conclusion

Life is about balance. There are times when we need to work and there are times as well when we should rest. Figuring out this balance is the challenge which each of us faces. What is certain, is that every 24-hour day will be completely full by the time we get to the end of it.

God sees us and our limitations and desires for us to achieve this balance between our work and our times of rest. If we can only focus ourselves on Him, we will receive guidance in this balance.

Most of all, we will receive a peace that is without price, that will allow us to find rest—even during a storm.

Ik draaide me om in bed en luisterde naar het geluid van mijn pieper. Het kon niet meer dan 15 minuten geleden zijn dat ik na mijn laatste opname in bed was gedoken. Ik keek naar het nummer op mijn pieper. Ja hoor, weer de Spoedeisende Hulp.

Ik probeerde de slaap uit mijn ogen te wrijven en mijn nog slaperige brein wakker te schudden. Ik pakte de telefoon en belde de SEH. ‘Hé,’ zei de SEH-arts. ‘Ik heb twee opnames voor je.’

‘O,’ zei ik slaperig.

‘Je klinkt moe,’ zei hij gekscherend.

Ik was moe. Na hun afstuderen aan de medische faculteit doorlopen artsen een intensieve opleidingsperiode die residency wordt genoemd. De eerste twee jaar van die opleiding bestonden uit nachtdiensten in het ziekenhuis. Het was niet ongebruikelijk om in een week honderd uur in het ziekenhuis te werken.

Ook als we geen dienst hadden, begonnen de dagen vroeg en eindigden ze laat. Ik vocht vaak tegen de slaap terwijl ik naar huis reed vanuit het ziekenhuis. Ik heb in die tijd zeker veel geleerd, maar ik ben ook blij dat die dagen achter me liggen.

Vermoeidheid hoort bij het menselijk bestaan. Iedereen heeft weleens geworsteld met moeheid. Misschien kwam het door werk dat gedaan moest worden, een lange reis of slapeloze nachten vanwege een nieuwe baby in het gezin—wat de moeilijkheid ook was, vastberaden zetten we door om deze uitdagende tijden door te komen.

Al van jongs af aan leren we dat werk belangrijk is. We moeten verantwoordelijk zijn en de taken uitvoeren die ons zijn opgedragen.

Werk is door God ingesteld. In Genesis hoofdstuk 2 gaf God Adam de taak om de hof van Eden te verzorgen. Later, in Deuteronomium 5:13, kregen de Israëlieten het gebod om al hun werk in zes dagen te doen en op de zevende dag te rusten.

Het Nieuwe Testament geeft nog een paar redenen om te werken. We moeten werken zodat we voor onze gezinnen kunnen zorgen (zie 2 Tessalonicenzen 3:10). Daarnaast moeten we werken zodat we kunnen geven aan anderen die hulp nodig hebben (zie Efeziërs 4:28).

God verwacht van ons dat we werken en dat op een manier doen die Hem verheerlijkt. Maar we hebben ook rust nodig, en daarin heeft God eveneens voorzien.

God gaf bij de schepping het voorbeeld van rust

En God had op de zevende dag Zijn werk, dat Hij gemaakt had, voltooid; en Hij rustte op de zevende dag van al Zijn werk, dat Hij gemaakt had. En God zegende de zevende dag en heiligde die, omdat Hij daarop gerust heeft van al Zijn werk, dat God geschapen had door het te maken –Genesis 2:2-3.

Toen God het heelal schiep, met inbegrip van de aarde en alles wat daarop is, kostte Hem dat slechts zes dagen. Omdat God God is, kunnen we er zeker van zijn dat Hij aan het einde van dit werk niet moe was. Toch nam Hij, ondanks dat, een rustdag en zonderde die af. Hij deed dat als voorbeeld voor ons.

Hoewel de sabbatswet pas minstens tweeduizend jaar later zou worden ingevoerd, werd het voorbeeld al bij de schepping gegeven… Eén dag per week rusten.

God schreef rust voor in de wet

Wat waarschijnlijk als eerste bij ons opkomt, zijn de wetten over de sabbatdag die in Exodus 20:8-11 werden gegeven. Er werd uitdrukkelijk geboden dat het volk op de sabbat niet mocht werken. Bovendien mochten ze ook anderen niet laten werken.

Een andere wet die sterk gericht leek op de noodzaak van rust, was het jubeljaar. In Leviticus 25 schreef deze wet voor dat het land om de zeven jaar een heel jaar braak moest blijven liggen, slaven moesten worden vrijgelaten, land moest terugkeren naar het oorspronkelijke familiebezit en schulden moesten worden kwijtgescholden.

In de geboden over het jubeljaar lagen bepaalde beloften besloten. Er was de belofte van vrijheid—hoe slecht de afgelopen zes jaar ook waren geweest, er kwam een nieuwe start. Het was een belofte van erfbezit—wat verloren was gegaan en verkocht was, zou weer worden teruggekregen. Het was een belofte van overvloed—En als u zegt: Wat zullen wij in het zevende jaar eten? Zie, wij mogen niet zaaien en onze opbrengst niet inzamelen, dan zal Ik Mijn zegen over u gebieden in het zesde jaar, en dat zal een opbrengst geven voor drie jaren –Leviticus 25:20-21. Bovenal was het een belofte van rust van het werk—voor het volk en het land.

Deze geboden werden het volk niet opgelegd om het te kwellen. God gaf ze juist omdat Hij wist dat Zijn volk zonder die geboden niet genoeg zou rusten en niet genoeg tijd zou nemen om zich te richten op Hem, hun Schepper.

Ieder van ons heeft momenten van rust nodig, maar we moeten begrijpen dat het houden van de sabbat niet alleen betekent dat we ons van werk onthouden. Onze inspanningen om de sabbat te houden moeten zowel rust als aanbidding omvatten, en daarbij moet Gods aanwezigheid in ons leven centraal staan, zonder afleiding.

Het Nieuwe Testament veranderde niets aan de behoefte aan rust

Een van de verzen waaraan ik denk als ik over rust nadenk, is een belofte die Jezus deed. Kom naar Mij toe, allen die vermoeid en belast zijn, en Ik zal u rust geven. Neem Mijn juk op u, en leer van Mij dat Ik zachtmoedig ben en nederig van hart; en u zult rust vinden voor uw ziel. Want Mijn juk is zacht en Mijn last is licht –Mattheüs 11:28-30.

Ook het Bijbelboek Hebreeën spreekt over het belang van rust en over het binnengaan in Gods rust. Er blijft dus een sabbatsrust over voor het volk van God. Want wie Zijn rust binnengegaan is, is ook zelf van zijn werken gaan rusten, zoals God van de Zijne. Laten wij ons dan beijveren om die rust binnen te gaan, opdat niemand ten val komt door dit voorbeeld van ongehoorzaamheid te volgen –Hebreeën 4:9-11.

Het is belangrijk om te beseffen dat het nieuwtestamentische begrip van rust meer inhoudt dan alleen vrij zijn van werk. Ware Bijbelse vrede is onlosmakelijk verbonden met rust, zelfs midden in een chaotische wereld. Vrede laat Ik u, Mijn vrede geef Ik u; niet zoals de wereld die geeft, geef Ik die u. Laat uw hart niet in beroering raken en niet bevreesd worden –Johannes 14:27. Jezus gaf Zijn volgelingen vrede, waardoor ze rust konden vinden, zelfs wanneer ze met grote stress te maken hadden.

Dat is een zegen, want alleen tijd vrij nemen van ons gewone werk is niet genoeg. We hebben de vrede en kalmte nodig die een band met Jezus ons biedt. Zonder …de vrede van God, die alle begrip te boven gaat… –Filippenzen 4:7 zal onze vrije tijd net zo onrustig zijn als onze tijd op het werk.

Het is duidelijk dat God wil dat we rusten. Hij weet dat we die nodig hebben, niet alleen om geestelijke redenen, maar ook voor onze lichamelijke gezondheid.

******************************

De leiders van de Franse Revolutie probeerden alle instellingen uit het verleden af te schaffen. Het was een bijzonder goddeloos streven en onder andere besloot de nieuwe regering de kalender te ‘hervormen’.

In 1793 voerden ze een werkweek van tien dagen in. Iedere maand zou uit drie weken bestaan, met in elk van die weken van tien dagen één rustdag. Een van hun doelen was om alle religieuze feestdagen en de viering van de zondag als rustdag af te schaffen. Ze geloofden dat er meer werk zou worden verzet als er elke maand minder rustdagen waren.

Dit bezorgde horlogemakers grote problemen. Ze moesten op de een of andere manier horloges maken die voldeden aan de details van deze nieuwe decreten—elke dag zou tien uur duren, elk uur zou honderd minuten bevatten en elke minuut zou honderd seconden duren.

Het bleek een ramp. De mensen hadden een hekel aan de veranderingen en de productiviteit daalde in heel Frankrijk aanzienlijk. Uiteindelijk schafte Napoleon dit in 1806 af en keerde hij terug naar de oude kalender en het systeem met zondagen als rustdagen. Dit wetenschappelijke ‘experiment’ was voorbij. Het blijkt dat mensen rust en momenten om op te laden nodig hebben, en dat een week van zeven dagen met één rustdag niet alleen een christelijk concept is, maar ook noodzakelijk is voor gezondheid en welzijn.

Ook de Sovjet-Unie probeerde onder Jozef Stalin een soortgelijk experiment om de zondagsrust af te schaffen, met vergelijkbare resultaten.

******************************

De week zoals God die heeft geschapen (met één rustdag op de zeven) is noodzakelijk om productief te blijven.

Rust vermindert ontstekingen

Een deel van het probleem waar moderne mensen mee te maken hebben, is dat ze hoge niveaus van stresshormonen hebben, zoals adrenaline en cortisol. Deze hormonen verhogen de bloeddruk en hartslag. Ze verhogen ook de ontstekingsniveaus in ons lichaam.

Chronische ontstekingen zijn niet gezond, maar gelukkig lijkt rust er echt voor te zorgen dat die hormoonspiegels flink dalen. Een goede nachtrust is essentieel voor herstel, juist omdat de hoeveelheid van deze hormonen erdoor afneemt en overbelaste zenuwen en weefsels kunnen herstellen.

Auto-immuunziekten en pijn nemen af wanneer mensen voldoende slapen. Ook de bloeddruk en hartaandoeningen varen wel bij voldoende herstellende slaap.

Rust maakt herstel mogelijk

Bewegen is goed. Artsen raden aan regelmatig cardiovasculaire oefeningen te doen, omdat die goed zijn voor ons hart, onze geest en ons algehele welzijn.

Het is niet verstandig om elke dag te sporten. Ook daardoor stijgen de stresshormoonspiegels en krijgt ons lichaam niet genoeg tijd om te herstellen. Mensen die te vaak en te intensief sporten, lopen veel meer kans op hardnekkige blessures, gewrichts- en spierpijn en vermoeidheid. Uit één onderzoek bleek dat spieren na krachttraining 72 uur nodig hebben om volledig te herstellen.

Idealiter hebben mensen die sporten één tot twee dagen per week vrij nodig om hun lichaam te laten herstellen van de inspanning. Hoe harder je traint, hoe meer je die rustmomenten nodig hebt. Zelfs iemand die intensief traint voor bijvoorbeeld een marathon moet regelmatig dagen zonder hardlopen inlassen, anders raakt diegene geblesseerd.

Rust vermindert pijn

Er zijn veel onderzoeken gedaan naar wat mensen vertellen over hun slaap en naar zaken als chronische pijn en spanningshoofdpijn. Minstens 50 procent van de mensen met slapeloosheid heeft ook chronische pijn. Natuurlijk kan het ook gewoon zo zijn dat mensen met chronische pijn minder goed slapen dan mensen die daar geen last van hebben.

Er zijn verschillende onderzoeken gedaan naar de pijntolerantie van mensen na slaapgebrek. Daaruit bleek dat zelfs één nacht zonder slaap al voldoende was om mensen pijn scherper te laten voelen.

Rust verbetert ons immuunsysteem

Er zijn verschillende onderzoeken gedaan naar de werking van verschillende onderdelen van ons immuunsysteem. Daaruit bleek dat ze beter werken wanneer deelnemers aan het onderzoek voldoende slapen. Waarschijnlijk verhoogt het feit dat ontstekingsniveaus hoger zijn wanneer we niet rusten het risico op infecties.

Als we onszelf te veel pushen zonder rust, is dat zwaar voor ons immuunsysteem. Aan de andere kant is voldoende rust nemen de beste manier om te herstellen.

Rust doet nog veel meer. Het helpt de stemming te verbeteren. Het kan helpen bij schoolprestaties en geheugentaken.

Zoals met alles is matigheid belangrijk. Iemand die alleen maar rust en slaapt, zal niet beter functioneren dan iemand die elke nacht zeven uur goed slaapt, en zal ook niet erg productief zijn.

Er zijn enkele eenvoudige regels die ons kunnen helpen om momenten van rust in te lassen.

Rust regelmatig

De boodschap van de sabbat is dat we regelmatig korte periodes moeten nemen om te rusten. De jubeljaren leren ons dat we minder vaak langere periodes nodig hebben om op te laden. Het kost moeite en planning om ervoor te zorgen dat die momenten echt rustgevend zijn.

Misschien is het een beetje zoals met een auto. Je kunt maar een bepaalde afstand rijden op een tank benzine. Als je altijd wacht tot het waarschuwingslampje gaat branden om te tanken, zal het uiteindelijk gebeuren dat je te ver van een tankstation bent om te tanken voordat je zonder benzine komt te staan. Er is nooit een goed moment om zonder benzine te vallen. Zo moeten we ook geregeld onze geestelijke, emotionele en lichamelijke batterijen opladen. Er is geen reden om te wachten tot de waarschuwingssignalen verschijnen dat we dringend een pauze nodig hebben.

Rust vraagt om voorbereiding

Het verhaal over het geschenk van manna in Exodus 16 vertelt ons dat er elke dag manna kwam. Het volk kon het niet bewaren voor een tweede dag, omdat het dan bedierf. Maar op vrijdag moesten ze extra verzamelen, omdat de volgende dag een rustdag was en er op de sabbat geen manna kwam. Wie de dag ervoor niet extra had verzameld, kreeg honger.

Zo vraagt ook dit soort momenten om voorbereiding. Het zal niet makkelijk zijn, maar het is belangrijk.

Doe gezonde dingen tijdens je rust

Wanneer mensen onder stress staan, hebben ze de neiging ongezonde dingen te eten. Als mensen uitgeput zijn, hebben ze meestal geen zin om te sporten of te wandelen. Juist dat soort dingen kan ons echt helpen om zowel lichamelijk als emotioneel op te laden.

Ook dit kost wat moeite, maar gezonde keuzes maken is belangrijk voor ons welzijn.

Richt je op God

Ik heb dit tot het laatst bewaard, maar het is het belangrijkste aspect van rust. Echte rust komt niet voort uit medicijnen of zelfs uit meerdere vakanties, maar uit een hart dat vervuld is van vrede. De vrede die alle begrip te boven gaat, komt voort uit een hart dat op God gericht is.

Onze momenten van gebed en Bijbellezen zouden momenten van rust moeten zijn. Als we afleidingen en de uitdagingen van ons werk en thuis kunnen uitschakelen en onze blik richten op Hem die het belangrijkst is, ontvangen we een echte zegen en de nieuwe kracht die onze geest nodig heeft.

Ik ben bang dat veel mensen moeite hebben om rust te vinden omdat ze niet echt vrede hebben. Laten wij ons dan beijveren om die rust binnen te gaan, opdat niemand ten val komt door dit voorbeeld van ongehoorzaamheid te volgen –Hebreeën 4:11. De rust waar het hier om gaat, is beloofd aan wie volharden en Gods vrede ontvangen.

Conclusie

Het leven draait om evenwicht. Soms moeten we werken, maar er zijn ook momenten waarop we moeten rusten. Uitvinden hoe we dat evenwicht kunnen bewaren, is de uitdaging waar ieder van ons voor staat. Eén ding is zeker: elke periode van 24 uur zal helemaal gevuld zijn tegen de tijd dat die voorbij is.

God ziet ons en onze beperkingen en wil dat we een evenwicht vinden tussen ons werk en onze rustmomenten. Als we ons op Hem richten, zullen we daarin leiding ontvangen.

Bovenal zullen we een onbetaalbare vrede ontvangen, waardoor we rust kunnen vinden—zelfs tijdens een storm.

I rolled over in bed, listening to the sound of my pager going off. It couldn’t have been more than 15 minutes since I had dropped into bed from my last admission. I looked at the number on the pager. Yes, it was the Emergency Department again.

I attempted to rub the sleep out of my eyes and stir my still sleepy brain to wakefulness. I picked up the phone and dialed the ER. “Hey,” the ER doctor said. “I’ve got two admissions for you.”

“Oh,” I said sleepily.

“You sound tired,” he said, jokingly.

I was tired. After graduating from Medical School, doctors go through an intense training period called residency. The first two years of that training period involved overnight calls in the hospital. It wasn’t unusual to put in one hundred hours at the hospital in a week’s time.

Even when we weren’t on call, the days started early and went late. I often fought sleep as I was driving home from the hospital. I certainly learned a lot during that time, but I am also glad that those days are behind me.

Fatigue is part of the human condition. Everyone has had times when they struggled with tiredness. Maybe it was due to a job that needed to get done, a long trip, or sleepless nights due to a new baby in the family—whatever the difficulty, we determinedly push ourselves to make it through these challenging times.

From our childhood days we are taught that work is important. We need to be responsible and take care of the tasks that are set for us to do.

Work is ordained by God. In Genesis Chapter 2, God gave Adam the task of caring for the Garden of Eden. Later, in Deuteronomy 5:13, the Israelites were commanded to do all their work in six days and then rest the seventh day.

The New Testament gives a couple of more reasons to work. We are to work so we can provide for our families (see II Thessalonians 3:10). In addition, we are to work so we can give to others who are in need (see Ephesians 4:28).

God expects us to work and that we do it in a way that will glorify Him. However, we also have need of rest, which God made provision for as well.

God Exemplified Rest in the Creation

And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made –Genesis 2:2-3.

When God created the universe, including the earth and all it contains, it took Him just six days. Since God is God, we can be certain that He wasn’t tired at the end of this work. Yet, despite that fact, He took a day of rest and set it apart. He did it as an example for us.

Even though the law of the Sabbath would not be instituted for at least two thousand years, the precedent was set in Creation… Rest one day a week.

God Mandated Rest in the Law

Perhaps the thing that comes to mind first is the Sabbath Day laws that were given in Exodus 20:8-11. It was specifically commanded that the people were not to work on the Sabbath. And further, they were not to cause other people to work either.

Another law which seemed very much focused on the need for rest was the Year of Jubilee. In Leviticus 25, this law mandated that every seven years the land was to lie fallow for the whole year, slaves were to be released, land was to revert to its original family’s ownership, and debts were to be cancelled.

Within the Jubilee commands were certain promises. There was the promise of freedom—no matter how bad things had been the previous six years there would be a reset. It was a promise of inheritance—the things that had been lost and sold would be reclaimed. It was a promise of abundance—And if ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase: Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years –Leviticus 25:20-21. Most of all, it was a promise of rest from labor—for the people and the land.

These commands were not put on the people to afflict them. Rather, God gave them knowing that without them His people would not rest enough and would not take enough time to focus on Him, their Creator.

Each one of us needs times of rest, but we need to understand that keeping the Sabbath is not simply about abstinence from work. Our efforts at keeping the Sabbath must include both rest and worship and it must be emphasized with the presence of God in our lives, without distraction.

The New Testament did not Change the Need for Rest

One of the verses that comes to my mind when I think about rest, is a promise that Jesus gave. Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light –Matthew 11:28-30.

The biblical book of Hebrews also speaks of the importance of rest and of our entering into God’s rest. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrews 4:9-11.

It is important to see that the New Testament concept of rest is more than simply time off from work. True biblical peace is intrinsically intertwined with the concept of peace, even in the midst of a chaotic world. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. Jesus gave peace to His followers that allowed them to be at rest, even when they were dealing with high levels of stress.

This is a blessing, for it is not enough simply to take time off from our normal work. We need to have that peace and calm which a connection with Jesus offers. Without …the peace of God, which passeth all understanding… –Philippians 4:7, our time off will be just as unrestful as our time at work.

It is clear that God wants us to rest. He knows that we need it, not just for spiritual reasons, but also for our physical health.

******************************

The folks in charge of the French Revolution made an attempt to eliminate all the institutions of the past. It was a particularly godless endeavor and among other things, the new government decided to “reform” the calendar.

In 1793, they established a ten-day work week. Each month would have three weeks with one rest day in each of these ten-day weeks. Their goal, among other things, was to eliminate all religious holidays and the celebration of Sunday as a day of rest. They believed that more work would be done by having fewer days of rest each month.

This created a huge headache for watchmakers. They needed to somehow make watches that would support the details of these new decrees—each day would be ten hours long, each hour would contain one hundred minutes, and each minute would be 100 seconds long.

It turned out to be a disaster. The people hated the changes and productivity dropped considerably across France. Finally, in 1806, Napoleon abolished it and went back to the old calendar and the system of Sunday days of rest. This scientific “experiment” was over. It turns out that people need times of rest and recharging and that a seven-day week with one day off to rest is not just a Christian concept, it is something that is necessary for health and wellbeing.

The Soviet Union, under Joseph Stalin, also tried a similar experiment of eliminating Sunday rest, with similar results.

******************************

The week, as God created it, (with one day in seven for rest) is necessary for us to remain productive.

Rest Reduces Inflammation

Part of the problem that modern people face is that they deal with high levels stress hormones, like adrenaline and cortisol. These hormones increase blood pressure and pulse rates. They also increase levels of inflammation in our bodies.

Chronic inflammation is not healthy, but fortunately, rest really seems to help bring those hormone levels down a lot. A good night of sleep is essential for healing, precisely because it turns down these hormones and allows healing of overworked nerves and tissues.

Autoimmune diseases and pain levels improve when people get adequate levels of sleep. Blood pressure and heart conditions also benefit when a person gets adequate amounts of restorative sleep.

Rest Allows for Healing

Exercise is a good thing. Doctors recommend doing regular cardiovascular exercise because it is healthy for our hearts, minds, and overall wellbeing.

It is not wise to exercise every day. It too, raises stress hormone levels and does not give our bodies adequate times to heal. People who exercise too frequently and with too much intensity are much more likely to end up with nagging injuries, joint and muscle pain, and fatigue. One study found that it takes 72 hours after doing weight training for muscles to fully recover.

People who exercise ideally need one to two days off a week to let their bodies recover from the activity. The harder you are training, the more you need those times of rest. Even someone who is training intensively for something like a marathon needs to take periodic days with no running or they will injure themselves.

Rest Decreases Pain Levels

There have been many studies that looked at people’s reports of sleep and looked at things like chronic pain and tension headaches. At least 50 percent of people with insomnia also have chronic pain. Of course, it could simply be that people with chronic pain don’t sleep as well as people who don’t have that.

There have been several studies that looked at people’s pain tolerance after sleep deprivation. They found that even a single night of sleep deprivation was enough to make people feel pain more acutely.

Rest Improves Our Immune Systems

There have been several studies that looked at function of different parts of our immune systems and found that they work better when study participants have adequate levels of sleep. Probably the fact that inflammation levels are higher when we don’t rest, increases the risks of infection.

When we push ourselves too hard without rest it is hard on our immune systems. On the other hand, the best way to recover is to make certain that we get sufficient rest.

There are many other things that rest does. It helps improve mood. It can help with academic performance and memory tasks.

As with all things, moderation is key. Someone who does nothing but rest and sleep, is not going to have any better function than someone who sleeps well for seven hours a night, nor will they be very productive.

There are some basic rules that can help us with times of rest.

Rest Regularly

The message of the Sabbath is that we need to take regular, short periods of time to rest. The Jubilee Years tell us that we need less frequent, longer times to recharge. It takes effort and scheduling to make certain that these times are truly restful.

Maybe it is a bit like a car. You can only drive so far on a tank of gas. If you always wait until the warning light turns on to fill up that tank, eventually you will have this happen when you are too far from a gas station to fill up before you run out of gas. There is never a good time to run out of gas. In the same way, we need to periodically recharge our spiritual, emotional, and physical batteries. There is no reason to wait until warning signs show up that we desperately need to take a break.

Rest Takes Preparation

The story of the gift of manna in Exodus 16 tells us that manna came every day. The people could not keep it for a second day because it would spoil. However, on Fridays, they were to gather extra since the next day was a day of rest and no manna came on the Sabbath. Those who had not gathered extra the day before went hungry.

In the same way, it takes preparation to have these sorts of times. It won’t be easy, but it is important.

Do Healthy Things With Your Rest

There is a tendency when people are under stress to eat unhealthy things. When people are exhausted, they don’t usually feel like exercising or taking walks. These are the sorts of things that can really help recharge us, both physically and emotionally.

Once again, this takes some effort, but choosing healthy options is important for our well-being.

Focus on God

I have left this till the last, but it is the most important aspect of rest. True rest grows, not out of medication or even multiple vacations, but out of a heart that is filled with peace. The peace which passes understanding comes from a heart that is focused on God.

Our times of prayer and Bible reading should be times of rest. If we can eliminate distractions and the challenges of our work and home life and train our gaze on the One who matters most, we will receive a real blessing and the recharging that our spirits need.

I am afraid that many people struggle to find rest because they are not truly at peace. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrew 4:11. The rest here is one that is promised to those who persevere and receive God’s peace.

Conclusion

Life is about balance. There are times when we need to work and there are times as well when we should rest. Figuring out this balance is the challenge which each of us faces. What is certain, is that every 24-hour day will be completely full by the time we get to the end of it.

God sees us and our limitations and desires for us to achieve this balance between our work and our times of rest. If we can only focus ourselves on Him, we will receive guidance in this balance.

Most of all, we will receive a peace that is without price, that will allow us to find rest—even during a storm.

Niligeuka kitandani, nikisikiliza mlio wa kipaji changu ukilia. Haingeweza kuwa imepita zaidi ya dakika 15 tangu nilipojilaza kitandani baada ya mgonjwa wangu wa mwisho kulazwa. Niliangalia namba iliyoonyeshwa kwenye kipaji. Ndiyo, ilikuwa tena Idara ya Dharura.

Nilijaribu kujifuta usingizi machoni na kuichochea akili yangu iliyokuwa bado na usingizi iamke. Niliinua simu na kupiga nambari ya ER. “Habari,” daktari wa ER alisema. “Nina wagonjwa wawili wa kulazwa kwa ajili yako.”

“Lo,” nikasema kwa sauti ya usingizi.

“Unasikika umechoka,” alisema kwa utani.

Nilikuwa nimechoka. Baada ya kuhitimu shule ya udaktari, madaktari hupitia kipindi kigumu cha mafunzo kinachoitwa ukaazi wa udaktari. Miaka miwili ya kwanza ya kipindi hicho cha mafunzo ilihusisha zamu za usiku hospitalini. Haikuwa ajabu kufanya kazi hospitalini kwa saa mia moja katika muda wa wiki moja.

Hata tulipokuwa hatuko zamu, siku zilianza mapema na kumalizika usiku. Mara nyingi nilipambana na usingizi nilipokuwa nikiendesha gari kurudi nyumbani kutoka hospitalini. Bila shaka nilijifunza mengi wakati huo, lakini pia ninafurahi kwamba siku hizo zimepita.

Uchovu ni sehemu ya hali ya kibinadamu. Kila mtu amewahi kukabiliana na uchovu. Labda ulitokana na kazi iliyopaswa kukamilishwa, safari ndefu, au usiku wa kukosa usingizi kwa sababu ya mtoto mchanga katika familia—chochote kile kilichokuwa kigumu, tunajikaza kwa uthabiti ili kuvuka nyakati hizi zenye changamoto.

Tangu utotoni tunafundishwa kwamba kazi ni muhimu. Tunahitaji kuwajibika na kutimiza majukumu tuliyopewa.

Kazi imewekwa na Mungu. Katika Mwanzo sura ya 2, Mungu alimpa Adamu jukumu la kuitunza Bustani ya Edeni. Baadaye, katika Kumbukumbu la Torati 5:13, Waisraeli waliamriwa kufanya kazi yao yote kwa siku sita na kisha kupumzika siku ya saba.

Agano Jipya linatoa sababu kadhaa zaidi za kufanya kazi. Tunapaswa kufanya kazi ili tuweze kuitunza familia yetu (tazama 2 Wathesalonike 3:10). Zaidi ya hayo, tunapaswa kufanya kazi ili tuweze kuwapa wengine wenye uhitaji (tazama Waefeso 4:28).

Mungu anatarajia tufanye kazi na tuifanye kwa namna itakayomtukuza. Hata hivyo, tunahitaji pia kupumzika, na Mungu ametoa mpango kwa ajili ya hilo pia.

Mungu Alionyesha Mfano wa Kupumzika Katika Uumbaji

Ikawa siku ya saba Mungu alimaliza kazi yake yote aliyoifanya; akastarehe siku ya saba, akaacha kufanya kazi yake yote aliyoifanya. Mungu akaibarikia siku ya saba, akaitakasa; kwa sababu katika siku hiyo Mungu alistarehe, akaacha kufanya kazi yake yote aliyoiumba na kuifanya –Mwanzo 2:2-3.

Mungu alipoumba ulimwengu, kutia ndani dunia na vyote vilivyomo, ilimchukua siku sita tu. Kwa kuwa Mungu ni Mungu, tunaweza kuwa na uhakika kwamba hakuchoka baada ya kazi hii. Hata hivyo, licha ya jambo hilo, alichukua siku ya kupumzika na kuitenga. Alifanya hivyo ili kutupatia mfano.

Ingawa sheria ya Sabato isingewekwa kwa angalau miaka elfu mbili, msingi wake uliwekwa wakati wa Uumbaji… Pumzika siku moja kila juma.

Mungu Aliamuru Kupumzika Katika Sheria

Huenda jambo la kwanza linalokuja akilini ni sheria za siku ya Sabato zilizotolewa katika Kutoka 20:8-11. Iliamriwa waziwazi kwamba watu hawakupaswa kufanya kazi siku ya Sabato. Isitoshe, hawakupaswa kuwafanya watu wengine wafanye kazi pia.

Sheria nyingine iliyoonekana kulenga sana uhitaji wa kupumzika ilikuwa Mwaka wa Yubile. Katika Mambo ya Walawi 25, sheria hii iliamuru kwamba kila baada ya miaka saba ardhi iachwe bila kulimwa kwa mwaka mzima, watumwa waachiliwe huru, ardhi irudishwe kwa familia yake ya awali, na madeni yafutwe.

Amri za Yubile zilikuwa na ahadi fulani. Kulikuwa na ahadi ya uhuru—hata hali iwe ilikuwa mbaya kiasi gani katika miaka sita iliyotangulia, mambo yangeanza upya. Ilikuwa ahadi ya urithi—vitu vilivyokuwa vimepotea na kuuzwa vingechukuliwa tena. Ilikuwa ahadi ya wingi—Nanyi mkiuliza, Tule nini mwaka wa saba? Tazama, hatutapanda, wala hatutavuna maongeo yetu; ndipo nitawaamuru baraka yangu iwe juu yenu mwaka wa sita, nao utazaa matunda kwa miaka mitatu –Mambo ya Walawi 25:20-21. Zaidi ya yote, ilikuwa ahadi ya kupumzika kutokana na kazi—kwa watu na ardhi.

Amri hizi hazikuwekwa juu ya watu ili kuwatesa. Badala yake, Mungu alizitoa akijua kwamba bila amri hizo watu wake hawangepumzika vya kutosha wala kuchukua muda wa kutosha kumkazia fikira yeye, Muumba wao.

Kila mmoja wetu anahitaji nyakati za kupumzika, lakini tunahitaji kuelewa kwamba kushika Sabato hakuhusu tu kujizuia kufanya kazi. Jitihada zetu za kushika Sabato lazima zijumuishe kupumzika na kuabudu, na lazima zisisitizwe kwa uwepo wa Mungu katika maisha yetu, bila vikengeusha-fikira.

Agano Jipya Halikubadili Uhitaji wa Kupumzika

Mojawapo ya mistari inayonijia akilini ninapofikiria kuhusu kupumzika ni ahadi ambayo Yesu alitoa. Njoni kwangu, ninyi nyote msumbukao na wenye kulemewa na mizigo, nami nitawapumzisha. Jitieni nira yangu, mjifunze kwangu; kwa kuwa mimi ni mpole na mnyenyekevu wa moyo; nanyi mtapata raha nafsini mwenu. Kwa maana nira yangu ni laini, na mzigo wangu ni mwepesi –Mathayo 11:28-30.

Kitabu cha Biblia cha Waebrania pia kinazungumzia umuhimu wa kupumzika na kuingia katika raha ya Mungu. Basi, imesalia raha ya sabato kwa watu wa Mungu. Maana yeye aliyeingia katika raha yake amestarehe mwenyewe katika kazi yake, kama vile Mungu alivyostarehe katika kazi zake. Basi, na tufanye bidii kuingia katika raha ile, ili kwamba mtu ye yote asije akaanguka kwa mfano uo huo wa kuasi –Waebrania 4:9-11.

Ni muhimu kuona kwamba dhana ya kupumzika katika Agano Jipya ni zaidi ya kupata tu muda wa kutofanya kazi. Amani ya kweli ya kibiblia imefungamana kwa kina na dhana ya amani, hata katikati ya ulimwengu wenye vurugu. Amani nawaachieni; amani yangu nawapa; niwapavyo mimi sivyo kama ulimwengu utoavyo. Msifadhaike mioyoni mwenu, wala msiwe na woga –Yohana 14:27. Yesu aliwapa wafuasi wake amani iliyowawezesha kutulia, hata walipokuwa wakikabiliwa na msongo mkubwa.

Hii ni baraka, kwa kuwa haitoshi tu kuchukua muda wa kupumzika kutoka katika kazi zetu za kawaida. Tunahitaji kuwa na amani na utulivu unaotokana na uhusiano na Yesu. Bila …amani ya Mungu, ipitayo akili zote… –Wafilipi 4:7, muda wetu wa mapumziko hautakuwa na utulivu kama vile muda wetu wa kazi.

Ni wazi kwamba Mungu anataka tupumzike. Anajua kwamba tunahitaji kupumzika, si kwa sababu za kiroho tu, bali pia kwa afya yetu ya kimwili.

******************************

Viongozi wa Mapinduzi ya Ufaransa walijaribu kufutilia mbali taasisi zote za zamani. Lilikuwa jaribio lililokuwa halimcha Mungu kabisa, na miongoni mwa mambo mengine, serikali mpya iliamua “kurekebisha” kalenda.

Mwaka wa 1793, walianzisha juma la kazi la siku kumi. Kila mwezi ungekuwa na majuma matatu, kila moja likiwa na siku moja ya mapumziko ndani ya juma hilo la siku kumi. Lengo lao, miongoni mwa mambo mengine, lilikuwa kufutilia mbali sikukuu zote za kidini na maadhimisho ya Jumapili kuwa siku ya mapumziko. Waliamini kwamba kazi nyingi zaidi zingefanywa kwa kuwa na siku chache za mapumziko kila mwezi.

Jambo hili liliwasababishia watengenezaji saa tatizo kubwa sana. Walihitaji kwa namna fulani kutengeneza saa zilizoweza kufuata maelezo ya maagizo haya mapya—kila siku ingekuwa na saa kumi, kila saa ingekuwa na dakika mia moja, na kila dakika ingekuwa na sekunde 100.

Hatimaye, jambo hilo likawa janga. Watu walichukia mabadiliko hayo na uzalishaji ulipungua sana kote Ufaransa. Mwishowe, mwaka wa 1806, Napolioni alivifuta na kurudia kalenda ya zamani na mfumo wa siku za mapumziko za Jumapili. “Jaribio” hili la kisayansi lilikuwa limekwisha. Inavyoonekana, watu wanahitaji nyakati za kupumzika na kupata nguvu upya, na kwamba juma la siku saba lenye siku moja ya kupumzika si dhana ya Kikristo tu; ni jambo muhimu kwa afya na ustawi.

Umoja wa Kisovyeti, chini ya Joseph Stalin, pia ulijaribu jaribio kama hilo la kufutilia mbali mapumziko ya Jumapili, likiwa na matokeo kama hayo.

******************************

Juma, kama Mungu alivyoliumba (likiwa na siku moja ya kupumzika kati ya siku saba), ni muhimu ili tuendelee kuwa na uwezo wa kufanya kazi.

Kupumzika Hupunguza Uvimbe

Sehemu ya tatizo linalowakabili watu wa kisasa ni kwamba wanakabiliwa na viwango vya juu vya homoni za msongo, kama vile adrenalini na kortisoli. Homoni hizi huongeza shinikizo la damu na kasi ya mapigo ya moyo. Pia huongeza viwango vya uvimbe katika miili yetu.

Uvimbe wa muda mrefu si mzuri kwa afya, lakini kwa bahati nzuri, kupumzika kwa kweli huonekana kusaidia sana kupunguza viwango hivyo vya homoni. Usingizi mzuri wa usiku ni muhimu kwa uponyaji, hasa kwa sababu hupunguza homoni hizi na kuruhusu neva na tishu zilizofanya kazi kupita kiasi kupona.

Magonjwa ya kingamwili na viwango vya maumivu hupungua watu wanapopata usingizi wa kutosha. Shinikizo la damu na matatizo ya moyo pia hunufaika mtu anapopata usingizi wa kutosha unaorejesha nguvu.

Mapumziko Huwezesha Uponyaji

Mazoezi ni jambo zuri. Madaktari wanapendekeza kufanya mazoezi ya mara kwa mara ya moyo na mishipa ya damu kwa sababu ni mazuri kwa moyo, akili na ustawi wetu kwa ujumla.

Si busara kufanya mazoezi kila siku. Mazoezi pia huongeza viwango vya homoni za msongo na hayaupi mwili wetu muda wa kutosha wa kupona. Watu wanaofanya mazoezi mara nyingi mno na kwa nguvu kupita kiasi wana uwezekano mkubwa zaidi wa kupata majeraha yanayosumbua kwa muda mrefu, maumivu ya viungo na misuli, pamoja na uchovu. Utafiti mmoja uligundua kwamba misuli huchukua saa 72 kupona kikamilifu baada ya mazoezi ya kunyanyua vyuma.

Ni vyema watu wanaofanya mazoezi wapumzike siku moja hadi mbili kwa juma ili kuupa mwili nafasi ya kupona kutokana na shughuli hizo. Kadiri unavyozidi kufanya mazoezi kwa bidii, ndivyo unavyohitaji zaidi nyakati hizo za mapumziko. Hata mtu anayefanya mazoezi kwa bidii kwa ajili ya jambo kama vile mbio za marathoni anahitaji kuchukua siku za hapa na pale bila kukimbia, la sivyo atajijeruhi.

Mapumziko Hupunguza Maumivu

Kumekuwa na tafiti nyingi zilizochunguza taarifa za watu kuhusu usingizi na kutazama mambo kama vile maumivu ya muda mrefu na maumivu ya kichwa yanayosababishwa na mkazo. Angalau asilimia 50 ya watu wenye tatizo la kukosa usingizi pia wana maumivu ya muda mrefu. Bila shaka, huenda tu ikawa kwamba watu wenye maumivu ya muda mrefu hawalali vizuri kama watu wasio na maumivu hayo.

Kumekuwa na tafiti kadhaa zilizochunguza uwezo wa watu kustahimili maumivu baada ya kunyimwa usingizi. Ziligundua kwamba hata usiku mmoja tu wa kunyimwa usingizi ulitosha kuwafanya watu wahisi maumivu kwa ukali zaidi.

Mapumziko Huboresha Mifumo Yetu ya Kinga

Kumekuwa na tafiti kadhaa zilizochunguza utendaji wa sehemu mbalimbali za mifumo yetu ya kinga na kugundua kwamba hufanya kazi vizuri zaidi washiriki wa utafiti wanapopata usingizi wa kutosha. Huenda viwango vya uvimbe vinavyokuwa juu zaidi tusipopumzika ndivyo vinavyoongeza hatari ya maambukizi.

Tunapojisukuma kupita kiasi bila kupumzika, mifumo yetu ya kinga huathirika. Kwa upande mwingine, njia bora zaidi ya kupona ni kuhakikisha kwamba tunapumzika vya kutosha.

Kuna mambo mengine mengi yanayofanywa na mapumziko. Husaidia kuboresha hali ya kihisia. Yanaweza kusaidia katika ufaulu wa masomo na kazi za kumbukumbu.

Kama ilivyo kwa mambo yote, kiasi cha wastani ndicho muhimu. Mtu asiyefanya chochote ila kupumzika na kulala hatakuwa na utendaji bora zaidi kuliko mtu anayelala vizuri kwa saa saba kila usiku, wala hatakuwa na tija sana.

Kuna kanuni kadhaa za msingi zinazoweza kutusaidia kupata nyakati za mapumziko.

Pumzika Mara kwa Mara

Ujumbe wa Sabato ni kwamba tunahitaji kutenga nyakati fupi za kupumzika mara kwa mara. Miaka ya Yubile inatuambia kwamba tunahitaji nyakati ndefu zaidi za kupata nguvu upya, ingawa si za mara kwa mara. Inahitaji juhudi na kupanga ratiba ili kuhakikisha kwamba nyakati hizi zinakuwa za mapumziko ya kweli.

Labda ni kama gari. Unaweza kusafiri umbali fulani tu kwa kutumia tanki moja la mafuta. Ukiendelea kusubiri hadi taa ya tahadhari iwake ndipo ujaze tanki hilo, hatimaye jambo hilo litakutokea ukiwa mbali mno na kituo cha mafuta kiasi kwamba hutaweza kujaza kabla mafuta hayajaisha. Hakuna wakati unaofaa wa kuishiwa mafuta. Vivyo hivyo, tunahitaji mara kwa mara kuchaji upya nguvu zetu za kiroho, kihisia na kimwili. Hakuna sababu ya kusubiri hadi dalili za tahadhari zionekane ndipo tupate kuona kwamba tunahitaji sana kupumzika.

Mapumziko Yanahitaji Maandalizi

Simulizi la zawadi ya mana katika Kutoka 16 linatuambia kwamba mana ilikuja kila siku. Watu hawangeweza kuihifadhi kwa siku ya pili kwa sababu ingeanza kuharibika. Hata hivyo, siku za Ijumaa walipaswa kukusanya zaidi kwa kuwa siku iliyofuata ilikuwa siku ya mapumziko, na mana haikuja siku ya Sabato. Wale ambao hawakukusanya ya ziada siku iliyotangulia walibaki na njaa.

Vivyo hivyo, inahitaji maandalizi ili kupata nyakati za aina hii. Haitakuwa rahisi, lakini ni muhimu.

Fanya Mambo Yenye Afya Wakati wa Mapumziko

Watu wanapokuwa na msongo wa mawazo huwa na mwelekeo wa kula vitu visivyo na afya. Watu wanapokuwa wamechoka sana kwa kawaida hawajisikii kufanya mazoezi au kutembea. Haya ndiyo mambo yanayoweza kutusaidia sana kupata nguvu upya, kimwili na kihisia.

Tena, hili linahitaji juhudi fulani, lakini ni muhimu kwa ustawi wetu kuchagua mambo yenye afya.

Mkazie Mungu Fikira

Nimeyaacha haya hadi mwisho, lakini ndiyo kipengele muhimu zaidi cha kupumzika. Mapumziko ya kweli hayatokani na dawa au hata likizo nyingi, bali hutokana na moyo uliojaa amani. Amani ipitayo ufahamu hutokana na moyo unaomkazia Mungu fikira.

Nyakati zetu za sala na kusoma Biblia zinapaswa kuwa nyakati za mapumziko. Tukiondoa vikengeusha-fikira na changamoto za kazi na maisha ya nyumbani, na kuelekeza macho yetu kwa Yule aliye wa maana kuliko wote, tutapokea baraka ya kweli na nguvu mpya ambazo roho zetu zinahitaji.

Nina wasiwasi kwamba watu wengi wanahangaika kupata pumziko kwa sababu hawana amani ya kweli. Basi, na tufanye bidii kuingia katika raha ile, ili kwamba mtu ye yote asije akaanguka kwa mfano uo huo wa kuasi –Waebrania 4:11. Pumziko linalozungumziwa hapa ni lile lililoahidiwa kwa wale wanaodumu na kupokea amani ya Mungu.

Hitimisho

Maisha yanahusu uwiano. Kuna nyakati tunazohitaji kufanya kazi na pia kuna nyakati tunazopaswa kupumzika. Kupata uwiano huo ndiyo changamoto inayomkabili kila mmoja wetu. Jambo lililo hakika ni kwamba kila siku ya saa 24 itajaa kabisa tunapofika mwisho wake.

Mungu anatuona pamoja na mipaka yetu, na anatamani tufikie uwiano huu kati ya kazi zetu na nyakati zetu za kupumzika. Tukielekeza fikira zetu kwake tu, atatuongoza kupata uwiano huo.

Zaidi ya yote, tutapokea amani isiyo na thamani, itakayotuwezesha kupata pumziko—hata wakati wa dhoruba.

Marejeo ya Mwisho

Thou hast the dew of thy youth. Psalm 110:3

There are many aspects of youth which are not virtuous. Many youth of our day experience an early season of callused carelessness and casualty. Often decisions that are made in youthful years set the foundation for the rest of their lives. It was a the younger prodigal brother that asked for an early draw on his inheritance then went and wasted it on riotous living. It was a young Dinah who wandered from her father’s house and …went out to see the daughters of the land –Genesis 34:1. There, she was exposed to the heathen young men of the land and occasioned a bloody massacre, leaving Jacob as a stench in the land. Many foolish young people have sown to the wind and reaped the havoc thereof. Those that are void of solid principles and parental authority are at high risk for spiritual shipwreck.

There are particular lusts that inflict youth more so than the aged, and the young are exhorted to flee them. (–see 2 Timothy 2:22) Solomon looked through his window casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding -Proverbs 7:6-7. The young man was in heartfelt pursuit of that which appeared lovely… [Un]Till a dart [struck] through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life –Proverbs 7:23. We could examine the vices from the youthful lives of Rehoboam, Amnon, Nadab and Abihu, and countless others. We also find no lack of modern, folly-filled examples about us fulfilled by frivolous youth.

But youth are not meant to be despised. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. In fact, God generally chooses the youth as the instruments of His propagation. Joseph, of sterling character, was sent by God into Egypt at the age of 17 to preserve life (–see Genesis 45:5). Miriam, at the age of twelve, stood post over the future deliverer of the entire Jewish nation and secured her own mother, Jochebed, to be the nurse of the baby Moses. David, as a youth, was sent to encourage his brethren in the army. He was despised by his brothers: …I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart… –1 Samuel 17:28. He was rejected by Saul: …Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth… –1 Samuel 17:33. He was scorned by Goliath: …Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves… –1 Samuel 17:43. But their contempt was all for naught when he was chosen by God to be king over all Israel.

These noble youthful ambitions were followed by Josiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Mary, and the disciples of the Lord, all who chose to remember their Creator in the days of their youth. But these were not naive specimens seeking to secure their place in life, they were graphic examples of youth who were seeking to imitate the image of their Lord.

We need not gaze long into the character of Christ before we find…

...Thou hast the dew of thy youth

Psalm 110 is perhaps the most referred-to scripture in the Old Testament. This rhetorical portrait of the Messiah reveals a vivid virtue for us to behold. Christ, as the Ancient of days, was described in the Revelation having His head and His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet, here He is depicted as eternally young, as He sits at the right hand of God (–see Psalm 110:1). No weariness of age can enter there, for Christ is the Morning Star. It is perpetual morning around the throne of God. Those saints who are following hard after His likeness will also reflect this virtue, for the light of Jesus is the light of youth.

The psalmist, describing the Messiah, draws from the natural beauty of the morning dew (–see Psalm 110:3). The thought of dew calls us back from the heavens and unveils before us a portrait of this earth on which we dwell. In heaven there is no night, no change of heat and cold, no need of the sun to light up the day and consequently… no dew. The nature of dew belongs to the terrestrial, where everyone who will but stoop to observe it will behold a uniformed regiment of grass sparkling as if embedded with a myriad of diamonds. After a long night of darkness, the dewdrops, like tears, stand in the eyes of the flowers as they weep for joy at the advent of the first morning sunbeam. Those who walk through the lowly vegetation will have their feet washed by a thousand caressing hands of God’s design. Christ is not depicted as the dew of the morning but as the dew of youth, and the imagery is stretched further.

Youth is the season of abounding energy. Some cannot sit still. They are generally interpersonal creatures who love social activity. This is neither a virtue nor a vice. Rather, it is nominal nature. There is a progressive strain in advancing years that tames and tempers the soul. As life progresses, there is a clearer vision and a steadier thought, and we rise to better things. But when the mid-life summit has been crossed and the feet are traveling downward on the slope, that tumultuous rush of bodily energy that plowed through anything becomes enshrined with memories of the past. It is the closest comfort many can find to the bygone days of their strength.

But Christ has not called us to foster a fondness for the past nor a wistful longing for the “DO” of our youth. So many today sadly lament that their ‘get-up-and-go’ has got up and went. These have no vision for higher things and are more energized by a can of Mountain Dew than the Dew of Youth. They are more inspired by a trip down memory lane and reminiscing events of the past than of the hope that lies before them.

Age is no hindrance to securing the dew of youth. The Ancient of Days still rides forth among the golden candlesticks. While John beheld His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet Solomon declares …his locks are bushy, and black as a raven –Song of Solomon 5:11. While age may steal our strength and hearing, …the LORD’S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: –Isaiah 59:1. He has secured the dew of youth and invites us to partake. The problem is not found in our deteriorating body but in a spiritually declining mind. The bane of old age predominately sets in when the mind follows the body.

It is not that life grows poorer as it advances or ceases to be noble when the charm of youth has faded. If we were placed here only to experience joy, the dying out of youthful romance would be terrible. God had a much greater end in view for His children than to just be vibrant ‘doers’. We are sent here to learn. Our allotted years upon earth are all meant to be a schooling, and it is not in the bright romance of youth that we learn the best and most abiding lessons. It is in the dogged doing of our duty, the quiet acceptance of our limitations, the patient carrying of our daily burden, and in the stretching out of a helping hand to our brother. These afford us the true opportunities for Christian culture and are the roots of ethical nobility. Christ labored …not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life… –John 6:27, and He finished His earthly task in 33 years. But the dew of youth did not dissipate as He sat down at the right hand of His Father.

Thus, we conclude that this youthfulness will not be secured by strength, but by…

...Hope

But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. –Hebrews 10:12-13.

How shall we picture this Christ now? Reclining in an easy chair, all worn out from His experience with the stubborn people of this earth? Is He busy putting together a scrap book of precious memories? This is too often the position of the aged and so their mind dies with their bodies.

And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope –Romans 5:3-4. At times, we wonder if this scripture can be true. Anyone with any age on their bones can testify to a poor experience and the subsequent feelings of hopelessness following. As people, we have all faced disappointing experiences with a spouse, a child, or a church relationship after which a nagging cloud of despair settles in. Outside of Christ, a sour experience always tends to pessimism. It was so in the world when Jesus came. It is still so today.

But the dew of youth is incurably hopeful. There is an effervescent expectation that is naturally and magnificently borne in youth and retained in Christ. In every winter, when the fields are bleak, and the cold gust goes whistling through the trees, there lies the hope that the flowers will spring again. In every spring there is the hope of summer. In every summer there is the hope of harvest. It is alive in nature and alive in youth. Those who are blind to it shall reap, at best, a dreary monotone existence. To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all. –Oscar Wilde.

The rest shall be brightly effected with a hope that…

…Heals Our Infirmities

Our bodies are destined for the grave and have no hope for renewal in this life. It is our minds that carry our greatest infirmities. The impotent man of 38 years at Bethesda could only utter a hopeless complaint when Christ asked him, …Wilt thou be made whole? –John 5:6. Upon the wake of his new day, a new remedy was given to him—… Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee –John 5:14. What could be worse than being a cripple for years? A mind that is beset by a doleful indulgence in the sorrows of this world. Age sets in when we have more memories of the past than hope for tomorrow. It is disappointing when folks grow old and have no vision for tomorrow, but it is a disaster to behold youth that are plagued by its crippling effects. Many grope aimlessly through life’s various trials, stupefied by the lack of blessedness. The noonday sun has evaporated the dew of their youth and the only praise that they can muster is culminated from a handful of yesterday’s pleasantries. A new attitude must be birthed by the dew of a new morning.

…Humbles Our Pursuits

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. –John 21:18. When we are young, we can overcome in the strength of our youth. As age takes its course, we will find a different alternative: victory through surrender.

…I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one. –1 John 2:14. The world entices us to selfish living. Youth are often subject to schools of learning that teach them to “be all that you can be”. There is a major focus on self-enhancement and preparation for the future. This may prepare them in a ‘survival of the fittest’ world but will leave them destitute when the strength and prowess of youth has departed.

For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever. –1 John 2:16-17. Overcoming evil with good is the Biblical antidote for channeling youthful energies. Whether it is the lust within or the longing without, hope is conceived by planting a seed of kindness in the life of another. The pursuit of pleasure and lieu of leisure will always disappoint its recipient and leave him in a valley of despair deeper than when he began. It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth … He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope. –Lamentations 3:27-29. We are created to work in God’s vineyard and those who have an appetite for it will reap in hope of its youthful reward.

…Hallows Our Trials

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope... –Romans 8:24. How often we can relate to Job in his pain. But before his pain had received an ounce of retribution, the healing streams began to flow as Job reverenced his Creator. When we can acknowledge that God is perfect in all the trials He allows, we then learn to worship in the temple not made with hands and disregard the frailties of the body. To sit down at the feet of Christ ignites a youthful spark that radiates the spirit within and conceives hope. The dew of youth then becomes our portion as Christ imparts eternal life and eternal youth to us. From the hour of the grave and through eternity we shall be young and bid defiance to weariness and death if we are living in the morning light of Jesus Christ. Heaven is a place of perpetual youth, and just like the light of the sun is reflected on the moon, so likewise the light of Christ is reflected on His bride. She is clean and young, …a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing… –Ephesians 5:27. Blessed is the venerable saint who arrives at the portals of heaven in such a condition.

주께서 청년의 이슬을 가지셨나이다. 시편 110:3

젊음에는 미덕이 아닌 측면도 많이 있습니다. 오늘날 많은 젊은이는 일찍부터 무감각한 부주의와 경솔함에 빠지는 시기를 겪습니다. 젊은 시절 내리는 결정은 흔히 남은 생애의 토대가 됩니다. 더 어린 탕자는 유산을 미리 달라고 한 뒤 떠나 방탕한 생활로 그것을 탕진했습니다. 젊은 디나도 아버지의 집을 떠나 …그 땅의 딸들을 보러 나갔더라—창세기 34:1. 그곳에서 그녀는 그 땅의 이방 젊은이들에게 노출되었고, 피비린내 나는 학살을 초래하여 야곱이 그 땅에서 악취가 되게 했습니다. 어리석은 젊은이들 가운데에는 바람에 씨를 뿌리고 그로 인한 참화를 거둔 이들이 많습니다. 견고한 원칙과 부모의 권위가 없는 이들은 영적으로 파선할 위험이 매우 큽니다.

나이 든 이들보다 젊은이들에게 더 큰 해를 끼치는 특별한 정욕들이 있으며, 젊은이들은 그것들을 피하라는 권고를 받습니다. (—디모데후서 2:22 참조) 솔로몬은 창문 틈으로 내다보다가, 어리석은 자들 중에서, 젊은이들 가운데서 분별 없는 한 청년을 보았나니—잠언 7:6-7. 그 젊은이는 마음을 다해 아름다워 보이는 것을 좇았습니다… [그때까지] 화살이 그의 간을 꿰뚫었나니, 새가 올가미로 급히 날아들면서 그것이 자기 생명을 노리는 줄 알지 못함과 같도다—잠언 7:23. 르호보암, 암논, 나답과 아비후, 그리고 셀 수 없이 많은 이들의 젊은 시절에 나타난 악덕들을 살펴볼 수도 있습니다. 우리 주변에는 경솔한 젊은이들이 저지르는 어리석음으로 가득한 현대의 사례도 얼마든지 있습니다.

그러나 젊은이들을 멸시해서는 안 됩니다. 아무도 네 젊음을 업신여기지 못하게 하고, 오직 말과 행실과 사랑과 영과 믿음과 정결에 있어서 믿는 자들의 본이 되라—디모데전서 4:12. 사실 하나님께서는 자신의 복음을 전하는 도구로 대체로 젊은이들을 택하십니다. 성품이 고결했던 요셉은 생명을 보존하도록 하나님께서 열일곱 살에 이집트로 보내셨습니다. (—창세기 45:5 참조) 열두 살의 미리암은 온 유대 민족의 미래의 구원자를 지키며 서 있었고, 자기 어머니 요게벳을 불러 아기 모세의 유모가 되게 했습니다. 다윗은 젊은 시절 군대에 있는 형제들을 격려하러 보내졌습니다. 형들은 그를 멸시했습니다. …나는 네 교만과 네 마음의 악함을 아노니…—사무엘상 17:28. 사울은 그를 거부했습니다. …너는 그 블레셋 사람과 싸우러 갈 수 없느니라. 너는 아직 소년이요…—사무엘상 17:33. 골리앗은 그를 조롱했습니다. …네가 막대기를 가지고 내게 오니 내가 개냐…—사무엘상 17:43. 그러나 하나님께서 그를 온 이스라엘의 왕으로 택하시자 그들의 멸시는 모두 헛된 것이 되었습니다.

이러한 고귀한 젊은 시절의 열망은 요시야, 이사야, 예레미야, 다니엘, 마리아와 주님의 제자들에게 이어졌습니다. 그들은 모두 젊은 시절에 창조주를 기억하기로 했습니다. 그러나 그들은 인생에서 자신의 자리를 확보하려는 순진한 표본이 아니었습니다. 주님의 형상을 본받고자 한 젊은이들의 생생한 본보기였습니다.

그리스도의 성품을 오래 들여다보지 않아도 우리는 다음을 발견합니다…

...주께서 청년의 이슬을 가지셨나이다

시편 110편은 구약성경에서 가장 자주 인용되는 말씀일 것입니다. 메시아를 수사적으로 그려 낸 이 초상은 우리가 바라볼 생생한 미덕을 보여 줍니다. 옛적부터 계신 이로서 그리스도께서는 계시록에서 그의 머리와 머리털은 … 양털같이 희고 눈같이 희더라…—요한계시록 1:14고 묘사되셨지만, 여기서는 하나님의 오른편에 앉으신 채 (—시편 110:1 참조) 영원히 젊으신 분으로 그려집니다. 그곳에는 나이에서 오는 피로가 들어설 수 없습니다. 그리스도께서는 새벽별이시기 때문입니다. 하나님의 보좌 둘레에는 언제나 아침이 있습니다. 그분의 모습을 온전히 좇는 성도들도 이 미덕을 반영할 것입니다. 예수님의 빛은 젊음의 빛이기 때문입니다.

시편 기자는 메시아를 묘사하며 아침 이슬의 자연스러운 아름다움을 끌어옵니다. (—시편 110:3 참조) 이슬을 생각하면 하늘에서 다시 이 땅으로 시선을 돌리게 되고, 우리가 사는 이 땅의 모습이 눈앞에 펼쳐집니다. 하늘에는 밤도, 더위와 추위의 변화도, 낮을 밝힐 해의 필요도 없으며, 따라서… 이슬도 없습니다. 이슬의 본성은 지상에 속한 것입니다. 몸을 굽혀 바라보기만 하면 누구나 무수한 다이아몬드가 박힌 듯 반짝이는 풀들의 가지런한 대열을 볼 수 있습니다. 긴 어둠의 밤이 지나면 이슬방울은 눈물처럼 꽃들의 눈에 맺혀 첫 아침 햇살이 찾아오는 기쁨에 웁니다. 낮은 풀숲 사이를 걷는 이들은 하나님의 솜씨로 마련된 천 개의 어루만지는 손에 발을 씻김 받을 것입니다. 그리스도께서는 아침 이슬이 아니라 청년의 이슬로 묘사되시며, 이 이미지는 더 확장됩니다.

젊음은 넘치는 활력의 시기입니다. 가만히 앉아 있지 못하는 이들도 있습니다. 이들은 대체로 사람들과 어울리기를 좋아하고 사교 활동을 즐깁니다. 이것은 미덕도 악덕도 아닙니다. 그저 타고난 본성입니다. 나이가 들수록 점진적인 긴장이 영혼을 길들이고 다듬습니다. 삶이 이어지면서 시야는 더 맑아지고 생각은 더 차분해지며, 우리는 더 나은 것을 향해 나아갑니다. 그러나 중년의 정점을 지나 발걸음이 내리막길로 향하면, 무엇이든 밀어붙이던 그 거센 신체적 활력은 과거의 추억 속에 자리 잡습니다. 많은 이들이 지난날의 힘에 가장 가까이 다가갈 수 있는 위안은 바로 그것입니다.

그러나 그리스도께서는 과거를 애틋하게 여기거나 젊은 시절의 “기운”을 그리워하라고 우리를 부르시지 않았습니다. 오늘날 너무나 많은 이들이 안타깝게도 “일어설 힘”이 사라졌다고 한탄합니다. 이들에게는 더 높은 것을 향한 비전이 없으며, 청년의 이슬보다 마운틴 듀 한 캔에서 더 큰 활력을 얻습니다. 앞에 놓인 소망보다 추억의 길을 거닐며 과거의 일을 회상하는 데서 더 큰 영감을 얻습니다.

나이는 청년의 이슬을 얻는 데 장애가 되지 않습니다. 옛적부터 계신 이께서는 여전히 금촛대 사이를 다니십니다. 요한은 그의 머리와 머리털은 … 양털같이 희고 눈같이 희더라…—요한계시록 1:14고 보았지만, 솔로몬은 …그의 머리털은 무성하고 까마귀같이 검구나—아가 5:11.라고 선언합니다. 나이가 우리의 힘과 청력을 앗아 갈 수는 있지만, …여호와의 손이 짧아 구원하지 못하심도 아니요 그의 귀가 둔하여 듣지 못하심도 아니니라—이사야 59:1. 주님께서는 청년의 이슬을 마련하셨고 우리에게 그것을 누리라고 초대하십니다. 문제는 쇠약해지는 몸이 아니라 영적으로 쇠퇴하는 마음에 있습니다. 노년의 고통은 대체로 마음이 몸을 따라 쇠퇴할 때 시작됩니다.

삶이 진전될수록 더 빈곤해지거나 젊음의 매력이 사라지면 고귀함도 사라진다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 우리가 오직 기쁨을 경험하기 위해 이곳에 놓였다면, 젊은 시절의 낭만이 사그라드는 일은 끔찍할 것입니다. 하나님께서는 자녀들이 그저 활기 넘치는 ‘행동가’가 되는 것보다 훨씬 더 큰 목적을 두셨습니다. 우리는 배우기 위해 이곳에 보내졌습니다. 이 땅에서 우리에게 주어진 세월은 모두 배움의 시간이며, 가장 훌륭하고 오래 남는 교훈은 젊음의 눈부신 낭만 속에서 배우는 것이 아닙니다. 의무를 끈기 있게 수행하고, 자신의 한계를 조용히 받아들이며, 매일의 짐을 인내로 지고, 형제에게 도움의 손길을 내미는 가운데 배웁니다. 이러한 일들이야말로 그리스도인의 인격을 함양할 진정한 기회이며 윤리적 고귀함의 뿌리입니다. 그리스도께서는 …썩는 양식을 위하여 일하지 말고 영생하도록 있는 양식을 위하여 하라…—요한복음 6:27고 하셨으며, 서른세 해 만에 이 땅에서 맡으신 일을 마치셨습니다. 그러나 아버지의 오른편에 앉으셨을 때에도 청년의 이슬은 사라지지 않았습니다.

그러므로 우리는 이러한 젊음이 힘으로 얻어지는 것이 아니라…로 얻어진다고 결론 내립니다.

...소망

이 사람은 죄를 위하여 한 영원한 제사를 드리신 후 하나님의 오른편에 앉으사, 그 후로는 그의 원수들이 그의 발등상이 될 때까지 기다리시느니라.—히브리서 10:12-13.

지금 이 그리스도를 어떻게 그려야 할까요? 이 땅의 완고한 백성과 겪은 일로 완전히 지쳐 안락의자에 기대어 계신 모습일까요? 소중한 추억을 모아 스크랩북을 만드느라 바쁘실까요? 나이 든 이들은 너무나 자주 그런 상태에 놓이고, 그리하여 그들의 마음도 몸과 함께 죽어 갑니다.

그뿐 아니라 우리가 환난 중에도 즐거워하나니, 이는 환난은 인내를, 인내는 연단을, 연단은 소망을 이루는 줄 앎이로다—로마서 5:3-4. 때로 우리는 이 말씀이 참일 수 있는지 의문을 품습니다. 나이가 든 사람이라면 누구나 좋지 않은 경험과 그 뒤를 잇는 절망감을 증언할 수 있습니다. 우리는 모두 사람으로서 배우자나 자녀, 교회와의 관계에서 실망스러운 일을 겪었고, 그 뒤에는 지독한 절망의 구름이 내려앉습니다. 그리스도 밖에서는 괴로운 경험이 언제나 비관적인 마음으로 이어지기 쉽습니다. 예수님께서 오셨을 때 세상도 그랬습니다. 오늘날에도 여전히 그렇습니다.

그러나 청년의 이슬은 고칠 수 없을 만큼 소망으로 가득합니다. 젊음에는 본래 넘치고 찬란한 기대가 있으며, 그 기대는 그리스도 안에서 보존됩니다. 들판이 황량하고 차가운 돌풍이 나무 사이로 휘파람을 불며 지나가는 겨울마다 꽃들이 다시 피어날 소망이 있습니다. 봄마다 여름의 소망이 있고, 여름마다 추수의 소망이 있습니다. 그것은 자연 속에서 살아 있고 젊음 속에서도 살아 있습니다. 이를 보지 못하는 이들은 기껏해야 음울하고 단조로운 삶을 거둘 것입니다. 산다는 것은 세상에서 가장 드문 일이다. 대부분의 사람은 그저 존재할 뿐이다.—오스카 와일드.

나머지 사람들은 다음과 같은 소망으로 환히 물들 것입니다…

…우리의 연약함을 치유합니다

우리의 몸은 무덤으로 향하며 이 생에서 새로워질 소망이 없습니다. 가장 큰 연약함은 우리 마음에 있습니다. 베데스다의 서른여덟 해 된 병자는 그리스도께서 …네가 낫고자 하느냐?—요한복음 5:6.고 물으셨을 때 절망스러운 하소연만 할 수 있었습니다. 새날이 밝자 그에게 새로운 처방이 주어졌습니다. …보라 네가 나았으니 더 심한 것이 생기지 않게 다시는 죄를 범하지 말라—요한복음 5:14. 여러 해 동안 걷지 못한 것보다 더 심한 것이 무엇이겠습니까? 이 세상의 슬픔에 침잠하여 비통함을 탐닉하는 마음입니다. 과거의 추억은 많아지고 내일의 소망은 줄어들 때 나이가 들어갑니다. 사람들이 늙어 내일을 바라보는 비전이 없게 되는 것은 실망스럽지만, 젊은이들이 그처럼 마비시키는 영향에 시달리는 것을 보는 것은 재앙입니다. 많은 이들이 삶의 여러 시련 속을 방향도 없이 더듬거리며, 복된 삶이 없다는 사실에 넋을 잃습니다. 한낮의 해가 그들의 청년의 이슬을 증발시켰고, 그들이 겨우 내놓을 수 있는 찬양은 어제의 즐거움 몇 가지를 모아 겨우 이루어집니다. 새 아침의 이슬로 새로운 태도가 태어나야 합니다.

…우리의 추구를 겸손하게 합니다

내가 진실로 진실로 네게 이르노니, 네가 젊어서는 스스로 띠 띠고 원하는 곳으로 다녔거니와 늙어서는 네 팔을 벌리리니 남이 네게 띠 띠우고 원하지 아니하는 곳으로 데려가리라.—요한복음 21:18. 젊을 때는 젊음의 힘으로 이겨 낼 수 있습니다. 나이가 들어감에 따라 우리는 다른 길, 곧 항복을 통한 승리를 발견하게 됩니다.

…청년들아 내가 너희에게 쓰는 것은 너희가 강하고 하나님의 말씀이 너희 안에 거하며 너희가 악한 자를 이겼음이라.—요한일서 2:14. 세상은 이기적인 삶을 살도록 우리를 유혹합니다. 젊은이들은 흔히 “할 수 있는 모든 것을 이루라”고 가르치는 교육에 노출됩니다. 자기 계발과 미래를 준비하는 데 크게 초점을 둡니다. 이는 ‘적자생존’의 세상에서 살아남도록 준비시킬 수는 있겠지만, 젊음의 힘과 기량이 사라지면 그들을 빈곤하게 만들 것입니다.

이는 세상에 있는 모든 것, 곧 육신의 정욕과 안목의 정욕과 이생의 자랑이 아버지께로부터 온 것이 아니요 세상으로부터 온 것이라. 이 세상도, 그 정욕도 지나가되 오직 하나님의 뜻을 행하는 자는 영원히 거하느니라.—요한일서 2:16-17. 선으로 악을 이기는 것은 젊음의 활력을 올바른 길로 이끄는 성경적 해독제입니다. 내면의 정욕이든 밖으로 향하는 갈망이든, 다른 사람의 삶에 친절의 씨앗을 심을 때 소망이 잉태됩니다. 쾌락을 좇고 여가를 추구하는 일은 언제나 그것을 좇는 사람을 실망시키고, 처음보다 더 깊은 절망의 골짜기에 빠뜨립니다. 사람이 젊었을 때에 멍에를 메는 것이 좋으니 … 그가 입을 티끌에 댈지어다. 혹시 소망이 있을지로다.—예레미야애가 3:27-29. 우리는 하나님의 포도원에서 일하도록 지음 받았으며, 그 일을 열망하는 사람들은 청년다운 보상을 소망하며 거두게 될 것입니다.

…우리의 시련을 거룩하게 합니다

우리가 소망으로 구원을 얻었으매 보이는 소망이 소망이 아니니…—로마서 8:24. 고통 가운데 있는 욥에게 공감할 때가 얼마나 많은지요. 그러나 그의 고통에 조금이라도 보응이 주어지기 전에, 욥이 창조주를 경외하자 치유의 물줄기가 흐르기 시작했습니다. 하나님께서 허락하시는 모든 시련 가운데 완전하시다는 사실을 인정할 때, 우리는 사람의 손으로 짓지 않은 성전에서 예배드리고 몸의 연약함을 개의치 않는 법을 배웁니다. 그리스도의 발치에 앉으면 우리 안의 영을 비추고 소망을 잉태하게 하는 젊음의 불꽃이 타오릅니다. 그리스도께서 우리에게 영원한 생명과 영원한 젊음을 주실 때 청년의 이슬은 우리의 몫이 됩니다. 예수 그리스도의 아침 빛 가운데 살아간다면, 무덤의 순간부터 영원토록 우리는 젊음을 누리며 피로와 죽음에 맞설 것입니다. 하늘은 영원한 젊음의 장소입니다. 태양의 빛이 달에 비치듯 그리스도의 빛은 그분의 신부에게 비칩니다. 신부는 깨끗하고 젊으며, …영광스러운 교회로서 티나 주름 잡힌 것이나 이런 것들이 없어야 하느니라…—에베소서 5:27. 이와 같은 모습으로 하늘의 문에 이르는 존귀한 성도는 복되도다.

I’ll walk with God—Today—
Tomorrow may not be.
I’ll make the best of TIME—right now—
That God has granted me.

I’ll plan not for a life
That I might live in ease,
But only for today to live
My God alone to please.

Nor dare I think in years
Or move from leaps to bounds;
With God shut out, and self shut in
And selfish aims surround.

There are those who plan their lives,
Who give God little thought;
Who weigh themselves, not with God’s truth,
As every day they ought!

“Boast not thyself,” I’m warned,
“Of what tomorrow brings;
Thy health and wealth—e’en life itself—
May all at once take wings!”

“This night, that soul of thine
May be required of thee:
And dost thou plan the New Year full
There, ‘neath some Christmas tree?”

“Wake up! Take stock, are you prepared?
Your lessons learned alright?
If God, in yet three hours, THIS DAY,
Should close your course TONIGHT?”

Nitatembea na Mungu—Leo—
Kesho huenda isiwepo.
Nitatumia VIZURI WAKATI—sasa hivi—
Ambao Mungu amenijalia.

Sitapanga maisha
Ambayo huenda nikaishi kwa raha,
Bali nitajitahidi kuishi leo
Ili kumpendeza Mungu wangu peke yake.

Wala sitathubutu kufikiria kwa miaka mingi
Au kupiga hatua kubwa;
Mungu akiwa ametengwa, na nafsi yangu ikiwa imefungiwa ndani,
Nikiwa nimezingirwa na malengo ya ubinafsi.

Wapo wanaopanga maisha yao,
Wasiofikiria sana kuhusu Mungu;
Wanaojipima, si kwa kweli ya Mungu,
Ingawa ndivyo wanavyopaswa kufanya kila siku!

“Usijisifu,” naonywa,
“Kwa yale yatakayoletwa na kesho;
Afya na mali yako—hata uhai wenyewe—
Vyote vinaweza kutoweka ghafla!”

“Usiku huu, nafsi yako
Inaweza kudaiwa kutoka kwako:
Je, unapanga mwaka mpya mzima
Huko, chini ya mti fulani wa Krismasi?”

“Amka! Jichunguze, je, umejiandaa?
Je, umejifunza masomo yako vizuri?
Ikiwa Mungu, baada ya saa tatu tu, SIKU HII,
Angehitimisha mwendo wako USIKU HUU?”
