Ainda que eu falasse as línguas dos homens e dos anjos, e não tivesse amor, seria como o metal que soa ou como o címbalo que retine. E ainda que tivesse o dom de profecia, e conhecesse todos os mistérios e toda a ciência, e ainda que tivesse toda a fé, de maneira tal que pudesse transportar montes, e não tivesse amor, nada seria. E ainda que distribuísse todos os meus bens para alimentar os pobres, e ainda que entregasse o meu corpo para ser queimado, e não tivesse amor, nada disso me aproveitaria. O amor é paciente e bondoso; o amor não inveja; o amor não se vangloria, não se ensoberbece, não se porta com indecência, não busca os seus próprios interesses, não se irrita facilmente, não suspeita mal; não se alegra com a injustiça, mas alegra-se com a verdade; tudo suporta, tudo crê, tudo espera, tudo persevera. O amor nunca falha; mas, havendo profecias, serão aniquiladas; havendo línguas, cessarão; havendo ciência, desaparecerá. Porque conhecemos em parte e profetizamos em parte. Mas, quando vier o que é perfeito, então o que é em parte será aniquilado. Quando eu era criança, falava como criança, entendia como criança, pensava como criança; mas, quando me tornei homem, deixei as coisas de criança. Porque agora vemos por espelho, obscuramente; mas então veremos face a face; agora conheço em parte, mas então conhecerei como também sou conhecido. Agora, pois, permanecem a fé, a esperança e o amor, estes três; mas o maior destes é o amor – 1 Coríntios 13:1-13.

Há vários anos, meu sobrinho passou muitos meses ocupado construindo uma casa para si e para sua futura esposa. Gostaria de comparar isso à construção de um casamento. Como sabem, ao construir uma casa, é preciso ter uma planta a seguir. O mesmo acontece quando construímos um casamento; precisamos seguir a planta da Palavra de Deus. Todos sabemos que o primeiro passo para construir uma casa é assentar um bom alicerce. O mesmo vale para o casamento. A todos vocês que são casados, confio que tenham construído e continuem construindo seu casamento sobre o alicerce de Jesus Cristo. Há muitos elementos de uma casa sólida que poderíamos comparar a um casamento sólido, mas hoje quero pensar no que dá força à sua casa ou ao casamento — essa coisa chama-se amor.

Quero considerar nove elementos do amor:

1. Paciência

O amor é paciente. O amor está pronto para realizar a obra do amor sempre que surge a necessidade. Nunca tem pressa; em vez disso, reveste-se dos ornamentos de um espírito manso e tranquilo. Esperará pela oportunidade perfeita e, da melhor maneira, instruirá discretamente ou exemplificará os propósitos de Deus diante da sua família, da sua igreja e do seu cônjuge. Às vezes, você terá de fazer isso por muito tempo… sozinho. Não vacilará nos momentos difíceis. Uma pessoa paciente é uma pessoa previsível. O amor persiste pacientemente; não permanece no que é temporal, mas no reino do eterno. O amor compreende isso; portanto, espera. Pode levar muito tempo para que uma pessoa se renda ao senhorio de Cristo. Esse tempo parecerá mais curto quando um homem de fé, com paciência, der o exemplo de uma vida de obediência e sacrifício. A paciência é uma atitude normal do amor.

2. Bondade

A bondade é o amor em ação! A maior coisa que um homem pode fazer por seu Pai Celestial é ser bondoso com os outros filhos de seu Pai. Isso não é difícil, e o mundo precisa disso. A todo homem casado que está lendo este artigo, peço que considere o seguinte: se você quiser conduzir sua esposa pela jornada do amor, não poderá fazê-lo com sucesso se tentar fazê-lo sem o elemento da bondade. A bondade torna atraente para quem observa viver os propósitos de Deus! Ela ajudará muito sua esposa a aproximar-se de Deus, porque ela vê os efeitos profundos dessa proximidade na vida do marido. Como Deus foi bondoso com você ao trazer-lhe a salvação? Comprar ferramentas de marcenaria e equipamentos automotivos para o aniversário de sua esposa não promoverá um casamento saudável. Como marido dela, você deve buscar enriquecer a vida dela, não a sua. A bondade é uma atitude normal do amor.

3. Generosidade

O amor não inveja! O oposto da inveja é a “generosidade”. O oposto da generosidade é a ganância, a amargura, a cobiça e a malícia. Maridos, talvez vocês se identifiquem comigo quando digo que, em todo trabalho, haverá outras pessoas fazendo o mesmo esforço que vocês e provavelmente fazendo-o melhor. O que complica as coisas é quando essa pessoa melhor é sua esposa. Nesse caso, a tentação é desenvolver um espírito de má vontade e cobiça. Quantas vezes fazemos pequenas coisas para atrapalhar o trabalho, por um espírito de inveja, sem outro motivo senão destruir as boas obras dela para que não brilhe mais do que nós?

Há apenas um traço de caráter que um cristão deveria invejar: possuir uma alma rica e generosa que não inveja. Quantas pessoas ficaram desanimadas de seguir a Cristo por inteiro porque lhes neguei as ferramentas necessárias para alcançar o sucesso, por inveja ciumenta? Nossa família tem uma marcenaria de armários. Carregar armários deixa as pessoas numa posição vulnerável. Se a inveja dominar, coisas sutis, como carregar um armário de maneira desajeitada, podem atrapalhar o trabalho. Prender os dedos de alguém numa porta estreita é uma maneira perfeita de rebaixar meu adversário ao meu nível; assim, o trabalho é prejudicado, e ainda posso manter minha inocência. Quantos casamentos e igrejas funcionam com esse tipo de pecado, semana após semana? Maridos, não fiquem zangados com sua esposa quando ela acabar sendo mais inteligente do que vocês em determinado assunto. Nisso, ela não cometeu erro nem falta. Meus amigos, que recursos Deus lhes negou que os impedem de ser vitoriosos nesse grande plano de redenção? Ele não tem sido generoso? A generosidade é uma atitude normal do amor.

4. Humildade

O amor não se vangloria, não se ensoberbece. Depois de terem sido pacientes, bondosos e generosos, e de o amor ter realizado sua bela obra no mundo, voltem às sombras e não digam nada a respeito. A natureza humana tende a exaltar a si mesma, o que só consegue interromper o amor, pois a autoexaltação é tão contrária à natureza divina do amor. A Escritura nos ordena: “Que outro te louve, e não a tua própria boca; um estranho, e não os teus lábios.” – Provérbios 27:2. Quantas vezes estraguei uma oportunidade de levar adiante a obra de Deus na vida de outra pessoa porque me coloquei entre o amor de Deus e o coração dela, e ela se ofendeu?

A soberba precede a destruição, e a altivez do espírito precede a queda – Provérbios 16:18.

A soberba do homem o abaterá, mas a honra sustentará o humilde de espírito – Provérbios 29:23.

O orgulho destruirá a obra de Deus e destruirá qualquer esforço de amar meu irmão ou minha irmã. A humildade é uma atitude normal do amor e auxilia grandemente o amor em seus propósitos eternos.

5. Cortesia

O amor não se porta com indecência. Isso diz respeito ao amor em relação às boas maneiras. A NVI diz melhor: “O amor não é rude!” A cortesia é o amor nas pequenas coisas. Quero que todos pensemos numa palavra específica: “cavalheiro”. A palavra “cavalheiro” é composta e, literalmente, significa “homem gentil”. Por definição, simplesmente descreve um homem que age com gentileza. Um homem que não possui essa qualidade não pode deixar de ser indelicado, insensível e rude. Não consegue evitar.

Irmãos casados... Vocês não conduzirão seu cônjuge a experimentar o amor de Deus se seu coração estiver desprovido de cortesia para com sua esposa. A cortesia é a graça que demonstra ternura e respeito especiais por outro ser humano. Conheço um casamento triste que começou mal. A arrogante declaração do noivo foi que seus sogros poderiam muito bem conhecê-lo mais cedo ou mais tarde. Desde o início, ele se expressava rudemente à mesa do jantar. Não é de admirar que, depois da lua de mel, sua esposa tenha descoberto que ele era um homem com quem não queria viver, e com bons motivos. O casamento não continuou “feliz para sempre” porque faltava completamente a cortesia. A cortesia é uma atitude normal do amor.

6. Abnegação

O amor não busca os seus próprios interesses. Ou poderíamos dizer assim: o amor não tentará tomar aquilo que me pertence, nem mesmo por direito. Chegará um dia em que um homem ou uma mulher, em nome do amor bíblico, terá de atender a um chamado mais elevado e renunciar aos próprios direitos pessoais para promover o reino de Deus. O amor nos atinge profundamente na área da abnegação. É muito difícil, depois de termos adquirido nossos direitos, conquistado-os, sonhado com eles, desejado-os e sacrificado por eles, precisarmos abrir mão deles. E, ainda assim, o amor renunciará a tudo para que os propósitos de Deus tenham preeminência. Somente pelos grandes e nobres propósitos do amor divino podemos justificar o desperdício de abrir mão daquilo que naturalmente consideramos que nos pertence por direito. Nenhum sacrifício é difícil demais para o amor fazer. O amor verdadeiro desfrutará daquilo que lhe for dado, mas sua própria natureza não pode tomar aquilo que não lhe é oferecido voluntariamente. O amor é o caminho para a vida e a liberdade. Não há felicidade em receber, mas somente em dar. Muitos casamentos existem com a ideia de que a felicidade está em possuir ou receber, mas esse não é o caminho de Deus. Haveria poucos divórcios se o marido se esforçasse tanto para conservar a esposa quanto se esforçou para conquistá-la no início. A abnegação é uma atitude normal do amor.

7. Bom temperamento

O amor não se irrita facilmente. Há muitas pessoas decentes, trabalhadoras e moralmente corretas neste mundo que têm uma falha fatal: são irritadiças e mal-humoradas — têm pavio curto. Poucas coisas tornam um bom homem mais anticristão do que um temperamento maligno. Essa falha pecaminosa de caráter devasta o lar, esgota a vitalidade dos homens e mulheres com quem ele convive e corrompe a beleza e a inocência de seus filhos. Esse poder de produzir sofrimento não tem igual. É composto de ciúme, ira, orgulho, crueldade, justiça própria, irritabilidade, teimosia, mau humor... Tudo isso compõe o caráter de uma alma sem amor. Alguém disse certa vez: Não há lugar no céu para um homem assim; pois, para entrar no céu, um homem precisa levar a si mesmo consigo. Meus amigos, o lar é como o inferno na terra quando uma pessoa desse tipo está no comando. Um rabugento é um homem que se avalia e fica ressentido com o resultado.

O temperamento é importante. Um homem não é maior do que aquilo que o deixa zangado. A questão não é tanto o que é um temperamento, mas o que ele revela sobre o que há dentro de uma pessoa. Revela falta de generosidade, cortesia e abnegação. A falta de paciência e de bondade é simbolizada instantaneamente num único acesso de ira. Não basta lidar com o sintoma superficial do temperamento. Precisamos ir à origem e permitir que o Senhor Jesus Cristo nos transforme nas profundezas mais profundas da nossa natureza, e a ira em nossa alma morrerá por si mesma. Quantas crianças não querem saber do cristianismo por causa do temperamento maligno no coração de um pai ou de uma mãe?! Na verdade, não temos tempo a perder. Com persistência paciente, uma esposa, um marido ou um pastor deve amar esse déspota moral. Pois ele também precisa ser conquistado pelo amor redentor de Jesus Cristo. Esse é o propósito do amor. Ser temperado pelo poder de Deus é uma atitude normal do amor.

8. Qualidade ou capacidade de “não suspeitar mal”

As pessoas que me inspiram são aquelas que acreditam em mim e me incentivam. Também é verdade que, num ambiente de suspeita e desconfiança, as pessoas definham e morrem. Na ausência de confiança e boa vontade, o amor não pode existir, muito menos prosperar. Nada enferruja tanto um casamento quanto a desconfiança. É algo delicioso e maravilhoso encontrar pessoas neste mundo sem amor que presumem o melhor a respeito de outra pessoa até que se prove o contrário. Quantas vezes descobri na vida que estava errado quanto às motivações de outra pessoa! A maneira mais rápida de destruir o amor no casamento é presumir algo negativo sobre as motivações de seu cônjuge, quando somente o Senhor conhece o coração. O amor divino quer que aquele em quem se concentra tenha sucesso, e não que caia de cara no chão e fracasse.

Será possível que, se conseguíssemos elevar os outros a novas alturas, descobriríamos que nosso próprio sucesso é ampliado pela visão ou crença do que aquela pessoa poderia se tornar? Será possível que o respeito, à moda antiga, por quem é objeto do nosso amor seja o primeiro passo para restaurar o autorrespeito que um homem perdeu? Se tratarmos nossos cônjuges de maneira desonrosa e desrespeitosa, há uma boa chance de que se tornem ou continuem sendo a pessoa que detestamos. Alguém disse certa vez: “Irmãs, uma esposa feliz às vezes tem o melhor marido, mas, com mais frequência, ela tira o melhor partido do marido que tem.” Vejam, o homem foi feito à imagem de Deus, e a maior coisa que vocês podem fazer por alguém é usar o poder do amor para ajudar a restaurar aquilo que se perdeu. O Filho do Homem veio buscar e salvar o que se havia perdido. Não suspeitar mal é uma atitude normal do amor.

9. Sinceridade

Irmãos e irmãs, entendemos tudo tão ao contrário. Um homem que conhece o amor de Cristo escolhe o caminho mais elevado para corrigir os erros. Seu maior deleite é ver os propósitos de Deus postos em prática na vida de outra pessoa, e não o contrário. Quantas vezes nos deleitamos ao ver nosso inimigo cair. A crítica destrutiva e a atenção excessiva às falhas ou aos pecados dos outros enfraquecem a capacidade deles de vencer. Exagerar e tirar proveito das falhas alheias impede que nossos casamentos e igrejas sejam cheios de pessoas vitoriosas. Casais, aquilo que vocês acreditam a respeito de seu cônjuge provavelmente é o que ele ou ela se tornará.

Aqueles que realmente amam os outros enchem-se de alegria e júbilo quando examinam uma situação e descobrem que as coisas eram melhores do que temiam.

Amor e confiança caminham juntos. Como minha alma está segura nas mãos de um Deus imutável, posso estender a mão com sinceridade àqueles que entraram na esfera da influência. Alegrar-se com a justiça e NÃO SUSPEITAR MAL é uma atitude normal e final do amor.

A grandeza do amor (a maior coisa do mundo)

a.) Tudo suporta

Irmãos, vocês podem suportar tudo por amor redentor e seus propósitos eternos? Quando forem tentados a deixar de amar, lembrem-se do que Jesus suportou por vocês. A capacidade de suportar tudo é uma atitude normal do amor. Vocês conseguem receber um insulto sem retribuí-lo? Até o diabo tem sabedoria para perseverar pacientemente, se isso lhe der uma vantagem maior no futuro.

b.) Tudo espera

E a esperança não nos deixa envergonhados, porque o amor de Deus está derramado em nosso coração pelo Espírito Santo que nos foi dado – Romanos 5:5.

Irmãs, se seu marido ficar aquém da glória com que vocês se casaram com ele, conseguem esperar pacientemente que o Senhor opere na vida dele? Quando seu marido a surpreender sendo diferente da pessoa com quem você pensava estar se casando, procure vê-lo pelo que ele poderia ser, em vez de pelo que não é, e então encoraje-o com esperança, em vez de desanimá-lo com desesperança.

c.) Tudo persevera.

Por isso, tudo suporto por causa dos eleitos, para que também eles obtenham a salvação que está em Cristo Jesus, com glória eterna – 2 Timóteo 2:10.

Deem graças ao SENHOR, porque ele é bom; porque a sua misericórdia dura para sempre – 1 Crônicas 16:34.

Irmãos e irmãs, quanto tempo dura a sua perseverança? Quando se cansarem de perseverar, lembrem-se de quanto tempo Deus persevera com vocês. A maioria dos problemas conjugais surge quando duas pessoas decidem não perseverar porque estão apaixonadas por si mesmas, e não por seu cônjuge.

d.) Nunca falha, porque Deus é a sua fonte.

As profecias falham.

As línguas falham.

A ciência desaparece.

O verdadeiro amor bíblico nunca desiste. Nunca falha; portanto, jamais pode ser derrotado.

O amor não pode ser alcançado pela eloquência das palavras. Não pode ser conquistado pela força de vontade. Não pode ser aprendido pela educação, nem comprado por meio de sacrifício humano. Não está à venda, nem pode ser trocado como uma mercadoria, pois é de natureza espiritual. O amor só pode ser recebido do Grande Doador Eterno, por aqueles que são dignos de possuir tal poder e glória em seu coração.

A sinceridade da minha busca pessoal por perseguir e compreender, de coração, o amor de Cristo determinará a quantidade e a qualidade do amor pelos outros. Foi o sincero clamor de Paulo aos filipenses: “... para que eu o conheça”.

Maridos e esposas, quando se conheceram, seu amor era muito imaturo. Vocês o viam como por um espelho, obscuramente, ou como um reflexo imperfeito no espelho. Falavam sobre o futuro do amor como crianças imaturas que não tinham experiência com ele. Começaram sabendo a seu respeito e profetizaram sobre ele. Agora que estão casados, sabem muito mais sobre o AMOR do que sabiam, mas ainda há muito mais a aprender. Meus amigos, que o espelho se torne mais claro para vocês com a maturidade e que compreendam o amor em sua perfeição nos dias que virão. Mas a vereda dos justos é como a luz da aurora, que brilha cada vez mais até ser dia perfeito – Provérbios 4:18.

Maridos e esposas, a melhor coisa que podem fazer um pelo outro é cultivar diariamente um relacionamento com o Senhor Jesus Cristo. Lembrem-se de que todo sucesso na vida exige prática. Pratiquem amar um ao outro. Sejam pacientes, bondosos, generosos, humildes e abnegados. Com toda sinceridade, incentivem um ao outro a entregar o coração ao senhorio de Jesus Cristo, e seu casamento será muito além de tudo o que vocês já imaginaram. Um jovem orou certa vez... “Senhor, envia-me uma esposa que te ame, pois sei que, se ela te amar, também me amará.” Ele era um homem sábio.

O grande amor tem um grande custo. Custou a vida do Senhor Jesus Cristo. Só depois de entregarem o coração ao Senhor em plena confiança vocês poderão entregar o coração um ao outro. Vocês já ganharam tudo; portanto, não têm nada a perder ao dar tudo de si num relacionamento terreno. Esse é o custo do amor, e vale a pena. O amor é vida, e a vida é amor. É melhor não viver do que não amar. Se houver amor em seu lar, vocês encontrarão um propósito vigoroso para viver, e tudo estará bem. Ponham sua esperança e fé no Deus de Amor e encontrarão... a maior coisa do mundo.

Amados, amemo-nos uns aos outros, porque o amor é de Deus; e todo aquele que ama é nascido de Deus e conhece a Deus – 1 João 4:7.

Porque todo aquele que é nascido de Deus vence o mundo; e esta é a vitória que vence o mundo: a nossa fé – 1 João 5:4.

Que Deus abençoe cada noiva e cada noivo.

Greetings of Christian love to each one. Another year has passed us by, and another is spread out before us to navigate. What is our perspective? Do we have hope and joy bubbling up in our hearts or does the future seem full of gloom and doom? Do we see God’s sovereign hand at work in the situations and circumstances around us or does the world seem out of control from our vantage point?

As I interact with folks from around the country there seems to be a common issue that many folks are struggling with—weariness. Weary of mandates. Weary of shutdowns. Weary of all the bickering and fighting that has surrounded the Covid issue. Weary of…

It appears that many people just “Don’t want to think about it”. Why? I’m really not sure what all the reasons are, but I am sure that each person has one. Let’s remember that God wants us to …be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves –Matthew 10:16.

Here, in the United States of America, Christians have had over 60 years (since World War 2) of relative peace and tranquility. For the most part, we have been left alone to raise our families and worship the God of our fathers according to our conscience. We have enjoyed the separation of Church and State that was implemented at the beginning of our country’s existence. We have been able to work with our hands and earn a living. Many of us have lived off the fat of the land.

Maybe we were living in an artificial bubble. Maybe we have been lulled into a false sense of security. What about our counterparts in countries around the world, what is their reality of living as true Christians in their world? Sure, we have been able to use our wealth and freedom of movement to do much good for the rest of the world who have endured much hardship due to following Christ. But at what cost? What have our children learned?

Sometimes, we hear about first generation Christians being “on fire” for their Lord. Sometimes so much so that second and third generation Christians think that first generation Christians are perhaps a little too zealous in their efforts of evangelizing those around them.

What about the next generation? They are learning from someone—about God, themselves, and life. What are they learning? And who are they learning from? We must take stock to ensure that our children are learning life’s lessons in a way that they will be prepared to face the reality of things to come.

And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world? And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many –Matthew 24:3-5.

Remember that this is Jesus Himself speaking to His followers regarding the end of the world. His very first concern is that we would NOT be deceived. He says that deception will be the major issue surrounding the end of time. He says that many will come claiming to be Christ [or His direct spokesperson] in an attempt to gain a listening ear, all in an effort to deceive the hearer and gain a following.

If not before now, we most certainly must be teaching our children certain specific things through word and action. That we are to be strangers and pilgrims as we journey through this life. That if we are friends of this world then God will be our enemy. And that Jesus’ Kingdom is not of this world, therefore, His children must learn to live as ambassadors in a foreign land. Our children need to know that ALL who live godly in Christ Jesus WILL suffer persecution.

Many of the doctrines that have been taught in our churches and para-church functions have severely crippled the next generation of the church. We have been taught that we can have the “power of His resurrection” without needing to be a partaker of the “fellowship of His sufferings”. A suffering Christ with suffering followers has been thrown out in favor of following a Jesus who will not let anything bad happen to you. While there is much emphasis on a Jesus who suffered and died for you, there is very little to NO teaching on the need to “take up your cross daily” and follow Him.

Mental Health and Emotional Stability

Some years ago, I came across the story of a soldier, who, after serving a term of service in Iraq, was struggling to cope with PTSD. Sure, I believe that PTSD is real, and the struggles are real, but as I read this man’s story, I found myself becoming increasingly frustrated with the lack of answers that were being provided to a severely struggling young man. Some of his deepest struggles stemmed from the flashback memories he had of when he had personally killed several of the enemy. No matter how many counseling sessions he went to he just couldn’t come to a place of inner peace and rest. His mind was troubled. He had difficulty sleeping. He had problems getting along with others.

I had to think “If only someone could come alongside this young man and share the Gospel of Jesus Christ with him. If only he could be shown the Truth of God’s Word that to take another human’s life is sin in God’s eyes (even if he is the enemy) and God will not allow him to have peace in his heart until that is taken care of. Also, that the real excitement is that IF he would come to God according to the terms of the Bible and repent of his sin, then he could start walking with God and God could start giving him peace for his troubled soul.”

Over the last number of years, there have been numerous mass shootings here in the United States. Each time the public officials hold news conferences and share their thoughts in an effort to try to make sense out of another seemingly unexplainable tragic event. Usually, it’s not long until someone is talking about mental health and the need to step up public efforts to provide safety nets, screenings, and better and more treatments to curb this senseless violence.

Several weeks ago, there was a terrible, tragic event that took place in another state from where I live. In one of the big cities, a man pushed a woman off of the platform and into the path of an oncoming subway train. She didn’t survive. In the aftermath of such a horrific happening, the public officials made statements to the public in an effort to stem the potential public fear. They concluded that the man must have been emotionally troubled and that they would be stepping up their efforts in trying to provide a safety net for those with mental health issues, so that such things wouldn’t happen again.

Sure, when we look at the issue through the eyes of the world it seems to make sense. But is this the whole of the matter? Have we as Christians become so used to the ways of the world that we forget how far they have strayed from the Truth of God’s Word?

Let’s not point our finger at the world and the elected public officials. Are we, as the church, any better? How well do we know our Bible? How well do we know our Savior? When someone comes to us seeking peace and rest within do we know how to take them to the Scriptures, and lead them to Jesus who can then show them the way to the Father?

Why am I saying all this? If we continue to provide the next generation of the church with artificial answers and temporary solutions to the problems of life, then they will NOT be prepared to …endure unto the end… –Matthew 24:13.

And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24.

Salutations dans l’amour chrétien à chacun de vous. Une autre année est passée, et une autre s’étend devant nous, à traverser. Quel est notre regard ? L’espérance et la joie bouillonnent-elles dans nos cœurs, ou l’avenir semble-t-il plein de tristesse et de malheur ? Voyons-nous la main souveraine de Dieu à l’œuvre dans les situations et les circonstances qui nous entourent, ou le monde semble-t-il échapper à tout contrôle de notre point de vue ?

Quand j’échange avec des gens de tout le pays, un problème commun semble toucher beaucoup d’entre eux : la lassitude. Lassés des directives. Lassés des fermetures. Lassés de toutes les querelles et disputes qui ont entouré la question du Covid. Lassés de…

Il semble que beaucoup de gens ne veuillent tout simplement « pas y penser ». Pourquoi ? Je ne suis vraiment pas sûr de toutes les raisons, mais je suis sûr que chacun en a une. Souvenons-nous que Dieu veut que nous …soyons donc prudents comme les serpents, et simples comme les colombes –Matthieu 10:16.

Ici, aux États-Unis d’Amérique, les chrétiens ont connu plus de 60 ans (depuis la Seconde Guerre mondiale) de paix et de tranquillité relatives. Pour l’essentiel, on nous a laissés élever nos familles et adorer le Dieu de nos pères selon notre conscience. Nous avons bénéficié de la séparation de l’Église et de l’État, instaurée au début de l’existence de notre pays. Nous avons pu travailler de nos mains et gagner notre vie. Beaucoup d’entre nous ont vécu dans l’abondance.

Peut-être vivions-nous dans une bulle artificielle. Peut-être nous sommes-nous laissé bercer dans un faux sentiment de sécurité. Qu’en est-il de nos homologues dans les pays du monde entier ? Quelle est leur réalité, celle de vivre en vrais chrétiens dans leur monde ? Certes, nous avons pu mettre à profit notre richesse et notre liberté de mouvement pour faire beaucoup de bien au reste du monde, dont les habitants ont enduré de grandes épreuves à cause de leur fidélité au Christ. Mais à quel prix ? Qu’ont appris nos enfants ?

Parfois, nous entendons parler de chrétiens de première génération qui sont « en feu » pour leur Seigneur. Parfois, au point que des chrétiens de deuxième et de troisième génération pensent que ceux de la première génération sont peut-être un peu trop zélés dans leurs efforts pour évangéliser leur entourage.

Qu’en est-il de la prochaine génération ? Elle apprend de quelqu’un — au sujet de Dieu, d’elle-même et de la vie. Qu’apprend-elle ? Et de qui l’apprend-elle ? Nous devons faire le point afin de nous assurer que nos enfants apprennent les leçons de la vie d’une manière qui les préparera à affronter la réalité des choses à venir.

Comme Jésus était assis sur le mont des Oliviers, les disciples vinrent à lui en particulier et dirent : Dis-nous, quand cela arrivera-t-il, et quel sera le signe de ton avènement et de la fin du monde ? Jésus leur répondit : Prenez garde que personne ne vous séduise. Car plusieurs viendront en mon nom, disant : C’est moi qui suis le Christ, et ils séduiront beaucoup de gens –Matthieu 24:3-5.

Souvenons-nous que c’est Jésus lui-même qui parle ainsi à ses disciples de la fin du monde. Sa toute première préoccupation est que nous ne soyons PAS séduits. Il dit que la séduction sera le problème majeur à l’approche de la fin des temps. Il dit que beaucoup viendront en prétendant être le Christ [ou son porte-parole direct], pour attirer l’attention et inciter les gens à les écouter, dans le but de séduire leurs auditeurs et de se constituer un groupe de fidèles.

Si nous ne le faisons pas déjà, nous devons absolument enseigner à nos enfants certaines choses précises, par nos paroles et par nos actes : que nous devons être étrangers et pèlerins tout au long de notre parcours dans cette vie ; que si nous sommes amis de ce monde, Dieu sera notre ennemi ; et que le Royaume de Jésus n’est pas de ce monde, si bien que ses enfants doivent apprendre à vivre comme des ambassadeurs dans un pays étranger. Nos enfants doivent savoir que TOUS ceux qui vivent pieusement en Jésus-Christ seront persécutés.

Beaucoup de doctrines enseignées dans nos églises et dans les activités paraecclésiastiques ont gravement handicapé la prochaine génération de l’Église. On nous a enseigné que nous pouvons connaître la « puissance de sa résurrection » sans avoir à prendre part à la « communion de ses souffrances ». On a rejeté le Christ souffrant et ses disciples souffrants au profit d’un Jésus qui ne laissera rien de mauvais nous arriver. Alors que l’on insiste beaucoup sur Jésus qui a souffert et qui est mort pour nous, on enseigne très peu, voire PAS DU TOUT, la nécessité de « prendre chaque jour sa croix » et de le suivre.

Santé mentale et stabilité émotionnelle

Il y a quelques années, j’ai découvert l’histoire d’un soldat qui, après avoir effectué une période de service en Irak, éprouvait des difficultés à faire face à un syndrome de stress post-traumatique. Certes, je crois que le SSPT est réel et que les difficultés sont réelles, mais, en lisant le récit de cet homme, je me suis senti de plus en plus frustré par le manque de réponses apportées à un jeune homme en grande détresse. Certaines de ses plus grandes souffrances venaient des souvenirs qui lui revenaient de ces moments où il avait lui-même tué plusieurs ennemis. Peu importe le nombre de séances de conseil auxquelles il assistait, il ne parvenait pas à trouver la paix intérieure et le repos. Son esprit était troublé. Il avait du mal à dormir. Il avait du mal à s’entendre avec les autres.

Je me suis dit : « Si seulement quelqu’un pouvait accompagner ce jeune homme et partager avec lui l’Évangile de Jésus-Christ. Si seulement on pouvait lui montrer la vérité de la Parole de Dieu : ôter la vie à un autre être humain est un péché aux yeux de Dieu (même s’il s’agit de l’ennemi), et Dieu ne lui permettra pas d’avoir la paix dans son cœur tant que cette question ne sera pas réglée. Et ce qui est vraiment réjouissant, c’est que S’IL venait à Dieu selon les conditions de la Bible et se repentait de son péché, il pourrait alors commencer à marcher avec Dieu, et Dieu pourrait commencer à donner la paix à son âme troublée. »

Ces dernières années, il y a eu de nombreuses fusillades meurtrières de masse ici, aux États-Unis. À chaque fois, les responsables publics tiennent des conférences de presse et expriment leurs réflexions pour tenter de comprendre un autre événement tragique qui semble inexplicable. En général, il ne faut pas longtemps avant que quelqu’un parle de santé mentale et de la nécessité d’intensifier les efforts publics afin de mettre en place des dispositifs de protection, des dépistages et de meilleurs traitements, et d’en offrir davantage, pour endiguer cette violence insensée.

Il y a plusieurs semaines, un événement terrible et tragique s’est produit dans un autre État que le mien. Dans l’une des grandes villes, un homme a poussé une femme du quai, sur la voie d’un métro qui arrivait. Elle n’a pas survécu. À la suite de cet événement horrible, les responsables publics se sont adressés à la population pour tenter d’apaiser les craintes que cela pouvait susciter. Ils ont conclu que l’homme devait avoir des troubles émotionnels et qu’ils allaient intensifier leurs efforts pour fournir un dispositif de protection aux personnes ayant des problèmes de santé mentale, afin que de tels événements ne se reproduisent pas.

Certes, quand nous considérons la question à travers les yeux du monde, cela semble logique. Mais est-ce là toute la question ? En tant que chrétiens, nous sommes-nous tellement habitués aux façons de faire du monde que nous oublions à quel point il s’est éloigné de la vérité de la Parole de Dieu ?

Ne montrons pas du doigt le monde et les responsables publics élus. En tant qu’Église, sommes-nous meilleurs ? Dans quelle mesure connaissons-nous notre Bible ? Dans quelle mesure connaissons-nous notre Sauveur ? Quand quelqu’un vient à nous en quête de paix et de repos intérieur, savons-nous le conduire aux Écritures et le mener à Jésus, qui pourra alors lui montrer le chemin vers le Père ?

Pourquoi est-ce que je dis tout cela ? Si nous continuons à proposer à la prochaine génération de l’Église des réponses artificielles et des solutions temporaires aux problèmes de la vie, alors elle ne sera PAS prête à …persévérer jusqu’à la fin… –Matthieu 24:13.

Il dit à tous : Si quelqu’un veut venir après moi, qu’il renonce à lui-même, qu’il se charge chaque jour de sa croix et qu’il me suive. Car celui qui voudra sauver sa vie la perdra, mais celui qui perdra sa vie à cause de moi la sauvera –Luc 9:23-24.

Thou hast the dew of thy youth. Psalm 110:3

There are many aspects of youth which are not virtuous. Many youth of our day experience an early season of callused carelessness and casualty. Often decisions that are made in youthful years set the foundation for the rest of their lives. It was a the younger prodigal brother that asked for an early draw on his inheritance then went and wasted it on riotous living. It was a young Dinah who wandered from her father’s house and …went out to see the daughters of the land –Genesis 34:1. There, she was exposed to the heathen young men of the land and occasioned a bloody massacre, leaving Jacob as a stench in the land. Many foolish young people have sown to the wind and reaped the havoc thereof. Those that are void of solid principles and parental authority are at high risk for spiritual shipwreck.

There are particular lusts that inflict youth more so than the aged, and the young are exhorted to flee them. (–see 2 Timothy 2:22) Solomon looked through his window casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding -Proverbs 7:6-7. The young man was in heartfelt pursuit of that which appeared lovely… [Un]Till a dart [struck] through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life –Proverbs 7:23. We could examine the vices from the youthful lives of Rehoboam, Amnon, Nadab and Abihu, and countless others. We also find no lack of modern, folly-filled examples about us fulfilled by frivolous youth.

But youth are not meant to be despised. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. In fact, God generally chooses the youth as the instruments of His propagation. Joseph, of sterling character, was sent by God into Egypt at the age of 17 to preserve life (–see Genesis 45:5). Miriam, at the age of twelve, stood post over the future deliverer of the entire Jewish nation and secured her own mother, Jochebed, to be the nurse of the baby Moses. David, as a youth, was sent to encourage his brethren in the army. He was despised by his brothers: …I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart… –1 Samuel 17:28. He was rejected by Saul: …Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth… –1 Samuel 17:33. He was scorned by Goliath: …Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves… –1 Samuel 17:43. But their contempt was all for naught when he was chosen by God to be king over all Israel.

These noble youthful ambitions were followed by Josiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Mary, and the disciples of the Lord, all who chose to remember their Creator in the days of their youth. But these were not naive specimens seeking to secure their place in life, they were graphic examples of youth who were seeking to imitate the image of their Lord.

We need not gaze long into the character of Christ before we find…

...Thou hast the dew of thy youth

Psalm 110 is perhaps the most referred-to scripture in the Old Testament. This rhetorical portrait of the Messiah reveals a vivid virtue for us to behold. Christ, as the Ancient of days, was described in the Revelation having His head and His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet, here He is depicted as eternally young, as He sits at the right hand of God (–see Psalm 110:1). No weariness of age can enter there, for Christ is the Morning Star. It is perpetual morning around the throne of God. Those saints who are following hard after His likeness will also reflect this virtue, for the light of Jesus is the light of youth.

The psalmist, describing the Messiah, draws from the natural beauty of the morning dew (–see Psalm 110:3). The thought of dew calls us back from the heavens and unveils before us a portrait of this earth on which we dwell. In heaven there is no night, no change of heat and cold, no need of the sun to light up the day and consequently… no dew. The nature of dew belongs to the terrestrial, where everyone who will but stoop to observe it will behold a uniformed regiment of grass sparkling as if embedded with a myriad of diamonds. After a long night of darkness, the dewdrops, like tears, stand in the eyes of the flowers as they weep for joy at the advent of the first morning sunbeam. Those who walk through the lowly vegetation will have their feet washed by a thousand caressing hands of God’s design. Christ is not depicted as the dew of the morning but as the dew of youth, and the imagery is stretched further.

Youth is the season of abounding energy. Some cannot sit still. They are generally interpersonal creatures who love social activity. This is neither a virtue nor a vice. Rather, it is nominal nature. There is a progressive strain in advancing years that tames and tempers the soul. As life progresses, there is a clearer vision and a steadier thought, and we rise to better things. But when the mid-life summit has been crossed and the feet are traveling downward on the slope, that tumultuous rush of bodily energy that plowed through anything becomes enshrined with memories of the past. It is the closest comfort many can find to the bygone days of their strength.

But Christ has not called us to foster a fondness for the past nor a wistful longing for the “DO” of our youth. So many today sadly lament that their ‘get-up-and-go’ has got up and went. These have no vision for higher things and are more energized by a can of Mountain Dew than the Dew of Youth. They are more inspired by a trip down memory lane and reminiscing events of the past than of the hope that lies before them.

Age is no hindrance to securing the dew of youth. The Ancient of Days still rides forth among the golden candlesticks. While John beheld His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet Solomon declares …his locks are bushy, and black as a raven –Song of Solomon 5:11. While age may steal our strength and hearing, …the LORD’S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: –Isaiah 59:1. He has secured the dew of youth and invites us to partake. The problem is not found in our deteriorating body but in a spiritually declining mind. The bane of old age predominately sets in when the mind follows the body.

It is not that life grows poorer as it advances or ceases to be noble when the charm of youth has faded. If we were placed here only to experience joy, the dying out of youthful romance would be terrible. God had a much greater end in view for His children than to just be vibrant ‘doers’. We are sent here to learn. Our allotted years upon earth are all meant to be a schooling, and it is not in the bright romance of youth that we learn the best and most abiding lessons. It is in the dogged doing of our duty, the quiet acceptance of our limitations, the patient carrying of our daily burden, and in the stretching out of a helping hand to our brother. These afford us the true opportunities for Christian culture and are the roots of ethical nobility. Christ labored …not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life… –John 6:27, and He finished His earthly task in 33 years. But the dew of youth did not dissipate as He sat down at the right hand of His Father.

Thus, we conclude that this youthfulness will not be secured by strength, but by…

...Hope

But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. –Hebrews 10:12-13.

How shall we picture this Christ now? Reclining in an easy chair, all worn out from His experience with the stubborn people of this earth? Is He busy putting together a scrap book of precious memories? This is too often the position of the aged and so their mind dies with their bodies.

And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope –Romans 5:3-4. At times, we wonder if this scripture can be true. Anyone with any age on their bones can testify to a poor experience and the subsequent feelings of hopelessness following. As people, we have all faced disappointing experiences with a spouse, a child, or a church relationship after which a nagging cloud of despair settles in. Outside of Christ, a sour experience always tends to pessimism. It was so in the world when Jesus came. It is still so today.

But the dew of youth is incurably hopeful. There is an effervescent expectation that is naturally and magnificently borne in youth and retained in Christ. In every winter, when the fields are bleak, and the cold gust goes whistling through the trees, there lies the hope that the flowers will spring again. In every spring there is the hope of summer. In every summer there is the hope of harvest. It is alive in nature and alive in youth. Those who are blind to it shall reap, at best, a dreary monotone existence. To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all. –Oscar Wilde.

The rest shall be brightly effected with a hope that…

…Heals Our Infirmities

Our bodies are destined for the grave and have no hope for renewal in this life. It is our minds that carry our greatest infirmities. The impotent man of 38 years at Bethesda could only utter a hopeless complaint when Christ asked him, …Wilt thou be made whole? –John 5:6. Upon the wake of his new day, a new remedy was given to him—… Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee –John 5:14. What could be worse than being a cripple for years? A mind that is beset by a doleful indulgence in the sorrows of this world. Age sets in when we have more memories of the past than hope for tomorrow. It is disappointing when folks grow old and have no vision for tomorrow, but it is a disaster to behold youth that are plagued by its crippling effects. Many grope aimlessly through life’s various trials, stupefied by the lack of blessedness. The noonday sun has evaporated the dew of their youth and the only praise that they can muster is culminated from a handful of yesterday’s pleasantries. A new attitude must be birthed by the dew of a new morning.

…Humbles Our Pursuits

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. –John 21:18. When we are young, we can overcome in the strength of our youth. As age takes its course, we will find a different alternative: victory through surrender.

…I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one. –1 John 2:14. The world entices us to selfish living. Youth are often subject to schools of learning that teach them to “be all that you can be”. There is a major focus on self-enhancement and preparation for the future. This may prepare them in a ‘survival of the fittest’ world but will leave them destitute when the strength and prowess of youth has departed.

For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever. –1 John 2:16-17. Overcoming evil with good is the Biblical antidote for channeling youthful energies. Whether it is the lust within or the longing without, hope is conceived by planting a seed of kindness in the life of another. The pursuit of pleasure and lieu of leisure will always disappoint its recipient and leave him in a valley of despair deeper than when he began. It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth … He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope. –Lamentations 3:27-29. We are created to work in God’s vineyard and those who have an appetite for it will reap in hope of its youthful reward.

…Hallows Our Trials

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope... –Romans 8:24. How often we can relate to Job in his pain. But before his pain had received an ounce of retribution, the healing streams began to flow as Job reverenced his Creator. When we can acknowledge that God is perfect in all the trials He allows, we then learn to worship in the temple not made with hands and disregard the frailties of the body. To sit down at the feet of Christ ignites a youthful spark that radiates the spirit within and conceives hope. The dew of youth then becomes our portion as Christ imparts eternal life and eternal youth to us. From the hour of the grave and through eternity we shall be young and bid defiance to weariness and death if we are living in the morning light of Jesus Christ. Heaven is a place of perpetual youth, and just like the light of the sun is reflected on the moon, so likewise the light of Christ is reflected on His bride. She is clean and young, …a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing… –Ephesians 5:27. Blessed is the venerable saint who arrives at the portals of heaven in such a condition.

Engkau memiliki embun kemudaan-Mu. Mazmur 110:3

Ada banyak aspek masa muda yang tidak bajik. Banyak orang muda zaman kita mengalami masa dini yang ditandai oleh ketidakpedulian dan kecerobohan yang keras. Sering kali keputusan yang dibuat pada masa muda meletakkan dasar bagi sisa hidup mereka. Adik yang bungsu, si anak yang hilang, yang meminta bagian warisannya lebih awal, lalu pergi menghambur-hamburkannya dalam hidup berfoya-foya. Dinah yang masih muda mengembara jauh dari rumah ayahnya dan …pergi melihat-lihat perempuan-perempuan di negeri itu –Kejadian 34:1. Di sana, ia terpapar kepada para pemuda kafir negeri itu dan menyebabkan pembantaian berdarah, sehingga Yakub menjadi bau busuk di negeri itu. Banyak orang muda yang bodoh menabur angin dan menuai kekacauan yang ditimbulkannya. Mereka yang tidak memiliki prinsip kokoh dan otoritas orang tua sangat berisiko mengalami kehancuran rohani.

Ada hawa nafsu tertentu yang lebih banyak menimpa kaum muda daripada orang lanjut usia, dan kaum muda dinasihati untuk menjauhinya. (–lihat 2 Timotius 2:22) Salomo melihat dari jendela kisi-kisinya, Dan tampaklah di antara orang-orang yang tak berpengalaman, di antara para pemuda, seorang muda yang tidak berakal budi –Amsal 7:6-7. Pemuda itu dengan sepenuh hati mengejar sesuatu yang tampak elok… [Sampai] sebuah anak panah menembus hatinya; seperti burung yang bergegas ke dalam jerat, tanpa mengetahui bahwa itu merenggut nyawanya –Amsal 7:23. Kita dapat menelaah keburukan dalam kehidupan muda Rehabeam, Amnon, Nadab dan Abihu, serta banyak orang lainnya. Kita juga tidak kekurangan contoh modern yang penuh kebodohan di sekitar kita, yang diwujudkan oleh kaum muda yang sembrono.

Namun, kaum muda tidak dimaksudkan untuk dihina. Jangan seorang pun menganggap engkau rendah karena engkau muda; tetapi jadilah teladan bagi orang-orang percaya, dalam perkataan, tingkah laku, kasih, roh, iman, dan kemurnian –1 Timotius 4:12. Bahkan, Allah pada umumnya memilih kaum muda sebagai alat untuk menyebarkan karya-Nya. Yusuf, yang berkarakter luhur, diutus Allah ke Mesir pada usia 17 tahun untuk memelihara kehidupan (–lihat Kejadian 45:5). Miryam, pada usia dua belas tahun, berjaga-jaga atas calon pembebas seluruh bangsa Yahudi dan mengatur agar ibunya sendiri, Yokhebed, menjadi pengasuh bayi Musa. Daud, semasa muda, diutus untuk menguatkan saudara-saudaranya di dalam tentara. Ia dihina oleh saudara-saudaranya: …Aku tahu kesombonganmu dan kejahatan hatimu… –1 Samuel 17:28. Ia ditolak oleh Saul: …Engkau tidak sanggup melawan orang Filistin ini untuk berperang dengannya, sebab engkau masih muda… –1 Samuel 17:33. Ia dicemooh oleh Goliat: …Apakah aku ini anjing, sehingga engkau datang kepadaku dengan tongkat… –1 Samuel 17:43. Namun, penghinaan mereka sia-sia belaka ketika ia dipilih Allah untuk menjadi raja atas seluruh Israel.

Ambisi luhur kaum muda ini diikuti oleh Yosia, Yesaya, Yeremia, Daniel, Maria, dan para murid Tuhan, yang semuanya memilih untuk mengingat Pencipta mereka pada masa muda mereka. Namun, mereka bukanlah contoh-contoh naif yang berusaha mengamankan kedudukan mereka dalam hidup; mereka adalah teladan nyata kaum muda yang berusaha meneladani citra Tuhan mereka.

Kita tidak perlu lama-lama menatap karakter Kristus sebelum menemukan…

...Engkau memiliki embun kemudaan-Mu

Mazmur 110 mungkin merupakan ayat yang paling sering dirujuk dalam Perjanjian Lama. Gambaran retoris tentang Mesias ini mengungkapkan kebajikan yang hidup untuk kita renungkan. Kristus, sebagai Yang Lanjut Usianya, digambarkan dalam Kitab Wahyu memiliki kepala dan rambut-Nya ... putih seperti bulu domba, seputih salju… –Wahyu 1:14, tetapi di sini Ia digambarkan selalu muda, saat duduk di sebelah kanan Allah (–lihat Mazmur 110:1). Tak ada keletihan karena usia yang dapat masuk ke sana, sebab Kristus adalah Bintang Fajar. Di sekitar takhta Allah senantiasa pagi. Orang-orang kudus yang sungguh-sungguh mengikuti rupa-Nya juga akan memancarkan kebajikan ini, sebab terang Yesus adalah terang kemudaan.

Penulis mazmur, ketika menggambarkan Mesias, mengambil ilham dari keindahan alam embun pagi (–lihat Mazmur 110:3). Gagasan tentang embun mengalihkan pandangan kita dari langit dan menyingkapkan di hadapan kita gambaran bumi tempat kita tinggal. Di surga tidak ada malam, tidak ada perubahan panas dan dingin, tidak perlu matahari untuk menerangi siang, dan karena itu… tidak ada embun. Sifat embun adalah bagian dari dunia fana, tempat siapa pun yang mau merendahkan diri untuk mengamatinya akan melihat barisan rumput yang seragam berkilauan seolah bertabur berjuta-juta berlian. Setelah malam panjang yang gelap, titik-titik embun, seperti air mata, menggenang di mata bunga-bunga saat mereka menangis bahagia menyambut sinar matahari pagi yang pertama. Mereka yang berjalan melewati tumbuh-tumbuhan rendah akan dibasuh kakinya oleh seribu tangan lembut hasil rancangan Allah. Kristus tidak digambarkan sebagai embun pagi, melainkan sebagai embun kemudaan, dan gambaran ini dikembangkan lebih jauh.

Masa muda adalah masa ketika energi melimpah. Ada yang tidak bisa duduk diam. Mereka umumnya makhluk sosial yang menyukai kegiatan bersama orang lain. Ini bukan kebajikan ataupun keburukan. Sebaliknya, ini adalah sifat yang lumrah. Seiring bertambahnya usia, ada proses bertahap yang menenangkan dan mengendalikan jiwa. Seiring hidup berjalan, pandangan menjadi lebih jelas dan pikiran lebih mantap, dan kita bangkit menuju hal-hal yang lebih baik. Namun, setelah puncak usia pertengahan terlewati dan kaki melangkah menuruni lereng kehidupan, gejolak energi tubuh yang dahulu menerjang segala rintangan menjadi tersimpan dalam kenangan masa lalu. Bagi banyak orang, inilah penghiburan terdekat yang dapat mereka temukan dari masa ketika mereka masih kuat.

Namun, Kristus tidak memanggil kita untuk memupuk kegemaran akan masa lalu ataupun kerinduan penuh pilu akan “daya juang” masa muda kita. Begitu banyak orang sekarang dengan sedih meratapi bahwa semangat mereka untuk bergerak telah pergi. Mereka tidak memiliki visi untuk hal-hal yang lebih tinggi dan lebih bersemangat oleh sekaleng Mountain Dew daripada Embun Kemudaan. Mereka lebih terilhami oleh perjalanan menyusuri kenangan dan mengenang peristiwa masa lalu daripada oleh pengharapan yang terbentang di hadapan mereka.

Usia bukanlah penghalang untuk memperoleh embun kemudaan. Yang Lanjut Usianya masih berjalan di antara kaki-kaki dian emas. Ketika Yohanes melihat rambut-Nya ... putih seperti bulu domba, seputih salju… –Wahyu 1:14, Salomo menyatakan …rambut-Nya lebat dan hitam seperti gagak –Kidung Agung 5:11. Sekalipun usia dapat merampas kekuatan dan pendengaran kita, …tangan TUHAN tidak kurang panjang untuk menyelamatkan, dan telinga-Nya tidak kurang tajam untuk mendengar: –Yesaya 59:1. Ia telah menyediakan embun kemudaan dan mengundang kita untuk menikmatinya. Masalahnya bukan terdapat pada tubuh kita yang makin merosot, melainkan pada pikiran yang merosot secara rohani. Bencana usia tua terutama mulai terjadi ketika pikiran mengikuti tubuh.

Bukan berarti hidup menjadi lebih buruk seiring kemajuannya atau berhenti menjadi luhur ketika pesona masa muda memudar. Jika kita ditempatkan di sini hanya untuk mengalami sukacita, pudarnya romansa masa muda akan sangat menyedihkan. Allah memiliki tujuan yang jauh lebih besar bagi anak-anak-Nya daripada sekadar menjadi “pelaku” yang bersemangat. Kita diutus ke sini untuk belajar. Tahun-tahun yang diberikan kepada kita di bumi dimaksudkan sebagai masa pendidikan, dan pelajaran terbaik serta paling bertahan lama tidak kita pelajari dalam romansa masa muda yang gemilang. Kita mempelajarinya melalui ketekunan dalam menjalankan kewajiban, penerimaan yang tenang atas keterbatasan kita, kesabaran memikul beban sehari-hari, dan kesediaan mengulurkan tangan untuk menolong saudara kita. Semua ini memberi kita kesempatan nyata untuk membentuk karakter Kristen dan merupakan akar keluhuran etis. Kristus bekerja …bukan untuk makanan yang dapat binasa, melainkan untuk makanan yang bertahan sampai hidup yang kekal… –Yohanes 6:27, dan Ia menuntaskan tugas-Nya di bumi dalam 33 tahun. Namun, embun kemudaan tidak menguap ketika Ia duduk di sebelah kanan Bapa-Nya.

Dengan demikian, kita menyimpulkan bahwa kemudaan ini tidak diperoleh melalui kekuatan, melainkan melalui…

...Pengharapan

Namun, Ia, setelah mempersembahkan satu korban untuk dosa-dosa untuk selama-lamanya, duduk di sebelah kanan Allah; sejak saat itu Ia menantikan sampai musuh-musuh-Nya dijadikan tumpuan kaki-Nya. –Ibrani 10:12-13.

Bagaimana kita harus membayangkan Kristus sekarang? Bersandar di kursi empuk, kehabisan tenaga setelah menghadapi orang-orang bumi yang keras kepala? Apakah Ia sibuk menyusun album kenangan berharga? Terlalu sering, orang lanjut usia berada dalam keadaan seperti ini, sehingga pikiran mereka mati bersama tubuh mereka.

Dan bukan hanya itu, kita juga bermegah dalam kesengsaraan: karena kita tahu, bahwa kesengsaraan menghasilkan ketekunan; dan ketekunan menghasilkan tahan uji; dan tahan uji menghasilkan pengharapan –Roma 5:3-4. Terkadang, kita bertanya-tanya apakah ayat ini benar. Siapa pun yang telah cukup lama hidup dapat bersaksi tentang pengalaman buruk dan perasaan putus asa yang menyusulnya. Sebagai manusia, kita semua pernah mengalami kekecewaan dalam hubungan dengan pasangan, anak, atau jemaat, yang kemudian disusul awan keputusasaan yang terus mengganggu. Di luar Kristus, pengalaman pahit selalu cenderung membawa pesimisme. Demikianlah keadaannya di dunia ketika Yesus datang. Demikian pula keadaannya sekarang.

Namun, embun kemudaan tak mungkin kehilangan pengharapan. Ada harapan penuh semangat yang secara alami dan luar biasa tumbuh dalam diri kaum muda dan tetap terpelihara di dalam Kristus. Setiap musim dingin, ketika ladang tampak gersang dan embusan angin dingin bersiul di antara pepohonan, tetap ada harapan bahwa bunga-bunga akan bermekaran kembali. Setiap musim semi membawa harapan akan musim panas. Setiap musim panas membawa harapan akan panen. Pengharapan itu hidup di alam dan hidup dalam diri kaum muda. Mereka yang buta terhadapnya paling-paling akan menjalani hidup monoton yang muram. Hidup adalah hal yang paling langka di dunia. Kebanyakan orang hanya ada, itu saja. –Oscar Wilde.

Yang lain akan sungguh-sungguh mengalami pengaruh baik pengharapan yang…

…Menyembuhkan Kelemahan Kita

Tubuh kita ditakdirkan untuk masuk ke liang kubur dan tidak memiliki harapan untuk diperbarui dalam hidup ini. Pikiran kitalah yang menanggung kelemahan terbesar kita. Orang lumpuh yang telah 38 tahun berada di Betesda hanya mampu mengucapkan keluhan putus asa ketika Kristus bertanya kepadanya, …Maukah engkau sembuh? –Yohanes 5:6. Saat hari barunya dimulai, obat baru diberikan kepadanya—…Lihat, engkau sudah sembuh; jangan berbuat dosa lagi, supaya jangan terjadi sesuatu yang lebih buruk kepadamu –Yohanes 5:14. Apa yang lebih buruk daripada menjadi orang lumpuh selama bertahun-tahun? Pikiran yang diliputi kegemaran menyedihkan akan dukacita dunia ini. Usia tua mulai datang ketika kenangan masa lalu kita lebih banyak daripada pengharapan untuk hari esok. Mengecewakan ketika orang-orang menjadi tua tanpa memiliki visi untuk hari esok, tetapi sungguh malang menyaksikan kaum muda yang dilanda dampak melumpuhkan itu. Banyak orang meraba-raba tanpa arah melewati berbagai pencobaan hidup, terpaku karena tidak memiliki kebahagiaan. Matahari tengah hari telah menguapkan embun kemudaan mereka, dan satu-satunya pujian yang mampu mereka ucapkan dirangkai dari segenggam kesenangan masa lalu. Sikap baru harus dilahirkan oleh embun pagi yang baru.

…Merendahkan Ambisi Kita

Aku berkata kepadamu dengan sesungguhnya: Ketika engkau masih muda, engkau sendiri mengikat pinggangmu dan berjalan ke mana saja yang kaukehendaki; tetapi apabila engkau sudah tua, engkau akan mengulurkan tanganmu dan orang lain akan mengikat pinggangmu dan membawa engkau ke tempat yang tidak kaukehendaki. –Yohanes 21:18. Ketika masih muda, kita dapat menang dengan kekuatan masa muda. Seiring berjalannya usia, kita akan menemukan jalan lain: kemenangan melalui penyerahan diri.

…Aku menulis kepadamu, hai orang-orang muda, sebab kamu kuat dan firman Allah diam di dalam kamu, dan kamu telah mengalahkan si jahat. –1 Yohanes 2:14. Dunia membujuk kita untuk hidup mementingkan diri sendiri. Kaum muda sering mengikuti pendidikan yang mengajari mereka untuk “menjadi segala yang dapat kamu capai”. Penekanan besar diberikan pada pengembangan diri dan persiapan masa depan. Ini mungkin mempersiapkan mereka untuk dunia “yang kuatlah yang bertahan”, tetapi akan membuat mereka melarat ketika kekuatan dan keperkasaan masa muda telah pergi.

Sebab semua yang ada di dalam dunia, yaitu keinginan daging, keinginan mata, dan keangkuhan hidup, bukan berasal dari Bapa, melainkan dari dunia. Dan dunia ini sedang lenyap dengan keinginannya, tetapi orang yang melakukan kehendak Allah tetap hidup selama-lamanya. –1 Yohanes 2:16-17. Mengalahkan kejahatan dengan kebaikan adalah penawar alkitabiah untuk menyalurkan energi kaum muda. Entah itu hawa nafsu di dalam diri ataupun kerinduan akan hal-hal di luar diri, pengharapan tumbuh dengan menanam benih kebaikan dalam hidup orang lain. Mengejar kesenangan dan memilih bersantai akan selalu mengecewakan orang yang menikmatinya dan meninggalkannya di lembah keputusasaan yang lebih dalam daripada sebelumnya. Adalah baik bagi seorang laki-laki memikul kuk pada masa mudanya … Biarlah ia merebahkan mulutnya dalam debu; mungkin masih ada harapan. –Ratapan 3:27-29. Kita diciptakan untuk bekerja di kebun anggur Allah, dan mereka yang memiliki hasrat untuk melakukannya akan menuai dengan pengharapan akan upah kemudaan itu.

…Menguduskan Pencobaan Kita

Sebab kita diselamatkan dalam pengharapan; tetapi pengharapan yang terlihat bukanlah pengharapan... –Roma 8:24. Betapa sering kita dapat memahami penderitaan Ayub. Namun, bahkan sebelum penderitaannya menerima balasan sedikit pun, aliran penyembuhan mulai mengalir ketika Ayub menghormati Penciptanya. Ketika kita mengakui bahwa Allah sempurna dalam segala pencobaan yang Ia izinkan, kita belajar beribadah di dalam bait yang tidak dibuat oleh tangan manusia dan mengabaikan kelemahan tubuh. Duduk di kaki Kristus menyalakan percikan kemudaan yang memancarkan roh di dalam diri dan menumbuhkan pengharapan. Embun kemudaan pun menjadi bagian kita ketika Kristus menganugerahkan hidup kekal dan kemudaan kekal kepada kita. Sejak saat kematian dan sepanjang kekekalan, kita akan tetap muda dan menentang keletihan serta kematian jika kita hidup dalam terang pagi Yesus Kristus. Surga adalah tempat kemudaan yang abadi, dan sebagaimana cahaya matahari dipantulkan oleh bulan, demikian pula cahaya Kristus dipantulkan oleh mempelai perempuan-Nya. Ia suci dan muda, …jemaat yang mulia, tanpa noda atau kerut atau hal semacam itu… –Efesus 5:27. Berbahagialah orang kudus yang lanjut usia yang tiba di gerbang surga dalam keadaan demikian.

Sometimes my heart is heavy,
Weighted with fears and care.
It’s then my Lord calls out to me,
“Come My child, your burden I’ll bear.”

Sometimes questions flood my mind,
The answers seem evasive and trying.
That’s when I lift these eyes to my God,
Claiming His love on me overlying.

Sometimes I feel like quitting,
The way before me seems long and hard.
But I think of the path of my Shepherd,
It was for me He was scarred.

Sometimes my mind is clouded,
I stumble with each step that I take.
Yet out of the fog, I hear a whisper,
“You are Mine, trust Me, a way I will make.”

Sometimes I find my circumstances,
Seemingly harsh, and unfair.
But then my Father whispers,
“Dear one, do not despair.”

Sometimes I feel all alone,
The ache within chokes and burns.
The Master speaks, “My chosen one,
I alone can fulfill, that for which your heart yearns.

Sometimes my eyes are full of tears
My heart feels near to burst.
And then my Savior reminds me,
This path, before me, He traversed.

Sometimes I worry and wonder,
How things will ever turn out right.
Yet the promise remains, all works out well,
For him that in God does delight.

Sometimes the future seems scary,
Not at all like what I had hoped.
Still, I set my eyes on His ultimate goal,
Knowing it’s better than for what I had groped.

Sometimes I feel left behind,
While others lives go on so free.
But, in my Father’s plans I will trust,
And look forward to His eternal jubilee!

Sometimes I find myself dreaming,
Of the future in heaven to come.
Oh what bliss will be the feeling,
To hear those words, “Well done.”

때로 내 마음은 무겁고,
두려움과 근심에 짓눌립니다.
그때 주님께서 내게 부르십니다.
“오너라, 내 아이야. 네 짐은 내가 지마.”

때로 온갖 질문이 마음에 밀려오고,
답은 피하는 듯 난감하기만 합니다.
그럴 때 나는 눈을 들어 하나님을 바라보며,
나를 덮고 있는 그분의 사랑을 붙듭니다.

때로는 그만두고 싶고,
내 앞에 놓인 길은 멀고 험해 보입니다.
하지만 목자께서 걸으신 길을 생각합니다.
그분은 나를 위해 상처를 입으셨습니다.

때로 내 마음은 흐려지고,
한 걸음 내디딜 때마다 비틀거립니다.
그러나 안개 속에서 속삭임이 들려옵니다.
“너는 내 것이다. 나를 믿어라. 내가 길을 내리라.”

때로 내 처지가
모질고 불공평하게만 보입니다.
그러나 그때 아버지께서 속삭이십니다.
“사랑하는 아이야, 절망하지 마라.”

때로는 나 홀로인 듯하고,
가슴속 아픔은 목을 죄고 타오릅니다.
주님께서 말씀하십니다. “내가 택한 자야,
네 마음이 바라는 것을 채워 줄 이는 나뿐이란다.

때로 내 눈에는 눈물이 가득하고,
가슴은 터질 듯합니다.
그때 구주께서 내게 일러 주십니다.
그분은 내 앞에 놓인 이 길을 이미 지나가셨다고.

때로 걱정하며 궁금해합니다.
일이 과연 어떻게 잘 풀릴지.
그러나 약속은 변함없습니다. 모든 일이 잘 이루어지리니,
하나님을 기뻐하는 자에게 그러합니다.

때로 미래는 두렵고,
내가 바라던 모습과는 전혀 다릅니다.
그래도 나는 그분이 궁극에 이루실 목적에 눈을 둡니다.
내가 바라며 더듬어 찾던 것보다 나으리라 믿으며.

때로 나는 뒤처진 듯 느끼고,
다른 이들의 삶은 자유롭게 흘러갑니다.
그러나 아버지의 계획을 신뢰하며,
그분의 영원한 기쁨의 잔치를 고대하겠습니다!

때로 나는 꿈을 꿉니다.
다가올 하늘나라의 미래를.
오, 그 기쁨이 얼마나 크리요,
“잘하였다”라는 말씀을 듣는다면.

Greetings of Christian love to each one. Another year has passed us by, and another is spread out before us to navigate. What is our perspective? Do we have hope and joy bubbling up in our hearts or does the future seem full of gloom and doom? Do we see God’s sovereign hand at work in the situations and circumstances around us or does the world seem out of control from our vantage point?

As I interact with folks from around the country there seems to be a common issue that many folks are struggling with—weariness. Weary of mandates. Weary of shutdowns. Weary of all the bickering and fighting that has surrounded the Covid issue. Weary of…

It appears that many people just “Don’t want to think about it”. Why? I’m really not sure what all the reasons are, but I am sure that each person has one. Let’s remember that God wants us to …be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves –Matthew 10:16.

Here, in the United States of America, Christians have had over 60 years (since World War 2) of relative peace and tranquility. For the most part, we have been left alone to raise our families and worship the God of our fathers according to our conscience. We have enjoyed the separation of Church and State that was implemented at the beginning of our country’s existence. We have been able to work with our hands and earn a living. Many of us have lived off the fat of the land.

Maybe we were living in an artificial bubble. Maybe we have been lulled into a false sense of security. What about our counterparts in countries around the world, what is their reality of living as true Christians in their world? Sure, we have been able to use our wealth and freedom of movement to do much good for the rest of the world who have endured much hardship due to following Christ. But at what cost? What have our children learned?

Sometimes, we hear about first generation Christians being “on fire” for their Lord. Sometimes so much so that second and third generation Christians think that first generation Christians are perhaps a little too zealous in their efforts of evangelizing those around them.

What about the next generation? They are learning from someone—about God, themselves, and life. What are they learning? And who are they learning from? We must take stock to ensure that our children are learning life’s lessons in a way that they will be prepared to face the reality of things to come.

And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world? And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many –Matthew 24:3-5.

Remember that this is Jesus Himself speaking to His followers regarding the end of the world. His very first concern is that we would NOT be deceived. He says that deception will be the major issue surrounding the end of time. He says that many will come claiming to be Christ [or His direct spokesperson] in an attempt to gain a listening ear, all in an effort to deceive the hearer and gain a following.

If not before now, we most certainly must be teaching our children certain specific things through word and action. That we are to be strangers and pilgrims as we journey through this life. That if we are friends of this world then God will be our enemy. And that Jesus’ Kingdom is not of this world, therefore, His children must learn to live as ambassadors in a foreign land. Our children need to know that ALL who live godly in Christ Jesus WILL suffer persecution.

Many of the doctrines that have been taught in our churches and para-church functions have severely crippled the next generation of the church. We have been taught that we can have the “power of His resurrection” without needing to be a partaker of the “fellowship of His sufferings”. A suffering Christ with suffering followers has been thrown out in favor of following a Jesus who will not let anything bad happen to you. While there is much emphasis on a Jesus who suffered and died for you, there is very little to NO teaching on the need to “take up your cross daily” and follow Him.

Mental Health and Emotional Stability

Some years ago, I came across the story of a soldier, who, after serving a term of service in Iraq, was struggling to cope with PTSD. Sure, I believe that PTSD is real, and the struggles are real, but as I read this man’s story, I found myself becoming increasingly frustrated with the lack of answers that were being provided to a severely struggling young man. Some of his deepest struggles stemmed from the flashback memories he had of when he had personally killed several of the enemy. No matter how many counseling sessions he went to he just couldn’t come to a place of inner peace and rest. His mind was troubled. He had difficulty sleeping. He had problems getting along with others.

I had to think “If only someone could come alongside this young man and share the Gospel of Jesus Christ with him. If only he could be shown the Truth of God’s Word that to take another human’s life is sin in God’s eyes (even if he is the enemy) and God will not allow him to have peace in his heart until that is taken care of. Also, that the real excitement is that IF he would come to God according to the terms of the Bible and repent of his sin, then he could start walking with God and God could start giving him peace for his troubled soul.”

Over the last number of years, there have been numerous mass shootings here in the United States. Each time the public officials hold news conferences and share their thoughts in an effort to try to make sense out of another seemingly unexplainable tragic event. Usually, it’s not long until someone is talking about mental health and the need to step up public efforts to provide safety nets, screenings, and better and more treatments to curb this senseless violence.

Several weeks ago, there was a terrible, tragic event that took place in another state from where I live. In one of the big cities, a man pushed a woman off of the platform and into the path of an oncoming subway train. She didn’t survive. In the aftermath of such a horrific happening, the public officials made statements to the public in an effort to stem the potential public fear. They concluded that the man must have been emotionally troubled and that they would be stepping up their efforts in trying to provide a safety net for those with mental health issues, so that such things wouldn’t happen again.

Sure, when we look at the issue through the eyes of the world it seems to make sense. But is this the whole of the matter? Have we as Christians become so used to the ways of the world that we forget how far they have strayed from the Truth of God’s Word?

Let’s not point our finger at the world and the elected public officials. Are we, as the church, any better? How well do we know our Bible? How well do we know our Savior? When someone comes to us seeking peace and rest within do we know how to take them to the Scriptures, and lead them to Jesus who can then show them the way to the Father?

Why am I saying all this? If we continue to provide the next generation of the church with artificial answers and temporary solutions to the problems of life, then they will NOT be prepared to …endure unto the end… –Matthew 24:13.

And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24.
