Thou hast the dew of thy youth. Psalm 110:3

There are many aspects of youth which are not virtuous. Many youth of our day experience an early season of callused carelessness and casualty. Often decisions that are made in youthful years set the foundation for the rest of their lives. It was a the younger prodigal brother that asked for an early draw on his inheritance then went and wasted it on riotous living. It was a young Dinah who wandered from her father’s house and …went out to see the daughters of the land –Genesis 34:1. There, she was exposed to the heathen young men of the land and occasioned a bloody massacre, leaving Jacob as a stench in the land. Many foolish young people have sown to the wind and reaped the havoc thereof. Those that are void of solid principles and parental authority are at high risk for spiritual shipwreck.

There are particular lusts that inflict youth more so than the aged, and the young are exhorted to flee them. (–see 2 Timothy 2:22) Solomon looked through his window casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding -Proverbs 7:6-7. The young man was in heartfelt pursuit of that which appeared lovely… [Un]Till a dart [struck] through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life –Proverbs 7:23. We could examine the vices from the youthful lives of Rehoboam, Amnon, Nadab and Abihu, and countless others. We also find no lack of modern, folly-filled examples about us fulfilled by frivolous youth.

But youth are not meant to be despised. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. In fact, God generally chooses the youth as the instruments of His propagation. Joseph, of sterling character, was sent by God into Egypt at the age of 17 to preserve life (–see Genesis 45:5). Miriam, at the age of twelve, stood post over the future deliverer of the entire Jewish nation and secured her own mother, Jochebed, to be the nurse of the baby Moses. David, as a youth, was sent to encourage his brethren in the army. He was despised by his brothers: …I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart… –1 Samuel 17:28. He was rejected by Saul: …Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth… –1 Samuel 17:33. He was scorned by Goliath: …Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves… –1 Samuel 17:43. But their contempt was all for naught when he was chosen by God to be king over all Israel.

These noble youthful ambitions were followed by Josiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Mary, and the disciples of the Lord, all who chose to remember their Creator in the days of their youth. But these were not naive specimens seeking to secure their place in life, they were graphic examples of youth who were seeking to imitate the image of their Lord.

We need not gaze long into the character of Christ before we find…

...Thou hast the dew of thy youth

Psalm 110 is perhaps the most referred-to scripture in the Old Testament. This rhetorical portrait of the Messiah reveals a vivid virtue for us to behold. Christ, as the Ancient of days, was described in the Revelation having His head and His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet, here He is depicted as eternally young, as He sits at the right hand of God (–see Psalm 110:1). No weariness of age can enter there, for Christ is the Morning Star. It is perpetual morning around the throne of God. Those saints who are following hard after His likeness will also reflect this virtue, for the light of Jesus is the light of youth.

The psalmist, describing the Messiah, draws from the natural beauty of the morning dew (–see Psalm 110:3). The thought of dew calls us back from the heavens and unveils before us a portrait of this earth on which we dwell. In heaven there is no night, no change of heat and cold, no need of the sun to light up the day and consequently… no dew. The nature of dew belongs to the terrestrial, where everyone who will but stoop to observe it will behold a uniformed regiment of grass sparkling as if embedded with a myriad of diamonds. After a long night of darkness, the dewdrops, like tears, stand in the eyes of the flowers as they weep for joy at the advent of the first morning sunbeam. Those who walk through the lowly vegetation will have their feet washed by a thousand caressing hands of God’s design. Christ is not depicted as the dew of the morning but as the dew of youth, and the imagery is stretched further.

Youth is the season of abounding energy. Some cannot sit still. They are generally interpersonal creatures who love social activity. This is neither a virtue nor a vice. Rather, it is nominal nature. There is a progressive strain in advancing years that tames and tempers the soul. As life progresses, there is a clearer vision and a steadier thought, and we rise to better things. But when the mid-life summit has been crossed and the feet are traveling downward on the slope, that tumultuous rush of bodily energy that plowed through anything becomes enshrined with memories of the past. It is the closest comfort many can find to the bygone days of their strength.

But Christ has not called us to foster a fondness for the past nor a wistful longing for the “DO” of our youth. So many today sadly lament that their ‘get-up-and-go’ has got up and went. These have no vision for higher things and are more energized by a can of Mountain Dew than the Dew of Youth. They are more inspired by a trip down memory lane and reminiscing events of the past than of the hope that lies before them.

Age is no hindrance to securing the dew of youth. The Ancient of Days still rides forth among the golden candlesticks. While John beheld His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet Solomon declares …his locks are bushy, and black as a raven –Song of Solomon 5:11. While age may steal our strength and hearing, …the LORD’S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: –Isaiah 59:1. He has secured the dew of youth and invites us to partake. The problem is not found in our deteriorating body but in a spiritually declining mind. The bane of old age predominately sets in when the mind follows the body.

It is not that life grows poorer as it advances or ceases to be noble when the charm of youth has faded. If we were placed here only to experience joy, the dying out of youthful romance would be terrible. God had a much greater end in view for His children than to just be vibrant ‘doers’. We are sent here to learn. Our allotted years upon earth are all meant to be a schooling, and it is not in the bright romance of youth that we learn the best and most abiding lessons. It is in the dogged doing of our duty, the quiet acceptance of our limitations, the patient carrying of our daily burden, and in the stretching out of a helping hand to our brother. These afford us the true opportunities for Christian culture and are the roots of ethical nobility. Christ labored …not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life… –John 6:27, and He finished His earthly task in 33 years. But the dew of youth did not dissipate as He sat down at the right hand of His Father.

Thus, we conclude that this youthfulness will not be secured by strength, but by…

...Hope

But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. –Hebrews 10:12-13.

How shall we picture this Christ now? Reclining in an easy chair, all worn out from His experience with the stubborn people of this earth? Is He busy putting together a scrap book of precious memories? This is too often the position of the aged and so their mind dies with their bodies.

And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope –Romans 5:3-4. At times, we wonder if this scripture can be true. Anyone with any age on their bones can testify to a poor experience and the subsequent feelings of hopelessness following. As people, we have all faced disappointing experiences with a spouse, a child, or a church relationship after which a nagging cloud of despair settles in. Outside of Christ, a sour experience always tends to pessimism. It was so in the world when Jesus came. It is still so today.

But the dew of youth is incurably hopeful. There is an effervescent expectation that is naturally and magnificently borne in youth and retained in Christ. In every winter, when the fields are bleak, and the cold gust goes whistling through the trees, there lies the hope that the flowers will spring again. In every spring there is the hope of summer. In every summer there is the hope of harvest. It is alive in nature and alive in youth. Those who are blind to it shall reap, at best, a dreary monotone existence. To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all. –Oscar Wilde.

The rest shall be brightly effected with a hope that…

…Heals Our Infirmities

Our bodies are destined for the grave and have no hope for renewal in this life. It is our minds that carry our greatest infirmities. The impotent man of 38 years at Bethesda could only utter a hopeless complaint when Christ asked him, …Wilt thou be made whole? –John 5:6. Upon the wake of his new day, a new remedy was given to him—… Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee –John 5:14. What could be worse than being a cripple for years? A mind that is beset by a doleful indulgence in the sorrows of this world. Age sets in when we have more memories of the past than hope for tomorrow. It is disappointing when folks grow old and have no vision for tomorrow, but it is a disaster to behold youth that are plagued by its crippling effects. Many grope aimlessly through life’s various trials, stupefied by the lack of blessedness. The noonday sun has evaporated the dew of their youth and the only praise that they can muster is culminated from a handful of yesterday’s pleasantries. A new attitude must be birthed by the dew of a new morning.

…Humbles Our Pursuits

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. –John 21:18. When we are young, we can overcome in the strength of our youth. As age takes its course, we will find a different alternative: victory through surrender.

…I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one. –1 John 2:14. The world entices us to selfish living. Youth are often subject to schools of learning that teach them to “be all that you can be”. There is a major focus on self-enhancement and preparation for the future. This may prepare them in a ‘survival of the fittest’ world but will leave them destitute when the strength and prowess of youth has departed.

For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever. –1 John 2:16-17. Overcoming evil with good is the Biblical antidote for channeling youthful energies. Whether it is the lust within or the longing without, hope is conceived by planting a seed of kindness in the life of another. The pursuit of pleasure and lieu of leisure will always disappoint its recipient and leave him in a valley of despair deeper than when he began. It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth … He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope. –Lamentations 3:27-29. We are created to work in God’s vineyard and those who have an appetite for it will reap in hope of its youthful reward.

…Hallows Our Trials

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope... –Romans 8:24. How often we can relate to Job in his pain. But before his pain had received an ounce of retribution, the healing streams began to flow as Job reverenced his Creator. When we can acknowledge that God is perfect in all the trials He allows, we then learn to worship in the temple not made with hands and disregard the frailties of the body. To sit down at the feet of Christ ignites a youthful spark that radiates the spirit within and conceives hope. The dew of youth then becomes our portion as Christ imparts eternal life and eternal youth to us. From the hour of the grave and through eternity we shall be young and bid defiance to weariness and death if we are living in the morning light of Jesus Christ. Heaven is a place of perpetual youth, and just like the light of the sun is reflected on the moon, so likewise the light of Christ is reflected on His bride. She is clean and young, …a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing… –Ephesians 5:27. Blessed is the venerable saint who arrives at the portals of heaven in such a condition.

Tienes el rocío de tu juventud. Salmo 110:3

Hay muchos aspectos de la juventud que no son virtuosos. Muchos jóvenes de nuestros días atraviesan tempranamente una etapa de indiferencia insensible y ruina. A menudo, las decisiones que se toman durante la juventud sientan las bases para el resto de la vida. Fue el hermano pródigo menor quien pidió recibir anticipadamente su herencia y luego la malgastó viviendo desenfrenadamente. Fue la joven Dina quien se alejó de la casa de su padre y …salió a ver a las hijas de la tierra –Génesis 34:1. Allí quedó expuesta a los jóvenes paganos de la tierra y provocó una sangrienta masacre, dejando a Jacob como hedor en la tierra. Muchos jóvenes insensatos han sembrado al viento y cosechado sus estragos. Quienes carecen de principios sólidos y de autoridad parental corren un alto riesgo de naufragar espiritualmente.

Hay deseos particulares que afligen más a los jóvenes que a los ancianos, y se exhorta a los jóvenes a huir de ellos. (–véase 2 Timoteo 2:22) Salomón miró por la ventana de su casa, Y vi entre los simples, discerní entre los jóvenes, a un joven falto de entendimiento –Proverbios 7:6-7. El joven perseguía con fervor aquello que parecía hermoso… [H]asta que una flecha le atravesó el hígado; como el ave que se apresura a la trampa, sin saber que es para su vida –Proverbios 7:23. Podríamos examinar los vicios de la juventud de Roboam, Amnón, Nadab y Abiú, y de incontables otros. Tampoco nos faltan a nuestro alrededor ejemplos modernos, llenos de insensatez, protagonizados por jóvenes frívolos.

Pero no se debe despreciar a los jóvenes. Ninguno tenga en poco tu juventud; sino sé ejemplo de los creyentes en palabra, conducta, amor, espíritu, fe y pureza –1 Timoteo 4:12. De hecho, por lo general Dios escoge a los jóvenes como instrumentos para propagar su obra. José, de carácter intachable, fue enviado por Dios a Egipto a los 17 años para preservar la vida (–véase Génesis 45:5). Miriam, a los doce años, vigiló al futuro libertador de toda la nación judía y consiguió que su propia madre, Jocabed, fuera la nodriza del niño Moisés. David, siendo joven, fue enviado a animar a sus hermanos en el ejército. Sus hermanos lo despreciaron: …Conozco tu orgullo y la maldad de tu corazón… –1 Samuel 17:28. Saúl lo rechazó: …No puedes ir contra este filisteo para pelear con él, porque tú no eres más que un muchacho… –1 Samuel 17:33. Goliat se burló de él: …¿Soy yo un perro, para que vengas contra mí con palos… –1 Samuel 17:43. Pero todo su desprecio fue en vano cuando Dios lo escogió para ser rey sobre todo Israel.

A estas nobles aspiraciones juveniles siguieron las de Josías, Isaías, Jeremías, Daniel, María y los discípulos del Señor, quienes escogieron acordarse de su Creador en los días de su juventud. Pero no eran ingenuos que buscaban asegurarse un lugar en la vida; eran ejemplos elocuentes de jóvenes que procuraban imitar la imagen de su Señor.

No necesitamos contemplar por mucho tiempo el carácter de Cristo antes de encontrar…

...Tienes el rocío de tu juventud

El Salmo 110 es quizá el pasaje más citado del Antiguo Testamento. Este retrato retórico del Mesías nos revela una virtud vívida que podemos contemplar. Cristo, como el Anciano de días, fue descrito en Apocalipsis con su cabeza y sus cabellos ... blancos como la lana, tan blancos como la nieve… –Apocalipsis 1:14; sin embargo, aquí se lo representa eternamente joven, sentado a la diestra de Dios (–véase Salmo 110:1). Allí no puede entrar el cansancio de la edad, pues Cristo es la Estrella de la Mañana. Alrededor del trono de Dios siempre es de mañana. Los santos que siguen de cerca su semejanza también reflejarán esta virtud, pues la luz de Jesús es la luz de la juventud.

Al describir al Mesías, el salmista recurre a la belleza natural del rocío de la mañana (–véase Salmo 110:3). La idea del rocío nos hace volver del cielo y despliega ante nosotros un retrato de esta tierra en la que vivimos. En el cielo no hay noche, ni cambios de calor y frío, ni necesidad del sol para alumbrar el día y, por consiguiente… no hay rocío. El rocío pertenece al ámbito terrenal, donde todo el que se incline a observarlo verá un regimiento uniforme de hierba que resplandece como si estuviera cubierto de miríadas de diamantes. Después de una larga noche de oscuridad, las gotas de rocío, como lágrimas, brillan en los ojos de las flores mientras lloran de alegría ante la llegada del primer rayo de sol de la mañana. Quienes caminen entre la humilde vegetación sentirán que mil manos acariciadoras, obra de Dios, les lavan los pies. Cristo no aparece representado como el rocío de la mañana, sino como el rocío de la juventud, y la imagen se amplía aún más.

La juventud es la etapa de la energía abundante. Algunos no pueden quedarse quietos. Por lo general, son personas sociables a quienes les gusta la actividad en grupo. Esto no es ni una virtud ni un vicio; más bien, es algo propio de la naturaleza humana. Con el paso de los años hay un proceso gradual que amansa y templa el alma. A medida que avanza la vida, la visión se vuelve más clara y el pensamiento más sereno, y nos elevamos a cosas mejores. Pero, una vez cruzada la cima de la mediana edad y cuando los pies descienden por la pendiente, aquel tumultuoso torrente de energía física que arrollaba todo a su paso queda consagrado en los recuerdos del pasado. Para muchos, es el consuelo más cercano que pueden encontrar por los días idos de su vigor.

Pero Cristo no nos ha llamado a fomentar el apego al pasado ni el anhelo nostálgico por el «ímpetu» de nuestra juventud. Hoy tantos se lamentan tristemente de que su «energía» se haya esfumado. No tienen visión de cosas más elevadas y los anima más una lata de Mountain Dew que el rocío de la juventud. Les inspira más un paseo por los recuerdos y rememorar acontecimientos pasados que la esperanza que tienen por delante.

La edad no impide alcanzar el rocío de la juventud. El Anciano de días todavía avanza entre los candeleros de oro. Mientras Juan contemplaba sus cabellos ... blancos como la lana, tan blancos como la nieve… –Apocalipsis 1:14, Salomón declara: …sus cabellos son ondulados y negros como el cuervo –Cantar de los Cantares 5:11. Aunque la edad pueda arrebatarnos la fuerza y el oído, …la mano del SEÑOR no se ha acortado para salvar, ni su oído se ha agravado para oír: –Isaías 59:1. Él ha asegurado el rocío de la juventud y nos invita a participar de él. El problema no está en nuestro cuerpo deteriorado, sino en una mente que decae espiritualmente. El flagelo de la vejez se instala principalmente cuando la mente sigue el curso del cuerpo.

No es que la vida se empobrezca a medida que avanza ni que deje de ser noble cuando se desvanece el encanto de la juventud. Si solo estuviéramos aquí para experimentar alegría, el apagarse del romance juvenil sería terrible. Dios tenía para sus hijos un propósito mucho mayor que el de ser simplemente «hacedores» llenos de vitalidad. Estamos aquí para aprender. Todos los años que se nos conceden en la tierra están destinados a ser una etapa de formación, y no es en el brillante romance de la juventud donde aprendemos las lecciones mejores y más duraderas. Las aprendemos al cumplir tenazmente nuestro deber, aceptar en silencio nuestras limitaciones, llevar con paciencia nuestra carga cotidiana y tender una mano de ayuda a nuestro hermano. Estas cosas nos brindan verdaderas oportunidades para cultivar la vida cristiana y son las raíces de la nobleza ética. Cristo trabajó …no por el alimento que perece, sino por el alimento que permanece para vida eterna… –Juan 6:27, y terminó su tarea terrenal en 33 años. Pero el rocío de la juventud no se disipó cuando se sentó a la diestra de su Padre.

Por tanto, concluimos que esta juventud no se obtiene mediante la fuerza, sino mediante…

...La esperanza

Pero este, después de ofrecer un solo sacrificio por los pecados para siempre, se sentó a la diestra de Dios; desde entonces espera hasta que sus enemigos sean puestos por estrado de sus pies. –Hebreos 10:12-13.

¿Cómo hemos de imaginar ahora a este Cristo? ¿Recostado en un sillón, completamente agotado por su experiencia con la gente obstinada de esta tierra? ¿O está ocupado armando un álbum de recuerdos entrañables? Con demasiada frecuencia, esa es la postura de los ancianos, y así su mente muere junto con su cuerpo.

Y no solo esto, sino que también nos gloriamos en las tribulaciones, sabiendo que la tribulación produce paciencia; y la paciencia, experiencia; y la experiencia, esperanza –Romanos 5:3-4. A veces nos preguntamos si este pasaje puede ser verdad. Cualquiera que haya acumulado algunos años puede dar testimonio de una experiencia penosa y de los sentimientos de desesperanza que le siguen. Como personas, todos hemos tenido experiencias decepcionantes con nuestro cónyuge, un hijo o una relación en la iglesia, tras las cuales se instala una persistente nube de desesperación. Fuera de Cristo, una experiencia amarga siempre tiende al pesimismo. Así era el mundo cuando vino Jesús. Así sigue siendo hoy.

Pero el rocío de la juventud es incurablemente esperanzador. En la juventud nace de manera natural y magnífica una expectativa efervescente que se conserva en Cristo. Cada invierno, cuando los campos están desolados y la ráfaga fría silba entre los árboles, permanece la esperanza de que las flores vuelvan a brotar. Cada primavera alberga la esperanza del verano. Cada verano, la esperanza de la cosecha. Está viva en la naturaleza y viva en la juventud. Quienes no la ven cosecharán, en el mejor de los casos, una existencia monótona y sombría. Vivir es lo más raro del mundo. La mayoría de las personas existe, eso es todo. –Oscar Wilde.

Los demás serán vivificados por una esperanza que…

…Sana nuestras dolencias

Nuestros cuerpos están destinados a la tumba y no tienen esperanza de renovación en esta vida. Son nuestras mentes las que llevan nuestras mayores dolencias. El hombre inválido que llevaba 38 años en Betesda solo pudo expresar una queja desesperanzada cuando Cristo le preguntó: …¿Quieres ser sanado? –Juan 5:6. Al comenzar su nuevo día, se le dio un remedio nuevo: …Mira, has sido sanado; no peques más, para que no te suceda algo peor –Juan 5:14. ¿Qué podría ser peor que pasar años lisiado? Una mente afligida por regodearse tristemente en las penas de este mundo. La vejez comienza cuando tenemos más recuerdos del pasado que esperanza para el mañana. Es decepcionante que la gente envejezca sin tener visión del mañana, pero es desastroso ver a jóvenes aquejados por los efectos paralizantes de la vejez. Muchos avanzan a tientas sin rumbo por las diversas pruebas de la vida, aturdidos por la falta de dicha. El sol del mediodía ha evaporado el rocío de su juventud, y los únicos elogios que logran expresar se reducen a un puñado de alegrías de ayer. El rocío de una nueva mañana debe hacer nacer una actitud nueva.

…Humilla nuestras aspiraciones

De cierto, de cierto te digo: Cuando eras joven, te ceñías e ibas adonde querías; pero cuando seas viejo, extenderás las manos, y otro te ceñirá y te llevará adonde no quieras. –Juan 21:18. Cuando somos jóvenes, podemos vencer con la fuerza de nuestra juventud. Al avanzar la edad, encontraremos otra alternativa: la victoria por medio de la rendición.

…Os he escrito a vosotros, jóvenes, porque sois fuertes, y la palabra de Dios permanece en vosotros, y habéis vencido al maligno. –1 Juan 2:14. El mundo nos incita a vivir egoístamente. A menudo, los jóvenes están sujetos a sistemas educativos que les enseñan a «ser todo lo que puedan ser». Se hace mucho hincapié en el mejoramiento personal y la preparación para el futuro. Esto quizá los prepare para un mundo donde sobrevive el más apto, pero los dejará desamparados cuando se hayan ido la fuerza y el vigor de la juventud.

Porque todo lo que hay en el mundo —los deseos de la carne, los deseos de los ojos y la vanagloria de la vida— no proviene del Padre, sino del mundo. Y el mundo pasa, y sus deseos; pero el que hace la voluntad de Dios permanece para siempre. –1 Juan 2:16-17. Vencer el mal con el bien es el antídoto bíblico para encauzar las energías juveniles. Ya se trate del deseo interior o del anhelo exterior, la esperanza se concibe al sembrar una semilla de bondad en la vida de otra persona. La búsqueda del placer y la preferencia por el ocio siempre decepcionarán a quien las persiga y lo dejarán en un valle de desesperación más profundo que aquel en que empezó. Bueno es que el hombre lleve el yugo en su juventud… Ponga su boca en el polvo; quizá haya esperanza. –Lamentaciones 3:27-29. Fuimos creados para trabajar en la viña de Dios, y quienes tengan apetito por hacerlo cosecharán con la esperanza de su recompensa juvenil.

…Santifica nuestras pruebas

Porque en esperanza fuimos salvos; pero la esperanza que se ve no es esperanza… –Romanos 8:24. Cuántas veces podemos identificarnos con Job en su dolor. Pero antes de que su dolor recibiera siquiera una pizca de retribución, comenzaron a fluir las corrientes sanadoras cuando Job reverenció a su Creador. Cuando reconocemos que Dios es perfecto en todas las pruebas que permite, aprendemos entonces a adorar en el templo no hecho de manos y a no fijarnos en las debilidades del cuerpo. Sentarnos a los pies de Cristo enciende una chispa juvenil que irradia el espíritu interior y hace nacer esperanza. Entonces, el rocío de la juventud pasa a ser nuestra porción, pues Cristo nos imparte vida eterna y juventud eterna. Desde la hora de la tumba y por toda la eternidad seremos jóvenes y desafiaremos el cansancio y la muerte, si vivimos en la luz matutina de Jesucristo. El cielo es un lugar de juventud perpetua y, así como la luz del sol se refleja en la luna, también la luz de Cristo se refleja en su esposa. Ella está limpia y es joven, …una iglesia gloriosa, que no tenga mancha ni arruga ni cosa semejante… –Efesios 5:27. Bienaventurado el santo venerable que llega a las puertas del cielo en tal condición.

Have you ever tried to change the world? I have. As a teenager I dreamed of the daring exploits I was going to do for God. As I set the table in my parent’s house, I waited for the day when I would be able to do greater things—things like setting up house in Africa, speaking strange languages, and leading people to Jesus. The thought of living in a mud hut and dodging venomous snakes seemed thrilling.

And then, part of my dreams came true! I left all I had ever known and had an adrenaline-fueled landing in an African country. I tried to change the small world I was in—that God-forsaken village full of drunkenness, broken marriages, fights, and neglected children. Daily I felt the angst of being so busy with “insignificant,” earthly tasks and wondered how to make a difference. Then suddenly, our labors were abruptly ended by burn-out and a host of government suspicions. None of this was in my dreams.

I still ask the same question, “God, how can I make a difference?” The neighbor calls at the door. The laundry lady needs her pay. Lunch needs to be on the table in 15 minutes. Our fifth grader needs help with multiplying fractions. The sky fills up with dark clouds and the clothesline is full of laundry. I wipe the baby’s nose for the umpteenth time as she sits on top of the table disrupting her brother’s books and papers. I bake bread, make yogurt, and churn butter, and cook 21 meals a week. I fold mountains of laundry and the next week I do it all over again. I sweep the floor that has accumulated an astonishing amount of dirt in only two hours. In many ways, life is more mundane than it ever was before.

I had no ability to change the world as a starry-eyed teen and neither do I have the ability now. God isn’t asking that of me. He only asks me to walk with Him and obey His voice. Slowly I am learning that the spiritual and physical are inseparable—even Jesus taught the gospel of the kingdom while resting, sleeping, and eating. Scrubbing a floor and slicing bread can be acts of worship to my Creator if I will deem them so. It is He who designed that my spiritual walk and the propagation thereof happens as my hands touch the earthly. This is how my spirit is refined. It’s the only way I can express my faith as a living faith. It’s the only way I can touch the hearts of my children and live out a practical gospel for them to imitate. It’s how my faith proves itself to be real to the unbeliever, as they see me struggle through the same things they do, along with my resulting responses.

Slowly I am learning that serving God isn’t about determination or changing the world. It’s about allowing God’s spirit to inhabit me, guide me, and speak to me. I am learning that God is more interested in the person I am becoming instead of everything I want to do for Him. Perhaps I am after all just a smoking flax instead of the one who will change the world. I think Paul could relate to that feeling when he wrote, But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence –1 Corinthians 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot said, “Sometimes the light rises excruciatingly slowly. The Kingdom of God is like leaven and seed, things which work silently, secretly, slowly, but there is in them an incalculable transforming power. Even in the plain soil, even in the dull dough, lies the possibility of transformation.”1

To have my heart set on accomplishments and success is a selfish way to live. When that village and those people were taken from us in a whirl of government issues and misunderstandings, I felt like God couldn’t possibly use this for anyone’s good. He still needed us there, right? The fact is, He didn’t need us there anymore. We were not indispensable. Perhaps God allowed it all in order to learn that His acceptance of me is not based on my accomplishments.

For who hath despised the day of small things… –Zechariah 4:10.

Who am I to judge if a certain work is small or not? Am I restless with my duties, believing God would be more pleased with my perception of ‘great’ duties, seemingly always out of reach? Am I forgetting that serving Christ is not about me and my sense of fulfillment, it is about God and the work He wants to do through me?! Amy Carmichael said, “It is not the place where we are, or the work that we do or cannot do that matters, it is something else. It is the fire within that burns and shines, whatever be our circumstances.”2

The fire that burns and shines within is our secret. That fire can burn while we scrub floors, cook endless meals, and home-school our children. It will touch the laundry lady, the house helper, the struggling girl at church and the neighbors. Sometimes it will happen sub-consciously, sometimes it happens if we decide to reach out instead of taking a nap or something else enjoyable, but always it takes forgetting ourselves, loving others, and noticing the small opportunities.

But beware… we cannot confuse our resignation to the smallness in our lives, with lethargy. Too many Christians do not expect God to use them, so they settle into a lethargic spiritual position. We should expect God to work in amazing ways. God might use us to accomplish those things, but it often happens in ways we least think of or expect.

The widow of Zarephath agreed to give her last handful of flour and the last remaining drops of oil to a stranger. She could have opposed the prophet and demanded he leave immediately, as after all, she was responsible for her son and that little bit of flour was all she had to give him. But no, she chose to give it all. God blessed her willing obedience by miraculously replenishing her flour and oil as long as she needed it.3

God kept culling Gideon’s army until he eventually fought and won the battle with just a few hundred men. Normally, Gideon was accustomed to armies of thousands. and now God was asking him to fight a momentous battle with only a few hundred. In the end, this human impossibility became an opportunity for God to show his power.4

At the beginning of His ministry, Jesus chose only twelve men to disciple, instead of the crowds. In the end, His small band of men deserted Him. He was mocked and killed. To everyone looking on, the remains of Jesus’ work seemed to have died with Him, yet the cosmic plan of redemption was being put into effect—those simple fishermen turned the world upside down with the gospel.5

We see from these examples that God is not looking for the biggest, the strongest, or the best. He doesn’t only use people with specialized skills or impressive gifts. Our strength and resources are often like the few hundred soldiers in Gideon’s army—simply not enough for the need. But when we give what we have with a willing heart, God multiplies our small efforts into a showcase of His grace—a showcase meant for Him, often not visible to others. The simple act of setting a table is an act of faith, of giving, of service, no matter where we are. God has chosen these weak things to be significant in His kingdom.

The secret to a successful life is Jesus in us, not our preconceived ideas of success. With Him working in and through us, His power will burn in our homes and neighborhoods. When He is the reason that we are living, we can trust Him with the outcome. Listening to the voice of Jesus, we can make a difference—one person, one encounter, one small thing at a time.

  1. Elisabeth Elliot, The Savage My Kinsman (revised edition Servant Publications 1981) epilogue pg 147
  2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, pg 218
  3. 1 Kings 17: 11-16
  4. Judges 7
  5. Luke 6:13-16, John 19

Har du noen gang prøvd å forandre verden? Det har jeg. Som tenåring drømte jeg om de dristige bedriftene jeg skulle utføre for Gud. Mens jeg dekket bordet hjemme hos foreldrene mine, ventet jeg på dagen da jeg skulle kunne gjøre større ting – ting som å slå meg ned i Afrika, snakke fremmede språk og lede mennesker til Jesus. Tanken på å bo i en leirhytte og unngå giftige slanger virket spennende.

Og så gikk noen av drømmene mine i oppfyllelse! Jeg forlot alt jeg noen gang hadde kjent, og landet full av adrenalin i et afrikansk land. Jeg prøvde å forandre den lille verdenen jeg befant meg i – den gudsforlatte landsbyen, full av fyll, ødelagte ekteskap, slagsmål og forsømte barn. Hver dag kjente jeg på fortvilelsen over å være så opptatt med «ubetydelige», jordiske oppgaver, og jeg lurte på hvordan jeg kunne utgjøre en forskjell. Så ble arbeidet vårt plutselig brått avsluttet på grunn av utbrenthet og en rekke mistanker fra myndighetene. Ingenting av dette fantes i drømmene mine.

Jeg stiller fortsatt det samme spørsmålet: «Gud, hvordan kan jeg utgjøre en forskjell?» Naboen ringer på døren. Kvinnen som vasker klærne våre, skal ha lønnen sin. Lunsjen må stå på bordet om 15 minutter. Femteklassingen vår trenger hjelp med å multiplisere brøker. Himmelen fylles av mørke skyer, og klessnoren er full av klesvask. Jeg tørker babyen på nesen for tusende gang mens hun sitter oppå bordet og roter i brorens bøker og papirer. Jeg baker brød, lager yoghurt og kjerner smør, og lager 21 måltider i uken. Jeg bretter fjell av klesvask, og uken etter gjør jeg alt sammen om igjen. Jeg feier gulvet, som på bare to timer har samlet en forbløffende mengde skitt. På mange måter er livet mer hverdagslig enn det noen gang har vært før.

Jeg hadde ingen evne til å forandre verden som en drømmende tenåring, og det har jeg heller ikke nå. Gud ber meg ikke om det. Han ber meg bare om å vandre med ham og adlyde hans stemme. Sakte lærer jeg at det åndelige og det fysiske ikke kan skilles fra hverandre – selv Jesus forkynte evangeliet om riket mens han hvilte, sov og spiste. Å skrubbe et gulv og skjære brød kan være tilbedelseshandlinger for Skaperen min, hvis jeg velger å se på dem slik. Det er han som har bestemt at min åndelige vandring og utbredelsen av den skjer når hendene mine berører det jordiske. Slik blir ånden min foredlet. Det er den eneste måten jeg kan uttrykke troen min som en levende tro på. Det er den eneste måten jeg kan nå hjertene til barna mine og leve ut et praktisk evangelium som de kan etterligne. Slik viser troen min seg å være ekte for den som ikke tror, når de ser at jeg strever med de samme tingene som de gjør, og ser hvordan jeg reagerer på dem.

Sakte lærer jeg at det å tjene Gud ikke handler om besluttsomhet eller om å forandre verden. Det handler om å la Guds Ånd bo i meg, lede meg og tale til meg. Jeg lærer at Gud er mer opptatt av den personen jeg er i ferd med å bli, enn av alt jeg ønsker å gjøre for ham. Kanskje er jeg tross alt bare en rykende veke, og ikke den som skal forandre verden. Jeg tror Paulus kunne kjenne seg igjen i den følelsen da han skrev: Men Gud har utvalgt det som er tåpelig i verden, for å gjøre de vise til skamme. Gud har utvalgt det som er svakt i verden, for å gjøre det sterke til skamme. Det som er lavt i verden, det som blir foraktet, ja, det som ikke er noe, har Gud utvalgt for å gjøre til intet det som er noe, for at ingen mennesker skal rose seg overfor Gud –1. Korinter 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot sa: «Noen ganger stiger lyset opp uutholdelig langsomt. Guds rike er som surdeig og frø, ting som virker stille, i det skjulte og langsomt, men som rommer en uoverskuelig forvandlende kraft. Selv i den enkle jorden, selv i den tunge deigen, ligger muligheten for forvandling.»1

Å være opptatt av prestasjoner og suksess er en egoistisk måte å leve på. Da den landsbyen og menneskene der ble tatt fra oss i en virvelvind av saker med myndighetene og misforståelser, følte jeg at Gud umulig kunne bruke dette til beste for noen. Han trengte oss vel fortsatt der? Sannheten er at han ikke trengte oss der lenger. Vi var ikke uunnværlige. Kanskje lot Gud alt dette skje for at jeg skulle lære at hans aksept av meg ikke er basert på prestasjonene mine.

For hvem har foraktet den dagen da det begynte i det små … –Sakarja 4:10.

Hvem er jeg som skal avgjøre om en bestemt oppgave er liten eller ikke? Er jeg rastløs med pliktene mine fordi jeg tror Gud ville vært mer fornøyd hvis jeg utførte oppgaver jeg oppfatter som «store», som tilsynelatende alltid er utenfor rekkevidde? Glemmer jeg at det å tjene Kristus ikke handler om meg og min følelse av å være tilfreds, men om Gud og det arbeidet han vil gjøre gjennom meg?! Amy Carmichael sa: «Det er ikke stedet vi er på, eller arbeidet vi gjør eller ikke kan gjøre, som betyr noe; det er noe annet. Det er ilden på innsiden som brenner og skinner, uansett hvilke omstendigheter vi befinner oss i.»2

Ilden som brenner og skinner på innsiden, er hemmeligheten vår. Den ilden kan brenne mens vi skrubber gulv, lager utallige måltider og underviser barna våre hjemme. Den vil berøre kvinnen som vasker klærne, hushjelpen, jenta i menigheten som strever, og naboene. Noen ganger skjer det ubevisst, andre ganger skjer det når vi bestemmer oss for å rekke ut en hånd i stedet for å ta en lur eller gjøre noe annet vi liker, men alltid krever det at vi glemmer oss selv, elsker andre og legger merke til de små mulighetene.

Men pass på … vi må ikke forveksle det å godta at livet vårt er preget av små ting, med sløvhet. Altfor mange kristne forventer ikke at Gud skal bruke dem, og slår seg derfor til ro i en åndelig sløvhet. Vi bør forvente at Gud virker på fantastiske måter. Gud kan bruke oss til å utrette slike ting, men det skjer ofte på måter vi minst tenker på eller venter oss.

Enken i Sarepta gikk med på å gi den siste håndfullen mel og de siste dråpene med olje hun hadde, til en fremmed. Hun kunne ha satt seg opp mot profeten og krevd at han straks skulle gå, for hun hadde tross alt ansvaret for sønnen sin, og den lille mengden mel var alt hun hadde å gi ham. Men nei, hun valgte å gi alt. Gud velsignet hennes villige lydighet ved på mirakuløst vis å fylle opp melkrukken og oljekruset så lenge hun trengte det.3

Gud fortsatte å redusere Gideons hær helt til han til slutt kjempet og vant slaget med bare noen få hundre menn. Vanligvis var Gideon vant til hærer på flere tusen. og nå ba Gud ham kjempe et avgjørende slag med bare noen få hundre. Til slutt ble det som var umulig for mennesker, en anledning for Gud til å vise sin makt.4

Da Jesus begynte sin tjeneste, valgte han bare tolv menn som disipler, i stedet for folkemengdene. Til slutt forlot den lille gruppen menn ham. Han ble hånet og drept. For alle som så på, virket det som om resten av Jesu verk døde med ham, men den kosmiske frelsesplanen var i ferd med å bli satt ut i livet – disse enkle fiskerne snudde verden på hodet med evangeliet.5

Av disse eksemplene ser vi at Gud ikke leter etter de største, sterkeste eller beste. Han bruker ikke bare mennesker med spesialiserte ferdigheter eller imponerende gaver. Styrken og ressursene våre er ofte som de få hundre soldatene i Gideons hær – rett og slett ikke nok til å dekke behovet. Men når vi gir det vi har med et villig hjerte, mangfoldiggjør Gud de små anstrengelsene våre og gjør dem til et utstillingsvindu for sin nåde – et utstillingsvindu som er ment for ham, og som ofte ikke er synlig for andre. Den enkle handlingen å dekke et bord er en handling i tro, en handling der vi gir og tjener, uansett hvor vi er. Gud har valgt disse svake tingene til å ha betydning i riket sitt.

Hemmeligheten bak et vellykket liv er Jesus i oss, ikke våre forutinntatte forestillinger om suksess. Når han virker i og gjennom oss, vil hans kraft brenne i hjemmene og nabolagene våre. Når han er grunnen til at vi lever, kan vi stole på ham med utfallet. Når vi lytter til Jesu stemme, kan vi utgjøre en forskjell – én person, ett møte, én liten ting om gangen.

Do you want to have a good life? What is there that you believe you need to experience or accomplish so you can truly enjoy life? Many people’s main goal in life is to seek pleasure and to have fun. Much time and money are spent to achieve this. But do we accomplish it? In our natural mind we think that the circumstances need to be just right to please us. But we all know that circumstances are never ideal all the time. So, we can’t depend on those for our happiness. We need something bigger than that. Or Someone.

Obviously, we know that God alone is never changing and always faithful. Another thing about God is that He is sovereign. In other words, He’s in charge. But we like our independence; we like things to happen in a way that feels good to us. When life doesn’t happen that way, we are brought to a decision. Will we accept all of God—both His unchangeableness and His sovereignty—or will we fight to have our own way in our pursuit of a good life?

The root of joy is with God Himself. This is because He created us for Himself. He created us to bring pleasure to Himself, but we think we need to bring pleasure to ourselves. It started in the garden of Eden when the serpent convinced Eve that pleasing herself was more important than pleasing God. Since then, humans have been at war, both within their own hearts and without, with other folks. All in the effort of trying to find pleasure for themselves, yet not finding it because they were created to please God.

The solution for this war is found in James 4. It’s simple: submit to God. Humble yourselves before Him. This is not too much for Him to ask of us, because He is sovereign. He created us, so He has the say in how we live. If we will truly find enjoyment in life, it will be by putting our own life and desires on the cross and becoming one with God and His original purpose for us. Rather than it being restrictive, this opens up a world of opportunities and possibilities. It doesn’t mean we have to do things because God wants us to. Becoming one with God means that what He wants us to do is also what we want to do.

Worship and Gratitude

When we are one with God, our whole perspective changes. Instead of pining over all the things that aren’t ideal, we begin to see the many things that are true blessings. We can have a heart of worship and gratitude for all the good things that we do experience. We are able to see how unworthy we really are. We didn’t deserve anything good, but God has still given us so many things to enjoy!

Living in the Present

As young ladies, we have a tendency to dream, to live in a future that is idealistic and pleasant. We sometimes struggle to live in the present imperfect reality and find joy in it. But when God’s will becomes our will then true joy happens, because we are fulfilling His purpose for us.

We can learn to experience joy in any circumstance, even in mundane life. We’re afraid of living a boring life. We want it to be exciting. But He wants us to please Him, and when we do, we experience joy no matter the circumstances. However, we are also then available for Him to use in service to His Kingdom, and He may call us to opportunities that are exciting. But we won’t be effective in the exciting missions unless we have learned to be submitted to His will in everyday life.

Relationships

When we are finding joy and contentment in where God has us in the present, we are able to focus on developing solid, upbuilding relationships with those who are in our lives right now. God has created us as social people, and good relationships will bring true enjoyment to us. God is also able to use us in reaching out to other people. When we are one with Him, our focus is no longer on ourselves but on others. The life of God can flow through us and both show others the way to Him and give us joy and fulfillment in doing it.

Emotions

Another tendency we have is to let our emotions control us. And they will run wild if we are looking to our circumstances to give us pleasure. We will end up on a roller coaster of feelings dictated by whatever is happening at the moment. And then we escape to the dream world, which only distorts our view of reality even more. But God is steadfast, and when we are one with Him, He imparts to us stability and rest. And we are able to experience ever present joy—even in ever changing circumstances.

Let us continue to become ever more one with Him. And He will give us heavenly sunlight all of our journey, unchanged by circumstances on earth and realized in full when we see Him face to face. …in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore –Psalm 16:11.

Möchtest du ein gutes Leben führen? Was glaubst du, musst du erleben oder erreichen, damit du das Leben wirklich genießen kannst? Für viele Menschen ist das wichtigste Ziel im Leben, Vergnügen zu suchen und Spaß zu haben. Dafür werden viel Zeit und Geld aufgewendet. Aber gelingt uns das? Von Natur aus denken wir, dass die Umstände genau richtig sein müssen, damit wir zufrieden sind. Doch wir alle wissen, dass die Umstände nie ständig ideal sind. Deshalb können wir unser Glück nicht von ihnen abhängig machen. Wir brauchen etwas Größeres als das. Oder jemanden.

Natürlich wissen wir, dass Gott allein sich niemals verändert und immer treu ist. Eine weitere Eigenschaft Gottes ist, dass er souverän ist. Mit anderen Worten: Er hat das Sagen. Doch wir mögen unsere Unabhängigkeit; wir mögen es, wenn die Dinge so geschehen, dass es sich für uns gut anfühlt. Wenn das Leben nicht so verläuft, stehen wir vor einer Entscheidung. Werden wir Gott ganz annehmen – sowohl seine Unveränderlichkeit als auch seine Souveränität – oder werden wir darum kämpfen, unseren eigenen Willen durchzusetzen, während wir ein gutes Leben anstreben?

Die Quelle der Freude liegt bei Gott selbst. Denn er hat uns für sich geschaffen. Er hat uns geschaffen, damit wir ihm Freude bereiten; doch wir meinen, wir müssten uns selbst Freude bereiten. Es begann im Garten Eden, als die Schlange Eva davon überzeugte, dass es wichtiger sei, sich selbst zu gefallen, als Gott zu gefallen. Seitdem befinden sich die Menschen im Krieg – sowohl in ihrem eigenen Herzen als auch nach außen hin mit anderen. All das in dem Bemühen, für sich selbst Vergnügen zu finden, und doch finden sie es nicht, weil sie geschaffen wurden, um Gott zu gefallen.

Die Lösung für diesen Krieg findet sich in Jakobus 4. Sie ist einfach: Unterwerft euch Gott. Demütigt euch vor ihm. Das ist nicht zu viel von ihm verlangt, denn er ist souverän. Er hat uns geschaffen, also bestimmt er, wie wir leben. Wenn wir wirklich Freude am Leben finden wollen, dann dadurch, dass wir unser eigenes Leben und unsere Wünsche ans Kreuz bringen und eins werden mit Gott und seinem ursprünglichen Zweck für uns. Statt uns einzuengen, eröffnet uns das eine Welt voller Chancen und Möglichkeiten. Das bedeutet nicht, dass wir Dinge tun müssen, weil Gott es von uns will. Eins mit Gott zu werden bedeutet, dass wir ebenfalls tun wollen, was er von uns möchte.

Anbetung und Dankbarkeit

Wenn wir eins mit Gott sind, verändert sich unsere gesamte Sichtweise. Statt all den Dingen nachzutrauern, die nicht ideal sind, beginnen wir, die vielen Dinge als wahre Segnungen zu erkennen. Wir können ein Herz voller Anbetung und Dankbarkeit für all das Gute haben, das wir tatsächlich erleben. Wir können erkennen, wie unwürdig wir wirklich sind. Wir haben nichts Gutes verdient, und doch hat Gott uns so viele Dinge geschenkt, an denen wir uns erfreuen können!

In der Gegenwart leben

Als junge Frauen neigen wir dazu, zu träumen und in einer idealistischen, angenehmen Zukunft zu leben. Manchmal fällt es uns schwer, in der unvollkommenen Wirklichkeit der Gegenwart zu leben und Freude darin zu finden. Doch wenn Gottes Wille zu unserem Willen wird, entsteht wahre Freude, denn dann erfüllen wir seinen Zweck für uns.

Wir können lernen, unter allen Umständen Freude zu erleben, sogar im eintönigen Alltag. Wir haben Angst vor einem langweiligen Leben. Wir wollen, dass es aufregend ist. Doch er möchte, dass wir ihm gefallen, und wenn wir das tun, erleben wir Freude, unabhängig von den Umständen. Zugleich stehen wir ihm dann zur Verfügung, damit er uns in seinem Reich dienen lassen kann, und vielleicht ruft er uns zu aufregenden Möglichkeiten. Doch bei aufregenden Aufgaben werden wir nicht wirksam sein, wenn wir nicht gelernt haben, uns im Alltag seinem Willen unterzuordnen.

Beziehungen

Wenn wir Freude und Zufriedenheit darin finden, wo Gott uns in der Gegenwart hingestellt hat, können wir uns darauf konzentrieren, feste, aufbauende Beziehungen zu den Menschen zu entwickeln, die jetzt in unserem Leben sind. Gott hat uns als soziale Wesen geschaffen, und gute Beziehungen bereiten uns wahre Freude. Gott kann uns auch gebrauchen, um auf andere Menschen zuzugehen. Wenn wir eins mit ihm sind, richten wir unseren Blick nicht länger auf uns selbst, sondern auf andere. Gottes Leben kann durch uns hindurchfließen, anderen den Weg zu ihm zeigen und uns zugleich Freude und Erfüllung darin schenken.

Gefühle

Eine weitere Neigung von uns ist, uns von unseren Gefühlen beherrschen zu lassen. Und sie geraten außer Kontrolle, wenn wir von den Umständen erwarten, dass sie uns Freude bereiten. Am Ende fahren unsere Gefühle Achterbahn und werden von allem bestimmt, was gerade geschieht. Dann flüchten wir uns in eine Traumwelt, die unseren Blick auf die Wirklichkeit nur noch mehr verzerrt. Doch Gott ist beständig, und wenn wir eins mit ihm sind, schenkt er uns Stabilität und Ruhe. So können wir beständige Freude erleben – selbst in ständig wechselnden Umständen.

Lasst uns immer mehr eins mit ihm werden. Und er wird uns auf unserem ganzen Weg himmlisches Sonnenlicht schenken, unberührt von den Umständen auf Erden und in seiner Fülle erfahrbar, wenn wir ihm von Angesicht zu Angesicht begegnen. …vor dir ist Freude die Fülle; Wonne zu deiner Rechten immerdar –Psalm 16,11.

Greetings of Christian love to each one. Another year has passed us by, and another is spread out before us to navigate. What is our perspective? Do we have hope and joy bubbling up in our hearts or does the future seem full of gloom and doom? Do we see God’s sovereign hand at work in the situations and circumstances around us or does the world seem out of control from our vantage point?

As I interact with folks from around the country there seems to be a common issue that many folks are struggling with—weariness. Weary of mandates. Weary of shutdowns. Weary of all the bickering and fighting that has surrounded the Covid issue. Weary of…

It appears that many people just “Don’t want to think about it”. Why? I’m really not sure what all the reasons are, but I am sure that each person has one. Let’s remember that God wants us to …be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves –Matthew 10:16.

Here, in the United States of America, Christians have had over 60 years (since World War 2) of relative peace and tranquility. For the most part, we have been left alone to raise our families and worship the God of our fathers according to our conscience. We have enjoyed the separation of Church and State that was implemented at the beginning of our country’s existence. We have been able to work with our hands and earn a living. Many of us have lived off the fat of the land.

Maybe we were living in an artificial bubble. Maybe we have been lulled into a false sense of security. What about our counterparts in countries around the world, what is their reality of living as true Christians in their world? Sure, we have been able to use our wealth and freedom of movement to do much good for the rest of the world who have endured much hardship due to following Christ. But at what cost? What have our children learned?

Sometimes, we hear about first generation Christians being “on fire” for their Lord. Sometimes so much so that second and third generation Christians think that first generation Christians are perhaps a little too zealous in their efforts of evangelizing those around them.

What about the next generation? They are learning from someone—about God, themselves, and life. What are they learning? And who are they learning from? We must take stock to ensure that our children are learning life’s lessons in a way that they will be prepared to face the reality of things to come.

And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world? And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many –Matthew 24:3-5.

Remember that this is Jesus Himself speaking to His followers regarding the end of the world. His very first concern is that we would NOT be deceived. He says that deception will be the major issue surrounding the end of time. He says that many will come claiming to be Christ [or His direct spokesperson] in an attempt to gain a listening ear, all in an effort to deceive the hearer and gain a following.

If not before now, we most certainly must be teaching our children certain specific things through word and action. That we are to be strangers and pilgrims as we journey through this life. That if we are friends of this world then God will be our enemy. And that Jesus’ Kingdom is not of this world, therefore, His children must learn to live as ambassadors in a foreign land. Our children need to know that ALL who live godly in Christ Jesus WILL suffer persecution.

Many of the doctrines that have been taught in our churches and para-church functions have severely crippled the next generation of the church. We have been taught that we can have the “power of His resurrection” without needing to be a partaker of the “fellowship of His sufferings”. A suffering Christ with suffering followers has been thrown out in favor of following a Jesus who will not let anything bad happen to you. While there is much emphasis on a Jesus who suffered and died for you, there is very little to NO teaching on the need to “take up your cross daily” and follow Him.

Mental Health and Emotional Stability

Some years ago, I came across the story of a soldier, who, after serving a term of service in Iraq, was struggling to cope with PTSD. Sure, I believe that PTSD is real, and the struggles are real, but as I read this man’s story, I found myself becoming increasingly frustrated with the lack of answers that were being provided to a severely struggling young man. Some of his deepest struggles stemmed from the flashback memories he had of when he had personally killed several of the enemy. No matter how many counseling sessions he went to he just couldn’t come to a place of inner peace and rest. His mind was troubled. He had difficulty sleeping. He had problems getting along with others.

I had to think “If only someone could come alongside this young man and share the Gospel of Jesus Christ with him. If only he could be shown the Truth of God’s Word that to take another human’s life is sin in God’s eyes (even if he is the enemy) and God will not allow him to have peace in his heart until that is taken care of. Also, that the real excitement is that IF he would come to God according to the terms of the Bible and repent of his sin, then he could start walking with God and God could start giving him peace for his troubled soul.”

Over the last number of years, there have been numerous mass shootings here in the United States. Each time the public officials hold news conferences and share their thoughts in an effort to try to make sense out of another seemingly unexplainable tragic event. Usually, it’s not long until someone is talking about mental health and the need to step up public efforts to provide safety nets, screenings, and better and more treatments to curb this senseless violence.

Several weeks ago, there was a terrible, tragic event that took place in another state from where I live. In one of the big cities, a man pushed a woman off of the platform and into the path of an oncoming subway train. She didn’t survive. In the aftermath of such a horrific happening, the public officials made statements to the public in an effort to stem the potential public fear. They concluded that the man must have been emotionally troubled and that they would be stepping up their efforts in trying to provide a safety net for those with mental health issues, so that such things wouldn’t happen again.

Sure, when we look at the issue through the eyes of the world it seems to make sense. But is this the whole of the matter? Have we as Christians become so used to the ways of the world that we forget how far they have strayed from the Truth of God’s Word?

Let’s not point our finger at the world and the elected public officials. Are we, as the church, any better? How well do we know our Bible? How well do we know our Savior? When someone comes to us seeking peace and rest within do we know how to take them to the Scriptures, and lead them to Jesus who can then show them the way to the Father?

Why am I saying all this? If we continue to provide the next generation of the church with artificial answers and temporary solutions to the problems of life, then they will NOT be prepared to …endure unto the end… –Matthew 24:13.

And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24.

تحيات المحبة المسيحية لكل واحد منكم. لقد مضى عام آخر، وها هو عام آخر يمتد أمامنا لنسير فيه. ما هي نظرتنا؟ هل يتفجر الرجاء والفرح في قلوبنا، أم يبدو المستقبل مليئًا بالكآبة والشؤم؟ هل نرى يد الله صاحبة السيادة تعمل في المواقف والظروف المحيطة بنا، أم يبدو العالم خارجًا عن السيطرة من منظورنا؟

في تفاعلي مع الناس من مختلف أنحاء البلاد، يبدو أن هناك أمرًا مشتركًا يعاني منه كثيرون: الإرهاق. الإرهاق من الأوامر الإلزامية. الإرهاق من الإغلاقات. الإرهاق من كل المشاحنات والخصام التي أحاطت بمسألة كوفيد. الإرهاق من…

يبدو أن كثيرين لا يريدون ببساطة «التفكير في الأمر». لماذا؟ لست متأكدًا حقًا من جميع الأسباب، لكنني متأكد من أن لكل شخص سببًا. لنتذكر أن الله يريدنا أن …نكون حكماء كالحيات وبسطاء كالحمام –متى 10:16.

هنا، في الولايات المتحدة الأمريكية، نَعِم المسيحيون بأكثر من 60 عامًا (منذ الحرب العالمية الثانية) من السلام والهدوء النسبيين. وفي الغالب، تُركنا وشأننا لنربي عائلاتنا ونعبد إله آبائنا بحسب ضمائرنا. وتمتعنا بفصل الكنيسة عن الدولة، الذي أُقرّ في بداية وجود بلدنا. وتمكنا من العمل بأيدينا وكسب عيشنا. وقد عاش كثيرون منا في وفرة من خيرات الأرض.

ربما كنا نعيش في فقاعة مصطنعة. وربما خُدّرنا بشعور زائف بالأمان. وماذا عن نظرائنا في بلدان العالم، ما حقيقة عيشهم كمسيحيين حقيقيين في عالمهم؟ صحيح أننا تمكنا من استخدام ثروتنا وحرية تنقلنا لفعل الكثير من الخير لبقية العالم، ممن قاسوا مشقات كثيرة بسبب اتباع المسيح. لكن بأي ثمن؟ ماذا تعلم أولادنا؟

نسمع أحيانًا عن مسيحيين من الجيل الأول بأنهم «متقدون حماسة» لربهم. وأحيانًا إلى حد أن مسيحيي الجيلين الثاني والثالث يظنون أن مسيحيي الجيل الأول ربما يبالغون قليلًا في حماستهم إلى تبشير من حولهم.

وماذا عن الجيل القادم؟ إنهم يتعلمون من شخص ما عن الله وعن أنفسهم وعن الحياة. ماذا يتعلمون؟ وممّن يتعلمون؟ علينا أن نقيّم الأمور لنتأكد من أن أولادنا يتعلمون دروس الحياة بطريقة تهيئهم لمواجهة حقيقة الأمور الآتية.

وفيما هو جالس على جبل الزيتون، تقدم إليه التلاميذ على انفراد قائلين: قل لنا، متى يكون هذا؟ وما علامة مجيئك وانقضاء العالم؟ فأجاب يسوع وقال لهم: انظروا، لا يضلكم أحد. فإن كثيرين سيأتون باسمي قائلين: أنا هو المسيح، ويضلون كثيرين –متى 24:3-5.

تذكروا أن يسوع نفسه هو الذي يتحدث هنا إلى أتباعه عن نهاية العالم. وأول ما يشغله هو ألا نُضلَّ. يقول إن الضلال سيكون القضية الرئيسية المحيطة بنهاية الزمان. ويقول إن كثيرين سيأتون مدّعين أنهم المسيح [أو الناطقون باسمه مباشرة] في محاولة لاستمالة من يصغي إليهم، وكل ذلك بقصد تضليل السامع وكسب أتباع.

إن لم نكن قد فعلنا ذلك من قبل، فعلينا بالتأكيد الآن أن نعلّم أولادنا أمورًا محددة، قولًا وفعلًا. علينا أن نكون غرباء ونزلاء ونحن نجتاز هذه الحياة. وإذا كنا أصدقاء هذا العالم، فسيكون الله عدونا. ومملكة يسوع ليست من هذا العالم، ولذلك يجب أن يتعلم أولاده العيش كسفراء في أرض غريبة. وينبغي أن يعرف أولادنا أن جميع الذين يعيشون بالتقوى في المسيح يسوع سيتعرضون للاضطهاد.

لقد أعاقت تعاليم كثيرة دُرّست في كنائسنا وفي أنشطة المؤسسات المرتبطة بالكنائس، الجيل القادم من الكنيسة إعاقة شديدة. فقد عُلّمنا أنه يمكننا نوال «قوة قيامته» من دون أن نحتاج إلى الاشتراك في «شركة آلامه». وأُقصي المسيح المتألم وأتباعه المتألمون، واستُبدل باتباع يسوع الذي لن يدع أي شيء سيئ يحدث لك. وبينما يُشدَّد كثيرًا على يسوع الذي تألم ومات من أجلك، لا يوجد إلا القليل جدًا، بل لا يوجد أي تعليم، عن ضرورة أن «يحمل كل يوم صليبه» ويتبعه.

الصحة النفسية والاستقرار العاطفي

قبل سنوات، صادفت قصة جندي كان يعاني، بعد أن خدم فترة في العراق، من صعوبة التعايش مع اضطراب ما بعد الصدمة. صحيح أنني أؤمن بأن اضطراب ما بعد الصدمة حقيقي، وأن المعاناة حقيقية، لكنني كلما قرأت قصة هذا الرجل، وجدت نفسي أشعر بإحباط متزايد إزاء غياب الإجابات التي كانت تُقدَّم لشاب يعاني معاناة شديدة. وكانت بعض أعمق معاناته تنبع من ذكريات ومضات الماضي التي تعود إليه عن قتله بنفسه عددًا من الأعداء. ومهما بلغ عدد جلسات الإرشاد التي حضرها، لم يستطع أن يبلغ مكانًا من السلام الداخلي والراحة. كان ذهنه مضطربًا. وكان يجد صعوبة في النوم. وكانت لديه مشكلات في التفاهم مع الآخرين.

كان عليّ أن أفكر: «ليت أحدًا يستطيع أن يقف إلى جانب هذا الشاب ويشاركه إنجيل يسوع المسيح. ليت أحدًا يستطيع أن يريه حق كلمة الله، وهو أن قتل حياة إنسان آخر خطية في عيني الله (حتى لو كان عدوًا)، وأن الله لن يسمح له بأن ينعم بالسلام في قلبه إلى أن تُسوّى هذه المسألة. والأمر المثير حقًا هو أنه إن أتى إلى الله بحسب شروط الكتاب المقدس وتاب عن خطيته، فسيستطيع أن يبدأ السير مع الله، ويستطيع الله أن يبدأ بمنحه السلام لنفسه المضطربة».

على مدى السنوات الماضية، وقعت حوادث إطلاق نار جماعي عديدة هنا في الولايات المتحدة. وفي كل مرة، يعقد المسؤولون العموميون مؤتمرات صحفية ويعرضون آراءهم في محاولة لفهم حدث مأساوي آخر يبدو غير قابل للتفسير. وعادة لا يطول الأمر قبل أن يتحدث أحدهم عن الصحة النفسية وعن ضرورة تكثيف الجهود العامة لتوفير شبكات أمان وفحوصات وعلاجات أفضل وأكثر، للحد من هذا العنف العبثي.

قبل أسابيع عدة، وقعت حادثة مروعة ومأساوية في ولاية أخرى غير الولاية التي أعيش فيها. ففي إحدى المدن الكبرى، دفع رجل امرأة من الرصيف إلى مسار قطار أنفاق قادم. ولم تنجُ. وفي أعقاب حادثة مروعة كهذه، أدلى المسؤولون العموميون بتصريحات للجمهور في محاولة لاحتواء الخوف المحتمل لدى العامة. وخلصوا إلى أن الرجل لا بد أنه كان مضطربًا عاطفيًا، وأنهم سيكثفون جهودهم لمحاولة توفير شبكة أمان لمن يعانون مشكلات في الصحة النفسية، كيلا تتكرر مثل هذه الأمور.

صحيح أنه حين ننظر إلى المسألة بعين العالم، يبدو الأمر منطقيًا. لكن أهذه هي المسألة كلها؟ هل اعتدنا نحن المسيحيين أساليب العالم إلى حد أننا نسينا كم ابتعدوا عن حق كلمة الله؟

دعونا لا نوجه أصابع الاتهام إلى العالم والمسؤولين العموميين المنتخبين. هل نحن، ككنيسة، أفضل حالًا؟ ما مدى معرفتنا بكتابنا المقدس؟ وما مدى معرفتنا بمخلصنا؟ حين يأتي إلينا أحدهم طالبًا السلام والراحة في داخله، هل نعرف كيف نوجهه إلى الكتب المقدسة ونقوده إلى يسوع، الذي يستطيع عندئذ أن يريه الطريق إلى الآب؟

لماذا أقول كل هذا؟ إذا واصلنا تزويد الجيل القادم من الكنيسة بإجابات مصطنعة وحلول مؤقتة لمشكلات الحياة، فلن يكونوا مستعدين …للصبر إلى المنتهى… –متى 24:13.

وقال للجميع: إن أراد أحد أن يأتي ورائي، فلينكر نفسه ويحمل صليبه كل يوم ويتبعني. فإن من أراد أن يخلّص حياته يخسرها، ومن خسر حياته من أجلي فهذا يخلّصها –لوقا 9:23-24.
