The grinding sound of truck tires driving in the gravel lane filled the air as I sat in the house reading an encyclopedia. Leaping to my feet, I peered out the window.

Mom had just returned from the produce auction in Lewisburg with some peaches.

Slamming the door behind me, I raced across the thick green grass and leaped onto the bed of our truck.

On the back of the pickup sat four boxes of peaches. Grinning triumphantly, I reached into a box searching until I found a ripe one. Just before I bit into it, Mom said, “Steven, don’t eat any peaches; it will ruin your supper.” Sadly, I tossed the peach back into the box and then slowly walked away.

Several hours later, Dad called from the veal barn. “Steven, go pick the radishes for our Friday market produce stand.”

After picking, washing, and banding the radishes, I carried them into the old cooler which was inside the red bank barn. The cooler door squeaked as I yanked it open. There along the cooler walls sat the four boxes of the tantalizing peaches. I stared at the peaches, my mouth watering. I quickly set the radishes down. Oh, how good they looked. Surely a little peach wouldn’t ruin a starving ten-year-old’s supper. Mom wouldn’t know if I only took one peach.

Deep in my heart, a battle between right and wrong started to develop. I knew that sneaking was wrong, but those peaches looked way too good.

After devouring the peach, I scanned the dark interior of the barn for a good hiding place to put the peach stone. I looked across the onions, laying on drying racks, to the open hay bale. The only problem was that if I put the stone under the hay someone could find it. Then I spied the holes in the barn siding boards on the west side of the barn. If I pushed the stone through one of those holes it would land beside the road. Then, if someone saw it, they would think that it came from a passing vehicle.

I jammed the stone through the hole, peering out as it fell beside the road. At that split second, I felt a searing pain on my forehead. Frantically, I sprang back. There above the hole hung a yellow jacket nest. Then I saw the culprit as it hovered over me trying to sting me again. I sprinted out the barn door, slamming the door into the yellow jacket’s face.

That evening my forehead swelled like a balloon, making it difficult to look out of my eyes.

A few hours later, everyone else went to bed. I laid on the couch so that Mom could occasionally check up on me during the night. But I just couldn’t fall asleep. My face was inflamed and itchy, but all that I could think about was the guilt and remorse of what I had done.

After several agonizing hours, I gathered the courage to slide off the couch and tiptoed over to my parent’s bedroom. Awakening my parents, I told them the whole story… how I ate the peach, then tried to hide the stone, and how I had gotten stung.

My parents forgave me, deciding that this was one lesson that I wouldn’t soon forget. Walking back to the couch with a light heart, I laid down, and quickly fell into a peaceful sleep.

Suara deru ban truk yang melaju di jalan berkerikil memenuhi udara saat aku duduk di rumah membaca ensiklopedia. Aku segera berdiri dan mengintip ke luar jendela.

Ibu baru saja pulang dari lelang hasil bumi di Lewisburg membawa beberapa buah persik.

Setelah membanting pintu di belakangku, aku berlari menyeberangi rumput hijau yang lebat dan melompat ke bak truk kami.

Di bagian belakang truk pikap itu ada empat kotak berisi buah persik. Sambil menyeringai penuh kemenangan, aku merogoh sebuah kotak, mencari-cari sampai menemukan buah yang matang. Tepat sebelum aku menggigitnya, Ibu berkata, “Steven, jangan makan buah persik; nanti makan malammu jadi tidak enak.” Dengan sedih, aku melemparkan kembali buah persik itu ke dalam kotak, lalu berjalan pergi perlahan-lahan.

Beberapa jam kemudian, Ayah memanggil dari kandang anak sapi. “Steven, pergilah memetik lobak untuk lapak hasil bumi kita di pasar hari Jumat.”

Setelah memetik, mencuci, dan mengikat lobak-lobak itu, aku membawanya ke dalam ruang pendingin tua yang berada di dalam lumbung merah. Pintu ruang pendingin itu berderit saat kutarik hingga terbuka. Di sepanjang dinding ruang pendingin itu terletak empat kotak berisi buah persik yang menggoda. Aku menatap buah-buah persik itu, dan air liurku menetes. Aku cepat-cepat meletakkan lobak-lobak itu. Aduh, tampaknya lezat sekali. Tentunya sedikit saja buah persik tidak akan merusak makan malam anak berusia sepuluh tahun yang kelaparan. Ibu tak akan tahu kalau aku hanya mengambil satu buah persik.

Jauh di lubuk hatiku, pergulatan antara benar dan salah mulai berkecamuk. Aku tahu bahwa menyelinap itu salah, tetapi buah-buah persik itu tampak terlalu lezat.

Setelah melahap buah persik itu, aku mengamati bagian dalam lumbung yang gelap untuk mencari tempat persembunyian yang bagus bagi bijinya. Aku memandang ke seberang bawang-bawang yang terhampar di rak pengering menuju bal jerami yang terbuka. Masalahnya, kalau kutaruh biji itu di bawah jerami, seseorang bisa menemukannya. Lalu aku melihat lubang-lubang pada papan dinding lumbung di sisi barat. Kalau kudorong biji itu melewati salah satu lubang tersebut, biji itu akan jatuh di pinggir jalan. Jadi, kalau ada yang melihatnya, mereka akan mengira biji itu berasal dari kendaraan yang lewat.

Dengan sekuat tenaga kudorong biji itu melewati lubang, sambil mengintip saat biji itu jatuh di pinggir jalan. Tepat pada saat itu, dahiku terasa nyeri terbakar. Aku segera melompat mundur. Di atas lubang itu tergantung sarang tawon jaket kuning. Lalu kulihat pelakunya, yang melayang-layang di atasku dan berusaha menyengatku lagi. Aku berlari secepatnya keluar dari pintu lumbung, membanting pintu hingga mengenai wajah tawon jaket kuning itu.

Malam itu dahiku membengkak seperti balon, sehingga sulit bagiku untuk melihat dengan jelas.

Beberapa jam kemudian, semua orang pergi tidur. Aku berbaring di sofa agar Ibu bisa sesekali memeriksaku sepanjang malam. Tetapi aku benar-benar tidak bisa tidur. Wajahku meradang dan gatal, tetapi yang terus kupikirkan hanyalah rasa bersalah dan penyesalan atas perbuatanku.

Setelah beberapa jam yang terasa menyiksa, aku mengumpulkan keberanian untuk turun dari sofa dan berjalan berjingkat-jingkat ke kamar tidur orang tuaku. Aku membangunkan orang tuaku dan menceritakan seluruhnya… bagaimana aku memakan buah persik itu, lalu mencoba menyembunyikan bijinya, dan bagaimana aku tersengat.

Orang tuaku memaafkanku dan memutuskan bahwa ini adalah pelajaran yang tak akan segera kulupakan. Dengan hati lega, aku berjalan kembali ke sofa, berbaring, dan segera tertidur nyenyak.

Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal. And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing. And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing. Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth; Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things. Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away. For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away. When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things. For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known. And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity –1 Corinthians 13:1-13.

Several years ago, my nephew was quite busy for a number of months building a house for himself and his soon-to-be bride. I’d like to compare that to the building of a marriage. As you know when you build a house you need to have a blueprint to follow. So it is when we build a marriage; we need to follow the blueprint of God’s Word. We all know that the first step in building a house is to lay a good foundation. So it is with marriage. For all of you who are married, I trust you have been, and will continue building your marriage on the foundation of Jesus Christ. There are many elements to a strong house that we could compare to a strong marriage but today I want to think about what it is that gives power to your house or power to a marriage—that thing is called love.

I want to look at nine elements of love:

1. Patience

Love suffereth long. Love is ready to do the work of love whenever the need arises. It is never in a hurry, instead it wears the ornaments of a meek and a quiet spirit. It will wait for the perfect opportunity and will, in the best way, quietly instruct, or exemplify, the purposes of God before your family, before your church, and before your spouse. Sometimes you are going to have to do it for a long time… alone. It will not falter in times of difficulty. A patient person is a predictable person. Love is patiently persistent; it does not abide in the temporal but in the realm of the eternal. Love understands this; therefore, love waits. It can take a long time for a human to surrender to the Lordship of Christ. That time will be shortened in perspective when a man of faith exemplifies a life of obedience and sacrifice in patience. Patience is the normal attitude of love.

2. Kindness

Kindness is love in action! The greatest thing a man can do for his Heavenly Father is to be kind to his Father’s other children. This is not hard to do, and the world needs it. To every married man reading this article, I ask that you consider this—if you would lead your wife on the journey of love, you cannot do it successfully if you try to do it without the element of kindness. Kindness makes living out the purposes of God attractive to those looking on! It will go a long way in helping your wife to draw near to God because she sees the profound effects of that nearness on her husband’s life. How kind has God been to you in bringing salvation to you? Buying woodworking tools and automotive equipment for your wife’s birthday will not promote a healthy marriage. As her husband, you must seek to enrich her life, not yours. Kindness is a normal attitude of love.

3. Generosity

Love envieth not! The opposite of envy is “generosity”. The opposite of generosity is greed, bitterness, covetousness, and spite. Husbands, you might be able to identify with me when I say that in every labor there will be other people who are engaging in the same toil as you are and probably doing it better. What complicates things is when that better person is your wife. Here the temptation is to develop a mood of ill-will and covetousness. How often do we do little things to throw a wrench in the works out of a spirit of envy, for no other reason than to destroy her good works so that she doesn’t outshine us?

There is only one character trait that a Christian should envy. That is to possess a rich and generous soul which envieth not. How many people have become discouraged from wholly following Christ because I withheld from them the needed tools for success out of jealous envy? Our family owns a cabinet shop. Carrying cabinets puts people in a vulnerable position. If envy rules, subtle things like carrying a cabinet awkwardly can hinder the work. Pinching someone’s fingers in a tight doorway is a perfect way to reduce my foe down to his size and the work successfully is hindered, and I can still maintain my innocence. How many marriages and churches operate with these kinds of sins, week after week? Husbands don’t be angry with your wife when she ends up being smarter than you are in a certain matter. In this she has not committed an error or a fault. My friends, what resources has God withheld from you that keeps you from being victorious in that great plan of redemption? Has He not been generous? Generosity is a normal attitude of love.

4. Humility

Love vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up. After you have been patient, kind, and generous and love has done its beautiful work in the world, go back into the shadows and say nothing about it. Human nature has a tendency to exalt itself which only succeeds in stopping love in its tracks because self-exultation is so contrary to love’s divine nature. The scripture commands us to, Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips. –Proverbs 27:2. How many times have I spoiled an opportunity to further the work of God in another person’s life because I got in between God’s love and their heart, and they were offended?

Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall –Proverbs 16:18.

A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit –Proverbs 29:23.

Pride will destroy the work of God and it will destroy any effort to love my brother or sister. Humility is a normal attitude of love, and it assists love greatly in its eternal purposes.

5. Courtesy

Love doth not behave itself unseemly. This is love in relation to etiquette. The NIV says it better. “Love is not rude! Courtesy is love in the little things.” I want all of us to think of a particular word. It is the word “gentleman.” The word ‘gentleman’ is a compound word, and it literally means “gentle man”. By definition, it simply defines a man who does things gently. A man who does not possess this quality can do nothing less than to be ungentle, unsympathetic, and rude. He cannot help it.

Married brothers... You will not guide your spouse into experiencing the love of God if your heart is devoid of courtesy for your wife. Courtesy is the grace that shows a special tenderness and respect for a fellow human being. I have knowledge of a sad marriage which started badly. The groom’s brash boast was that his in-laws may as well get to know him sooner than later. He started out very early on, expressing himself rudely at the supper table. It is no wonder that after the honeymoon was over his wife found him to be a man she didn’t want to live with and for good reason. The marriage didn’t continue “happily ever after” because there was a complete lack of courtesy. Courtesy is a normal attitude of love.

6. Unselfishness

Love seeketh not her own. Or we could say it this way—love will not attempt to snatch that which belongs to me, even by right. There will come a day when a man or a woman, in the name of biblical love, must exercise a higher calling of giving up his own personal rights in order to advance the kingdom of God. Love strikes us deeply in the area of unselfishness. It is a very difficult thing after we have purchased our rights, won them, dreamed about them, desired them, and sacrificed for them, to need to give them up. And yet love will relinquish it all so that the purposes of God might be pre-eminent. Only for the great and noble purposes of divine love can we justify the waste of having given up that which we naturally perceive belongs to us by right. No sacrifice is too hard for love to make. True love will enjoy what is given but its very nature cannot take that which is not voluntarily offered. Love is the path to life and freedom. There is no happiness in getting but only in giving. Many marriages exist with the attitude that happiness comes in having or in getting, but that is not God’s way. There would be few divorces if a husband worked as hard to keep his wife as he did to get her in the first place. Unselfishness is a normal attitude of love.

7. Good Temper

Love is not easily provoked. There are many decent, hardworking moral people in this world who are fatally flawed by being touchy and ill tempered—they have a short fuse. Few things unchristianize a good man than an evil temper. This sinful character flaw devastates the home, saps the vitality of men and women he rubs shoulders with, and it corrupts the beauty and innocence of his children. This misery-producing power stands alone. It is made up of jealousy, anger, pride, cruelty, self-righteousness, touchiness, doggedness, sullenness... These all make up the character of a loveless soul. Someone once said; There is no place in heaven for a man like this; for to enter into heaven a man must take himself along. My friends, the home is like hell on earth when an individual of this caliber is at the helm. A grouch is a man who sizes himself up and is sore about it.

Temper is significant. A man is no bigger than the thing that makes him angry. It is not so much about what a temper is, but what it reveals about what is inside a person. It reveals a lack of generosity, courtesy, and unselfishness. A lack of patience, and a lack of kindness, are instantaneously symbolized in one flash of temper. It is not enough to deal with the surface symptom of temper. We must go to the source and allow the Lord Jesus Christ to change us from the deepest depth of our nature, and the anger in our souls will die by itself. How many children want nothing to do with Christianity because of an evil temper in the heart of a father or a mother?! We really have no time to lose. It is with patient persistence that a wife, a husband, or a pastor must love this moral despot. For he too must be conquered by the redemptive love of Jesus Christ. This is the purpose of love. To be tempered by the power of God is a normal attitude of love.

8. Quality or ability to “think no evil”

The people who inspire me are the people who believe in me and encourage me. It is also true that in an atmosphere of suspicion and mistrust, people shrivel up and die. In the absence of trust and goodwill, love cannot exist, let alone thrive. Nothing makes a marriage rust like distrust. It is a delightful and a wonderful thing to find people in this loveless world who assume the best about another person until it is proven otherwise. How often I have found in life that I was wrong about the motives of another person! The quickest way to destroy love in marriage is to assume something negative about the motives of your spouse when only the Lord knows the heart. Divine love wants the object of its focus to succeed and not to fall on its face and fail.

Is it possible that if we would succeed in elevating others to new heights, we would find that our own success is enhanced by our vision or belief of what that person could become? Is it possible that good, old-fashioned respect for the object of our love is the first step to restoring the self-respect a man has lost? If we treat our spouses dishonorably and with disrespect, there is a good chance they will become or remain the person we detest. Someone once said “Sisters, a happy wife sometimes has the best husband, but more often she makes the best out of the husband she has.” You see, man was made in the image of God and the greatest thing you can do for a person is to use the power of love to aid in the restoration of what has been lost. The Son of man came to seek and to save that which was lost. Thinking no evil is a normal attitude of love.

9. Sincerity

Brothers and sisters, we get it so backwards. A man who knows the love of Christ chooses the high road to make wrongs right. It is his highest delight to see the purposes of God practically worked out in another person’s life, not the other way around. How often we delight to see our enemy fall. Destructive criticism and an over-focus on the faults or sins of others weakens their ability to overcome. Overplaying and capitalizing on the faults of others hinders our marriages and churches from being filled with overcoming people. Couples, whatever it is that you believe about your spouse is probably what he or she will become.

Those who truly love others are filled with delight and rejoicing when they examine a situation and find out things were better than they had feared.

Love and trust go hand in hand. Because my soul is secure in the hands of an unchanging God, I can safely reach out in sincerity to those who have entered into the realm of influence. Rejoicing in righteousness and thinking NO EVIL is a normal and final attitude of love.

The Greatness of Love (the Greatest Thing in the World)

a.) It bears all things

Brothers, can you bear all things for the sake of redemptive love and its eternal purposes? When you are tempted to quit loving, remember what Jesus bore for you. The ability to bear all things is a normal attitude of love. Can you take an insult without returning one? Even the devil has the wisdom to patiently endure if it gives him a greater future advantage.

b.) It hopeth all things

And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us –Romans 5:5.

Sisters, if your husband falls short of the glory you married him with, can you wait patiently for the Lord to work in his life? When your husband surprises you by being a different person than you thought you married, practice seeing him for what he could be instead of what he isn’t and then encourage him in hope rather than discourage him with hopelessness.

c.) It endureth all things.

Therefore I endure all things for the elect’s sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory –2 Timothy 2:10.

O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever –1 Chronicles 16:34.

Brothers and sisters, how long is your endurance? When you get tired of enduring, remember how long God endures with you. Most matrimonial troubles come when two people choose to not endure because they are in love with themselves instead of their spouse.

d.) It never faileth because God is the source of it.

Prophecies fail.

Tongues fail.

Knowledge vanishes away.

True biblical love never gives up. It never fails; therefore, it can never be defeated.

Love cannot be achieved through the eloquence of words. It cannot be seized by willpower. It cannot be learned through education, and it cannot be purchased through human sacrifice. It is not for sale, nor can it be traded like a commodity for it is spiritual in nature. Love can only be received from the Great Eternal Giver, to those worthy to possess such power and glory in their hearts.

The sincerity of my personal quest to pursue and to comprehend from the heart, the love of Christ, will determine the quantity and the quality of love for others. It was Paul’s sincere cry to the Philippians “...that I might know him”.

Husbands and wives, when you first met each other, your love was very immature. You saw it as through a glass darkly or as a poor reflection in the mirror. You spoke about the future of your love like immature children who had no experience with it. You began knowing about it and you prophesied about it. Now that you are married, you know a lot more about LOVE than you did, but there is so much more still to learn. My friends, may the looking glass become clearer for you with maturity and may you understand love in its perfection in the days to come. But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day –Proverbs 4:18.

Husbands and wives, the best thing you can do for each other is to pursue a daily relationship with the Lord Jesus Christ. Remember that any success in life requires practice. Practice loving each other. Be patient, be kind, be generous, be humble, be unselfish. In all sincerity encourage each other to surrender your hearts to the Lordship of Jesus Christ and your marriage will be above and beyond everything you have ever imagined. A young man once prayed... “Lord, send me a wife that loves you for I know that if she loves you, she will also love me.” He was a wise man.

Great love comes at a great cost. It cost the Lord Jesus Christ His life. Only after you have given your hearts to the Lord in complete trust, will you be able to give your hearts to each other. You have already gained everything; therefore, you have nothing to lose by giving your all in an earthly relationship. That is the cost of love, and it is worth it. Love is life and life is love. It is better not to live than to not love. If love is present in your home, you will find energetic purpose for living and all will be well. Place your hope and faith in the God of Love and you will find... the Greatest Thing in the World.

Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God –1 John 4:7.

For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith –1 John 5:4.

May God bless every bride and groom.

إن كنت أتكلم بألسنة الناس والملائكة، ولكن ليس لي محبة، فقد صرت نحاسًا يطن أو صنجًا يرن. وإن كانت لي نبوة، وأعلم جميع الأسرار وكل علم، وإن كان لي كل الإيمان حتى أنقل الجبال، ولكن ليس لي محبة، فلست شيئًا. وإن أطعمت كل أموالي للمساكين، وإن سلّمت جسدي حتى أحترق، ولكن ليس لي محبة، فلا أنتفع شيئًا. المحبة تتأنى وترفق. المحبة لا تحسد، المحبة لا تتفاخر ولا تنتفخ، ولا تقبح، ولا تطلب ما لنفسها، ولا تحتد، ولا تظن السوء، ولا تفرح بالإثم بل تفرح بالحق، وتحتمل كل شيء، وتصدق كل شيء، وترجو كل شيء، وتصبر على كل شيء. المحبة لا تسقط أبدًا. أما النبوات فستبطل، والألسنة فستنتهي، والعلم فسيبطل. لأننا نعلم بعض العلم ونتنبأ بعض التنبؤ. ولكن متى جاء الكامل فحينئذ يبطل ما هو بعض. لما كنت طفلًا كطفل كنت أتكلم، وكطفل كنت أفطن، وكطفل كنت أفتكر. ولكن لما صرت رجلًا أبطلت ما للطفل. فإننا ننظر الآن في مرآة، في لغز، لكن حينئذ وجهًا لوجه. الآن أعرف بعض المعرفة، لكن حينئذ سأعرف كما عرفت. أما الآن فيثبت الإيمان والرجاء والمحبة، هذه الثلاثة، ولكن أعظمهن المحبة –كورنثوس الأولى 13:1-13.

قبل عدة سنوات، كان ابن أخي منشغلًا جدًا عدة أشهر ببناء منزل لنفسه ولعروسه التي كان سيتزوجها قريبًا. أود أن أقارن ذلك ببناء الزواج. كما تعلمون، عندما تبنون منزلًا، تحتاجون إلى مخطط تتبعونه. وهكذا حين نبني زواجًا، علينا أن نتبع مخطط كلمة الله. نعلم جميعًا أن الخطوة الأولى في بناء منزل هي وضع أساس متين. وكذلك الزواج. ولكل المتزوجين منكم، أرجو أنكم قد بنيتم زواجكم على أساس يسوع المسيح، وأنكم ستواصلون بناءه عليه. ثمة عناصر كثيرة تجعل المنزل قويًا، ويمكننا أن نقارنها بزواج قوي، لكنني أريد اليوم أن أفكر فيما يمنح منزلكم أو زواجكم قوته؛ وهذا الشيء يسمى المحبة.

أريد أن أتأمل في تسعة عناصر للمحبة:

1. الصبر

المحبة تتأنى. المحبة مستعدة للقيام بعمل المحبة كلما دعت الحاجة. لا تستعجل أبدًا، بل تتحلى بزينة الروح الوديع الهادئ. إنها تنتظر الفرصة المناسبة، وتوضح مقاصد الله لعائلتك وكنيستك وزوجك بهدوء وبأفضل طريقة، بالتعليم أو بالقدوة. أحيانًا ستضطر إلى القيام بذلك مدة طويلة... وحدك. ولا تضعف في أوقات الشدة. الإنسان الصبور إنسان يمكن التنبؤ بتصرفاته. المحبة مثابرة بصبر؛ لا تقيم في الزائل، بل في عالم الأبدي. المحبة تفهم ذلك، ولذلك تنتظر. قد يستغرق الأمر وقتًا طويلًا حتى يخضع إنسان لسيادة المسيح. ويبدو ذلك الوقت أقصر حين يجسد رجل الإيمان حياة الطاعة والتضحية بصبر. الصبر هو السمة المعتادة للمحبة.

2. اللطف

اللطف هو المحبة في عمل! أعظم ما يستطيع المرء أن يفعله لأبيه السماوي هو أن يرفق بأبناء أبيه الآخرين. ليس هذا بالأمر العسير، والعالم بحاجة إليه. إلى كل رجل متزوج يقرأ هذا المقال، أرجو أن تفكر في هذا: إذا أردت أن تقود زوجتك في مسيرة المحبة، فلن تنجح إن حاولت ذلك من دون عنصر اللطف. يجعل اللطف عيش مقاصد الله أمرًا جذابًا لمن يشاهدون! ويساعد زوجتك كثيرًا على الاقتراب من الله، لأنها ترى الأثر العميق لهذا القرب في حياة زوجها. ما أرفق الله بك إذ أتاك بالخلاص! إن شراء أدوات النجارة ومعدات السيارات لزوجتك في عيد ميلادها لن يعزز زواجًا سليمًا. وبصفتك زوجها، عليك أن تسعى إلى إثراء حياتها، لا حياتك. اللطف هو السمة المعتادة للمحبة.

3. السخاء

المحبة لا تحسد! نقيض الحسد هو «السخاء». ونقيض السخاء هو الجشع والمرارة والطمع والحقد. أيها الأزواج، لعلكم تتفهمون ما أعنيه حين أقول إن في كل عمل أناسًا آخرين يمارسون الكدح نفسه الذي تمارسونه، وربما يؤدونه على نحو أفضل. وتتعقد الأمور حين تكون تلك الشخصة الأفضل هي زوجتك. هنا يكون الإغراء أن يستولي علينا سوء النية والطمع. كم مرة نفعل أمورًا صغيرة تعرقل العمل بدافع الحسد، لا لسبب سوى تخريب أعمالها الجيدة كيلا تتفوق علينا؟

ليس هناك سوى سمة شخصية واحدة ينبغي للمسيحي أن يحسد عليها، وهي امتلاك نفس غنية سخية لا تحسد. كم شخصًا تثبط عن اتباع المسيح بكل إخلاص لأنني حجبت عنهم الأدوات اللازمة للنجاح بدافع حسد غيور؟ تملك عائلتنا ورشة لصناعة الخزائن. وحمل الخزائن يضع الناس في موقف ضعيف. فإذا حكم الحسد، فإن أمورًا خفية، مثل حمل الخزانة بطريقة غير ملائمة، قد تعرقل العمل. وقرص أصابع شخص ما في مدخل ضيق طريقة مثالية لأحط خصمي إلى مستواه، فيتعطل العمل بنجاح، وأظل قادرًا على الحفاظ على براءتي. كم من زيجات وكنائس تستمر في ممارسة هذه الخطايا أسبوعًا بعد أسبوع؟ أيها الأزواج، لا تغضبوا من زوجاتكم حين يتبين أنهن أذكى منكم في أمر معين. لم ترتكب زوجتك خطأ أو ذنبًا في ذلك. يا أصدقائي، ما الموارد التي حجبها الله عنكم فتمنعكم من الانتصار في خطة الفداء العظيمة؟ ألم يكن سخيًا؟ السخاء هو السمة المعتادة للمحبة.

4. التواضع

المحبة لا تتفاخر ولا تنتفخ. بعد أن تكون قد صبرت ولطفت وسخت، وتكون المحبة قد أنجزت عملها الجميل في العالم، عُد إلى الظل ولا تقل شيئًا عن ذلك. تميل الطبيعة البشرية إلى تمجيد ذاتها، وهذا لا يفعل إلا إيقاف المحبة في مسارها، لأن تمجيد الذات يتعارض بشدة مع طبيعة المحبة الإلهية. يأمرنا الكتاب المقدس قائلًا: «ليمدحك الغريب لا فمك، والأجنبي لا شفتاك». –أمثال 27:2. كم مرة أفسدت فرصة لتعزيز عمل الله في حياة شخص آخر، لأنني وقفت بين محبة الله وقلبه، فأُسيء إليه؟

قبل الكسر الكبرياء، وقبل السقوط تشامخ الروح. –أمثال 16:18.

كِبْرِيَاءُ الإِنْسَانِ تُخْفِضُهُ، وَالرُّوحُ الْمُتَوَاضِعَةُ تُمَسِّكُ الْمَجْدَ. –أمثال 29:23.

الكبرياء سيدمر عمل الله، وسيدمر كل جهد لمحبة أخي أو أختي. التواضع سمة معتادة للمحبة، ويساعد المحبة كثيرًا في تحقيق مقاصدها الأبدية.

5. اللباقة

المحبة لا تقبح. وهذا يتعلق بالآداب. وتقول الترجمة الدولية الجديدة الأمر على نحو أفضل: «المحبة لا تسيء الأدب!» اللباقة هي المحبة في الأمور الصغيرة. أريد أن نفكر جميعًا في كلمة بعينها، وهي كلمة «رجل مهذب». والكلمة مركبة، ومعناها الحرفي «رجل لطيف». وهي ببساطة، بحسب تعريفها، تصف رجلًا يتصرف بلطف. والرجل الذي لا يتحلى بهذه الصفة لا يسعه إلا أن يكون فظًا وقاسيًا وغير مهذب. فهو لا يستطيع منع ذلك.

أيها الإخوة المتزوجون... لن تهدوا زوجاتكم إلى اختبار محبة الله إن خلا قلبكم من اللباقة في التعامل مع زوجاتكم. اللباقة هي النعمة التي تظهر رقة خاصة واحترامًا للإنسان الآخر. أعرف زواجًا حزينًا بدأ بداية سيئة. تفاخر العريس بفظاظة قائلًا إن أهل زوجته قد يتعرفون إليه عاجلًا لا آجلًا. ومنذ البداية، أخذ يعبر عن نفسه بفظاظة على مائدة العشاء. فلا عجب أن زوجته، بعد انتهاء شهر العسل، وجدته رجلًا لا تريد العيش معه، ولسبب وجيه. لم يستمر الزواج «بسعادة إلى الأبد» لغياب اللباقة تمامًا. اللباقة سمة معتادة للمحبة.

6. الإيثار

المحبة لا تطلب ما لنفسها. أو يمكننا أن نقولها هكذا: المحبة لا تحاول أن تنتزع ما يخصني، حتى لو كان من حقي. سيأتي يوم يتعين فيه على رجل أو امرأة، باسم المحبة الكتابية، أن يمارس دعوة أسمى بالتخلي عن حقوقه الشخصية من أجل تقدم ملكوت الله. تمس المحبة أعماقنا في مجال الإيثار. فمن الصعب جدًا، بعد أن نكون قد اشترينا حقوقنا، وانتزعناها، وحلمنا بها، ورغبنا فيها، وضحينا من أجلها، أن نحتاج إلى التخلي عنها. ومع ذلك، ستتنازل المحبة عن كل شيء لكي تكون مقاصد الله هي العليا. ولا يمكننا تبرير ضياع ما نرى بطبيعتنا أنه حق لنا إلا من أجل مقاصد المحبة الإلهية العظيمة والنبيلة. لا توجد تضحية يصعب على المحبة تقديمها. المحبة الحقيقية تستمتع بما يُعطى لها، لكن طبيعتها لا تسمح لها بأخذ ما لم يُقدَّم طوعًا. المحبة طريق الحياة والحرية. لا سعادة في الأخذ، بل في العطاء وحده. تقوم زيجات كثيرة على الاعتقاد بأن السعادة تأتي من الامتلاك أو الأخذ، لكن هذا ليس طريق الله. لكانت حالات الطلاق قليلة لو أن الزوج بذل الجهد نفسه للاحتفاظ بزوجته الذي بذله للفوز بها في البداية. الإيثار سمة معتادة للمحبة.

7. هدوء الطبع

المحبة لا تحتد. في هذا العالم أناس كثيرون محترمون ومجتهدون وأخلاقيون، لكنهم يعانون عيبًا قاتلًا هو سرعة التأثر وسوء الطبع؛ فهم سريعو الغضب. قلما يوجد ما يجعل الرجل الصالح أقل مسيحية من سوء الطبع. هذه العلة الخاطئة في الشخصية تدمر البيت، وتستنزف حيوية الرجال والنساء الذين يخالطهم، وتفسد جمال أطفاله وبراءتهم. وهذه القدرة على جلب البؤس لا مثيل لها. فهي تتكون من الغيرة والغضب والكبرياء والقسوة والبر الذاتي وسرعة التأثر والعناد والعبوس... كل هذه الصفات تصنع شخصية النفس الخالية من المحبة. قال أحدهم ذات مرة: لا مكان في السماء لرجل كهذا، لأن دخول السماء يقتضي أن يأخذ المرء نفسه معه. يا أصدقائي، يصبح البيت جحيمًا على الأرض حين يتولى القيادة شخص من هذا النوع. والعبوس رجل يقيّم نفسه ثم يغضب مما يراه.

الطبع مهم. فالرجل ليس أكبر من الشيء الذي يغضبه. والمسألة ليست كثيرًا في ماهية الطبع، بل فيما يكشفه عما في داخل الإنسان. إنه يكشف نقصًا في السخاء واللباقة والإيثار. فنقص الصبر ونقص اللطف يظهران في نوبة غضب خاطفة. لا يكفي أن نعالج العرض الظاهر لسوء الطبع. علينا أن نذهب إلى مصدره ونسمح للرب يسوع المسيح أن يغيرنا من أعمق أعماق طبيعتنا، وعندئذ يموت الغضب في نفوسنا من تلقاء نفسه. كم من طفل لا يريد أن تكون له صلة بالمسيحية بسبب سوء الطبع في قلب أب أو أم؟! ليس لدينا وقت لنضيعه حقًا. على الزوجة أو الزوج أو الراعي أن يحب هذا المتسلط الأخلاقي بمثابرة صبورة، إذ لا بد له هو أيضًا أن يُغلب بمحبة يسوع المسيح الفدائية. هذا هو غرض المحبة. أن يضبطنا سلطان الله هو سمة معتادة للمحبة.

8. صفة «لا تظن السوء» أو القدرة عليها

الناس الذين يلهمونني هم الذين يؤمنون بي ويشجعونني. ومن الصحيح أيضًا أن الناس يذبلون ويموتون في جو من الشك وانعدام الثقة. فحيث تغيب الثقة وحسن النية، لا يمكن للمحبة أن توجد، فضلًا عن أن تزدهر. لا شيء يجعل الزواج يصدأ مثل انعدام الثقة. إنه لأمر مبهج ورائع أن نجد في هذا العالم الخالي من المحبة أناسًا يحسنون الظن بالآخر إلى أن يثبت العكس. كم مرة اكتشفت في حياتي أنني كنت مخطئًا بشأن دوافع شخص آخر! أسرع طريقة لتدمير المحبة في الزواج هي افتراض سوء النية في زوجك، مع أن الرب وحده يعلم القلب. تريد المحبة الإلهية لمن تركز عليه أن ينجح لا أن يسقط على وجهه ويفشل.

أيمكن أن نجد أن نجاحنا نحن يتعزز برؤيتنا أو إيماننا بما يمكن أن يصير إليه الآخرون، إن نجحنا في رفعهم إلى آفاق جديدة؟ أيمكن أن يكون الاحترام الأصيل، الذي عُرف به الناس قديمًا، لمن نحبهم الخطوة الأولى لاستعادة احترام الرجل لذاته بعدما فقده؟ إذا عاملنا أزواجنا بغير شرف وبلا احترام، فهناك احتمال كبير أن يصيروا أو يظلوا الأشخاص الذين نمقتهم. قال أحدهم ذات مرة: «أيتها الأخوات، الزوج السعيد قد تكون زوجته هي أفضل زوجة له، ولكنها في أغلب الأحيان تصنع أفضل ما يمكن من الزوج الذي لديها». أرأيتم، لقد خُلق الإنسان على صورة الله، وأعظم ما تستطيعون فعله لشخص هو استخدام قوة المحبة للمساعدة في استعادة ما فُقد. جاء ابن الإنسان لكي يطلب ويخلص ما قد هلك. عدم ظن السوء سمة معتادة للمحبة.

9. الإخلاص

أيها الإخوة والأخوات، نحن نقلب الأمور رأسًا على عقب. الرجل الذي يعرف محبة المسيح يختار الطريق الأسمى ليصلح الأخطاء. وأعظم ما يسعده أن يرى مقاصد الله تتحقق عمليًا في حياة شخص آخر، لا العكس. كم نفرح كثيرًا حين نرى عدونا يسقط. إن النقد الهدام والتركيز المفرط على أخطاء الآخرين أو خطاياهم يضعف قدرتهم على التغلب عليها. والمبالغة في إبراز أخطاء الآخرين واستغلالها تعوق زيجاتنا وكنائسنا عن الامتلاء بأناس ينتصرون. أيها الأزواج، ما تعتقدونه عن أزواجكم غالبًا هو ما سيصيرون إليه.

يمتلئ الذين يحبون الآخرين حقًا بالبهجة والفرح حين يتفحصون موقفًا ويكتشفون أن الأمور كانت أفضل مما خشوا.

المحبة والثقة متلازمتان. ولأن نفسي آمنة في يدي إله لا يتغير، أستطيع أن أتوجه بإخلاص وأمان إلى الذين دخلوا نطاق تأثيري. الفرح بالبر وعدم ظن السوء أبدًا هما السمة المعتادة والأخيرة للمحبة.

عظمة المحبة (أعظم شيء في العالم)

a.) تحتمل كل شيء

أيها الإخوة، هل تستطيعون احتمال كل شيء من أجل المحبة الفدائية ومقاصدها الأبدية؟ عندما يراودكم إغراء التوقف عن المحبة، تذكروا ما احتمله يسوع من أجلكم. القدرة على احتمال كل شيء سمة معتادة للمحبة. هل تستطيعون احتمال إهانة من دون أن تردوا بمثلها؟ حتى إبليس لديه الحكمة ليصبر باحتمال إذا كان ذلك يمنحه ميزة أكبر في المستقبل.

b.) ترجو كل شيء

والرجاء لا يخزي، لأن محبة الله قد انسكبت في قلوبنا بالروح القدس المعطى لنا. –رومية 5:5.

أيتها الأخوات، إذا قصر زوجك عن مستوى المجد الذي رأيتنه فيه حين تزوجتنه، فهل تستطيعن أن تنتظرن بصبر عمل الرب في حياته؟ حين يفاجئك زوجك بأن يكون شخصًا مختلفًا عما ظننت أنك تزوجته، تدربي على أن تري ما يمكن أن يصير إليه بدلًا مما ليس هو عليه، ثم شجعيه بالرجاء بدلًا من تثبيط عزيمته باليأس.

c.) تصبر على كل شيء.

لذلك أنا أصبر على كل شيء لأجل المختارين، لكي يحصلوا هم أيضًا على الخلاص الذي في المسيح يسوع مع مجد أبدي. –تيموثاوس الثانية 2:10.

احمدوا الرب لأنه صالح، لأن إلى الأبد رحمته. –أخبار الأيام الأول 16:34.

أيها الإخوة والأخوات، ما مدى طول أناةكم؟ حين تملّون من الاحتمال، تذكروا طول أناة الله عليكم. تنشأ معظم المشكلات الزوجية حين يختار شخصان ألا يصبرا، لأنهما يحبان نفسيهما بدلًا من زوجهما.

d.) لا تسقط أبدًا لأن الله مصدرها.

النبوات تبطل.

الألسنة تبطل.

العلم يبطل.

المحبة الكتابية الحقيقية لا تستسلم أبدًا. إنها لا تسقط، ولذلك لا يمكن هزيمتها أبدًا.

لا يمكن بلوغ المحبة ببلاغة الكلام. ولا يمكن انتزاعها بقوة الإرادة. ولا يمكن تعلمها بالتعليم، ولا شراؤها بتضحية بشرية. إنها ليست للبيع، ولا يمكن مبادلتها كسلعة، لأنها ذات طبيعة روحية. لا يمكن أن تُنال المحبة إلا من المعطي العظيم الأبدي، لمن يستحقون أن يمتلكوا مثل هذا السلطان والمجد في قلوبهم.

إن إخلاص سعيي الشخصي إلى التماس محبة المسيح وفهمها من القلب هو ما سيحدد مقدار محبتي للآخرين ونوعيتها. وكان صراخ بولس المخلص إلى أهل فيلبي: «...لكي أعرفه».

أيها الأزواج والزوجات، حين التقيتم أول مرة، كانت محبتكم غير ناضجة جدًا. رأيتموها كما في مرآة، على نحو ملتبس، أو كانعكاس باهت. وتحدثتم عن مستقبل محبتكم كأطفال غير ناضجين لم يختبروها. بدأتم تعرفون عنها وتنبأتم بها. والآن، بعد أن تزوجتم، تعرفون عن المحبة أكثر بكثير مما كنتم تعرفون، لكن ما زال أمامكم الكثير لتتعلموه. يا أصدقائي، لعل المرآة تصفو لكم مع النضج، ولعلكم تفهمون المحبة في كمالها في الأيام المقبلة. أما سبيل الصديقين فكنور مشرق يتزايد وينير إلى النهار الكامل. –أمثال 4:18.

أيها الأزواج والزوجات، أفضل ما تستطيعون فعله بعضكم لبعض هو أن تسعوا إلى علاقة يومية مع الرب يسوع المسيح. تذكروا أن النجاح في الحياة يتطلب الممارسة. تمرنوا على محبة بعضكم بعضًا. كونوا صبورين، لطفاء، أسخياء، متواضعين، ومؤثرين الغير على أنفسكم. وبكل إخلاص، شجعوا بعضكم بعضًا على تسليم قلوبكم لسيادة يسوع المسيح، وسيكون زواجكم فوق كل ما تخيلتموه وأسمى منه. صلى شاب ذات مرة قائلًا... «يا رب، أرسل إليّ زوجة تحبك، لأني أعلم أنها إن أحبتك فستحبني أيضًا». لقد كان رجلًا حكيمًا.

المحبة العظيمة لها ثمن عظيم. كلفت الرب يسوع المسيح حياته. ولن تستطيعوا أن تعطوا قلوبكم بعضكم لبعض إلا بعد أن تسلموا قلوبكم للرب بثقة كاملة. لقد ربحتم كل شيء بالفعل، ولذلك ليس لديكم ما تخسرونه حين تعطون كل ما لديكم في علاقة أرضية. ذلك هو ثمن المحبة، وهو يستحق العناء. المحبة هي الحياة والحياة هي المحبة. خير للمرء ألا يعيش من ألا يحب. إذا كانت المحبة حاضرة في بيتكم، فستجدون غاية حيوية للحياة، وسيكون كل شيء على ما يرام. ضعوا رجاءكم وإيمانكم في إله المحبة، وستجدون... أعظم شيء في العالم.

أيها الأحباء، لنحب بعضنا بعضًا، لأن المحبة هي من الله، وكل من يحب فقد ولد من الله ويعرف الله. –يوحنا الأولى 4:7.

لأن كل من ولد من الله يغلب العالم. وهذه هي الغلبة التي تغلب العالم: إيماننا. –يوحنا الأولى 5:4.

ليبارك الله كل عروس وعريس.

After living in Haiti for several months, I finally had the opportunity to go visit the local witch doctor. As I walked up his long drive, I passed many statues and satanic symbols. It was eerie for sure. As I approached the voodoo temple that was connected to his house, I saw him standing there watching me approach. My heart began to race; I knew he was a powerful man. Then he began to laugh. The closer I got, the louder he laughed. I was a bit puzzled until I realized that many people from the village were following me up the lane. They were very interested in what was about to transpire. I approached the man, not knowing what would happen next.

“Are you a pastor?” he asked.

“Yes, I am,” was my reply. Again, he began to laugh loudly.

“You pastors are all the same,” he proclaimed. “You want everyone to come to your churches, but your churches have no power! When one of your people gets sick, they come to me. No power, you Christians!”

A heavy burden overtook me, and I explained to him how I agreed with him, but that the real church of Jesus Christ would always have power. The Bible actually says that the very gates of Hell shall not prevail against it.

This was the beginning of a very interesting relationship, but I will never forget those words—most certainly from the devil himself—“You Christians have no power!”

I have since traveled to hundreds of churches and need to agree with that voodoo priest. The Christian churches are lacking power. But why? We know that God is power. We have many things figured out, we look good and sound good, but do we still have the power of God in our churches?

In the Old Testament we have many examples of power and the lack of power. We can also learn how we receive power, and why we lose it.

In Joshua, chapter 6, we have the familiar account of the children of Israel and the city of Jericho. God tells Joshua and all the men of war to compass the city, and walk around it once every day, for six days. Then on the seventh day they were to march around the city not just once, but seven times. After they had completed the seven trips around the city, the priests were to blow their trumpets.

We know what happened when Joshua obeyed each command—those thick, impenetrable walls came tumbling down. God also gave Joshua a strict command about what the men should and should not do. They were to keep themselves from everything that God had pronounced was accursed; all the silver, gold, and vessels were to be consecrated into the treasury of the Lord; no man was to take any of the spoil.

However, Achan saw some nice things that he desired. He slipped them into his armor, then later hid them under his tent, and no one saw a thing.

After this great victory, Joshua sent spies to the next city, Ai, to discover how well the city was fortified. The men returned and told Joshua not to send all the men to Ai, for there were only a few defenders protecting the city.

However, the men of Ai smote the children of Israel and chased them away. Moreover, Joshua rent his clothes and cried out to God. Then God replied that there was sin in the camp of Israel.

In the Old Testament, the children of Israel are normally representative of the church of Jesus Christ today. Can we not glean much from this account? When there was no sin in the camp (or in the church) God’s people had complete victory; they lost not one. They did many wonderful things, they destroyed all their enemies around them, and they lived in COMPLETE victory. However, as soon as sin entered into their midst, even a small sin done by one man, they lost their power. They no longer had victory over their enemies.

What follows is a graphic description of how the children of Israel dealt with the sin that had entered the camp. It was totally destroyed.

And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor … And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire… –Joshua 7:24-26.

In this account it is clear why God’s people had lost their power—they had sin in the camp. It is also clear what it took for them to regain that power which they had lost—get rid of the sin.

In chapter 8 we read of the power being restored to Israel instantly after the sin was dealt with. Again, they lived in victory!

Another passage in the Old Testament that speaks of this topic is in Leviticus chapters 13 and 14. Leprosy was a strange disease. If one were to get leprosy, it was easily spread. Thus, there needed to be some strict guidelines regarding how to deal with the disease. The priest was to examine very closely to see if the person in question indeed had leprosy or not. If the priest was unsure, he would shut the person up in a room for seven days then examine him again. If it was determined that the person had leprosy, then they were sent outside of the city.

As Paul addresses the church in Corinth, he tells them that he has heard there is sin in the church. He seems surprised that the church is taking it so casually, …Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump? Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened… –1 Corinthians 5:6-7. Later he tells the church …Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person –1 Corinthians 5:13.

Let’s say that you heard the news that leprosy was again a problem in your village. This flesh-destroying disease had made a comeback and many from your village were now infected. Then you’re sitting in church on Sunday morning, when the doors open, and a man enters with skin and flesh hanging from his extremities. He is badly infected, but he does not seem to know it. What would you do? What if he wanted to come sit by you? What if he wanted to talk to your children? I think we all know what we would do; we would not allow him into our midst. We love our people, our families too much for that.

What about sin? Do we allow sin to come and join us? Do we take it seriously? What is worse, being infected with a flesh-destroying disease, or being infected by a soul-destroying sin? Remember, the wages of sin is death—spiritual death; eternal death. If we would treat sin in the same way as we would the disease (and we should) then our churches would once again have Holy Spirit power.

The Bible says …ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth –Acts 1:8.

We have already seen how sin separates us from the power of God, and we have also seen how God wants to give us power. He wants us to have victory over the enemy—the devil, the world, and flesh. However, something seems to be happening in our churches—we are allowing sin to enter. It is common to hear a preacher say, “No one is perfect.” Or, “We all sin.” Oh, that we would realize the damage these statements can make. Jesus came to save us from ALL sin; ALL unrighteousness. If we are left to continue in our sin, what has Jesus done for us?

I hear about churches drifting into the world. They gradually let go of convictions and allow some new fashion and pomp of the world to enter. Something that I hear little of is churches falling apart because of gross sin, such as fornication or drunkenness. The enemy of our souls, desires for us to become lukewarm. He wants the church to lose its power, to start living like everyone else. Here in Haiti, there are churches everywhere. On Sunday mornings starting at five o’clock in the morning, I start hearing the churches singing and worshipping. However, where are all those people on Monday morning? They are mixing right back into the world from whence they have come.

I was recently talking to a very wealthy Haitian man who owned resorts and properties all over Haiti. I asked him if he was a Christian. (I wanted to start a conversation.) I could tell that he wanted to say yes; instead, he became frustrated and said no. I asked him why not. He said exactly what I thought he would say. “I have desired to become a Christian, I’ve gone to all the churches around here, but I don’t feel they have anything to offer me. I have money; I have physical blessings; but that seems to be all that they are seeking for.”

If our churches today would refuse to settle for anything less than the infilling, empowering, and leading of the Holy Spirit, a full dose of heavenly power, then we would be able to offer something that would appeal to the lost around us. I believe this is exactly what the world is looking for; they are seeking for something better, something supernatural. What if we would settle for nothing less? What if we would stay on our knees until the power of God came back? What if we would again weep for our souls, and the souls of others?

I was working closely with a vicious gang leader who lived in the neighboring village. He was hard, but God had led him to me. For seven long months we met and communicated, I wanted him to catch a glimpse of the power of God; I wanted God to save him. He would often get drunk and threaten to kill me; I would continue to point him to the Savior. He and his gang came over one day to stop a work project, saying that they now owned the land. They brandished their guns and threatened all that were there. I explained to him that God owned the land. He said, “That is fine; tell God to come down here, and I’ll cut off His head.” I was troubled by this remark and asked him if he understood the power of the God he just threatened. One afternoon I drove to his house, and we sat outside and talked. God led me to preach a bold message to him that day. “You need to give up this gang life. God wants to save you, and change your heart!” He seemed very sober as I continued, “You never know when someone will come here and kill you! You can’t control that, but my friend you can control where you go after you are dead!” I then reminded him of the terrible thing he had said days before.

While we were still talking, two men from a neighboring gang approached on motorbikes. They were heavily armed; they had come at that very moment to kill him, but they saw me talking to him and waited for me to leave. “You have a wife and children, are you not tired of this life? God has something so much better for you!” I was pleading, pleading for his soul. It was his very last opportunity, death waited at the door. As I left I told him that I would be back.

After the shooting I rushed back, but it was over… all over.

When we live in the power of the resurrection, the power of the Almighty God, it is then that He works! I feel there is so much work to be done before the Lord returns, but God’s people are too busy, we do not have time.

Do we fear talking about the power of God and the Holy Ghost simply because the Pentecostal movement has twisted what the Bible teaches? God help us.

When we call out to God for salvation, we are doing so because we know we need to be saved; converted. We also know that we cannot save ourselves, so we ask God to help us. Then when God helps us, we are able to do things that we could not do before! Angry people are angry no more. People that could not control their lust now have control. Selfish people begin to put others first. Shy people begin to preach with boldness. Greedy people begin to give to others. God does a work that counselors and doctors cannot do, He changes the very core of a person, and then all things become new. We now live for something far better than what this world has to give; we rise above by the power of God and show this sin-sick world there is a better way!

All through the Bible, God’s people did supernatural things; they did not settle for just a nice life. They sought something bigger, something better. There is power in the blood of Jesus, but it took the cross to make that a possibility. It also takes a cross for us to find that power. And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24. Yes, it seems foolish to those that perish, but to those that believe, it is the Power of God.

Depois de viver no Haiti por vários meses, finalmente tive a oportunidade de visitar o feiticeiro local. Enquanto subia pela longa entrada de sua propriedade, passei por muitas estátuas e símbolos satânicos. Era realmente arrepiante. Ao me aproximar do templo vodu, que ficava ligado à casa dele, vi-o ali, observando-me chegar. Meu coração começou a disparar; eu sabia que ele era um homem poderoso. Então ele começou a rir. Quanto mais eu me aproximava, mais alto ele ria. Fiquei um pouco intrigado até perceber que muitas pessoas da aldeia me seguiam pela trilha. Estavam muito interessadas no que estava prestes a acontecer. Aproximei-me do homem, sem saber o que aconteceria em seguida.

“Você é pastor?”, perguntou ele.

“Sim, sou”, respondi. Mais uma vez, ele começou a rir alto.

“Vocês, pastores, são todos iguais”, declarou. “Querem que todos venham às suas igrejas, mas suas igrejas não têm poder! Quando alguém do seu povo fica doente, vem até mim. Não têm poder, vocês, cristãos!”

Um pesado fardo tomou conta de mim, e expliquei a ele que concordava, mas que a verdadeira igreja de Jesus Cristo sempre teria poder. A Bíblia de fato diz que as próprias portas do inferno não prevalecerão contra ela.

Esse foi o começo de um relacionamento muito interessante, mas nunca esquecerei aquelas palavras — certamente proferidas pelo próprio diabo: “Vocês, cristãos, não têm poder!”

Desde então, visitei centenas de igrejas e preciso concordar com aquele sacerdote vodu. Falta poder às igrejas cristãs. Mas por quê? Sabemos que Deus é poder. Já entendemos muitas coisas, temos boa aparência e falamos bem, mas será que o poder de Deus ainda está presente em nossas igrejas?

No Antigo Testamento, temos muitos exemplos de poder e de falta de poder. Também podemos aprender como recebemos poder e por que o perdemos.

Em Josué, capítulo 6, temos o conhecido relato dos filhos de Israel e da cidade de Jericó. Deus disse a Josué e a todos os homens de guerra que rodeassem a cidade, dando uma volta por dia, durante seis dias. Então, no sétimo dia, deveriam marchar ao redor da cidade não apenas uma vez, mas sete vezes. Depois de completarem as sete voltas ao redor da cidade, os sacerdotes deveriam tocar as trombetas.

Sabemos o que aconteceu quando Josué obedeceu a cada ordem: aquelas muralhas espessas e impenetráveis vieram abaixo. Deus também deu a Josué uma ordem rigorosa sobre o que os homens deveriam ou não fazer. Deviam manter-se afastados de tudo o que Deus havia declarado maldito; toda a prata, o ouro e os utensílios deveriam ser consagrados ao tesouro do Senhor; nenhum homem deveria tomar qualquer parte dos despojos.

No entanto, Acã viu algumas coisas bonitas que desejou. Escondeu-as dentro de sua armadura e, mais tarde, ocultou-as debaixo de sua tenda, sem que ninguém percebesse.

Depois dessa grande vitória, Josué enviou espias à cidade seguinte, Ai, para descobrir quão bem fortificada era. Os homens voltaram e disseram a Josué que não enviasse todos os homens a Ai, pois havia apenas poucos defensores protegendo a cidade.

No entanto, os homens de Ai derrotaram os filhos de Israel e os puseram em fuga. Além disso, Josué rasgou suas vestes e clamou a Deus. Então Deus respondeu que havia pecado no acampamento de Israel.

No Antigo Testamento, os filhos de Israel normalmente representam a igreja de Jesus Cristo de hoje. Não podemos aprender muito com esse relato? Quando não havia pecado no acampamento (ou na igreja), o povo de Deus obtinha vitória completa; não perdia ninguém. Realizavam muitas coisas maravilhosas, destruíam todos os inimigos ao redor e viviam em vitória COMPLETA. No entanto, assim que o pecado entrou em seu meio, mesmo sendo um pequeno pecado cometido por um só homem, perderam o poder. Já não tinham vitória sobre seus inimigos.

O que se segue é uma descrição vívida de como os filhos de Israel lidaram com o pecado que havia entrado no acampamento. Ele foi totalmente destruído.

Então Josué, e todo o Israel com ele, tomaram Acã, filho de Zerá, a prata, a veste, a barra de ouro, seus filhos e suas filhas, seus bois, seus jumentos, suas ovelhas, sua tenda e tudo o que possuía; e os levaram ao vale de Acor… E todo o Israel o apedrejou; e os queimaram no fogo… –Josué 7:24-26.

Nesse relato, fica claro por que o povo de Deus havia perdido o poder: havia pecado no acampamento. Também fica claro o que foi necessário para recuperar o poder que haviam perdido: livrar-se do pecado.

No capítulo 8, lemos que o poder foi restaurado a Israel imediatamente depois que o pecado foi tratado. Mais uma vez, viveram em vitória!

Outra passagem do Antigo Testamento que trata desse tema está nos capítulos 13 e 14 de Levítico. A lepra era uma doença estranha. Se alguém contraísse lepra, ela se espalhava com facilidade. Por isso, eram necessárias diretrizes rigorosas sobre como lidar com a doença. O sacerdote deveria examinar cuidadosamente a pessoa para determinar se ela realmente tinha lepra ou não. Se não tivesse certeza, isolaria a pessoa por sete dias e depois a examinaria novamente. Se fosse determinado que a pessoa tinha lepra, ela era enviada para fora da cidade.

Ao se dirigir à igreja de Corinto, Paulo lhes diz que ouviu que havia pecado na igreja. Parece surpreso que a igreja esteja tratando o assunto com tanta despreocupação: …Não sabeis que um pouco de fermento leveda toda a massa? Expurgai, pois, o fermento velho, para que sejais massa nova, assim como sois sem fermento… –1 Coríntios 5:6-7. Mais adiante, diz à igreja: …Afastai, pois, de entre vós esse iníquo –1 Coríntios 5:13.

Suponhamos que você recebesse a notícia de que a lepra voltou a ser um problema em sua aldeia. Essa doença que destrói a carne havia reaparecido e muitos de sua aldeia estavam infectados. Então você está sentado na igreja, no domingo de manhã, quando as portas se abrem e um homem entra, com pele e carne pendendo de suas extremidades. Ele está gravemente infectado, mas parece não saber. O que você faria? E se ele quisesse sentar-se ao seu lado? E se quisesse conversar com seus filhos? Acho que todos sabemos o que faríamos: não permitiríamos que ele ficasse entre nós. Amamos demais nosso povo e nossas famílias para fazer isso.

E quanto ao pecado? Permitimos que o pecado venha e se junte a nós? Levamos isso a sério? O que é pior: ser infectado por uma doença que destrói a carne ou ser infectado por um pecado que destrói a alma? Lembrem-se: o salário do pecado é a morte — morte espiritual; morte eterna. Se tratássemos o pecado da mesma maneira que trataríamos a doença (e deveríamos fazê-lo), nossas igrejas voltariam a ter o poder do Espírito Santo.

A Bíblia diz: …recebereis poder, ao descer sobre vós o Espírito Santo, e sereis minhas testemunhas tanto em Jerusalém como em toda a Judeia e Samaria, e até os confins da terra –Atos 1:8.

Já vimos como o pecado nos separa do poder de Deus, e também vimos como Deus quer nos dar poder. Ele quer que tenhamos vitória sobre o inimigo — o diabo, o mundo e a carne. No entanto, parece que algo está acontecendo em nossas igrejas: estamos permitindo que o pecado entre. É comum ouvir um pregador dizer: “Ninguém é perfeito.” Ou: “Todos pecamos.” Ah, se percebêssemos o dano que essas afirmações podem causar! Jesus veio para nos salvar de TODO pecado; de TODA injustiça. Se ficamos entregues à continuação do pecado, o que Jesus fez por nós?

Ouço falar de igrejas que se deixam levar pelo mundo. Aos poucos, abandonam suas convicções e permitem que entrem algumas novas modas e pompas do mundo. O que ouço pouco é sobre igrejas que desmoronam por causa de pecados grosseiros, como a fornicação ou a embriaguez. O inimigo de nossas almas deseja que nos tornemos mornos. Ele quer que a igreja perca seu poder e comece a viver como todos os outros. Aqui no Haiti, há igrejas por toda parte. Aos domingos de manhã, a partir das cinco horas, começo a ouvir as igrejas cantando e adorando. Mas onde estão todas essas pessoas na segunda-feira de manhã? Estão se misturando novamente ao mundo de onde vieram.

Recentemente, conversei com um haitiano muito rico, dono de resorts e propriedades por todo o Haiti. Perguntei-lhe se era cristão. (Queria iniciar uma conversa.) Percebi que ele queria dizer que sim; em vez disso, ficou frustrado e disse que não. Perguntei-lhe por que não. Ele disse exatamente o que eu imaginava que diria: “Desejei tornar-me cristão, fui a todas as igrejas daqui, mas não sinto que elas tenham algo a me oferecer. Tenho dinheiro; tenho bênçãos materiais; mas parece que é só isso que elas estão buscando.”

Se nossas igrejas hoje se recusassem a aceitar algo menos do que o enchimento, o fortalecimento e a direção do Espírito Santo, uma dose completa do poder celestial, então poderíamos oferecer algo que atraísse os perdidos ao nosso redor. Creio que é exatamente isso que o mundo procura; as pessoas estão buscando algo melhor, algo sobrenatural. E se não aceitássemos nada menos? E se permanecêssemos de joelhos até que o poder de Deus voltasse? E se voltássemos a chorar por nossas almas e pelas almas dos outros?

Eu trabalhava de perto com um violento líder de gangue que vivia na aldeia vizinha. Ele era um homem duro, mas Deus o havia conduzido até mim. Durante sete longos meses, nos encontramos e nos comunicamos. Eu queria que ele vislumbrasse o poder de Deus; queria que Deus o salvasse. Muitas vezes, ele ficava bêbado e ameaçava me matar; eu continuava a apontá-lo para o Salvador. Um dia, ele e sua gangue apareceram para interromper um projeto de trabalho, dizendo que agora eram donos da terra. Brandiram as armas e ameaçaram todos os que estavam ali. Expliquei-lhe que a terra pertencia a Deus. Ele disse: “Tudo bem; diga a Deus para vir aqui, e eu lhe cortarei a cabeça.” Fiquei perturbado com essa fala e perguntei se ele compreendia o poder do Deus que acabara de ameaçar. Numa tarde, fui de carro até a casa dele, e nos sentamos do lado de fora para conversar. Naquele dia, Deus me conduziu a lhe pregar uma mensagem ousada: “Você precisa abandonar essa vida de gangue. Deus quer salvá-lo e transformar seu coração!” Ele parecia muito sóbrio enquanto eu continuava: “Você nunca sabe quando alguém virá aqui e o matará! Você não pode controlar isso, mas, meu amigo, pode controlar para onde irá depois de morrer!” Então o lembrei da coisa terrível que havia dito dias antes.

Enquanto ainda conversávamos, dois homens de uma gangue vizinha se aproximaram de moto. Estavam fortemente armados; tinham vindo naquele exato momento para matá-lo, mas me viram conversando com ele e esperaram que eu fosse embora. “Você tem esposa e filhos. Não está cansado desta vida? Deus tem algo muito melhor para você!” Eu implorava, implorava por sua alma. Era sua última oportunidade; a morte esperava à porta. Ao sair, disse-lhe que voltaria.

Depois dos tiros, corri de volta, mas já tinha acabado… tudo acabado.

Quando vivemos no poder da ressurreição, no poder do Deus Todo-Poderoso, é então que Ele age! Sinto que há tanto trabalho a fazer antes que o Senhor volte, mas o povo de Deus está ocupado demais; não temos tempo.

Temos medo de falar sobre o poder de Deus e do Espírito Santo simplesmente porque o movimento pentecostal distorceu o que a Bíblia ensina? Deus nos ajude.

Quando clamamos a Deus por salvação, fazemos isso porque sabemos que precisamos ser salvos; convertidos. Também sabemos que não podemos salvar a nós mesmos, por isso pedimos a ajuda de Deus. Então, quando Deus nos ajuda, somos capazes de fazer coisas que antes não podíamos! Pessoas iradas deixam de ser iradas. Pessoas que não conseguiam controlar sua luxúria passam a ter controle. Pessoas egoístas começam a colocar os outros em primeiro lugar. Pessoas tímidas começam a pregar com ousadia. Pessoas gananciosas começam a dar aos outros. Deus realiza uma obra que conselheiros e médicos não conseguem realizar: transforma o próprio âmago de uma pessoa, e então todas as coisas se tornam novas. Agora vivemos por algo muito melhor do que aquilo que este mundo tem a oferecer; elevamo-nos pelo poder de Deus e mostramos a este mundo enfermo pelo pecado que existe um caminho melhor!

Ao longo de toda a Bíblia, o povo de Deus realizou coisas sobrenaturais; não se contentava apenas com uma vida agradável. Buscava algo maior, algo melhor. Há poder no sangue de Jesus, mas foi preciso a cruz para tornar isso possível. Também é preciso uma cruz para encontrarmos esse poder. E disse a todos: Se alguém quer vir após mim, negue-se a si mesmo, tome diariamente a sua cruz e siga-me. Pois quem quiser salvar a sua vida a perderá; mas quem perder a sua vida por minha causa, esse a salvará –Lucas 9:23-24. Sim, parece loucura para os que perecem, mas, para os que creem, é o Poder de Deus.

Do you want to have a good life? What is there that you believe you need to experience or accomplish so you can truly enjoy life? Many people’s main goal in life is to seek pleasure and to have fun. Much time and money are spent to achieve this. But do we accomplish it? In our natural mind we think that the circumstances need to be just right to please us. But we all know that circumstances are never ideal all the time. So, we can’t depend on those for our happiness. We need something bigger than that. Or Someone.

Obviously, we know that God alone is never changing and always faithful. Another thing about God is that He is sovereign. In other words, He’s in charge. But we like our independence; we like things to happen in a way that feels good to us. When life doesn’t happen that way, we are brought to a decision. Will we accept all of God—both His unchangeableness and His sovereignty—or will we fight to have our own way in our pursuit of a good life?

The root of joy is with God Himself. This is because He created us for Himself. He created us to bring pleasure to Himself, but we think we need to bring pleasure to ourselves. It started in the garden of Eden when the serpent convinced Eve that pleasing herself was more important than pleasing God. Since then, humans have been at war, both within their own hearts and without, with other folks. All in the effort of trying to find pleasure for themselves, yet not finding it because they were created to please God.

The solution for this war is found in James 4. It’s simple: submit to God. Humble yourselves before Him. This is not too much for Him to ask of us, because He is sovereign. He created us, so He has the say in how we live. If we will truly find enjoyment in life, it will be by putting our own life and desires on the cross and becoming one with God and His original purpose for us. Rather than it being restrictive, this opens up a world of opportunities and possibilities. It doesn’t mean we have to do things because God wants us to. Becoming one with God means that what He wants us to do is also what we want to do.

Worship and Gratitude

When we are one with God, our whole perspective changes. Instead of pining over all the things that aren’t ideal, we begin to see the many things that are true blessings. We can have a heart of worship and gratitude for all the good things that we do experience. We are able to see how unworthy we really are. We didn’t deserve anything good, but God has still given us so many things to enjoy!

Living in the Present

As young ladies, we have a tendency to dream, to live in a future that is idealistic and pleasant. We sometimes struggle to live in the present imperfect reality and find joy in it. But when God’s will becomes our will then true joy happens, because we are fulfilling His purpose for us.

We can learn to experience joy in any circumstance, even in mundane life. We’re afraid of living a boring life. We want it to be exciting. But He wants us to please Him, and when we do, we experience joy no matter the circumstances. However, we are also then available for Him to use in service to His Kingdom, and He may call us to opportunities that are exciting. But we won’t be effective in the exciting missions unless we have learned to be submitted to His will in everyday life.

Relationships

When we are finding joy and contentment in where God has us in the present, we are able to focus on developing solid, upbuilding relationships with those who are in our lives right now. God has created us as social people, and good relationships will bring true enjoyment to us. God is also able to use us in reaching out to other people. When we are one with Him, our focus is no longer on ourselves but on others. The life of God can flow through us and both show others the way to Him and give us joy and fulfillment in doing it.

Emotions

Another tendency we have is to let our emotions control us. And they will run wild if we are looking to our circumstances to give us pleasure. We will end up on a roller coaster of feelings dictated by whatever is happening at the moment. And then we escape to the dream world, which only distorts our view of reality even more. But God is steadfast, and when we are one with Him, He imparts to us stability and rest. And we are able to experience ever present joy—even in ever changing circumstances.

Let us continue to become ever more one with Him. And He will give us heavenly sunlight all of our journey, unchanged by circumstances on earth and realized in full when we see Him face to face. …in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore –Psalm 16:11.

کیا آپ اچھی زندگی گزارنا چاہتی ہیں؟ آپ کے خیال میں آپ کو کن چیزوں کا تجربہ کرنے یا کون سے کام انجام دینے کی ضرورت ہے تاکہ آپ واقعی زندگی سے لطف اندوز ہو سکیں؟ بہت سے لوگوں کی زندگی کا بنیادی مقصد خوشی کی تلاش اور تفریح کرنا ہوتا ہے۔ اسے حاصل کرنے کے لیے بہت وقت اور پیسہ خرچ کیا جاتا ہے۔ لیکن کیا ہم یہ حاصل کر پاتے ہیں؟ ہماری فطری سوچ یہ ہے کہ ہمیں خوش کرنے کے لیے حالات بالکل سازگار ہونے چاہییں۔ لیکن ہم سب جانتے ہیں کہ حالات ہر وقت مثالی نہیں ہوتے۔ اس لیے ہم اپنی خوشی کے لیے ان پر بھروسا نہیں کر سکتے۔ ہمیں اس سے بڑھ کر کسی چیز کی ضرورت ہے۔ یا کسی ہستی کی۔

ظاہر ہے، ہم جانتے ہیں کہ صرف خدا ہی کبھی نہیں بدلتا اور ہمیشہ وفادار رہتا ہے۔ خدا کی ایک اور بات یہ ہے کہ وہ صاحبِ اختیار ہے۔ دوسرے لفظوں میں، اختیار اسی کے ہاتھ میں ہے۔ لیکن ہمیں اپنی خودمختاری پسند ہے؛ ہم چاہتے ہیں کہ چیزیں اس طرح ہوں جو ہمیں اچھا محسوس کرائے۔ جب زندگی اس طرح نہیں گزرتی تو ہمیں ایک فیصلہ کرنا پڑتا ہے۔ کیا ہم خدا کو مکمل طور پر قبول کریں گے—اس کی بے تغیری اور اس کے اختیار دونوں کو—یا اچھی زندگی کی جستجو میں اپنی مرضی چلانے کے لیے جدوجہد کریں گے؟

خوشی کی جڑ خود خدا میں ہے۔ اس کی وجہ یہ ہے کہ اس نے ہمیں اپنے لیے پیدا کیا۔ اس نے ہمیں اپنی خوشنودی کے لیے پیدا کیا، لیکن ہم سمجھتے ہیں کہ ہمیں خود اپنی خوشنودی کا سامان کرنا چاہیے۔ اس کا آغاز باغِ عدن میں ہوا، جب سانپ نے حوا کو یقین دلایا کہ خود کو خوش کرنا، خدا کو خوش کرنے سے زیادہ اہم ہے۔ تب سے انسان آپس میں بھی اور اپنے دلوں میں بھی جنگ کرتے آئے ہیں۔ یہ سب اپنے لیے خوشی تلاش کرنے کی کوشش میں ہے، مگر وہ اسے پا نہیں پاتے، کیونکہ انہیں خدا کو خوش کرنے کے لیے پیدا کیا گیا تھا۔

اس جنگ کا حل یعقوب 4 میں ملتا ہے۔ یہ سادہ ہے: خدا کے تابع ہو جاؤ۔ اس کے حضور فروتنی اختیار کرو۔ ہم سے یہ مطالبہ کرنا اس کے لیے کوئی بڑی بات نہیں، کیونکہ وہ صاحبِ اختیار ہے۔ اس نے ہمیں پیدا کیا، اس لیے ہماری زندگی کیسے گزرے، اس کا فیصلہ کرنے کا حق اسی کو ہے۔ اگر ہم واقعی زندگی سے لطف اندوز ہونا چاہتے ہیں تو یہ اپنی زندگی اور خواہشات کو صلیب پر چڑھانے اور خدا اور ہمارے لیے اس کے اصل مقصد کے ساتھ متحد ہونے سے ممکن ہوگا۔ یہ پابندی لگانے کے بجائے مواقع اور امکانات کی ایک دنیا کھول دیتا ہے۔ اس کا مطلب یہ نہیں کہ ہمیں کام صرف اس لیے کرنے ہیں کہ خدا چاہتا ہے۔ خدا کے ساتھ متحد ہونے کا مطلب ہے کہ جو کچھ وہ ہم سے کروانا چاہتا ہے، ہم بھی وہی کرنا چاہتے ہیں۔

عبادت اور شکرگزاری

جب ہم خدا کے ساتھ متحد ہوتے ہیں تو ہمارا پورا نقطۂ نظر بدل جاتا ہے۔ ان سب چیزوں پر افسوس کرنے کے بجائے جو مثالی نہیں ہیں، ہم ان بہت سی چیزوں کو دیکھنے لگتے ہیں جو واقعی برکتیں ہیں۔ ہم ان تمام اچھی چیزوں کے لیے جن کا ہم تجربہ کرتے ہیں، عبادت اور شکرگزاری کا دل رکھ سکتے ہیں۔ ہم یہ دیکھ پاتے ہیں کہ ہم درحقیقت کتنے نااہل ہیں۔ ہم کسی اچھی چیز کے مستحق نہیں تھے، پھر بھی خدا نے ہمیں لطف اندوز ہونے کے لیے بہت سی چیزیں عطا کی ہیں!

حال میں جینا

نوجوان خواتین کی حیثیت سے ہمارا رجحان خواب دیکھنے اور ایک مثالی اور خوشگوار مستقبل میں جینے کا ہوتا ہے۔ کبھی کبھی ہمیں حال کی نامکمل حقیقت میں جینے اور اس میں خوشی پانے میں مشکل پیش آتی ہے۔ لیکن جب خدا کی مرضی ہماری مرضی بن جاتی ہے تو حقیقی خوشی حاصل ہوتی ہے، کیونکہ ہم ہمارے لیے اس کے مقصد کو پورا کر رہے ہوتے ہیں۔

ہم ہر حال میں، حتیٰ کہ روزمرہ کی معمولی زندگی میں بھی، خوشی کا تجربہ کرنا سیکھ سکتے ہیں۔ ہمیں ڈر ہے کہ ہماری زندگی بے مزہ ہوگی۔ ہم چاہتے ہیں کہ وہ پُر جوش ہو۔ لیکن وہ چاہتا ہے کہ ہم اسے خوش کریں، اور جب ہم ایسا کرتے ہیں تو حالات جیسے بھی ہوں، ہم خوشی کا تجربہ کرتے ہیں۔ تاہم، پھر ہم اس کے لیے اس کی بادشاہی کی خدمت میں استعمال ہونے کے لیے بھی دستیاب ہوتے ہیں، اور وہ ہمیں ایسے مواقع کی طرف بلا سکتا ہے جو پُر جوش ہوں۔ لیکن جب تک ہم روزمرہ کی زندگی میں اس کی مرضی کے تابع رہنا نہیں سیکھ لیتے، ہم ان پُر جوش مہمات میں مؤثر نہیں ہوں گے۔

تعلقات

جب ہم اس جگہ اور حالت میں خوشی اور اطمینان پاتے ہیں جہاں خدا نے ہمیں حال میں رکھا ہے، تو ہم ان لوگوں کے ساتھ مضبوط اور ایک دوسرے کی ترقی کا باعث بننے والے تعلقات قائم کرنے پر توجہ دے سکتے ہیں جو اس وقت ہماری زندگی میں ہیں۔ خدا نے ہمیں سماجی مخلوق بنایا ہے، اور اچھے تعلقات ہمیں حقیقی خوشی دیں گے۔ خدا ہمیں دوسرے لوگوں تک پہنچنے کے لیے بھی استعمال کر سکتا ہے۔ جب ہم اس کے ساتھ متحد ہوتے ہیں تو ہماری توجہ اپنی ذات پر نہیں بلکہ دوسروں پر ہوتی ہے۔ خدا کی زندگی ہم میں سے گزر سکتی ہے، دوسروں کو اس تک پہنچنے کا راستہ دکھا سکتی ہے اور ایسا کرنے میں ہمیں خوشی اور تکمیل بخش سکتی ہے۔

جذبات

ہمارا ایک اور رجحان یہ ہے کہ ہم اپنے جذبات کو اپنے اوپر حاوی ہونے دیتے ہیں۔ اور اگر ہم اپنی خوشی کے لیے حالات پر نظر رکھیں تو جذبات بے قابو ہو جائیں گے۔ ہم احساسات کے ایسے جھولے میں پھنس جائیں گے جن کا رخ اس وقت پیش آنے والی باتوں کے مطابق بدلتا رہے گا۔ پھر ہم خوابوں کی دنیا میں پناہ لیتے ہیں، جو حقیقت کے بارے میں ہمارے تصور کو اور بھی مسخ کر دیتی ہے۔ لیکن خدا ثابت قدم ہے، اور جب ہم اس کے ساتھ متحد ہوتے ہیں تو وہ ہمیں استحکام اور آرام بخشتا ہے۔ اور ہم ہر وقت موجود خوشی کا تجربہ کر سکتے ہیں—یہاں تک کہ ایسے حالات میں بھی جو مسلسل بدلتے رہتے ہیں۔

آئیے، ہم اس کے ساتھ مزید سے مزید متحد ہوتے جائیں۔ اور وہ ہمارے پورے سفر میں ہمیں آسمانی دھوپ عطا کرے گا، جو زمین کے حالات سے نہیں بدلے گی اور اس وقت پوری طرح آشکار ہوگی جب ہم اسے روبرو دیکھیں گے۔ …تیرے حضور میں کامل شادمانی ہے؛ تیرے دہنے ہاتھ میں ہمیشہ کی مسرتیں ہیں—زبور 16:11۔

The grinding sound of truck tires driving in the gravel lane filled the air as I sat in the house reading an encyclopedia. Leaping to my feet, I peered out the window.

Mom had just returned from the produce auction in Lewisburg with some peaches.

Slamming the door behind me, I raced across the thick green grass and leaped onto the bed of our truck.

On the back of the pickup sat four boxes of peaches. Grinning triumphantly, I reached into a box searching until I found a ripe one. Just before I bit into it, Mom said, “Steven, don’t eat any peaches; it will ruin your supper.” Sadly, I tossed the peach back into the box and then slowly walked away.

Several hours later, Dad called from the veal barn. “Steven, go pick the radishes for our Friday market produce stand.”

After picking, washing, and banding the radishes, I carried them into the old cooler which was inside the red bank barn. The cooler door squeaked as I yanked it open. There along the cooler walls sat the four boxes of the tantalizing peaches. I stared at the peaches, my mouth watering. I quickly set the radishes down. Oh, how good they looked. Surely a little peach wouldn’t ruin a starving ten-year-old’s supper. Mom wouldn’t know if I only took one peach.

Deep in my heart, a battle between right and wrong started to develop. I knew that sneaking was wrong, but those peaches looked way too good.

After devouring the peach, I scanned the dark interior of the barn for a good hiding place to put the peach stone. I looked across the onions, laying on drying racks, to the open hay bale. The only problem was that if I put the stone under the hay someone could find it. Then I spied the holes in the barn siding boards on the west side of the barn. If I pushed the stone through one of those holes it would land beside the road. Then, if someone saw it, they would think that it came from a passing vehicle.

I jammed the stone through the hole, peering out as it fell beside the road. At that split second, I felt a searing pain on my forehead. Frantically, I sprang back. There above the hole hung a yellow jacket nest. Then I saw the culprit as it hovered over me trying to sting me again. I sprinted out the barn door, slamming the door into the yellow jacket’s face.

That evening my forehead swelled like a balloon, making it difficult to look out of my eyes.

A few hours later, everyone else went to bed. I laid on the couch so that Mom could occasionally check up on me during the night. But I just couldn’t fall asleep. My face was inflamed and itchy, but all that I could think about was the guilt and remorse of what I had done.

After several agonizing hours, I gathered the courage to slide off the couch and tiptoed over to my parent’s bedroom. Awakening my parents, I told them the whole story… how I ate the peach, then tried to hide the stone, and how I had gotten stung.

My parents forgave me, deciding that this was one lesson that I wouldn’t soon forget. Walking back to the couch with a light heart, I laid down, and quickly fell into a peaceful sleep.

Den malende lyden av lastebildekk som kjørte på grusveien, fylte luften mens jeg satt inne i huset og leste i et leksikon. Jeg spratt opp på beina og kikket ut av vinduet.

Mamma hadde nettopp kommet tilbake fra frukt- og grøntauksjonen i Lewisburg med noen ferskener.

Jeg smelte døren igjen bak meg, løp tvers over det tykke, grønne gresset og hoppet opp på lasteplanet på pickupen vår.

Bak på pickupen sto det fire kasser med ferskener. Jeg smilte triumferende og stakk hånden ned i en kasse og lette til jeg fant en moden fersken. Like før jeg bet i den, sa mamma: «Steven, ikke spis noen ferskener; da ødelegger du middagen.» Jeg kastet ferskenen trist tilbake i kassen og gikk så langsomt bort.

Flere timer senere ropte pappa fra kalvefjøset. «Steven, gå og plukk reddikene til frukt- og grøntboden vår på fredagsmarkedet.»

Da jeg hadde plukket, vasket og buntet reddikene, bar jeg dem inn i det gamle kjølerommet inne i den røde låven. Døren til kjølerommet knirket da jeg dro den opp. Der, langs veggene i kjølerommet, sto de fire kassene med de fristende ferskenene. Jeg stirret på dem mens munnen løp i vann. Jeg satte raskt reddikene fra meg. Å, så gode de så ut. En liten fersken kunne vel ikke ødelegge middagen for en utsultet tiåring. Mamma ville ikke merke det hvis jeg bare tok én fersken.

Dypt inne i hjertet mitt begynte det å utspille seg en kamp mellom rett og galt. Jeg visste at det var galt å snike seg til det, men ferskenene så altfor gode ut.

Etter at jeg hadde slukt ferskenen, speidet jeg rundt i den mørke låven etter et godt gjemmested for steinen. Jeg så forbi løkene som lå på tørkestativene, bort på den åpne høyballen. Problemet var bare at hvis jeg la steinen under høyet, kunne noen finne den. Så fikk jeg øye på hullene i bordkledningen på vestsiden av låven. Hvis jeg dyttet steinen gjennom et av hullene, ville den lande ved siden av veien. Hvis noen så den, ville de tro at den hadde falt av et kjøretøy som passerte.

Jeg presset steinen gjennom hullet og så ut mens den falt ned ved veien. I samme øyeblikk kjente jeg en brennende smerte i pannen. Jeg fór forskrekket bakover. Over hullet hang det et vepsebol. Så fikk jeg øye på synderen, som svevde over meg og prøvde å stikke meg igjen. Jeg spurtet ut gjennom låvedøren og smalt døren i ansiktet på vepsen.

Den kvelden hovnet pannen min opp som en ballong, og det ble vanskelig å se.

Noen timer senere gikk alle de andre og la seg. Jeg lå på sofaen, så mamma kunne se til meg av og til i løpet av natten. Men jeg klarte ikke å sovne. Ansiktet var betent og klødde, men alt jeg kunne tenke på, var skyldfølelsen og angeren over det jeg hadde gjort.

Etter flere pinefulle timer samlet jeg mot til å gli ned fra sofaen og liste meg bort til soverommet til foreldrene mine. Jeg vekket dem og fortalte hele historien … hvordan jeg hadde spist ferskenen, prøvd å gjemme steinen og blitt stukket.

Foreldrene mine tilga meg og bestemte seg for at dette var en lekse jeg ikke kom til å glemme med det første. Med lett hjerte gikk jeg tilbake til sofaen, la meg ned og sovnet snart en fredelig søvn.
