After living in Haiti for several months, I finally had the opportunity to go visit the local witch doctor. As I walked up his long drive, I passed many statues and satanic symbols. It was eerie for sure. As I approached the voodoo temple that was connected to his house, I saw him standing there watching me approach. My heart began to race; I knew he was a powerful man. Then he began to laugh. The closer I got, the louder he laughed. I was a bit puzzled until I realized that many people from the village were following me up the lane. They were very interested in what was about to transpire. I approached the man, not knowing what would happen next.

“Are you a pastor?” he asked.

“Yes, I am,” was my reply. Again, he began to laugh loudly.

“You pastors are all the same,” he proclaimed. “You want everyone to come to your churches, but your churches have no power! When one of your people gets sick, they come to me. No power, you Christians!”

A heavy burden overtook me, and I explained to him how I agreed with him, but that the real church of Jesus Christ would always have power. The Bible actually says that the very gates of Hell shall not prevail against it.

This was the beginning of a very interesting relationship, but I will never forget those words—most certainly from the devil himself—“You Christians have no power!”

I have since traveled to hundreds of churches and need to agree with that voodoo priest. The Christian churches are lacking power. But why? We know that God is power. We have many things figured out, we look good and sound good, but do we still have the power of God in our churches?

In the Old Testament we have many examples of power and the lack of power. We can also learn how we receive power, and why we lose it.

In Joshua, chapter 6, we have the familiar account of the children of Israel and the city of Jericho. God tells Joshua and all the men of war to compass the city, and walk around it once every day, for six days. Then on the seventh day they were to march around the city not just once, but seven times. After they had completed the seven trips around the city, the priests were to blow their trumpets.

We know what happened when Joshua obeyed each command—those thick, impenetrable walls came tumbling down. God also gave Joshua a strict command about what the men should and should not do. They were to keep themselves from everything that God had pronounced was accursed; all the silver, gold, and vessels were to be consecrated into the treasury of the Lord; no man was to take any of the spoil.

However, Achan saw some nice things that he desired. He slipped them into his armor, then later hid them under his tent, and no one saw a thing.

After this great victory, Joshua sent spies to the next city, Ai, to discover how well the city was fortified. The men returned and told Joshua not to send all the men to Ai, for there were only a few defenders protecting the city.

However, the men of Ai smote the children of Israel and chased them away. Moreover, Joshua rent his clothes and cried out to God. Then God replied that there was sin in the camp of Israel.

In the Old Testament, the children of Israel are normally representative of the church of Jesus Christ today. Can we not glean much from this account? When there was no sin in the camp (or in the church) God’s people had complete victory; they lost not one. They did many wonderful things, they destroyed all their enemies around them, and they lived in COMPLETE victory. However, as soon as sin entered into their midst, even a small sin done by one man, they lost their power. They no longer had victory over their enemies.

What follows is a graphic description of how the children of Israel dealt with the sin that had entered the camp. It was totally destroyed.

And Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan the son of Zerah, and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor … And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire… –Joshua 7:24-26.

In this account it is clear why God’s people had lost their power—they had sin in the camp. It is also clear what it took for them to regain that power which they had lost—get rid of the sin.

In chapter 8 we read of the power being restored to Israel instantly after the sin was dealt with. Again, they lived in victory!

Another passage in the Old Testament that speaks of this topic is in Leviticus chapters 13 and 14. Leprosy was a strange disease. If one were to get leprosy, it was easily spread. Thus, there needed to be some strict guidelines regarding how to deal with the disease. The priest was to examine very closely to see if the person in question indeed had leprosy or not. If the priest was unsure, he would shut the person up in a room for seven days then examine him again. If it was determined that the person had leprosy, then they were sent outside of the city.

As Paul addresses the church in Corinth, he tells them that he has heard there is sin in the church. He seems surprised that the church is taking it so casually, …Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump? Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened… –1 Corinthians 5:6-7. Later he tells the church …Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person –1 Corinthians 5:13.

Let’s say that you heard the news that leprosy was again a problem in your village. This flesh-destroying disease had made a comeback and many from your village were now infected. Then you’re sitting in church on Sunday morning, when the doors open, and a man enters with skin and flesh hanging from his extremities. He is badly infected, but he does not seem to know it. What would you do? What if he wanted to come sit by you? What if he wanted to talk to your children? I think we all know what we would do; we would not allow him into our midst. We love our people, our families too much for that.

What about sin? Do we allow sin to come and join us? Do we take it seriously? What is worse, being infected with a flesh-destroying disease, or being infected by a soul-destroying sin? Remember, the wages of sin is death—spiritual death; eternal death. If we would treat sin in the same way as we would the disease (and we should) then our churches would once again have Holy Spirit power.

The Bible says …ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth –Acts 1:8.

We have already seen how sin separates us from the power of God, and we have also seen how God wants to give us power. He wants us to have victory over the enemy—the devil, the world, and flesh. However, something seems to be happening in our churches—we are allowing sin to enter. It is common to hear a preacher say, “No one is perfect.” Or, “We all sin.” Oh, that we would realize the damage these statements can make. Jesus came to save us from ALL sin; ALL unrighteousness. If we are left to continue in our sin, what has Jesus done for us?

I hear about churches drifting into the world. They gradually let go of convictions and allow some new fashion and pomp of the world to enter. Something that I hear little of is churches falling apart because of gross sin, such as fornication or drunkenness. The enemy of our souls, desires for us to become lukewarm. He wants the church to lose its power, to start living like everyone else. Here in Haiti, there are churches everywhere. On Sunday mornings starting at five o’clock in the morning, I start hearing the churches singing and worshipping. However, where are all those people on Monday morning? They are mixing right back into the world from whence they have come.

I was recently talking to a very wealthy Haitian man who owned resorts and properties all over Haiti. I asked him if he was a Christian. (I wanted to start a conversation.) I could tell that he wanted to say yes; instead, he became frustrated and said no. I asked him why not. He said exactly what I thought he would say. “I have desired to become a Christian, I’ve gone to all the churches around here, but I don’t feel they have anything to offer me. I have money; I have physical blessings; but that seems to be all that they are seeking for.”

If our churches today would refuse to settle for anything less than the infilling, empowering, and leading of the Holy Spirit, a full dose of heavenly power, then we would be able to offer something that would appeal to the lost around us. I believe this is exactly what the world is looking for; they are seeking for something better, something supernatural. What if we would settle for nothing less? What if we would stay on our knees until the power of God came back? What if we would again weep for our souls, and the souls of others?

I was working closely with a vicious gang leader who lived in the neighboring village. He was hard, but God had led him to me. For seven long months we met and communicated, I wanted him to catch a glimpse of the power of God; I wanted God to save him. He would often get drunk and threaten to kill me; I would continue to point him to the Savior. He and his gang came over one day to stop a work project, saying that they now owned the land. They brandished their guns and threatened all that were there. I explained to him that God owned the land. He said, “That is fine; tell God to come down here, and I’ll cut off His head.” I was troubled by this remark and asked him if he understood the power of the God he just threatened. One afternoon I drove to his house, and we sat outside and talked. God led me to preach a bold message to him that day. “You need to give up this gang life. God wants to save you, and change your heart!” He seemed very sober as I continued, “You never know when someone will come here and kill you! You can’t control that, but my friend you can control where you go after you are dead!” I then reminded him of the terrible thing he had said days before.

While we were still talking, two men from a neighboring gang approached on motorbikes. They were heavily armed; they had come at that very moment to kill him, but they saw me talking to him and waited for me to leave. “You have a wife and children, are you not tired of this life? God has something so much better for you!” I was pleading, pleading for his soul. It was his very last opportunity, death waited at the door. As I left I told him that I would be back.

After the shooting I rushed back, but it was over… all over.

When we live in the power of the resurrection, the power of the Almighty God, it is then that He works! I feel there is so much work to be done before the Lord returns, but God’s people are too busy, we do not have time.

Do we fear talking about the power of God and the Holy Ghost simply because the Pentecostal movement has twisted what the Bible teaches? God help us.

When we call out to God for salvation, we are doing so because we know we need to be saved; converted. We also know that we cannot save ourselves, so we ask God to help us. Then when God helps us, we are able to do things that we could not do before! Angry people are angry no more. People that could not control their lust now have control. Selfish people begin to put others first. Shy people begin to preach with boldness. Greedy people begin to give to others. God does a work that counselors and doctors cannot do, He changes the very core of a person, and then all things become new. We now live for something far better than what this world has to give; we rise above by the power of God and show this sin-sick world there is a better way!

All through the Bible, God’s people did supernatural things; they did not settle for just a nice life. They sought something bigger, something better. There is power in the blood of Jesus, but it took the cross to make that a possibility. It also takes a cross for us to find that power. And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24. Yes, it seems foolish to those that perish, but to those that believe, it is the Power of God.

Après avoir vécu plusieurs mois en Haïti, j’ai enfin eu l’occasion d’aller rendre visite au sorcier local. En remontant sa longue allée, je suis passé devant de nombreuses statues et des symboles sataniques. C’était assurément sinistre. En approchant du temple vaudou qui était attenant à sa maison, je l’ai vu debout, qui me regardait venir. Mon cœur s’est mis à battre la chamade ; je savais que c’était un homme puissant. Puis il s’est mis à rire. Plus je m’approchais, plus il riait fort. J’étais quelque peu perplexe jusqu’à ce que je comprenne que beaucoup d’habitants du village me suivaient sur le chemin. Ils étaient très intéressés par ce qui allait se passer. Je me suis approché de l’homme, sans savoir ce qui allait arriver ensuite.

« Êtes-vous pasteur ? » m’a-t-il demandé.

« Oui, je le suis », lui ai-je répondu. De nouveau, il s’est mis à rire bruyamment.

« Vous, les pasteurs, vous êtes tous pareils, a-t-il déclaré. Vous voulez que tout le monde vienne dans vos églises, mais vos églises n’ont aucun pouvoir ! Quand quelqu’un de votre communauté tombe malade, il vient me voir. Vous n’avez aucun pouvoir, vous les chrétiens ! »

Un lourd fardeau m’a envahi, et je lui ai expliqué que j’étais d’accord avec lui, mais que la véritable Église de Jésus-Christ aurait toujours du pouvoir. La Bible dit en fait que les portes mêmes de l’enfer ne prévaudront pas contre elle.

Ce fut le début d’une relation très intéressante, mais je n’oublierai jamais ces paroles — venant très certainement du diable lui-même — : « Vous, les chrétiens, vous n’avez aucun pouvoir ! »

Depuis, j’ai visité des centaines d’églises et je dois reconnaître que ce prêtre vaudou avait raison. Les églises chrétiennes manquent de puissance. Mais pourquoi ? Nous savons que Dieu est puissance. Nous avons compris bien des choses, nous avons belle apparence et nous nous exprimons bien, mais avons-nous encore la puissance de Dieu dans nos églises ?

Dans l’Ancien Testament, nous trouvons de nombreux exemples de puissance et d’absence de puissance. Nous pouvons aussi apprendre comment recevoir la puissance et pourquoi nous la perdons.

Dans Josué, chapitre 6, nous avons le récit bien connu des enfants d’Israël et de la ville de Jéricho. Dieu dit à Josué et à tous les hommes de guerre de faire le tour de la ville une fois par jour, pendant six jours. Puis, le septième jour, ils devaient faire le tour de la ville non pas une seule fois, mais sept fois. Après avoir fait les sept tours de la ville, les prêtres devaient sonner de leurs trompettes.

Nous savons ce qui s’est passé lorsque Josué a obéi à chacun des commandements : ces épaisses murailles réputées imprenables se sont écroulées. Dieu donna aussi à Josué un ordre strict concernant ce que les hommes devaient et ne devaient pas faire. Ils devaient se garder de tout ce que Dieu avait déclaré voué à la destruction ; tout l’argent, l’or et les objets devaient être consacrés au trésor du Seigneur ; aucun homme ne devait prendre quoi que ce soit du butin.

Cependant, Acan vit de belles choses qu’il désirait. Il les glissa sous son armure, puis les cacha plus tard sous sa tente, et personne ne vit rien.

Après cette grande victoire, Josué envoya des espions à la ville suivante, Aï, pour découvrir à quel point elle était fortifiée. Les hommes revinrent et dirent à Josué de ne pas envoyer tous les hommes à Aï, car il n’y avait que quelques défenseurs pour protéger la ville.

Pourtant, les hommes d’Aï battirent les enfants d’Israël et les mirent en fuite. De plus, Josué déchira ses vêtements et cria vers Dieu. Alors Dieu lui répondit qu’il y avait du péché dans le camp d’Israël.

Dans l’Ancien Testament, les enfants d’Israël représentent généralement l’Église de Jésus-Christ aujourd’hui. Ne pouvons-nous pas tirer beaucoup de leçons de ce récit ? Tant qu’il n’y avait pas de péché dans le camp (ou dans l’Église), le peuple de Dieu remportait une victoire totale ; il ne perdait aucun homme. Il accomplissait de grandes choses, détruisait tous ses ennemis autour de lui et vivait dans une VICTOIRE TOTALE. Cependant, dès que le péché entra dans son sein, même un petit péché commis par un seul homme, il perdit sa puissance. Il ne remportait plus la victoire sur ses ennemis.

Ce qui suit est une description frappante de la manière dont les enfants d’Israël traitèrent le péché qui était entré dans le camp. Il fut entièrement éliminé.

Josué, et tout Israël avec lui, prirent Acan, fils de Zérach, l’argent, le vêtement, le lingot d’or, ses fils et ses filles, ses bœufs, ses ânes, ses brebis, sa tente et tout ce qui lui appartenait ; et ils les conduisirent dans la vallée d’Acor… Et tout Israël le lapida, puis les brûla au feu… –Josué 7:24-26.

Dans ce récit, la raison pour laquelle le peuple de Dieu avait perdu sa puissance est évidente : il y avait du péché dans le camp. Il est tout aussi clair ce qu’il lui fallut faire pour retrouver cette puissance perdue : éliminer le péché.

Au chapitre 8, nous lisons que la puissance fut immédiatement rendue à Israël après que le péché eut été traité. De nouveau, ils vécurent dans la victoire !

Un autre passage de l’Ancien Testament traite de ce sujet : les chapitres 13 et 14 du Lévitique. La lèpre était une maladie étrange. Si quelqu’un contractait la lèpre, elle se propageait facilement. Il fallait donc des directives strictes sur la manière de traiter cette maladie. Le prêtre devait examiner très attentivement la personne concernée afin de déterminer si elle avait effectivement la lèpre ou non. S’il n’en était pas certain, il enfermait la personne dans une pièce pendant sept jours, puis l’examinait de nouveau. S’il était établi qu’elle avait la lèpre, elle était alors envoyée hors de la ville.

Lorsque Paul s’adresse à l’Église de Corinthe, il leur dit qu’il a appris qu’il y a du péché dans l’Église. Il semble surpris que l’Église prenne cela avec autant de légèreté : …Ne savez-vous pas qu’un peu de levain fait lever toute la pâte ? Purgez-vous donc du vieux levain, afin que vous soyez une pâte nouvelle, puisque vous êtes sans levain… –1 Corinthiens 5:6-7. Plus tard, il dit à l’Église : …Ôtez le méchant du milieu de vous –1 Corinthiens 5:13.

Supposons que vous appreniez que la lèpre est de nouveau un problème dans votre village. Cette maladie qui détruit la chair est réapparue et beaucoup d’habitants de votre village en sont maintenant atteints. Puis, un dimanche matin, vous êtes assis à l’église lorsque les portes s’ouvrent et qu’un homme entre, la peau et la chair pendantes aux extrémités de ses membres. Il est gravement atteint, mais ne semble pas s’en rendre compte. Que feriez-vous ? Et s’il voulait venir s’asseoir à côté de vous ? Et s’il voulait parler à vos enfants ? Je pense que nous savons tous ce que nous ferions : nous ne le laisserions pas se joindre à nous. Nous aimons trop les gens de notre communauté et nos familles pour cela.

Et le péché ? Le laissons-nous venir se joindre à nous ? Le prenons-nous au sérieux ? Qu’est-ce qui est pire : être atteint d’une maladie qui détruit la chair, ou être contaminé par un péché qui détruit l’âme ? Souvenez-vous : le salaire du péché, c’est la mort — la mort spirituelle, la mort éternelle. Si nous traitions le péché comme nous traiterions cette maladie (et nous le devrions), alors nos églises retrouveraient la puissance du Saint-Esprit.

La Bible dit… vous recevrez une puissance, le Saint-Esprit survenant sur vous, et vous serez mes témoins à Jérusalem, dans toute la Judée, dans la Samarie, et jusqu’aux extrémités de la terre –Actes 1:8.

Nous avons déjà vu comment le péché nous sépare de la puissance de Dieu, et nous avons aussi vu que Dieu veut nous donner sa puissance. Il veut que nous remportions la victoire sur l’ennemi — le diable, le monde et la chair. Pourtant, quelque chose semble se passer dans nos églises : nous laissons le péché y entrer. Il est courant d’entendre un prédicateur dire : « Personne n’est parfait. » Ou : « Nous péchons tous. » Oh, si seulement nous comprenions les dégâts que ces affirmations peuvent causer. Jésus est venu nous sauver de TOUT péché, de TOUTE injustice. Si nous sommes laissés à continuer dans notre péché, qu’a fait Jésus pour nous ?

J’entends parler d’églises qui dérivent vers le monde. Peu à peu, elles abandonnent leurs convictions et laissent entrer certaines nouvelles modes et le faste du monde. J’entends peu parler d’églises qui se désagrègent à cause de péchés graves, comme la fornication ou l’ivrognerie. L’ennemi de nos âmes désire que nous devenions tièdes. Il veut que l’Église perde sa puissance et commence à vivre comme tout le monde. Ici, en Haïti, il y a des églises partout. Le dimanche matin, dès cinq heures, je commence à entendre les églises chanter et louer Dieu. Pourtant, où sont tous ces gens le lundi matin ? Ils se mêlent de nouveau au monde dont ils sont sortis.

Je parlais récemment avec un Haïtien très riche qui possédait des centres de villégiature et des propriétés dans toute Haïti. Je lui ai demandé s’il était chrétien. (Je voulais engager la conversation.) Je voyais qu’il voulait répondre oui ; au lieu de cela, il s’est agacé et a répondu non. Je lui ai demandé pourquoi. Il a dit exactement ce que je pensais qu’il dirait : « J’ai voulu devenir chrétien, je suis allé dans toutes les églises du coin, mais je n’ai pas l’impression qu’elles aient quoi que ce soit à m’offrir. J’ai de l’argent ; j’ai des biens matériels ; mais on dirait que c’est tout ce qu’elles recherchent. »

Si nos églises aujourd’hui refusaient de se contenter de moins que la plénitude, la puissance et la direction du Saint-Esprit — d’une pleine mesure de la puissance céleste —, alors nous pourrions offrir quelque chose qui attirerait les perdus autour de nous. Je crois que c’est précisément ce que le monde recherche : il aspire à quelque chose de meilleur, à quelque chose de surnaturel. Et si nous refusions de nous contenter de moins ? Et si nous restions à genoux jusqu’à ce que la puissance de Dieu revienne ? Et si nous pleurions de nouveau pour nos âmes et pour celles des autres ?

Je travaillais en étroite collaboration avec un chef de gang violent qui vivait dans le village voisin. Il était endurci, mais Dieu l’avait conduit à moi. Pendant sept longs mois, nous nous sommes rencontrés et avons échangé. Je voulais qu’il entrevoie la puissance de Dieu ; je voulais que Dieu le sauve. Il s’enivrait souvent et menaçait de me tuer ; je continuais à lui montrer le Sauveur. Un jour, lui et sa bande sont venus interrompre un chantier, en disant que le terrain leur appartenait désormais. Ils brandissaient leurs armes et menaçaient tous ceux qui se trouvaient là. Je lui ai expliqué que le terrain appartenait à Dieu. Il a dit : « Très bien ; dis à Dieu de descendre ici, et je lui couperai la tête. » Cette remarque m’a troublé et je lui ai demandé s’il comprenait la puissance du Dieu qu’il venait de défier. Un après-midi, je suis allé en voiture chez lui, et nous nous sommes assis dehors pour parler. Ce jour-là, Dieu m’a poussé à lui prêcher un message hardi : « Tu dois renoncer à cette vie de gang. Dieu veut te sauver et changer ton cœur ! » Il semblait très sérieux tandis que je poursuivais : « Tu ne sais jamais quand quelqu’un va venir ici et te tuer ! Tu ne peux pas contrôler cela, mais mon ami, tu peux contrôler où tu iras après ta mort ! » Je lui ai alors rappelé la terrible chose qu’il avait dite quelques jours plus tôt.

Alors que nous parlions encore, deux hommes d’un gang voisin se sont approchés à moto. Ils étaient lourdement armés ; ils étaient venus à cet instant même pour le tuer, mais ils m’ont vu lui parler et ont attendu que je parte. « Tu as une femme et des enfants ; tu n’en as pas assez de cette vie ? Dieu a quelque chose de tellement meilleur pour toi ! » Je le suppliais, je suppliais pour son âme. C’était sa toute dernière occasion ; la mort attendait à la porte. En partant, je lui ai dit que je reviendrais.

Après la fusillade, je suis revenu en toute hâte, mais c’était fini… complètement fini.

C’est lorsque nous vivons dans la puissance de la résurrection, la puissance du Dieu tout-puissant, qu’Il agit ! Je sens qu’il y a tant de travail à accomplir avant le retour du Seigneur, mais le peuple de Dieu est trop occupé ; nous n’avons pas le temps.

Avons-nous peur de parler de la puissance de Dieu et du Saint-Esprit simplement parce que le mouvement pentecôtiste a déformé ce que la Bible enseigne ? Que Dieu nous vienne en aide.

Lorsque nous crions à Dieu pour être sauvés, nous le faisons parce que nous savons que nous avons besoin d’être sauvés, d’être convertis. Nous savons aussi que nous ne pouvons pas nous sauver nous-mêmes, alors nous demandons à Dieu de nous aider. Et lorsque Dieu nous aide, nous sommes capables de faire des choses que nous ne pouvions pas faire auparavant ! Les gens colériques ne le sont plus. Ceux qui ne parvenaient pas à maîtriser leur convoitise la maîtrisent maintenant. Les égoïstes commencent à faire passer les autres avant eux. Les personnes timides se mettent à prêcher avec assurance. Les avares commencent à donner aux autres. Dieu accomplit une œuvre que les conseillers et les médecins ne peuvent accomplir : Il transforme le cœur même d’une personne, et alors tout devient nouveau. Nous vivons désormais pour quelque chose de bien meilleur que ce que ce monde peut offrir ; par la puissance de Dieu, nous nous élevons au-dessus de tout cela et montrons à ce monde malade du péché qu’il existe une meilleure voie !

Tout au long de la Bible, le peuple de Dieu a accompli des choses surnaturelles ; il ne s’est pas contenté d’une vie agréable. Il aspirait à quelque chose de plus grand, de meilleur. Il y a de la puissance dans le sang de Jésus, mais il a fallu la croix pour rendre cela possible. Il faut aussi une croix pour que nous trouvions cette puissance. Et il dit à tous : Si quelqu’un veut venir après moi, qu’il renonce à lui-même, qu’il se charge chaque jour de sa croix, et qu’il me suive. Car celui qui voudra sauver sa vie la perdra, mais celui qui perdra sa vie à cause de moi la sauvera –Luc 9:23-24. Oui, cela semble insensé à ceux qui périssent, mais pour ceux qui croient, c’est la puissance de Dieu.

I rolled over in bed, listening to the sound of my pager going off. It couldn’t have been more than 15 minutes since I had dropped into bed from my last admission. I looked at the number on the pager. Yes, it was the Emergency Department again.

I attempted to rub the sleep out of my eyes and stir my still sleepy brain to wakefulness. I picked up the phone and dialed the ER. “Hey,” the ER doctor said. “I’ve got two admissions for you.”

“Oh,” I said sleepily.

“You sound tired,” he said, jokingly.

I was tired. After graduating from Medical School, doctors go through an intense training period called residency. The first two years of that training period involved overnight calls in the hospital. It wasn’t unusual to put in one hundred hours at the hospital in a week’s time.

Even when we weren’t on call, the days started early and went late. I often fought sleep as I was driving home from the hospital. I certainly learned a lot during that time, but I am also glad that those days are behind me.

Fatigue is part of the human condition. Everyone has had times when they struggled with tiredness. Maybe it was due to a job that needed to get done, a long trip, or sleepless nights due to a new baby in the family—whatever the difficulty, we determinedly push ourselves to make it through these challenging times.

From our childhood days we are taught that work is important. We need to be responsible and take care of the tasks that are set for us to do.

Work is ordained by God. In Genesis Chapter 2, God gave Adam the task of caring for the Garden of Eden. Later, in Deuteronomy 5:13, the Israelites were commanded to do all their work in six days and then rest the seventh day.

The New Testament gives a couple of more reasons to work. We are to work so we can provide for our families (see II Thessalonians 3:10). In addition, we are to work so we can give to others who are in need (see Ephesians 4:28).

God expects us to work and that we do it in a way that will glorify Him. However, we also have need of rest, which God made provision for as well.

God Exemplified Rest in the Creation

And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made –Genesis 2:2-3.

When God created the universe, including the earth and all it contains, it took Him just six days. Since God is God, we can be certain that He wasn’t tired at the end of this work. Yet, despite that fact, He took a day of rest and set it apart. He did it as an example for us.

Even though the law of the Sabbath would not be instituted for at least two thousand years, the precedent was set in Creation… Rest one day a week.

God Mandated Rest in the Law

Perhaps the thing that comes to mind first is the Sabbath Day laws that were given in Exodus 20:8-11. It was specifically commanded that the people were not to work on the Sabbath. And further, they were not to cause other people to work either.

Another law which seemed very much focused on the need for rest was the Year of Jubilee. In Leviticus 25, this law mandated that every seven years the land was to lie fallow for the whole year, slaves were to be released, land was to revert to its original family’s ownership, and debts were to be cancelled.

Within the Jubilee commands were certain promises. There was the promise of freedom—no matter how bad things had been the previous six years there would be a reset. It was a promise of inheritance—the things that had been lost and sold would be reclaimed. It was a promise of abundance—And if ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase: Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years –Leviticus 25:20-21. Most of all, it was a promise of rest from labor—for the people and the land.

These commands were not put on the people to afflict them. Rather, God gave them knowing that without them His people would not rest enough and would not take enough time to focus on Him, their Creator.

Each one of us needs times of rest, but we need to understand that keeping the Sabbath is not simply about abstinence from work. Our efforts at keeping the Sabbath must include both rest and worship and it must be emphasized with the presence of God in our lives, without distraction.

The New Testament did not Change the Need for Rest

One of the verses that comes to my mind when I think about rest, is a promise that Jesus gave. Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light –Matthew 11:28-30.

The biblical book of Hebrews also speaks of the importance of rest and of our entering into God’s rest. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrews 4:9-11.

It is important to see that the New Testament concept of rest is more than simply time off from work. True biblical peace is intrinsically intertwined with the concept of peace, even in the midst of a chaotic world. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. Jesus gave peace to His followers that allowed them to be at rest, even when they were dealing with high levels of stress.

This is a blessing, for it is not enough simply to take time off from our normal work. We need to have that peace and calm which a connection with Jesus offers. Without …the peace of God, which passeth all understanding… –Philippians 4:7, our time off will be just as unrestful as our time at work.

It is clear that God wants us to rest. He knows that we need it, not just for spiritual reasons, but also for our physical health.

******************************

The folks in charge of the French Revolution made an attempt to eliminate all the institutions of the past. It was a particularly godless endeavor and among other things, the new government decided to “reform” the calendar.

In 1793, they established a ten-day work week. Each month would have three weeks with one rest day in each of these ten-day weeks. Their goal, among other things, was to eliminate all religious holidays and the celebration of Sunday as a day of rest. They believed that more work would be done by having fewer days of rest each month.

This created a huge headache for watchmakers. They needed to somehow make watches that would support the details of these new decrees—each day would be ten hours long, each hour would contain one hundred minutes, and each minute would be 100 seconds long.

It turned out to be a disaster. The people hated the changes and productivity dropped considerably across France. Finally, in 1806, Napoleon abolished it and went back to the old calendar and the system of Sunday days of rest. This scientific “experiment” was over. It turns out that people need times of rest and recharging and that a seven-day week with one day off to rest is not just a Christian concept, it is something that is necessary for health and wellbeing.

The Soviet Union, under Joseph Stalin, also tried a similar experiment of eliminating Sunday rest, with similar results.

******************************

The week, as God created it, (with one day in seven for rest) is necessary for us to remain productive.

Rest Reduces Inflammation

Part of the problem that modern people face is that they deal with high levels stress hormones, like adrenaline and cortisol. These hormones increase blood pressure and pulse rates. They also increase levels of inflammation in our bodies.

Chronic inflammation is not healthy, but fortunately, rest really seems to help bring those hormone levels down a lot. A good night of sleep is essential for healing, precisely because it turns down these hormones and allows healing of overworked nerves and tissues.

Autoimmune diseases and pain levels improve when people get adequate levels of sleep. Blood pressure and heart conditions also benefit when a person gets adequate amounts of restorative sleep.

Rest Allows for Healing

Exercise is a good thing. Doctors recommend doing regular cardiovascular exercise because it is healthy for our hearts, minds, and overall wellbeing.

It is not wise to exercise every day. It too, raises stress hormone levels and does not give our bodies adequate times to heal. People who exercise too frequently and with too much intensity are much more likely to end up with nagging injuries, joint and muscle pain, and fatigue. One study found that it takes 72 hours after doing weight training for muscles to fully recover.

People who exercise ideally need one to two days off a week to let their bodies recover from the activity. The harder you are training, the more you need those times of rest. Even someone who is training intensively for something like a marathon needs to take periodic days with no running or they will injure themselves.

Rest Decreases Pain Levels

There have been many studies that looked at people’s reports of sleep and looked at things like chronic pain and tension headaches. At least 50 percent of people with insomnia also have chronic pain. Of course, it could simply be that people with chronic pain don’t sleep as well as people who don’t have that.

There have been several studies that looked at people’s pain tolerance after sleep deprivation. They found that even a single night of sleep deprivation was enough to make people feel pain more acutely.

Rest Improves Our Immune Systems

There have been several studies that looked at function of different parts of our immune systems and found that they work better when study participants have adequate levels of sleep. Probably the fact that inflammation levels are higher when we don’t rest, increases the risks of infection.

When we push ourselves too hard without rest it is hard on our immune systems. On the other hand, the best way to recover is to make certain that we get sufficient rest.

There are many other things that rest does. It helps improve mood. It can help with academic performance and memory tasks.

As with all things, moderation is key. Someone who does nothing but rest and sleep, is not going to have any better function than someone who sleeps well for seven hours a night, nor will they be very productive.

There are some basic rules that can help us with times of rest.

Rest Regularly

The message of the Sabbath is that we need to take regular, short periods of time to rest. The Jubilee Years tell us that we need less frequent, longer times to recharge. It takes effort and scheduling to make certain that these times are truly restful.

Maybe it is a bit like a car. You can only drive so far on a tank of gas. If you always wait until the warning light turns on to fill up that tank, eventually you will have this happen when you are too far from a gas station to fill up before you run out of gas. There is never a good time to run out of gas. In the same way, we need to periodically recharge our spiritual, emotional, and physical batteries. There is no reason to wait until warning signs show up that we desperately need to take a break.

Rest Takes Preparation

The story of the gift of manna in Exodus 16 tells us that manna came every day. The people could not keep it for a second day because it would spoil. However, on Fridays, they were to gather extra since the next day was a day of rest and no manna came on the Sabbath. Those who had not gathered extra the day before went hungry.

In the same way, it takes preparation to have these sorts of times. It won’t be easy, but it is important.

Do Healthy Things With Your Rest

There is a tendency when people are under stress to eat unhealthy things. When people are exhausted, they don’t usually feel like exercising or taking walks. These are the sorts of things that can really help recharge us, both physically and emotionally.

Once again, this takes some effort, but choosing healthy options is important for our well-being.

Focus on God

I have left this till the last, but it is the most important aspect of rest. True rest grows, not out of medication or even multiple vacations, but out of a heart that is filled with peace. The peace which passes understanding comes from a heart that is focused on God.

Our times of prayer and Bible reading should be times of rest. If we can eliminate distractions and the challenges of our work and home life and train our gaze on the One who matters most, we will receive a real blessing and the recharging that our spirits need.

I am afraid that many people struggle to find rest because they are not truly at peace. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrew 4:11. The rest here is one that is promised to those who persevere and receive God’s peace.

Conclusion

Life is about balance. There are times when we need to work and there are times as well when we should rest. Figuring out this balance is the challenge which each of us faces. What is certain, is that every 24-hour day will be completely full by the time we get to the end of it.

God sees us and our limitations and desires for us to achieve this balance between our work and our times of rest. If we can only focus ourselves on Him, we will receive guidance in this balance.

Most of all, we will receive a peace that is without price, that will allow us to find rest—even during a storm.

Je me suis retourné dans mon lit en entendant mon téléavertisseur sonner. Il ne devait pas s’être écoulé plus de 15 minutes depuis que je m’étais couché après ma dernière admission. J’ai regardé le numéro affiché sur le téléavertisseur. Oui, c’était encore le service des urgences.

J’ai essayé de me frotter les yeux pour en chasser le sommeil et de réveiller mon cerveau encore embrumé. J’ai décroché le téléphone et appelé les urgences. « Hé, m’a dit le médecin des urgences. J’ai deux admissions pour vous. »

« Oh », ai-je répondu d’une voix ensommeillée.

« Vous avez l’air fatigué », a-t-il dit en plaisantant.

J’étais fatigué. Après leurs études de médecine, les médecins suivent une période de formation intensive appelée internat. Les deux premières années de cette formation comportaient des gardes de nuit à l’hôpital. Il n’était pas inhabituel de passer cent heures à l’hôpital en une semaine.

Même quand nous n’étions pas de garde, les journées commençaient tôt et finissaient tard. Je luttais souvent contre le sommeil en rentrant de l’hôpital en voiture. J’ai certainement beaucoup appris pendant cette période, mais je suis aussi heureux que ces jours soient derrière moi.

La fatigue fait partie de la condition humaine. Chacun a connu des moments où il a dû lutter contre l’épuisement. Cela était peut-être dû à un travail qu’il fallait terminer, à un long voyage ou à des nuits sans sommeil à cause de l’arrivée d’un nouveau bébé dans la famille. Quelle que soit la difficulté, nous nous efforçons résolument de tenir bon pendant ces périodes éprouvantes.

Dès l’enfance, on nous enseigne que le travail est important. Nous devons être responsables et accomplir les tâches qui nous sont confiées.

Le travail est ordonné par Dieu. Dans Genèse 2, Dieu a confié à Adam la tâche de prendre soin du jardin d’Éden. Plus tard, en Deutéronome 5:13, il a été commandé aux Israélites d’accomplir tout leur travail en six jours, puis de se reposer le septième jour.

Le Nouveau Testament donne encore deux raisons de travailler. Nous devons travailler afin de subvenir aux besoins de nos familles (voir 2 Thessaloniciens 3:10). De plus, nous devons travailler afin de pouvoir donner à ceux qui sont dans le besoin (voir Éphésiens 4:28).

Dieu attend de nous que nous travaillions et que nous le fassions de manière à le glorifier. Cependant, nous avons également besoin de repos, auquel Dieu a aussi pourvu.

Dieu a donné l’exemple du repos lors de la création

Le septième jour, Dieu avait achevé l’œuvre qu’il avait faite : il se reposa le septième jour de toute l’œuvre qu’il avait faite. Dieu bénit le septième jour et le sanctifia, parce qu’en ce jour il se reposa de toute l’œuvre qu’il avait créée et faite – Genèse 2:2-3.

Quand Dieu a créé l’univers, y compris la terre et tout ce qu’elle contient, cela ne lui a pris que six jours. Puisque Dieu est Dieu, nous pouvons être certains qu’il n’était pas fatigué à la fin de cette œuvre. Pourtant, malgré cela, il a pris une journée de repos et l’a mise à part. Il l’a fait pour nous donner l’exemple.

Bien que la loi du sabbat ne soit apparue que deux mille ans plus tard, le précédent avait été établi lors de la création… Se reposer un jour par semaine.

Dieu a prescrit le repos dans la Loi

La première chose qui vient peut-être à l’esprit, ce sont les lois relatives au jour du sabbat données en Exode 20:8-11. Il était expressément commandé au peuple de ne pas travailler le jour du sabbat. En outre, il ne devait pas non plus faire travailler d’autres personnes.

Une autre loi qui semblait particulièrement axée sur le besoin de repos était celle de l’année du jubilé. En Lévitique 25, cette loi prescrivait que tous les sept ans, la terre devait rester en jachère pendant toute l’année, que les esclaves devaient être libérés, que les terres devaient revenir à leur famille propriétaire d’origine et que les dettes devaient être annulées.

Les commandements du jubilé comportaient certaines promesses. Il y avait la promesse de liberté : quelles que soient les difficultés des six années précédentes, un nouveau départ serait possible. Il y avait la promesse d’un héritage : les biens qui avaient été perdus et vendus seraient récupérés. Il y avait la promesse d’abondance — Et si vous dites : Que mangerons-nous la septième année, puisque nous ne sèmerons pas et ne récolterons pas nos produits ? Je vous accorderai ma bénédiction la sixième année, et elle donnera des produits pour trois ans – Lévitique 25:20-21. Par-dessus tout, c’était la promesse du repos du travail, pour le peuple comme pour la terre.

Ces commandements n’ont pas été imposés au peuple pour l’accabler. Au contraire, Dieu les lui a donnés en sachant que, sans eux, son peuple ne se reposerait pas suffisamment et ne prendrait pas assez de temps pour se consacrer à lui, son Créateur.

Chacun de nous a besoin de périodes de repos, mais nous devons comprendre que l’observance du sabbat ne consiste pas simplement à s’abstenir de travailler. Nos efforts pour observer le sabbat doivent inclure à la fois le repos et le culte, et mettre l’accent sur la présence de Dieu dans nos vies, sans distractions.

Le Nouveau Testament n’a pas changé notre besoin de repos

L’un des versets qui me viennent à l’esprit quand je pense au repos est une promesse de Jésus. Venez à moi, vous tous qui êtes fatigués et chargés, et je vous donnerai du repos. Prenez mon joug sur vous et recevez mes instructions, car je suis doux et humble de cœur ; et vous trouverez du repos pour vos âmes. Car mon joug est doux, et mon fardeau léger – Matthieu 11:28-30.

Le livre biblique des Hébreux parle lui aussi de l’importance du repos et du fait d’entrer dans le repos de Dieu. Il y a donc un repos de sabbat réservé au peuple de Dieu. Car celui qui entre dans le repos de Dieu se repose aussi de ses œuvres, comme Dieu s’est reposé des siennes. Efforçons-nous donc d’entrer dans ce repos, afin que personne ne tombe en donnant le même exemple de désobéissance – Hébreux 4:9-11.

Il est important de comprendre que, dans le Nouveau Testament, le repos ne signifie pas simplement un congé loin du travail. La véritable paix biblique est intrinsèquement liée à la notion de paix, même au milieu d’un monde chaotique. Je vous laisse la paix, je vous donne ma paix. Je ne vous donne pas comme le monde donne. Que votre cœur ne se trouble point, et ne s’alarme point – Jean 14:27. Jésus a donné à ses disciples une paix qui leur permettait d’être en repos, même lorsqu’ils étaient soumis à un stress intense.

C’est une bénédiction, car il ne suffit pas simplement de prendre congé de notre travail habituel. Nous avons besoin de la paix et du calme qu’apporte une relation avec Jésus. Sans …la paix de Dieu, qui surpasse toute intelligence… – Philippiens 4:7, nos congés seront tout aussi agités que nos journées de travail.

Il est clair que Dieu veut que nous nous reposions. Il sait que nous en avons besoin, non seulement pour des raisons spirituelles, mais aussi pour notre santé physique.

******************************

Les responsables de la Révolution française ont tenté d’éliminer toutes les institutions du passé. Cette entreprise était particulièrement irréligieuse et, entre autres mesures, le nouveau gouvernement a décidé de « réformer » le calendrier.

En 1793, ils ont instauré une semaine de travail de dix jours. Chaque mois comportait trois semaines, avec un jour de repos dans chacune de ces semaines de dix jours. Leur objectif, entre autres, était d’éliminer toutes les fêtes religieuses et la célébration du dimanche comme jour de repos. Ils pensaient qu’on accomplirait davantage de travail en réduisant le nombre de jours de repos chaque mois.

Cette mesure a causé de sérieux problèmes aux horlogers. Il leur fallait trouver un moyen de fabriquer des montres capables de tenir compte des détails de ces nouveaux décrets : chaque journée durerait dix heures, chaque heure compterait cent minutes et chaque minute durerait 100 secondes.

Ce fut un désastre. Les gens détestaient ces changements et la productivité a considérablement baissé dans toute la France. Finalement, en 1806, Napoléon l’a aboli et est revenu à l’ancien calendrier et au système du dimanche comme jour de repos. Cette « expérience » scientifique était terminée. Il s’avère que les gens ont besoin de périodes de repos et de récupération et qu’une semaine de sept jours avec un jour de repos n’est pas seulement un concept chrétien : c’est une nécessité pour la santé et le bien-être.

L’Union soviétique, sous Joseph Staline, a également tenté une expérience similaire en supprimant le repos dominical, avec des résultats semblables.

******************************

La semaine telle que Dieu l’a créée (avec un jour de repos sur sept) est nécessaire pour que nous restions productifs.

Le repos réduit l’inflammation

Une partie du problème auquel sont confrontés les gens de notre époque est qu’ils subissent des niveaux élevés d’hormones du stress, comme l’adrénaline et le cortisol. Ces hormones font augmenter la tension artérielle et le rythme cardiaque. Elles augmentent également l’inflammation dans notre organisme.

L’inflammation chronique est néfaste pour la santé, mais heureusement, le repos semble vraiment contribuer à faire baisser considérablement le taux de ces hormones. Une bonne nuit de sommeil est essentielle à la guérison, précisément parce qu’elle réduit le taux de ces hormones et permet aux nerfs et aux tissus surmenés de se rétablir.

Les maladies auto-immunes et les douleurs s’atténuent lorsque les gens dorment suffisamment. La tension artérielle et les problèmes cardiaques bénéficient également d’un sommeil réparateur en quantité suffisante.

Le repos favorise la guérison

L’exercice est une bonne chose. Les médecins recommandent de pratiquer régulièrement des exercices cardiovasculaires, car ils sont bénéfiques pour le cœur, l’esprit et le bien-être général.

Il n’est pas sage de faire de l’exercice tous les jours. Cela aussi augmente le taux d’hormones du stress et ne laisse pas suffisamment de temps à notre corps pour guérir. Les personnes qui font de l’exercice trop fréquemment et avec trop d’intensité risquent beaucoup plus de souffrir de blessures persistantes, de douleurs articulaires et musculaires et de fatigue. Une étude a conclu qu’il faut 72 heures après une séance de musculation pour que les muscles récupèrent complètement.

Idéalement, les personnes qui font de l’exercice ont besoin d’un à deux jours de repos par semaine pour permettre à leur corps de récupérer après l’effort. Plus l’entraînement est intensif, plus ces périodes de repos sont nécessaires. Même une personne qui s’entraîne intensivement pour une épreuve comme un marathon doit prévoir régulièrement des journées sans course, faute de quoi elle se blessera.

Le repos réduit la douleur

De nombreuses études ont examiné les témoignages de personnes sur leur sommeil et se sont intéressées à des problèmes comme les douleurs chroniques et les céphalées de tension. Au moins 50 pour cent des personnes souffrant d’insomnie ont également des douleurs chroniques. Bien sûr, il se peut tout simplement que les personnes qui souffrent de douleurs chroniques dorment moins bien que celles qui n’en souffrent pas.

Plusieurs études ont examiné la tolérance à la douleur après une privation de sommeil. Elles ont conclu qu’une seule nuit sans sommeil suffisait à rendre les personnes plus sensibles à la douleur.

Le repos améliore notre système immunitaire

Plusieurs études ont évalué le fonctionnement de différentes composantes de notre système immunitaire et ont constaté qu’elles fonctionnent mieux lorsque les participants à l’étude dorment suffisamment. Le fait que l’inflammation augmente probablement lorsque nous ne nous reposons pas accroît les risques d’infection.

Quand nous nous poussons trop loin sans nous reposer, notre système immunitaire en souffre. À l’inverse, le meilleur moyen de récupérer est de veiller à nous reposer suffisamment.

Le repos a bien d’autres effets. Il contribue à améliorer l’humeur. Il peut aider à obtenir de meilleurs résultats scolaires et à accomplir des tâches de mémorisation.

Comme en toute chose, la modération est essentielle. Une personne qui ne fait que se reposer et dormir ne fonctionnera pas mieux qu’une personne qui dort bien sept heures par nuit, et elle ne sera pas très productive non plus.

Quelques règles de base peuvent nous aider à prévoir des périodes de repos.

Se reposer régulièrement

Le message du sabbat est que nous devons prendre régulièrement de courtes périodes de repos. Les années de jubilé nous enseignent qu’il nous faut des périodes de récupération plus longues, mais moins fréquentes. Il faut faire des efforts et s’organiser pour veiller à ce que ces périodes soient vraiment reposantes.

C’est peut-être un peu comme une voiture. On ne peut parcourir qu’une certaine distance avec un plein d’essence. Si l’on attend toujours que le voyant d’alerte s’allume pour faire le plein, il finira par s’allumer alors qu’on sera trop loin d’une station-service pour faire le plein avant de tomber en panne. Il n’y a jamais de bon moment pour tomber en panne d’essence. De même, nous devons régulièrement recharger nos batteries spirituelles, émotionnelles et physiques. Rien ne sert d’attendre l’apparition de signes avant-coureurs pour prendre enfin une pause dont nous avons désespérément besoin.

Le repos se prépare

Le récit du don de la manne en Exode 16 nous apprend que la manne arrivait chaque jour. Le peuple ne pouvait pas la conserver pour le lendemain, car elle se gâtait. Cependant, le vendredi, il devait en recueillir davantage, puisque le lendemain était un jour de repos et qu’il n’y avait pas de manne le jour du sabbat. Ceux qui n’en avaient pas recueilli davantage la veille ont eu faim.

De la même manière, il faut se préparer pour ces périodes de repos. Ce ne sera pas facile, mais c’est important.

Profiter de son repos pour faire des choses bonnes pour la santé

Lorsqu’ils sont stressés, les gens ont tendance à manger des aliments mauvais pour la santé. Quand ils sont épuisés, ils n’ont généralement pas envie de faire de l’exercice ni de se promener. Pourtant, ce sont précisément des activités qui peuvent vraiment nous aider à refaire le plein d’énergie, physiquement et émotionnellement.

Une fois encore, cela demande des efforts, mais choisir des options bonnes pour la santé est important pour notre bien-être.

Se concentrer sur Dieu

J’ai gardé cet aspect pour la fin, mais c’est le plus important du repos. Le véritable repos ne découle pas des médicaments ni même de vacances répétées, mais d’un cœur rempli de paix. La paix qui surpasse l’intelligence vient d’un cœur tourné vers Dieu.

Nos moments de prière et de lecture de la Bible devraient être des moments de repos. Si nous pouvons éliminer les distractions et les soucis liés à notre travail et à notre vie familiale, et fixer notre regard sur celui qui compte le plus, nous recevrons une véritable bénédiction et le regain d’énergie dont notre esprit a besoin.

Je crains que beaucoup de gens aient du mal à trouver le repos parce qu’ils ne sont pas véritablement en paix. Efforçons-nous donc d’entrer dans ce repos, afin que personne ne tombe en donnant le même exemple de désobéissance – Hébreux 4:11. Le repos évoqué ici est celui qui est promis à ceux qui persévèrent et reçoivent la paix de Dieu.

Conclusion

La vie est une question d’équilibre. Il y a des moments où nous devons travailler, et d’autres où nous devons nous reposer. Trouver cet équilibre est le défi auquel chacun de nous est confronté. Ce qui est certain, c’est que chaque journée de 24 heures sera entièrement remplie lorsque nous en arriverons à la fin.

Dieu nous voit, connaît nos limites et désire que nous trouvions cet équilibre entre notre travail et nos périodes de repos. Si seulement nous pouvions nous concentrer sur lui, nous recevrions ses conseils pour trouver cet équilibre.

Par-dessus tout, nous recevrons une paix inestimable, qui nous permettra de trouver le repos, même au cœur d’une tempête.

I rolled over in bed, listening to the sound of my pager going off. It couldn’t have been more than 15 minutes since I had dropped into bed from my last admission. I looked at the number on the pager. Yes, it was the Emergency Department again.

I attempted to rub the sleep out of my eyes and stir my still sleepy brain to wakefulness. I picked up the phone and dialed the ER. “Hey,” the ER doctor said. “I’ve got two admissions for you.”

“Oh,” I said sleepily.

“You sound tired,” he said, jokingly.

I was tired. After graduating from Medical School, doctors go through an intense training period called residency. The first two years of that training period involved overnight calls in the hospital. It wasn’t unusual to put in one hundred hours at the hospital in a week’s time.

Even when we weren’t on call, the days started early and went late. I often fought sleep as I was driving home from the hospital. I certainly learned a lot during that time, but I am also glad that those days are behind me.

Fatigue is part of the human condition. Everyone has had times when they struggled with tiredness. Maybe it was due to a job that needed to get done, a long trip, or sleepless nights due to a new baby in the family—whatever the difficulty, we determinedly push ourselves to make it through these challenging times.

From our childhood days we are taught that work is important. We need to be responsible and take care of the tasks that are set for us to do.

Work is ordained by God. In Genesis Chapter 2, God gave Adam the task of caring for the Garden of Eden. Later, in Deuteronomy 5:13, the Israelites were commanded to do all their work in six days and then rest the seventh day.

The New Testament gives a couple of more reasons to work. We are to work so we can provide for our families (see II Thessalonians 3:10). In addition, we are to work so we can give to others who are in need (see Ephesians 4:28).

God expects us to work and that we do it in a way that will glorify Him. However, we also have need of rest, which God made provision for as well.

God Exemplified Rest in the Creation

And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made –Genesis 2:2-3.

When God created the universe, including the earth and all it contains, it took Him just six days. Since God is God, we can be certain that He wasn’t tired at the end of this work. Yet, despite that fact, He took a day of rest and set it apart. He did it as an example for us.

Even though the law of the Sabbath would not be instituted for at least two thousand years, the precedent was set in Creation… Rest one day a week.

God Mandated Rest in the Law

Perhaps the thing that comes to mind first is the Sabbath Day laws that were given in Exodus 20:8-11. It was specifically commanded that the people were not to work on the Sabbath. And further, they were not to cause other people to work either.

Another law which seemed very much focused on the need for rest was the Year of Jubilee. In Leviticus 25, this law mandated that every seven years the land was to lie fallow for the whole year, slaves were to be released, land was to revert to its original family’s ownership, and debts were to be cancelled.

Within the Jubilee commands were certain promises. There was the promise of freedom—no matter how bad things had been the previous six years there would be a reset. It was a promise of inheritance—the things that had been lost and sold would be reclaimed. It was a promise of abundance—And if ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase: Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years –Leviticus 25:20-21. Most of all, it was a promise of rest from labor—for the people and the land.

These commands were not put on the people to afflict them. Rather, God gave them knowing that without them His people would not rest enough and would not take enough time to focus on Him, their Creator.

Each one of us needs times of rest, but we need to understand that keeping the Sabbath is not simply about abstinence from work. Our efforts at keeping the Sabbath must include both rest and worship and it must be emphasized with the presence of God in our lives, without distraction.

The New Testament did not Change the Need for Rest

One of the verses that comes to my mind when I think about rest, is a promise that Jesus gave. Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light –Matthew 11:28-30.

The biblical book of Hebrews also speaks of the importance of rest and of our entering into God’s rest. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrews 4:9-11.

It is important to see that the New Testament concept of rest is more than simply time off from work. True biblical peace is intrinsically intertwined with the concept of peace, even in the midst of a chaotic world. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. Jesus gave peace to His followers that allowed them to be at rest, even when they were dealing with high levels of stress.

This is a blessing, for it is not enough simply to take time off from our normal work. We need to have that peace and calm which a connection with Jesus offers. Without …the peace of God, which passeth all understanding… –Philippians 4:7, our time off will be just as unrestful as our time at work.

It is clear that God wants us to rest. He knows that we need it, not just for spiritual reasons, but also for our physical health.

******************************

The folks in charge of the French Revolution made an attempt to eliminate all the institutions of the past. It was a particularly godless endeavor and among other things, the new government decided to “reform” the calendar.

In 1793, they established a ten-day work week. Each month would have three weeks with one rest day in each of these ten-day weeks. Their goal, among other things, was to eliminate all religious holidays and the celebration of Sunday as a day of rest. They believed that more work would be done by having fewer days of rest each month.

This created a huge headache for watchmakers. They needed to somehow make watches that would support the details of these new decrees—each day would be ten hours long, each hour would contain one hundred minutes, and each minute would be 100 seconds long.

It turned out to be a disaster. The people hated the changes and productivity dropped considerably across France. Finally, in 1806, Napoleon abolished it and went back to the old calendar and the system of Sunday days of rest. This scientific “experiment” was over. It turns out that people need times of rest and recharging and that a seven-day week with one day off to rest is not just a Christian concept, it is something that is necessary for health and wellbeing.

The Soviet Union, under Joseph Stalin, also tried a similar experiment of eliminating Sunday rest, with similar results.

******************************

The week, as God created it, (with one day in seven for rest) is necessary for us to remain productive.

Rest Reduces Inflammation

Part of the problem that modern people face is that they deal with high levels stress hormones, like adrenaline and cortisol. These hormones increase blood pressure and pulse rates. They also increase levels of inflammation in our bodies.

Chronic inflammation is not healthy, but fortunately, rest really seems to help bring those hormone levels down a lot. A good night of sleep is essential for healing, precisely because it turns down these hormones and allows healing of overworked nerves and tissues.

Autoimmune diseases and pain levels improve when people get adequate levels of sleep. Blood pressure and heart conditions also benefit when a person gets adequate amounts of restorative sleep.

Rest Allows for Healing

Exercise is a good thing. Doctors recommend doing regular cardiovascular exercise because it is healthy for our hearts, minds, and overall wellbeing.

It is not wise to exercise every day. It too, raises stress hormone levels and does not give our bodies adequate times to heal. People who exercise too frequently and with too much intensity are much more likely to end up with nagging injuries, joint and muscle pain, and fatigue. One study found that it takes 72 hours after doing weight training for muscles to fully recover.

People who exercise ideally need one to two days off a week to let their bodies recover from the activity. The harder you are training, the more you need those times of rest. Even someone who is training intensively for something like a marathon needs to take periodic days with no running or they will injure themselves.

Rest Decreases Pain Levels

There have been many studies that looked at people’s reports of sleep and looked at things like chronic pain and tension headaches. At least 50 percent of people with insomnia also have chronic pain. Of course, it could simply be that people with chronic pain don’t sleep as well as people who don’t have that.

There have been several studies that looked at people’s pain tolerance after sleep deprivation. They found that even a single night of sleep deprivation was enough to make people feel pain more acutely.

Rest Improves Our Immune Systems

There have been several studies that looked at function of different parts of our immune systems and found that they work better when study participants have adequate levels of sleep. Probably the fact that inflammation levels are higher when we don’t rest, increases the risks of infection.

When we push ourselves too hard without rest it is hard on our immune systems. On the other hand, the best way to recover is to make certain that we get sufficient rest.

There are many other things that rest does. It helps improve mood. It can help with academic performance and memory tasks.

As with all things, moderation is key. Someone who does nothing but rest and sleep, is not going to have any better function than someone who sleeps well for seven hours a night, nor will they be very productive.

There are some basic rules that can help us with times of rest.

Rest Regularly

The message of the Sabbath is that we need to take regular, short periods of time to rest. The Jubilee Years tell us that we need less frequent, longer times to recharge. It takes effort and scheduling to make certain that these times are truly restful.

Maybe it is a bit like a car. You can only drive so far on a tank of gas. If you always wait until the warning light turns on to fill up that tank, eventually you will have this happen when you are too far from a gas station to fill up before you run out of gas. There is never a good time to run out of gas. In the same way, we need to periodically recharge our spiritual, emotional, and physical batteries. There is no reason to wait until warning signs show up that we desperately need to take a break.

Rest Takes Preparation

The story of the gift of manna in Exodus 16 tells us that manna came every day. The people could not keep it for a second day because it would spoil. However, on Fridays, they were to gather extra since the next day was a day of rest and no manna came on the Sabbath. Those who had not gathered extra the day before went hungry.

In the same way, it takes preparation to have these sorts of times. It won’t be easy, but it is important.

Do Healthy Things With Your Rest

There is a tendency when people are under stress to eat unhealthy things. When people are exhausted, they don’t usually feel like exercising or taking walks. These are the sorts of things that can really help recharge us, both physically and emotionally.

Once again, this takes some effort, but choosing healthy options is important for our well-being.

Focus on God

I have left this till the last, but it is the most important aspect of rest. True rest grows, not out of medication or even multiple vacations, but out of a heart that is filled with peace. The peace which passes understanding comes from a heart that is focused on God.

Our times of prayer and Bible reading should be times of rest. If we can eliminate distractions and the challenges of our work and home life and train our gaze on the One who matters most, we will receive a real blessing and the recharging that our spirits need.

I am afraid that many people struggle to find rest because they are not truly at peace. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrew 4:11. The rest here is one that is promised to those who persevere and receive God’s peace.

Conclusion

Life is about balance. There are times when we need to work and there are times as well when we should rest. Figuring out this balance is the challenge which each of us faces. What is certain, is that every 24-hour day will be completely full by the time we get to the end of it.

God sees us and our limitations and desires for us to achieve this balance between our work and our times of rest. If we can only focus ourselves on Him, we will receive guidance in this balance.

Most of all, we will receive a peace that is without price, that will allow us to find rest—even during a storm.
