Jag vände mig om i sängen och lyssnade på ljudet av min personsökare. Det kan inte ha gått mer än 15 minuter sedan jag stupade i säng efter min senaste inläggning. Jag tittade på numret på personsökaren. Ja, det var akutmottagningen igen.

Jag försökte gnugga sömnen ur ögonen och väcka min fortfarande sömniga hjärna. Jag tog upp telefonen och ringde akuten. ”Hej”, sa akutläkaren. ”Jag har två patienter som ska läggas in åt dig.”

”Jaha”, sa jag sömnigt.

”Du låter trött”, sa han skämtsamt.

Jag var trött. Efter läkarutbildningen genomgår läkare en intensiv utbildningsperiod som kallas specialistutbildning. De första två åren av den utbildningen innebar nattjourer på sjukhuset. Det var inte ovanligt att tillbringa hundra timmar på sjukhuset under en vecka.

Även när vi inte hade jour började dagarna tidigt och slutade sent. Jag kämpade ofta mot sömnen när jag körde hem från sjukhuset. Jag lärde mig naturligtvis mycket under den tiden, men jag är också glad att de dagarna ligger bakom mig.

Trötthet är en del av det mänskliga tillståndet. Alla har haft perioder då de kämpat med trötthet. Kanske berodde det på ett arbete som behövde bli gjort, en lång resa eller sömnlösa nätter på grund av en nyfödd i familjen – oavsett svårigheten pressar vi oss målmedvetet igenom dessa utmanande tider.

Ända sedan barndomen får vi lära oss att arbete är viktigt. Vi behöver vara ansvarsfulla och ta hand om de uppgifter som vi har fått.

Arbetet är instiftat av Gud. I Första Moseboken, kapitel 2, gav Gud Adam uppgiften att sköta Edens trädgård. Senare, i Femte Moseboken 5:13, befalldes israeliterna att utföra allt sitt arbete under sex dagar och sedan vila på den sjunde dagen.

Nya testamentet ger ytterligare ett par skäl att arbeta. Vi ska arbeta för att kunna försörja våra familjer (se Andra Thessalonikerbrevet 3:10). Dessutom ska vi arbeta för att kunna ge åt andra som behöver hjälp (se Efesierbrevet 4:28).

Gud förväntar sig att vi arbetar och att vi gör det på ett sätt som förhärligar honom. Men vi behöver också vila, och även det har Gud sörjt för.

Gud visade vägen till vila i skapelsen

På den sjunde dagen hade Gud fullbordat sitt verk, som han hade gjort, och på den sjunde dagen vilade han från allt sitt verk, som han hade gjort. Gud välsignade den sjunde dagen och helgade den, eftersom han på den dagen vilade från allt sitt verk, som Gud hade skapat och gjort – Första Moseboken 2:2–3.

När Gud skapade universum, däribland jorden och allt som finns på den, tog det honom bara sex dagar. Eftersom Gud är Gud kan vi vara säkra på att han inte var trött efter detta arbete. Trots det tog han en vilodag och avskilde den. Han gjorde det som ett exempel för oss.

Även om sabbatslagen inte skulle införas förrän minst två tusen år senare, sattes mönstret vid skapelsen … Vila en dag i veckan.

Gud föreskrev vila i lagen

Det första man kanske kommer att tänka på är sabbatsbuden i Andra Moseboken 20:8–11. Det befalldes uttryckligen att folket inte skulle arbeta på sabbaten. Dessutom skulle de inte heller låta andra arbeta.

En annan lag som tycktes vara starkt inriktad på behovet av vila var jubelåret. I Tredje Moseboken 25 föreskrev lagen att marken vart sjunde år skulle ligga i träda under hela året, att slavarna skulle friges, att marken skulle återgå till den ursprungliga familjens ägo och att skulderna skulle avskrivas.

I jubelårets bud fanns vissa löften. Där fanns löftet om frihet – hur illa det än hade gått under de föregående sex åren skulle man få börja om. Det var ett löfte om arvedel – det som hade gått förlorat och sålts skulle återtas. Det var ett löfte om överflöd – Om ni frågar: ”Vad ska vi äta det sjunde året? Vi får ju inte så och inte samla in vår gröda!” då ska jag befalla min välsignelse över er det sjätte året, så att det ger gröda för tre år – Tredje Moseboken 25:20–21. Framför allt var det ett löfte om vila från arbete – för folket och marken.

Dessa bud gavs inte för att plåga folket. Gud gav dem i stället eftersom han visste att hans folk annars inte skulle vila tillräckligt och inte skulle ta tillräckligt med tid för att fokusera på honom, sin Skapare.

Var och en av oss behöver stunder av vila, men vi behöver förstå att sabbatsfirande inte bara handlar om att avstå från arbete. När vi försöker hålla sabbaten måste det innefatta både vila och tillbedjan, och det måste präglas av Guds närvaro i våra liv, utan distraktioner.

Nya testamentet förändrade inte behovet av vila

En av verserna jag kommer att tänka på när jag tänker på vila är ett löfte som Jesus gav. Kom till mig, alla ni som arbetar och är tyngda av bördor, så ska jag ge er vila. Ta på er mitt ok och lär av mig, för jag är mild och ödmjuk i hjärtat. Då ska ni finna ro för era själar. Mitt ok är milt och min börda är lätt – Matteusevangeliet 11:28–30.

Den bibliska Hebreerbrevet talar också om hur viktig vilan är och om att vi får gå in i Guds vila. Alltså finns det en sabbatsvila kvar för Guds folk. Den som har kommit in i hans vila har också fått vila från sina gärningar, liksom Gud från sina. Låt oss därför göra allt vi kan för att komma in i den vilan, så att ingen faller genom samma slags olydnad – Hebreerbrevet 4:9–11.

Det är viktigt att se att Nya testamentets begrepp vila är mer än bara ledighet från arbetet. Verklig biblisk frid är oupplösligt förenad med begreppet frid, även mitt i en kaotisk värld. Frid lämnar jag kvar åt er, min frid ger jag er. Jag ger er inte det som världen ger. Låt inte era hjärtan oroas och tappa inte modet – Johannesevangeliet 14:27. Jesus gav sina efterföljare en frid som gjorde att de kunde vila, även när de utsattes för stark stress.

Detta är en välsignelse, för det räcker inte att bara ta ledigt från vårt vanliga arbete. Vi behöver den frid och det lugn som gemenskapen med Jesus ger. Utan … Guds frid, som övergår allt förstånd … – Filipperbrevet 4:7, kommer vår ledighet att vara lika orolig som tiden på arbetet.

Det är tydligt att Gud vill att vi ska vila. Han vet att vi behöver det, inte bara av andliga skäl, utan också för vår fysiska hälsa.

******************************

De som styrde under franska revolutionen försökte avskaffa alla tidigare institutioner. Det var ett särskilt gudlöst projekt och bland annat beslutade den nya regeringen att ”reformera” kalendern.

År 1793 införde de en tiodagars arbetsvecka. Varje månad skulle ha tre veckor med en vilodag i var och en av dessa tiodagarsveckor. Ett av deras mål var att avskaffa alla religiösa helgdagar och söndagens firande som vilodag. De trodde att man skulle få mer arbete gjort genom att ha färre vilodagar varje månad.

Detta skapade stora problem för urmakarna. De behövde på något sätt tillverka klockor som kunde hantera detaljerna i dessa nya dekret – varje dag skulle vara tio timmar lång, varje timme skulle innehålla hundra minuter och varje minut skulle vara 100 sekunder lång.

Det visade sig bli en katastrof. Folk avskydde förändringarna och produktiviteten sjönk kraftigt i hela Frankrike. Till slut avskaffade Napoleon systemet 1806 och återgick till den gamla kalendern och söndagar som vilodagar. Detta vetenskapliga ”experiment” var över. Det visar sig att människor behöver tid för vila och återhämtning, och att en sjudagarsvecka med en vilodag inte bara är ett kristet begrepp, utan något som är nödvändigt för hälsa och välbefinnande.

Sovjetunionen under Josef Stalin försökte också genomföra ett liknande experiment genom att avskaffa söndagsvilan, med liknande resultat.

******************************

Veckan sådan Gud skapade den (med en vilodag av sju) är nödvändig för att vi ska kunna fortsätta vara produktiva.

Vila minskar inflammation

En del av problemet som människor i vår tid möter är att de har höga nivåer av stresshormoner, som adrenalin och kortisol. Dessa hormoner höjer blodtrycket och pulsen. De ökar också inflammationsnivåerna i kroppen.

Kronisk inflammation är inte hälsosam, men lyckligtvis tycks vila verkligen bidra till att sänka hormonnivåerna rejält. En god natts sömn är avgörande för läkning, just eftersom den sänker nivåerna av dessa hormoner och låter överansträngda nerver och vävnader läka.

Autoimmuna sjukdomar och smärtnivåer förbättras när människor får tillräckligt med sömn. Även blodtrycket och hjärtproblem påverkas positivt när man får tillräckligt med återhämtande sömn.

Vila ger möjlighet till läkning

Motion är bra. Läkare rekommenderar regelbunden konditionsträning eftersom den är bra för hjärtat, sinnet och vårt allmänna välbefinnande.

Det är inte klokt att träna varje dag. Även träning höjer stresshormonnivåerna och ger inte kroppen tillräckligt med tid att läka. De som tränar alltför ofta och alltför intensivt löper mycket större risk att få envisa skador, led- och muskelsmärtor samt trötthet. En studie visade att det tar 72 timmar för musklerna att återhämta sig helt efter styrketräning.

Den som tränar behöver helst en till två vilodagar i veckan för att låta kroppen återhämta sig efter aktiviteten. Ju hårdare du tränar, desto mer behöver du dessa viloperioder. Även den som tränar intensivt inför något som ett maraton behöver ta lediga dagar utan löpning med jämna mellanrum, annars skadar hen sig.

Vila minskar smärta

Många studier har undersökt människors uppgifter om sin sömn och tittat på sådant som kronisk smärta och spänningshuvudvärk. Minst 50 procent av personer med sömnlöshet har också kronisk smärta. Naturligtvis kan det helt enkelt vara så att personer med kronisk smärta inte sover lika bra som personer utan sådan smärta.

Flera studier har undersökt människors smärttolerans efter sömnbrist. De fann att till och med en enda natt utan sömn räckte för att människor skulle uppleva smärta starkare.

Vila stärker vårt immunförsvar

Flera studier har undersökt hur olika delar av vårt immunförsvar fungerar och funnit att de fungerar bättre när studiedeltagarna får tillräckligt med sömn. Troligen ökar risken för infektioner av att inflammationsnivåerna blir högre när vi inte vilar.

När vi pressar oss för hårt utan vila belastar det immunförsvaret. Å andra sidan är det bästa sättet att återhämta sig att se till att vi får tillräckligt med vila.

Vilan gör också många andra saker. Den bidrar till bättre humör. Den kan hjälpa till med studieresultat och minnesuppgifter.

Som med allt annat är måttlighet nyckeln. Den som inte gör annat än att vila och sova kommer inte att fungera bättre än någon som sover gott i sju timmar per natt, och kommer inte heller att vara särskilt produktiv.

Det finns några grundläggande regler som kan hjälpa oss att få tid för vila.

Vila regelbundet

Sabbatens budskap är att vi regelbundet behöver ta kortare viloperioder. Jubelåren säger oss att vi också behöver längre perioder för återhämtning, men mer sällan. Det krävs ansträngning och planering för att försäkra sig om att dessa perioder verkligen ger vila.

Det kanske är lite som med en bil. Man kan bara köra en viss sträcka på en tank bensin. Om man alltid väntar tills varningslampan tänds innan man tankar, kommer det förr eller senare att hända när man är för långt från en bensinstation för att hinna tanka innan bensinen tar slut. Det finns aldrig någon bra tidpunkt att få slut på bensin. På samma sätt behöver vi regelbundet ladda våra andliga, känslomässiga och fysiska batterier. Det finns ingen anledning att vänta tills varningssignalerna visar att vi verkligen är i desperat behov av en paus.

Vila kräver förberedelser

Berättelsen om manna som gåva i Andra Moseboken 16 säger oss att manna kom varje dag. Folket kunde inte spara det till nästa dag, för då blev det förstört. På fredagar skulle de däremot samla in extra, eftersom nästa dag var en vilodag och det inte kom något manna på sabbaten. De som inte hade samlat in extra dagen före blev utan mat.

På samma sätt kräver sådana här perioder förberedelser. Det blir inte lätt, men det är viktigt.

Gör hälsosamma saker när du vilar

När människor är stressade har de en tendens att äta ohälsosam mat. När människor är utmattade känner de oftast inte för att motionera eller ta promenader. Det här är sådant som verkligen kan hjälpa oss att ladda batterierna, både fysiskt och känslomässigt.

Återigen kräver det en viss ansträngning, men det är viktigt för vårt välbefinnande att välja hälsosamma alternativ.

Fokusera på Gud

Jag har sparat detta till sist, men det är den viktigaste aspekten av vila. Verklig vila växer inte fram ur medicinering eller ens flera semestrar, utan ur ett hjärta fyllt av frid. Den frid som övergår förståndet kommer från ett hjärta som är inriktat på Gud.

Våra bönestunder och vår bibelläsning bör vara vilostunder. Om vi kan undanröja distraktioner och utmaningarna i arbets- och familjelivet och fästa blicken på den som betyder mest, får vi en verklig välsignelse och den återhämtning som vår ande behöver.

Jag är rädd att många människor har svårt att finna vila eftersom de inte verkligen har frid. Låt oss därför göra allt vi kan för att komma in i den vilan, så att ingen faller genom samma slags olydnad – Hebreerbrevet 4:11. Den vila som avses här är utlovad åt dem som håller ut och tar emot Guds frid.

Slutsats

Livet handlar om balans. Ibland behöver vi arbeta, och ibland behöver vi vila. Att hitta den balansen är en utmaning för var och en av oss. En sak är säker: varje dygn på 24 timmar kommer att vara helt fyllt när det är slut.

Gud ser oss och våra begränsningar och vill att vi ska finna balansen mellan arbete och vila. Om vi bara kan rikta in oss på honom får vi vägledning i att hitta denna balans.

Framför allt får vi en frid som är ovärderlig och som gör att vi kan finna vila – även mitt i en storm.

We can’t afford to win the gain that means another’s loss;
We can’t afford to miss the crown by stumbling at the cross.
We can’t afford the heedless jest that robs us of a friend;
We can’t afford the laugh that finds in bitter tears an end.
We can’t afford the feast today that brings tomorrow’s fast;
We can’t afford the race that comes to tragedy at last.

We can’t afford with serious heed to treat the cynic’s sneer;
We can’t afford to wise men’s words to turn a careless ear.
We can’t afford for hate to give like hatred in return;
We can’t afford to feed a flame and make it fiercer burn.
We can’t afford to lose the soul for this world’s fleeting breath;
We can’t afford to barter life in mad exchange for death.
But blind to good are we apart from THEE, all-seeing Lord;
Oh, grant us light that we may know the things we can’t afford!

1.
God has not promised skies always blue,
Flower-strewn pathways all our lives through;
God has not promised sun without rain,
Joy without sorrow, peace without pain.

Refrain:
But God has promised strength for the day,
Rest for the labor, light for the way,
Grace for the trials, help from above,
Unfailing kindness, undying love.

2.
God has not promised we shall not know
Toil and temptation, trouble and woe;
He has not told us we shall not bear
Many a burden, many a care.

3.
God has not promised smooth roads and wide,
Swift, easy travel, needing no guide;
Never a mountain rocky and steep,
Never a river turbid and deep.

۱۔
خدا نے یہ وعدہ نہیں کیا کہ آسمان ہمیشہ نیلے ہوں گے،
یا ہماری ساری عمر راستے پھولوں سے سجے ہوں گے؛
خدا نے یہ وعدہ نہیں کیا کہ سورج کے ساتھ بارش نہ ہوگی،
غم کے بغیر خوشی، درد کے بغیر سکون ہوگا۔

مکرر:
لیکن خدا نے دن کے لیے قوت کا وعدہ کیا ہے،
محنت کے لیے آرام، راہ کے لیے روشنی،
آزمائشوں کے لیے فضل، اوپر سے مدد،
کبھی نہ ختم ہونے والی مہربانی، کبھی نہ مرنے والی محبت۔

۲۔
خدا نے یہ وعدہ نہیں کیا کہ ہم
مشقت اور آزمائش، مصیبت اور رنج سے ناواقف رہیں گے؛
اُس نے ہمیں یہ نہیں بتایا کہ ہم نہیں اٹھائیں گے
بہت سے بوجھ، بہت سی فکریں۔

۳۔
خدا نے ہموار اور کشادہ راستوں کا وعدہ نہیں کیا،
نہ تیز، آسان سفر کا جس کے لیے کسی رہنما کی ضرورت نہ ہو؛
نہ کبھی کوئی پتھریلا اور کھڑا پہاڑ،
نہ کبھی کوئی گدلا اور گہرا دریا۔

Thou hast the dew of thy youth. Psalm 110:3

There are many aspects of youth which are not virtuous. Many youth of our day experience an early season of callused carelessness and casualty. Often decisions that are made in youthful years set the foundation for the rest of their lives. It was a the younger prodigal brother that asked for an early draw on his inheritance then went and wasted it on riotous living. It was a young Dinah who wandered from her father’s house and …went out to see the daughters of the land –Genesis 34:1. There, she was exposed to the heathen young men of the land and occasioned a bloody massacre, leaving Jacob as a stench in the land. Many foolish young people have sown to the wind and reaped the havoc thereof. Those that are void of solid principles and parental authority are at high risk for spiritual shipwreck.

There are particular lusts that inflict youth more so than the aged, and the young are exhorted to flee them. (–see 2 Timothy 2:22) Solomon looked through his window casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding -Proverbs 7:6-7. The young man was in heartfelt pursuit of that which appeared lovely… [Un]Till a dart [struck] through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life –Proverbs 7:23. We could examine the vices from the youthful lives of Rehoboam, Amnon, Nadab and Abihu, and countless others. We also find no lack of modern, folly-filled examples about us fulfilled by frivolous youth.

But youth are not meant to be despised. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. In fact, God generally chooses the youth as the instruments of His propagation. Joseph, of sterling character, was sent by God into Egypt at the age of 17 to preserve life (–see Genesis 45:5). Miriam, at the age of twelve, stood post over the future deliverer of the entire Jewish nation and secured her own mother, Jochebed, to be the nurse of the baby Moses. David, as a youth, was sent to encourage his brethren in the army. He was despised by his brothers: …I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart… –1 Samuel 17:28. He was rejected by Saul: …Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth… –1 Samuel 17:33. He was scorned by Goliath: …Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves… –1 Samuel 17:43. But their contempt was all for naught when he was chosen by God to be king over all Israel.

These noble youthful ambitions were followed by Josiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Mary, and the disciples of the Lord, all who chose to remember their Creator in the days of their youth. But these were not naive specimens seeking to secure their place in life, they were graphic examples of youth who were seeking to imitate the image of their Lord.

We need not gaze long into the character of Christ before we find…

...Thou hast the dew of thy youth

Psalm 110 is perhaps the most referred-to scripture in the Old Testament. This rhetorical portrait of the Messiah reveals a vivid virtue for us to behold. Christ, as the Ancient of days, was described in the Revelation having His head and His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet, here He is depicted as eternally young, as He sits at the right hand of God (–see Psalm 110:1). No weariness of age can enter there, for Christ is the Morning Star. It is perpetual morning around the throne of God. Those saints who are following hard after His likeness will also reflect this virtue, for the light of Jesus is the light of youth.

The psalmist, describing the Messiah, draws from the natural beauty of the morning dew (–see Psalm 110:3). The thought of dew calls us back from the heavens and unveils before us a portrait of this earth on which we dwell. In heaven there is no night, no change of heat and cold, no need of the sun to light up the day and consequently… no dew. The nature of dew belongs to the terrestrial, where everyone who will but stoop to observe it will behold a uniformed regiment of grass sparkling as if embedded with a myriad of diamonds. After a long night of darkness, the dewdrops, like tears, stand in the eyes of the flowers as they weep for joy at the advent of the first morning sunbeam. Those who walk through the lowly vegetation will have their feet washed by a thousand caressing hands of God’s design. Christ is not depicted as the dew of the morning but as the dew of youth, and the imagery is stretched further.

Youth is the season of abounding energy. Some cannot sit still. They are generally interpersonal creatures who love social activity. This is neither a virtue nor a vice. Rather, it is nominal nature. There is a progressive strain in advancing years that tames and tempers the soul. As life progresses, there is a clearer vision and a steadier thought, and we rise to better things. But when the mid-life summit has been crossed and the feet are traveling downward on the slope, that tumultuous rush of bodily energy that plowed through anything becomes enshrined with memories of the past. It is the closest comfort many can find to the bygone days of their strength.

But Christ has not called us to foster a fondness for the past nor a wistful longing for the “DO” of our youth. So many today sadly lament that their ‘get-up-and-go’ has got up and went. These have no vision for higher things and are more energized by a can of Mountain Dew than the Dew of Youth. They are more inspired by a trip down memory lane and reminiscing events of the past than of the hope that lies before them.

Age is no hindrance to securing the dew of youth. The Ancient of Days still rides forth among the golden candlesticks. While John beheld His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet Solomon declares …his locks are bushy, and black as a raven –Song of Solomon 5:11. While age may steal our strength and hearing, …the LORD’S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: –Isaiah 59:1. He has secured the dew of youth and invites us to partake. The problem is not found in our deteriorating body but in a spiritually declining mind. The bane of old age predominately sets in when the mind follows the body.

It is not that life grows poorer as it advances or ceases to be noble when the charm of youth has faded. If we were placed here only to experience joy, the dying out of youthful romance would be terrible. God had a much greater end in view for His children than to just be vibrant ‘doers’. We are sent here to learn. Our allotted years upon earth are all meant to be a schooling, and it is not in the bright romance of youth that we learn the best and most abiding lessons. It is in the dogged doing of our duty, the quiet acceptance of our limitations, the patient carrying of our daily burden, and in the stretching out of a helping hand to our brother. These afford us the true opportunities for Christian culture and are the roots of ethical nobility. Christ labored …not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life… –John 6:27, and He finished His earthly task in 33 years. But the dew of youth did not dissipate as He sat down at the right hand of His Father.

Thus, we conclude that this youthfulness will not be secured by strength, but by…

...Hope

But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. –Hebrews 10:12-13.

How shall we picture this Christ now? Reclining in an easy chair, all worn out from His experience with the stubborn people of this earth? Is He busy putting together a scrap book of precious memories? This is too often the position of the aged and so their mind dies with their bodies.

And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope –Romans 5:3-4. At times, we wonder if this scripture can be true. Anyone with any age on their bones can testify to a poor experience and the subsequent feelings of hopelessness following. As people, we have all faced disappointing experiences with a spouse, a child, or a church relationship after which a nagging cloud of despair settles in. Outside of Christ, a sour experience always tends to pessimism. It was so in the world when Jesus came. It is still so today.

But the dew of youth is incurably hopeful. There is an effervescent expectation that is naturally and magnificently borne in youth and retained in Christ. In every winter, when the fields are bleak, and the cold gust goes whistling through the trees, there lies the hope that the flowers will spring again. In every spring there is the hope of summer. In every summer there is the hope of harvest. It is alive in nature and alive in youth. Those who are blind to it shall reap, at best, a dreary monotone existence. To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all. –Oscar Wilde.

The rest shall be brightly effected with a hope that…

…Heals Our Infirmities

Our bodies are destined for the grave and have no hope for renewal in this life. It is our minds that carry our greatest infirmities. The impotent man of 38 years at Bethesda could only utter a hopeless complaint when Christ asked him, …Wilt thou be made whole? –John 5:6. Upon the wake of his new day, a new remedy was given to him—… Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee –John 5:14. What could be worse than being a cripple for years? A mind that is beset by a doleful indulgence in the sorrows of this world. Age sets in when we have more memories of the past than hope for tomorrow. It is disappointing when folks grow old and have no vision for tomorrow, but it is a disaster to behold youth that are plagued by its crippling effects. Many grope aimlessly through life’s various trials, stupefied by the lack of blessedness. The noonday sun has evaporated the dew of their youth and the only praise that they can muster is culminated from a handful of yesterday’s pleasantries. A new attitude must be birthed by the dew of a new morning.

…Humbles Our Pursuits

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. –John 21:18. When we are young, we can overcome in the strength of our youth. As age takes its course, we will find a different alternative: victory through surrender.

…I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one. –1 John 2:14. The world entices us to selfish living. Youth are often subject to schools of learning that teach them to “be all that you can be”. There is a major focus on self-enhancement and preparation for the future. This may prepare them in a ‘survival of the fittest’ world but will leave them destitute when the strength and prowess of youth has departed.

For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever. –1 John 2:16-17. Overcoming evil with good is the Biblical antidote for channeling youthful energies. Whether it is the lust within or the longing without, hope is conceived by planting a seed of kindness in the life of another. The pursuit of pleasure and lieu of leisure will always disappoint its recipient and leave him in a valley of despair deeper than when he began. It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth … He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope. –Lamentations 3:27-29. We are created to work in God’s vineyard and those who have an appetite for it will reap in hope of its youthful reward.

…Hallows Our Trials

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope... –Romans 8:24. How often we can relate to Job in his pain. But before his pain had received an ounce of retribution, the healing streams began to flow as Job reverenced his Creator. When we can acknowledge that God is perfect in all the trials He allows, we then learn to worship in the temple not made with hands and disregard the frailties of the body. To sit down at the feet of Christ ignites a youthful spark that radiates the spirit within and conceives hope. The dew of youth then becomes our portion as Christ imparts eternal life and eternal youth to us. From the hour of the grave and through eternity we shall be young and bid defiance to weariness and death if we are living in the morning light of Jesus Christ. Heaven is a place of perpetual youth, and just like the light of the sun is reflected on the moon, so likewise the light of Christ is reflected on His bride. She is clean and young, …a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing… –Ephesians 5:27. Blessed is the venerable saint who arrives at the portals of heaven in such a condition.

Tu tens o orvalho da tua mocidade. Salmo 110:3

Há muitos aspectos da juventude que não são virtuosos. Muitos jovens de nossos dias passam por uma fase precoce de descuido insensível e imprudência. Muitas vezes, decisões tomadas na juventude estabelecem os alicerces para o restante da vida. Foi o irmão mais novo e pródigo que pediu antecipadamente sua parte da herança e depois a desperdiçou vivendo dissolutamente. Foi a jovem Diná que se afastou da casa de seu pai e …saiu para ver as filhas da terra –Gênesis 34:1. Ali, foi exposta aos jovens pagãos da terra e deu ocasião a um massacre sangrento, deixando Jacó como mau cheiro naquela terra. Muitos jovens insensatos semearam ao vento e colheram a devastação resultante. Aqueles que carecem de princípios sólidos e da autoridade dos pais correm alto risco de naufrágio espiritual.

Há desejos particulares que afligem mais os jovens do que os idosos, e os jovens são exortados a fugir deles. (–ver 2 Timóteo 2:22) Salomão olhou pela janela de sua casa, E vi entre os simples, discerni entre os jovens, um jovem falto de entendimento –Provérbios 7:6-7. O jovem buscava ardentemente aquilo que parecia belo… [Até] que uma flecha [lhe atravessou] o fígado; como a ave que se apressa para o laço, sem saber que isso lhe custará a vida –Provérbios 7:23. Poderíamos examinar os vícios da juventude de Roboão, Amnom, Nadabe e Abiú, e de inúmeros outros. Também não faltam ao nosso redor exemplos modernos de jovens levianos que dão vida a toda sorte de insensatez.

Mas os jovens não devem ser desprezados. Ninguém despreze a tua mocidade; mas sê o exemplo dos fiéis, na palavra, no trato, no amor, no espírito, na fé, na pureza –1 Timóteo 4:12. De fato, Deus geralmente escolhe os jovens como instrumentos para levar adiante a Sua obra. José, de caráter íntegro, foi enviado por Deus ao Egito aos 17 anos para preservar vidas (–ver Gênesis 45:5). Miriã, aos doze anos, vigiou o futuro libertador de toda a nação judaica e conseguiu que sua própria mãe, Joquebede, fosse a ama do bebê Moisés. Davi, ainda jovem, foi enviado para encorajar seus irmãos no exército. Ele foi desprezado por seus irmãos: …Conheço a tua presunção e a maldade do teu coração… –1 Samuel 17:28. Foi rejeitado por Saul: …Não poderás ir contra este filisteu para pelejar com ele, pois tu és ainda jovem… –1 Samuel 17:33. Foi escarnecido por Golias: …Sou eu algum cão, para vires a mim com paus… –1 Samuel 17:43. Mas todo o desprezo deles foi em vão quando Deus o escolheu para ser rei sobre todo o Israel.

Essas nobres aspirações juvenis foram seguidas por Josias, Isaías, Jeremias, Daniel, Maria e os discípulos do Senhor, todos eles escolhendo lembrar-se de seu Criador nos dias de sua juventude. Mas eles não eram exemplos ingênuos tentando garantir seu lugar na vida; eram exemplos vivos de jovens que buscavam imitar a imagem de seu Senhor.

Não precisamos contemplar por muito tempo o caráter de Cristo antes de encontrarmos…

...Tu tens o orvalho da tua mocidade

O Salmo 110 é talvez a passagem mais citada do Antigo Testamento. Este retrato retórico do Messias revela uma virtude vívida que devemos contemplar. Cristo, como o Ancião de Dias, foi descrito no Apocalipse com a cabeça e os cabelos ... brancos como a lã, brancos como a neve… –Apocalipse 1:14; no entanto, aqui Ele é retratado como eternamente jovem, enquanto se assenta à direita de Deus (–ver Salmo 110:1). O cansaço da idade não pode chegar até Ele, pois Cristo é a Estrela da Manhã. É sempre manhã ao redor do trono de Deus. Os santos que seguem firmemente a Sua semelhança também refletirão essa virtude, pois a luz de Jesus é a luz da juventude.

Ao descrever o Messias, o salmista recorre à beleza natural do orvalho da manhã (–ver Salmo 110:3). A ideia do orvalho nos traz de volta dos céus e revela diante de nós um retrato desta terra em que habitamos. No céu não há noite, nem mudança de calor e frio, nem necessidade do sol para iluminar o dia e, por consequência… não há orvalho. A natureza do orvalho pertence ao mundo terrestre, onde todos os que se inclinarem para observá-lo verão um exército uniforme de grama cintilando como se estivesse incrustado com miríades de diamantes. Depois de uma longa noite de escuridão, as gotas de orvalho, como lágrimas, ficam nos olhos das flores enquanto elas choram de alegria com a chegada do primeiro raio de sol da manhã. Aqueles que caminham pela vegetação rasteira terão os pés lavados por mil mãos carinhosas, obra de Deus. Cristo não é retratado como o orvalho da manhã, mas como o orvalho da juventude, e a imagem se amplia ainda mais.

A juventude é a estação da energia abundante. Alguns não conseguem ficar parados. Em geral, são seres sociáveis que amam as atividades sociais. Isso não é virtude nem vício. É, antes, uma característica natural. Com o avanço dos anos, há uma tendência gradual que doma e tempera a alma. À medida que a vida progride, a visão se torna mais clara e o pensamento mais firme, e nos elevamos a coisas melhores. Mas, quando ultrapassamos o auge da meia-idade e os pés descem a encosta, aquele ímpeto tumultuoso de energia física que abria caminho por tudo passa a ser guardado como lembrança do passado. Para muitos, é o consolo mais próximo que encontram dos dias passados de vigor.

Mas Cristo não nos chamou a cultivar apego ao passado nem um anseio nostálgico pelo “vigor” da nossa juventude. Muitos hoje lamentam, tristemente, que sua disposição para agir tenha ido embora. Eles não têm visão de coisas mais elevadas e sentem mais energia com uma lata de Mountain Dew do que com o Orvalho da Juventude. Inspiram-se mais numa viagem pela estrada das lembranças e em recordar acontecimentos passados do que na esperança que está diante deles.

A idade não é impedimento para alcançar o orvalho da juventude. O Ancião de Dias ainda caminha entre os candeeiros de ouro. Enquanto João contemplava os cabelos ... brancos como a lã, brancos como a neve… –Apocalipse 1:14, Salomão declara …os seus cabelos são crespos e pretos como o corvo –Cântico dos Cânticos 5:11. Embora a idade possa roubar nossa força e audição, …a mão do SENHOR não está encolhida, para que não possa salvar, nem o seu ouvido agravado, para que não possa ouvir: –Isaías 59:1. Ele assegurou o orvalho da juventude e nos convida a dele participar. O problema não está em nosso corpo que se deteriora, mas numa mente que declina espiritualmente. O flagelo da velhice se instala predominantemente quando a mente acompanha o corpo.

Não é que a vida se torne mais pobre à medida que avança, ou deixe de ser nobre quando o encanto da juventude se dissipa. Se estivéssemos aqui apenas para experimentar alegria, o fim do romance juvenil seria terrível. Deus tinha um propósito muito maior para Seus filhos do que simplesmente serem “realizadores” cheios de vigor. Somos enviados aqui para aprender. Todos os anos que nos foram concedidos na terra devem ser um período de aprendizado, e não é no romance radiante da juventude que aprendemos as lições melhores e mais duradouras. Aprendemos ao cumprir tenazmente nossos deveres, aceitar com tranquilidade nossas limitações, carregar com paciência nosso fardo diário e estender a mão para ajudar nosso irmão. Essas coisas nos oferecem as verdadeiras oportunidades para o cultivo cristão e são as raízes da nobreza ética. Cristo trabalhou …não pela comida que perece, mas pela comida que permanece para a vida eterna… –João 6:27, e concluiu Sua tarefa terrena em 33 anos. Mas o orvalho da juventude não se dissipou quando Ele se assentou à direita de Seu Pai.

Assim, concluímos que essa juventude não será alcançada pela força, mas pela…

...Esperança

Mas este, havendo oferecido para sempre um único sacrifício pelos pecados, assentou-se à direita de Deus; daí em diante, esperando até que os seus inimigos sejam postos por escabelo dos seus pés. –Hebreus 10:12-13.

Como devemos imaginar Cristo agora? Reclinando-se numa poltrona, completamente exausto por Sua experiência com as pessoas obstinadas desta terra? Ocupado montando um álbum de lembranças preciosas? Essa é, com demasiada frequência, a condição dos idosos, e assim sua mente morre com o corpo.

E não somente isso, mas também nos gloriamos nas tribulações, sabendo que a tribulação produz paciência; e a paciência, experiência; e a experiência, esperança –Romanos 5:3-4. Às vezes, perguntamo-nos se essa passagem pode ser verdadeira. Qualquer pessoa que já tenha acumulado alguns anos de vida pode testemunhar uma experiência dolorosa e os sentimentos de desesperança que se seguem. Como pessoas, todos já enfrentamos experiências decepcionantes com o cônjuge, um filho ou uma relação na igreja, após as quais se instala uma persistente nuvem de desespero. Fora de Cristo, uma experiência amarga sempre tende ao pessimismo. Era assim no mundo quando Jesus veio. Continua assim hoje.

Mas o orvalho da juventude é incuravelmente esperançoso. Há uma expectativa efervescente, natural e magnífica, que nasce na juventude e permanece em Cristo. Em todo inverno, quando os campos estão desolados e o vento frio assobia por entre as árvores, permanece a esperança de que as flores voltarão a brotar. Em toda primavera há esperança de verão. Em todo verão há esperança de colheita. Isso vive na natureza e na juventude. Os que não conseguem enxergar isso colherão, na melhor das hipóteses, uma existência monótona e sombria. Viver é a coisa mais rara do mundo. A maioria das pessoas apenas existe. –Oscar Wilde.

Os demais serão grandemente beneficiados por uma esperança que…

…Cura Nossas Enfermidades

Nossos corpos estão destinados à sepultura e não têm esperança de renovação nesta vida. É em nossa mente que se encontram nossas maiores enfermidades. O homem paralítico de 38 anos em Betesda só conseguiu expressar uma queixa desesperançada quando Cristo lhe perguntou: …Queres ficar são? –João 5:6. Ao despertar para seu novo dia, recebeu um novo remédio: …Eis que já estás são; não peques mais, para que não te suceda coisa pior –João 5:14. O que poderia ser pior do que ficar paralítico por anos? Uma mente assolada pela indulgência dolorosa nas tristezas deste mundo. A idade se instala quando temos mais lembranças do passado do que esperança para o amanhã. É decepcionante quando as pessoas envelhecem sem ter visão para o amanhã, mas é desastroso ver jovens afligidos por seus efeitos paralisantes. Muitos tateiam sem rumo pelas diversas provações da vida, entorpecidos pela falta de bem-aventurança. O sol do meio-dia evaporou o orvalho de sua juventude, e o único louvor que conseguem reunir é composto de um punhado de prazeres de ontem. Uma nova atitude precisa nascer com o orvalho de uma nova manhã.

…Humilha Nossas Ambições

Em verdade, em verdade te digo que, quando eras jovem, te cingias a ti mesmo e andavas por onde querias; mas, quando fores velho, estenderás as mãos, e outro te cingirá e te levará para onde não queres. –João 21:18. Quando somos jovens, podemos vencer com a força da juventude. À medida que a idade avança, encontraremos outra alternativa: vitória por meio da rendição.

…Escrevi-vos, jovens, porque sois fortes, e a palavra de Deus permanece em vós, e já vencestes o maligno. –1 João 2:14. O mundo nos seduz a viver de modo egoísta. Os jovens muitas vezes frequentam instituições de ensino que lhes ensinam a “ser tudo o que puderem ser”. Há grande ênfase no aperfeiçoamento pessoal e na preparação para o futuro. Isso talvez os prepare para um mundo de “sobrevivência do mais apto”, mas os deixará desamparados quando a força e o vigor da juventude tiverem partido.

Porque tudo o que há no mundo, a concupiscência da carne, a concupiscência dos olhos e a soberba da vida, não procede do Pai, mas do mundo. E o mundo passa, e a sua concupiscência; mas aquele que faz a vontade de Deus permanece para sempre. –1 João 2:16-17. Vencer o mal com o bem é o antídoto bíblico para canalizar as energias juvenis. Quer se trate do desejo interior ou do anseio exterior, a esperança é concebida quando plantamos uma semente de bondade na vida de outra pessoa. A busca do prazer em lugar do lazer sempre decepcionará quem a busca e o deixará num vale de desespero mais profundo do que aquele em que começou. Bom é que o homem leve o jugo na sua mocidade … Ponha a boca no pó; talvez ainda haja esperança. –Lamentações 3:27-29. Fomos criados para trabalhar na vinha de Deus, e aqueles que tiverem apetite por isso colherão na esperança da recompensa juvenil que ela traz.

…Santifica Nossas Provações

Porque somos salvos pela esperança; mas a esperança que se vê não é esperança... –Romanos 8:24. Muitas vezes conseguimos nos identificar com Jó em seu sofrimento. Mas, antes que seu sofrimento recebesse sequer uma gota de retribuição, as correntes de cura começaram a fluir quando Jó reverenciou seu Criador. Quando reconhecemos que Deus é perfeito em todas as provações que permite, aprendemos então a adorar no templo não feito por mãos humanas e a desconsiderar as fraquezas do corpo. Sentar-se aos pés de Cristo acende uma centelha juvenil que irradia o espírito interior e concebe esperança. O orvalho da juventude torna-se então nossa porção, pois Cristo nos concede vida eterna e juventude eterna. Desde a hora da sepultura e por toda a eternidade seremos jovens e desafiaremos o cansaço e a morte, se estivermos vivendo na luz matinal de Jesus Cristo. O céu é um lugar de juventude perpétua; e, assim como a luz do sol se reflete na lua, também a luz de Cristo se reflete em Sua noiva. Ela é pura e jovem, …uma igreja gloriosa, sem mácula, nem ruga, nem coisa semelhante… –Efésios 5:27. Bendito o santo venerável que chega aos portais do céu nessa condição.

I rolled over in bed, listening to the sound of my pager going off. It couldn’t have been more than 15 minutes since I had dropped into bed from my last admission. I looked at the number on the pager. Yes, it was the Emergency Department again.

I attempted to rub the sleep out of my eyes and stir my still sleepy brain to wakefulness. I picked up the phone and dialed the ER. “Hey,” the ER doctor said. “I’ve got two admissions for you.”

“Oh,” I said sleepily.

“You sound tired,” he said, jokingly.

I was tired. After graduating from Medical School, doctors go through an intense training period called residency. The first two years of that training period involved overnight calls in the hospital. It wasn’t unusual to put in one hundred hours at the hospital in a week’s time.

Even when we weren’t on call, the days started early and went late. I often fought sleep as I was driving home from the hospital. I certainly learned a lot during that time, but I am also glad that those days are behind me.

Fatigue is part of the human condition. Everyone has had times when they struggled with tiredness. Maybe it was due to a job that needed to get done, a long trip, or sleepless nights due to a new baby in the family—whatever the difficulty, we determinedly push ourselves to make it through these challenging times.

From our childhood days we are taught that work is important. We need to be responsible and take care of the tasks that are set for us to do.

Work is ordained by God. In Genesis Chapter 2, God gave Adam the task of caring for the Garden of Eden. Later, in Deuteronomy 5:13, the Israelites were commanded to do all their work in six days and then rest the seventh day.

The New Testament gives a couple of more reasons to work. We are to work so we can provide for our families (see II Thessalonians 3:10). In addition, we are to work so we can give to others who are in need (see Ephesians 4:28).

God expects us to work and that we do it in a way that will glorify Him. However, we also have need of rest, which God made provision for as well.

God Exemplified Rest in the Creation

And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made. And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made –Genesis 2:2-3.

When God created the universe, including the earth and all it contains, it took Him just six days. Since God is God, we can be certain that He wasn’t tired at the end of this work. Yet, despite that fact, He took a day of rest and set it apart. He did it as an example for us.

Even though the law of the Sabbath would not be instituted for at least two thousand years, the precedent was set in Creation… Rest one day a week.

God Mandated Rest in the Law

Perhaps the thing that comes to mind first is the Sabbath Day laws that were given in Exodus 20:8-11. It was specifically commanded that the people were not to work on the Sabbath. And further, they were not to cause other people to work either.

Another law which seemed very much focused on the need for rest was the Year of Jubilee. In Leviticus 25, this law mandated that every seven years the land was to lie fallow for the whole year, slaves were to be released, land was to revert to its original family’s ownership, and debts were to be cancelled.

Within the Jubilee commands were certain promises. There was the promise of freedom—no matter how bad things had been the previous six years there would be a reset. It was a promise of inheritance—the things that had been lost and sold would be reclaimed. It was a promise of abundance—And if ye shall say, What shall we eat the seventh year? behold, we shall not sow, nor gather in our increase: Then I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth fruit for three years –Leviticus 25:20-21. Most of all, it was a promise of rest from labor—for the people and the land.

These commands were not put on the people to afflict them. Rather, God gave them knowing that without them His people would not rest enough and would not take enough time to focus on Him, their Creator.

Each one of us needs times of rest, but we need to understand that keeping the Sabbath is not simply about abstinence from work. Our efforts at keeping the Sabbath must include both rest and worship and it must be emphasized with the presence of God in our lives, without distraction.

The New Testament did not Change the Need for Rest

One of the verses that comes to my mind when I think about rest, is a promise that Jesus gave. Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light –Matthew 11:28-30.

The biblical book of Hebrews also speaks of the importance of rest and of our entering into God’s rest. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrews 4:9-11.

It is important to see that the New Testament concept of rest is more than simply time off from work. True biblical peace is intrinsically intertwined with the concept of peace, even in the midst of a chaotic world. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid –John 14:27. Jesus gave peace to His followers that allowed them to be at rest, even when they were dealing with high levels of stress.

This is a blessing, for it is not enough simply to take time off from our normal work. We need to have that peace and calm which a connection with Jesus offers. Without …the peace of God, which passeth all understanding… –Philippians 4:7, our time off will be just as unrestful as our time at work.

It is clear that God wants us to rest. He knows that we need it, not just for spiritual reasons, but also for our physical health.

******************************

The folks in charge of the French Revolution made an attempt to eliminate all the institutions of the past. It was a particularly godless endeavor and among other things, the new government decided to “reform” the calendar.

In 1793, they established a ten-day work week. Each month would have three weeks with one rest day in each of these ten-day weeks. Their goal, among other things, was to eliminate all religious holidays and the celebration of Sunday as a day of rest. They believed that more work would be done by having fewer days of rest each month.

This created a huge headache for watchmakers. They needed to somehow make watches that would support the details of these new decrees—each day would be ten hours long, each hour would contain one hundred minutes, and each minute would be 100 seconds long.

It turned out to be a disaster. The people hated the changes and productivity dropped considerably across France. Finally, in 1806, Napoleon abolished it and went back to the old calendar and the system of Sunday days of rest. This scientific “experiment” was over. It turns out that people need times of rest and recharging and that a seven-day week with one day off to rest is not just a Christian concept, it is something that is necessary for health and wellbeing.

The Soviet Union, under Joseph Stalin, also tried a similar experiment of eliminating Sunday rest, with similar results.

******************************

The week, as God created it, (with one day in seven for rest) is necessary for us to remain productive.

Rest Reduces Inflammation

Part of the problem that modern people face is that they deal with high levels stress hormones, like adrenaline and cortisol. These hormones increase blood pressure and pulse rates. They also increase levels of inflammation in our bodies.

Chronic inflammation is not healthy, but fortunately, rest really seems to help bring those hormone levels down a lot. A good night of sleep is essential for healing, precisely because it turns down these hormones and allows healing of overworked nerves and tissues.

Autoimmune diseases and pain levels improve when people get adequate levels of sleep. Blood pressure and heart conditions also benefit when a person gets adequate amounts of restorative sleep.

Rest Allows for Healing

Exercise is a good thing. Doctors recommend doing regular cardiovascular exercise because it is healthy for our hearts, minds, and overall wellbeing.

It is not wise to exercise every day. It too, raises stress hormone levels and does not give our bodies adequate times to heal. People who exercise too frequently and with too much intensity are much more likely to end up with nagging injuries, joint and muscle pain, and fatigue. One study found that it takes 72 hours after doing weight training for muscles to fully recover.

People who exercise ideally need one to two days off a week to let their bodies recover from the activity. The harder you are training, the more you need those times of rest. Even someone who is training intensively for something like a marathon needs to take periodic days with no running or they will injure themselves.

Rest Decreases Pain Levels

There have been many studies that looked at people’s reports of sleep and looked at things like chronic pain and tension headaches. At least 50 percent of people with insomnia also have chronic pain. Of course, it could simply be that people with chronic pain don’t sleep as well as people who don’t have that.

There have been several studies that looked at people’s pain tolerance after sleep deprivation. They found that even a single night of sleep deprivation was enough to make people feel pain more acutely.

Rest Improves Our Immune Systems

There have been several studies that looked at function of different parts of our immune systems and found that they work better when study participants have adequate levels of sleep. Probably the fact that inflammation levels are higher when we don’t rest, increases the risks of infection.

When we push ourselves too hard without rest it is hard on our immune systems. On the other hand, the best way to recover is to make certain that we get sufficient rest.

There are many other things that rest does. It helps improve mood. It can help with academic performance and memory tasks.

As with all things, moderation is key. Someone who does nothing but rest and sleep, is not going to have any better function than someone who sleeps well for seven hours a night, nor will they be very productive.

There are some basic rules that can help us with times of rest.

Rest Regularly

The message of the Sabbath is that we need to take regular, short periods of time to rest. The Jubilee Years tell us that we need less frequent, longer times to recharge. It takes effort and scheduling to make certain that these times are truly restful.

Maybe it is a bit like a car. You can only drive so far on a tank of gas. If you always wait until the warning light turns on to fill up that tank, eventually you will have this happen when you are too far from a gas station to fill up before you run out of gas. There is never a good time to run out of gas. In the same way, we need to periodically recharge our spiritual, emotional, and physical batteries. There is no reason to wait until warning signs show up that we desperately need to take a break.

Rest Takes Preparation

The story of the gift of manna in Exodus 16 tells us that manna came every day. The people could not keep it for a second day because it would spoil. However, on Fridays, they were to gather extra since the next day was a day of rest and no manna came on the Sabbath. Those who had not gathered extra the day before went hungry.

In the same way, it takes preparation to have these sorts of times. It won’t be easy, but it is important.

Do Healthy Things With Your Rest

There is a tendency when people are under stress to eat unhealthy things. When people are exhausted, they don’t usually feel like exercising or taking walks. These are the sorts of things that can really help recharge us, both physically and emotionally.

Once again, this takes some effort, but choosing healthy options is important for our well-being.

Focus on God

I have left this till the last, but it is the most important aspect of rest. True rest grows, not out of medication or even multiple vacations, but out of a heart that is filled with peace. The peace which passes understanding comes from a heart that is focused on God.

Our times of prayer and Bible reading should be times of rest. If we can eliminate distractions and the challenges of our work and home life and train our gaze on the One who matters most, we will receive a real blessing and the recharging that our spirits need.

I am afraid that many people struggle to find rest because they are not truly at peace. Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief –Hebrew 4:11. The rest here is one that is promised to those who persevere and receive God’s peace.

Conclusion

Life is about balance. There are times when we need to work and there are times as well when we should rest. Figuring out this balance is the challenge which each of us faces. What is certain, is that every 24-hour day will be completely full by the time we get to the end of it.

God sees us and our limitations and desires for us to achieve this balance between our work and our times of rest. If we can only focus ourselves on Him, we will receive guidance in this balance.

Most of all, we will receive a peace that is without price, that will allow us to find rest—even during a storm.

我在床上翻了个身，听着传呼机响起的声音。从上一次收治病人后我倒头睡下，到现在肯定还不到十五分钟。我看了看传呼机上的号码。没错，又是急诊室。

我试着揉掉眼里的睡意，让仍然昏昏欲睡的大脑清醒过来。我拿起电话，拨通急诊室。“喂，”急诊医生说，“我这儿有两位病人要收治给你。”

“哦，”我睡意朦胧地说。

“听起来你很累啊，”他开玩笑地说。

我确实很累。医学院毕业后，医生要经历一段强度很大的培训，称为住院医师培训。培训的头两年包括在医院值夜班。一个星期在医院工作一百个小时，并不稀奇。

即使不值班，我们也总是很早开始一天的工作，很晚才结束。我开车从医院回家时，常常努力不让自己睡着。那段时间我当然学到了很多，但我也很庆幸那些日子已经过去了。

疲惫是人类处境的一部分。每个人都有过与疲倦搏斗的时候。也许是因为有工作必须完成、要走一段很长的路，或者家里有了新生儿而夜夜难眠——无论困难是什么，我们都会坚定地逼自己撑过去。

从童年起，我们就被教导工作很重要。我们需要负起责任，完成交给我们的任务。

工作是上帝所设立的。创世记第二章中，上帝交给亚当照料伊甸园的任务。后来，在申命记5:13中，以色列人受命要在六天内做完一切工作，第七天则要安息。

新约还给出了另外几个工作的理由。我们工作，是为了供养家人（见帖撒罗尼迦后书3:10）。此外，我们工作也是为了能够帮助有需要的人（见以弗所书4:28）。

上帝期望我们工作，并且以荣耀祂的方式工作。然而，我们也需要休息；上帝也为此作了安排。

上帝在创造中以身作则，显明安息

到第七日，上帝造物的工已经完毕，就在第七日歇了他一切的工。上帝赐福给第七日，定为圣日，因为在这日上帝歇了他一切创造的工——创世记2:2-3。

上帝创造宇宙，包括地球和其中的一切，只用了六天。既然上帝是上帝，我们可以肯定，祂并没有因为这番工作而疲倦。然而，尽管如此，祂还是休息了一天，并把这一天分别出来。祂这样做是给我们作榜样。

虽然安息日的律法要到至少两千年后才颁布，但创造时已经立下先例……每周安息一天。

上帝在律法中规定安息

我们首先想到的，或许是出埃及记20:8-11所颁布的安息日律法。律法明确规定，百姓不可在安息日工作。此外，他们也不可使别人工作。

另一条似乎特别着重安息需要的律法，是禧年。在利未记25章中，这条律法规定每逢第七年，土地要整年休耕，奴隶要获释，土地要归还原来的家族所有，债务也要取消。

禧年的命令中包含着一些应许。那是自由的应许——无论前六年境况多么糟糕，都将重新开始。那是产业的应许——失去和卖掉的东西将得以收回。那是丰盛的应许——你们若说：‘这第七年我们不耕种，也不收藏出产，吃什么呢？’我必在第六年将我的福赐给你们，地便生三年的土产——利未记25:20-21。最重要的是，这是让百姓和土地都得以停止劳作、安然休息的应许。

这些命令并不是为了苦待百姓才加给他们的。相反，上帝颁布这些命令，是因为祂知道，如果没有这些命令，祂的子民就不会充分安息，也不会留出足够的时间专注于祂——他们的创造主。

我们每个人都需要休息的时候，但我们要明白，守安息日并不只是停止工作。我们守安息日，既要安息，也要敬拜；还必须强调让上帝临在我们的生命中，不受干扰。

新约并没有改变人需要安息这一事实

我想到安息时，脑海里浮现的一节经文，是耶稣赐下的一个应许。凡劳苦担重担的人，可以到我这里来，我就使你们得安息。我心里柔和谦卑，你们当负我的轭，向我学习；这样，你们的心灵就必得安息。因为我的轭是容易的，我的担子是轻省的——马太福音11:28-30。

圣经中的希伯来书也谈到安息的重要，以及我们进入上帝的安息。这样看来，必另有一安息为上帝的子民存留。因为那进入安息的，乃是歇了自己的工，正如上帝歇了他的工一样。所以，我们务必竭力进入那安息，免得有人学那不信从的样子跌倒——希伯来书4:9-11。

重要的是要明白，新约所说的安息不只是停止工作一段时间。真正符合圣经的平安与平静这一概念密不可分，即使身处混乱的世界也是如此。我留下平安给你们；我将我的平安赐给你们。我所赐的，不像世人所赐的。你们心里不要忧愁，也不要胆怯——约翰福音14:27。耶稣赐给跟随祂的人平安，使他们能够安息，即使他们正承受着巨大的压力。

这是一个福分，因为仅仅从日常工作中抽出时间休息，并不足够。我们需要耶稣所带来的那份平安与宁静。没有……上帝所赐、出人意外的平安……——腓立比书4:7，我们的休息时间也会和工作时间一样不得安宁。

很清楚，上帝希望我们安息。祂知道我们需要安息，不只是出于属灵的原因，也是为了身体健康。

******************************

法国大革命的掌权者试图废除过去的一切制度。这是一项特别不敬畏上帝的举措；除此之外，新政府还决定“改革”历法。

1793年，他们制定了十天为一周的工作周。每个月有三周，每个十天的一周中有一天休息。他们的目标之一，是废除所有宗教节日，以及把星期日作为休息日来庆祝的做法。他们认为，每个月少休几天，就能做更多工作。

这给制表师带来了很大的麻烦。他们得想办法制造出能适应这些新法令要求的手表——一天要有十个小时，每小时一百分钟，每分钟一百秒。

结果这场改革成了灾难。人们痛恨这些改变，法国各地的生产力也大幅下降。最后，拿破仑于1806年废除了这套制度，恢复旧历法和星期日休息的制度。这场科学“实验”就此结束。事实证明，人们需要休息和恢复精力；七天一周、其中一天休息，并不只是基督教的观念，也是维持健康和身心安适所必需的。

约瑟夫·斯大林统治下的苏联也曾尝试过类似的做法，取消星期日休息，结果也大同小异。

******************************

上帝所创造的一周（七天中有一天休息）是我们保持工作效率所必需的。

安息能减轻炎症

现代人面临的问题之一，是体内肾上腺素和皮质醇等压力荷尔蒙水平偏高。这些荷尔蒙会使血压和脉搏加快，也会增加我们体内的炎症水平。

慢性炎症不利于健康，但幸运的是，休息似乎确实有助于大幅降低这些荷尔蒙的水平。睡个好觉对康复至关重要，正是因为睡眠能降低这些荷尔蒙，并让过度劳累的神经和组织得以修复。

人们获得充足睡眠后，自身免疫性疾病和疼痛程度会有所改善。充足的恢复性睡眠也有益于血压和心脏状况。

安息有助于康复

运动是有益的。医生建议定期进行有氧运动，因为这有益于心脏、头脑和整体健康。

每天锻炼并不明智。锻炼也会升高压力荷尔蒙的水平，而且不给身体足够的时间恢复。锻炼过于频繁、强度过大的人，更容易出现挥之不去的伤痛、关节和肌肉疼痛以及疲劳。一项研究发现，举重训练后，肌肉需要72小时才能完全恢复。

理想情况下，锻炼的人每周需要休息一到两天，让身体从运动中恢复。训练越艰苦，就越需要这些休息时间。即使是为了马拉松之类的赛事进行高强度训练的人，也需要定期安排不跑步的日子，否则就会受伤。

安息能减轻疼痛

许多研究调查了人们对睡眠的报告，并考察了慢性疼痛和紧张性头痛等问题。至少百分之五十的失眠者也患有慢性疼痛。当然，也可能只是因为有慢性疼痛的人睡得不如没有慢性疼痛的人好。

有几项研究考察了睡眠不足后人们对疼痛的耐受程度。研究发现，仅仅一夜睡眠不足，就足以让人更敏锐地感受到疼痛。

安息能增强我们的免疫系统

有几项研究考察了免疫系统不同部分的功能，发现研究参与者睡眠充足时，这些部分的工作状态更好。我们不休息时，炎症水平可能会升高，从而增加感染风险。

如果我们不休息、过度逼迫自己，免疫系统就会承受很大负担。另一方面，恢复的最佳方法是确保我们得到充足的休息。

安息还有许多其他益处。它有助于改善情绪，也有助于提升学业表现和记忆能力。

凡事都要适度。一个人如果除了休息和睡觉什么都不做，身体机能并不会比每晚睡好七小时的人更好，工作效率也不会高。

有一些基本原则可以帮助我们安排休息时间。

规律地休息

安息日的信息告诉我们，需要定期抽出短时间休息。禧年告诉我们，也需要不那么频繁、但时间更长的休息来恢复精力。要确保这些时间真正能让人休息，就需要付出努力并做好安排。

这或许有点像汽车。油箱里的油只能让你开那么远。如果你总是等到警示灯亮了才加油，迟早会遇到这样的情况：你离加油站太远，车子就已经没油了。没油抛锚从来不会挑一个好时候。同样，我们也需要定期为属灵、情感和身体的电池充电。没有理由非要等到出现警讯、急需休息时才停下来。

休息需要预备

出埃及记16章关于吗哪恩赐的记载告诉我们，吗哪每天都会降下。百姓不能把吗哪留到第二天，因为它会坏掉。然而，星期五他们要多收一些，因为第二天是安息日，不会有吗哪降下。前一天没有多收的人就挨了饿。

同样，要有这样的休息时间，也需要预先安排。这并不容易，但很重要。

休息时做有益健康的事

人在压力之下，往往会倾向于吃不健康的东西。疲惫不堪时，人通常也不想锻炼或散步。这些事情其实能帮助我们恢复精力，无论是身体上还是情绪上。

再说一次，这需要付出一些努力，但选择健康的做法对我们的身心健康很重要。

专注于上帝

我把这一点留到最后说，但它是安息最重要的方面。真正的安息不是来自药物，甚至也不是来自多次度假，而是来自一颗满有平安的心。那超乎理解的平安，来自一颗专注于上帝的心。

我们的祷告和读经时间应当成为安息的时刻。如果我们能除去干扰，放下工作和家庭生活中的种种难题，把目光定睛在那位最重要的主身上，就会得到真正的福分，灵里也会获得所需的更新。

我担心许多人难以找到安息，是因为他们内心并没有真正的平安。所以，我们务必竭力进入那安息，免得有人学那不信从的样子跌倒——希伯来书4:11。这里所说的安息，是应许给那些持守到底、领受上帝平安之人的。

结语

人生在于平衡。有时我们需要工作，有时也应该休息。如何找到这种平衡，是我们每个人都要面对的挑战。可以确定的是，每个二十四小时的一天，到结束时都会被填得满满当当。

上帝看见我们，也看见我们的局限；祂渴望我们在工作和休息之间取得平衡。只要我们专心仰望祂，就会在这种平衡上得到指引。

最重要的是，我们会得到一种无价的平安，使我们能够找到安息——即使身处风暴之中。

Do you want to have a good life? What is there that you believe you need to experience or accomplish so you can truly enjoy life? Many people’s main goal in life is to seek pleasure and to have fun. Much time and money are spent to achieve this. But do we accomplish it? In our natural mind we think that the circumstances need to be just right to please us. But we all know that circumstances are never ideal all the time. So, we can’t depend on those for our happiness. We need something bigger than that. Or Someone.

Obviously, we know that God alone is never changing and always faithful. Another thing about God is that He is sovereign. In other words, He’s in charge. But we like our independence; we like things to happen in a way that feels good to us. When life doesn’t happen that way, we are brought to a decision. Will we accept all of God—both His unchangeableness and His sovereignty—or will we fight to have our own way in our pursuit of a good life?

The root of joy is with God Himself. This is because He created us for Himself. He created us to bring pleasure to Himself, but we think we need to bring pleasure to ourselves. It started in the garden of Eden when the serpent convinced Eve that pleasing herself was more important than pleasing God. Since then, humans have been at war, both within their own hearts and without, with other folks. All in the effort of trying to find pleasure for themselves, yet not finding it because they were created to please God.

The solution for this war is found in James 4. It’s simple: submit to God. Humble yourselves before Him. This is not too much for Him to ask of us, because He is sovereign. He created us, so He has the say in how we live. If we will truly find enjoyment in life, it will be by putting our own life and desires on the cross and becoming one with God and His original purpose for us. Rather than it being restrictive, this opens up a world of opportunities and possibilities. It doesn’t mean we have to do things because God wants us to. Becoming one with God means that what He wants us to do is also what we want to do.

Worship and Gratitude

When we are one with God, our whole perspective changes. Instead of pining over all the things that aren’t ideal, we begin to see the many things that are true blessings. We can have a heart of worship and gratitude for all the good things that we do experience. We are able to see how unworthy we really are. We didn’t deserve anything good, but God has still given us so many things to enjoy!

Living in the Present

As young ladies, we have a tendency to dream, to live in a future that is idealistic and pleasant. We sometimes struggle to live in the present imperfect reality and find joy in it. But when God’s will becomes our will then true joy happens, because we are fulfilling His purpose for us.

We can learn to experience joy in any circumstance, even in mundane life. We’re afraid of living a boring life. We want it to be exciting. But He wants us to please Him, and when we do, we experience joy no matter the circumstances. However, we are also then available for Him to use in service to His Kingdom, and He may call us to opportunities that are exciting. But we won’t be effective in the exciting missions unless we have learned to be submitted to His will in everyday life.

Relationships

When we are finding joy and contentment in where God has us in the present, we are able to focus on developing solid, upbuilding relationships with those who are in our lives right now. God has created us as social people, and good relationships will bring true enjoyment to us. God is also able to use us in reaching out to other people. When we are one with Him, our focus is no longer on ourselves but on others. The life of God can flow through us and both show others the way to Him and give us joy and fulfillment in doing it.

Emotions

Another tendency we have is to let our emotions control us. And they will run wild if we are looking to our circumstances to give us pleasure. We will end up on a roller coaster of feelings dictated by whatever is happening at the moment. And then we escape to the dream world, which only distorts our view of reality even more. But God is steadfast, and when we are one with Him, He imparts to us stability and rest. And we are able to experience ever present joy—even in ever changing circumstances.

Let us continue to become ever more one with Him. And He will give us heavenly sunlight all of our journey, unchanged by circumstances on earth and realized in full when we see Him face to face. …in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore –Psalm 16:11.

Bila shaka, tunajua kwamba Mungu pekee habadiliki kamwe na ni mwaminifu daima. Jambo jingine kumhusu Mungu ni kwamba Yeye ni mkuu mwenye mamlaka. Kwa maneno mengine, Yeye ndiye mwenye madaraka. Lakini tunapenda uhuru wetu wa kujitegemea; tunapenda mambo yatendeke kwa namna inayotupendeza. Maisha yasipotokea hivyo, tunakabiliwa na uamuzi. Je, tutamkubali Mungu katika ukamilifu wake—kutobadilika kwake na mamlaka yake—au tutapambana ili mambo yaende kwa njia yetu tunapotafuta maisha mazuri?

Msingi wa furaha uko kwa Mungu mwenyewe. Hii ni kwa sababu alituumba kwa ajili yake mwenyewe. Alituumba ili tumletee furaha, lakini tunafikiri tunahitaji kujifurahisha wenyewe. Jambo hilo lilianza katika bustani ya Edeni wakati nyoka alipomshawishi Hawa kwamba kujifurahisha mwenyewe kulikuwa muhimu zaidi kuliko kumpendeza Mungu. Tangu wakati huo, wanadamu wamekuwa vitani, ndani ya mioyo yao wenyewe na nje yao, na watu wengine. Yote hayo ni juhudi za kujaribu kujipatia raha, lakini hawapati kwa sababu waliumbwa ili kumpendeza Mungu.

Suluhisho la vita hivi linapatikana katika Yakobo 4. Ni rahisi: mtiini Mungu. Jinyenyekezeni mbele zake. Hili si jambo kubwa mno kwake kutuomba, kwa sababu Yeye ni mkuu mwenye mamlaka. Alituumba, kwa hiyo ana haki ya kusema jinsi tunavyopaswa kuishi. Ikiwa tutafurahia maisha kweli, itakuwa kwa kuweka maisha na tamaa zetu wenyewe msalabani na kuwa wamoja na Mungu na kusudi lake la awali kwetu. Badala ya kutuzuia, hili hufungua ulimwengu wa fursa na uwezekano. Haimaanishi kwamba tunapaswa kufanya mambo kwa sababu tu Mungu anataka tufanye hivyo. Kuwa wamoja na Mungu kunamaanisha kwamba yale anayotaka tuyafanye ni yale tunayotaka pia kufanya.

Ibada na Shukrani

Tunapokuwa wamoja na Mungu, mtazamo wetu wote hubadilika. Badala ya kuomboleza juu ya mambo yote yasiyo bora, tunaanza kuona mambo mengi ambayo kwa kweli ni baraka. Tunaweza kuwa na moyo wa ibada na shukrani kwa mambo yote mema tunayopitia. Tunaweza kuona jinsi ambavyo kwa kweli hatustahili. Hatukustahili jambo lolote jema, lakini bado Mungu ametupa mambo mengi sana ya kufurahia!

Kuishi Katika Wakati wa Sasa

Sisi wasichana vijana tuna mwelekeo wa kuota ndoto, wa kuishi katika wakati ujao ulio bora kupita kiasi na wenye kupendeza. Wakati mwingine tunapata shida kuishi katika uhalisi usio mkamilifu wa sasa na kupata furaha ndani yake. Lakini mapenzi ya Mungu yanapokuwa mapenzi yetu, ndipo furaha ya kweli hutokea, kwa sababu tunatimiza kusudi lake kwetu.

Tunaweza kujifunza kupata furaha katika hali yoyote, hata katika maisha ya kawaida. Tunaogopa kuishi maisha ya kuchosha. Tunataka yawe ya kusisimua. Lakini Yeye anataka tumpendeze, na tunapofanya hivyo, tunapata furaha bila kujali hali zilivyo. Hata hivyo, basi pia tunakuwa tayari kutumiwa naye katika huduma kwa Ufalme wake, naye anaweza kutuita kwenye fursa za kusisimua. Lakini hatutakuwa na matokeo katika misheni hizo za kusisimua tusipokuwa tumejifunza kujitiisha chini ya mapenzi yake katika maisha ya kila siku.

Mahusiano

Tunapopata furaha na kuridhika katika mahali ambapo Mungu ametuweka sasa, tunaweza kukazia fikira kukuza mahusiano imara na yenye kujenga pamoja na wale walio katika maisha yetu kwa sasa. Mungu alituumba tukiwa watu wa kijamii, na mahusiano mazuri yatatuletea furaha ya kweli. Mungu pia anaweza kututumia kuwafikia watu wengine. Tunapokuwa wamoja naye, fikira zetu hazielekezwi tena kwetu wenyewe bali kwa wengine. Uzima wa Mungu unaweza kutiririka kupitia kwetu na kuwaonyesha wengine njia ya kumwendea, na kutuletea furaha na utimilifu tunapofanya hivyo.

Hisia

Mwelekeo mwingine tulio nao ni kuziacha hisia zetu zitutawale. Nazo zitakuwa zisizodhibitika ikiwa tunatazamia hali zetu zitupe raha. Mwishowe tutajikuta kwenye mzunguko wa hisia zinazotawaliwa na chochote kinachotokea wakati huo. Kisha tunakimbilia katika ulimwengu wa ndoto, ambao hupotosha hata zaidi mtazamo wetu wa uhalisi. Lakini Mungu ni thabiti, na tunapokuwa wamoja naye, hutujalia uthabiti na pumziko. Nasi tunaweza kupata furaha ya kudumu—hata katika hali zinazobadilika daima.

Na tuendelee kuwa wamoja naye zaidi na zaidi. Naye atatupa mwanga wa jua wa mbinguni katika safari yetu yote, usiobadilishwa na hali za duniani, nao utatimia kikamilifu tutakapomwona uso kwa uso. …mbele za uso wako ziko furaha tele; mkono wako wa kuume mna mema ya milele –Zaburi 16:11.

I’ll walk with God—Today—
Tomorrow may not be.
I’ll make the best of TIME—right now—
That God has granted me.

I’ll plan not for a life
That I might live in ease,
But only for today to live
My God alone to please.

Nor dare I think in years
Or move from leaps to bounds;
With God shut out, and self shut in
And selfish aims surround.

There are those who plan their lives,
Who give God little thought;
Who weigh themselves, not with God’s truth,
As every day they ought!

“Boast not thyself,” I’m warned,
“Of what tomorrow brings;
Thy health and wealth—e’en life itself—
May all at once take wings!”

“This night, that soul of thine
May be required of thee:
And dost thou plan the New Year full
There, ‘neath some Christmas tree?”

“Wake up! Take stock, are you prepared?
Your lessons learned alright?
If God, in yet three hours, THIS DAY,
Should close your course TONIGHT?”

오늘—나는 하나님과 함께 걷겠습니다—
내일은 오지 않을지도 모릅니다.
하나님께서 내게 허락하신
이 시간을—바로 지금—가장 귀하게 쓰겠습니다.

편안하게 살아갈
인생을 계획하지 않고,
오직 오늘을 살아
나의 하나님만 기쁘시게 하겠습니다.

감히 여러 해를 내다보거나
단숨에 큰 도약을 꿈꾸지 않겠습니다.
하나님은 밀어내고 자신만 가둔 채,
이기적인 목표에 둘러싸이지 않겠습니다.

자신의 삶을 계획하면서도
하나님은 거의 생각지 않는 이들이 있습니다.
날마다 마땅히 해야 할 대로
하나님의 진리로 자신을 살피지 않는 이들 말입니다!

“내일에 닥칠 일을 두고
자랑하지 말라”고 경고받습니다.
건강과 재산, 심지어 목숨까지도—
한순간에 날개를 달고 떠날 수 있습니다!

“오늘 밤 네 영혼을
네게서 거두어 갈 수도 있거늘,
네가 새해를 온전히 계획하느냐,
저기 어느 크리스마스트리 아래서?”

“깨어나라! 돌아보라, 준비되었느냐?
배워야 할 것들을 제대로 배웠느냐?
하나님께서 아직 세 시간이 남은 이 오늘,
오늘 밤 네 삶의 여정을 끝내신다면?”

Have you ever tried to change the world? I have. As a teenager I dreamed of the daring exploits I was going to do for God. As I set the table in my parent’s house, I waited for the day when I would be able to do greater things—things like setting up house in Africa, speaking strange languages, and leading people to Jesus. The thought of living in a mud hut and dodging venomous snakes seemed thrilling.

And then, part of my dreams came true! I left all I had ever known and had an adrenaline-fueled landing in an African country. I tried to change the small world I was in—that God-forsaken village full of drunkenness, broken marriages, fights, and neglected children. Daily I felt the angst of being so busy with “insignificant,” earthly tasks and wondered how to make a difference. Then suddenly, our labors were abruptly ended by burn-out and a host of government suspicions. None of this was in my dreams.

I still ask the same question, “God, how can I make a difference?” The neighbor calls at the door. The laundry lady needs her pay. Lunch needs to be on the table in 15 minutes. Our fifth grader needs help with multiplying fractions. The sky fills up with dark clouds and the clothesline is full of laundry. I wipe the baby’s nose for the umpteenth time as she sits on top of the table disrupting her brother’s books and papers. I bake bread, make yogurt, and churn butter, and cook 21 meals a week. I fold mountains of laundry and the next week I do it all over again. I sweep the floor that has accumulated an astonishing amount of dirt in only two hours. In many ways, life is more mundane than it ever was before.

I had no ability to change the world as a starry-eyed teen and neither do I have the ability now. God isn’t asking that of me. He only asks me to walk with Him and obey His voice. Slowly I am learning that the spiritual and physical are inseparable—even Jesus taught the gospel of the kingdom while resting, sleeping, and eating. Scrubbing a floor and slicing bread can be acts of worship to my Creator if I will deem them so. It is He who designed that my spiritual walk and the propagation thereof happens as my hands touch the earthly. This is how my spirit is refined. It’s the only way I can express my faith as a living faith. It’s the only way I can touch the hearts of my children and live out a practical gospel for them to imitate. It’s how my faith proves itself to be real to the unbeliever, as they see me struggle through the same things they do, along with my resulting responses.

Slowly I am learning that serving God isn’t about determination or changing the world. It’s about allowing God’s spirit to inhabit me, guide me, and speak to me. I am learning that God is more interested in the person I am becoming instead of everything I want to do for Him. Perhaps I am after all just a smoking flax instead of the one who will change the world. I think Paul could relate to that feeling when he wrote, But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence –1 Corinthians 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot said, “Sometimes the light rises excruciatingly slowly. The Kingdom of God is like leaven and seed, things which work silently, secretly, slowly, but there is in them an incalculable transforming power. Even in the plain soil, even in the dull dough, lies the possibility of transformation.”1

To have my heart set on accomplishments and success is a selfish way to live. When that village and those people were taken from us in a whirl of government issues and misunderstandings, I felt like God couldn’t possibly use this for anyone’s good. He still needed us there, right? The fact is, He didn’t need us there anymore. We were not indispensable. Perhaps God allowed it all in order to learn that His acceptance of me is not based on my accomplishments.

For who hath despised the day of small things… –Zechariah 4:10.

Who am I to judge if a certain work is small or not? Am I restless with my duties, believing God would be more pleased with my perception of ‘great’ duties, seemingly always out of reach? Am I forgetting that serving Christ is not about me and my sense of fulfillment, it is about God and the work He wants to do through me?! Amy Carmichael said, “It is not the place where we are, or the work that we do or cannot do that matters, it is something else. It is the fire within that burns and shines, whatever be our circumstances.”2

The fire that burns and shines within is our secret. That fire can burn while we scrub floors, cook endless meals, and home-school our children. It will touch the laundry lady, the house helper, the struggling girl at church and the neighbors. Sometimes it will happen sub-consciously, sometimes it happens if we decide to reach out instead of taking a nap or something else enjoyable, but always it takes forgetting ourselves, loving others, and noticing the small opportunities.

But beware… we cannot confuse our resignation to the smallness in our lives, with lethargy. Too many Christians do not expect God to use them, so they settle into a lethargic spiritual position. We should expect God to work in amazing ways. God might use us to accomplish those things, but it often happens in ways we least think of or expect.

The widow of Zarephath agreed to give her last handful of flour and the last remaining drops of oil to a stranger. She could have opposed the prophet and demanded he leave immediately, as after all, she was responsible for her son and that little bit of flour was all she had to give him. But no, she chose to give it all. God blessed her willing obedience by miraculously replenishing her flour and oil as long as she needed it.3

God kept culling Gideon’s army until he eventually fought and won the battle with just a few hundred men. Normally, Gideon was accustomed to armies of thousands. and now God was asking him to fight a momentous battle with only a few hundred. In the end, this human impossibility became an opportunity for God to show his power.4

At the beginning of His ministry, Jesus chose only twelve men to disciple, instead of the crowds. In the end, His small band of men deserted Him. He was mocked and killed. To everyone looking on, the remains of Jesus’ work seemed to have died with Him, yet the cosmic plan of redemption was being put into effect—those simple fishermen turned the world upside down with the gospel.5

We see from these examples that God is not looking for the biggest, the strongest, or the best. He doesn’t only use people with specialized skills or impressive gifts. Our strength and resources are often like the few hundred soldiers in Gideon’s army—simply not enough for the need. But when we give what we have with a willing heart, God multiplies our small efforts into a showcase of His grace—a showcase meant for Him, often not visible to others. The simple act of setting a table is an act of faith, of giving, of service, no matter where we are. God has chosen these weak things to be significant in His kingdom.

The secret to a successful life is Jesus in us, not our preconceived ideas of success. With Him working in and through us, His power will burn in our homes and neighborhoods. When He is the reason that we are living, we can trust Him with the outcome. Listening to the voice of Jesus, we can make a difference—one person, one encounter, one small thing at a time.

  1. Elisabeth Elliot, The Savage My Kinsman (revised edition Servant Publications 1981) epilogue pg 147
  2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, pg 218
  3. 1 Kings 17: 11-16
  4. Judges 7
  5. Luke 6:13-16, John 19
