Virei-me na cama, ouvindo o som do meu pager a tocar. Não podiam ter passado mais de 15 minutos desde que me deitara depois da minha última admissão. Olhei para o número no pager. Sim, era o Serviço de Urgência outra vez.

Tentei esfregar o sono dos olhos e despertar o meu cérebro, ainda sonolento. Peguei no telefone e liguei para o serviço de urgência. «Olá», disse o médico do serviço de urgência. «Tenho duas admissões para si.»

«Ah», respondi, sonolento.

«Parece cansado», disse ele, em tom de brincadeira.

Eu estava cansado. Depois de se formarem em Medicina, os médicos passam por um período de formação intensiva chamado residência. Os primeiros dois anos dessa formação incluíam turnos noturnos no hospital. Não era invulgar trabalhar cem horas no hospital numa semana.

Mesmo quando não estávamos de prevenção, os dias começavam cedo e acabavam tarde. Muitas vezes lutava contra o sono enquanto conduzia para casa, vindo do hospital. Certamente aprendi muito durante esse período, mas também fico feliz por esses dias já terem ficado para trás.

A fadiga faz parte da condição humana. Todos já passaram por momentos em que tiveram dificuldade com o cansaço. Talvez fosse devido a um trabalho que precisava de ser feito, a uma viagem longa ou a noites sem dormir por causa de um bebé recém-nascido na família — fosse qual fosse a dificuldade, esforçamo-nos com determinação para atravessar esses períodos desafiantes.

Desde a infância, ensinam-nos que o trabalho é importante. Precisamos de ser responsáveis e de cuidar das tarefas que nos são atribuídas.

O trabalho foi ordenado por Deus. Em Génesis, capítulo 2, Deus deu a Adão a tarefa de cuidar do Jardim do Éden. Mais tarde, em Deuteronómio 5:13, os israelitas receberam a ordem de fazer todo o seu trabalho em seis dias e depois descansar no sétimo.

O Novo Testamento apresenta mais algumas razões para trabalharmos. Devemos trabalhar para poder sustentar as nossas famílias (ver II Tessalonicenses 3:10). Além disso, devemos trabalhar para poder ajudar os que têm necessidade (ver Efésios 4:28).

Deus espera que trabalhemos e que o façamos de uma forma que O glorifique. No entanto, também precisamos de descansar, e Deus providenciou isso.

Deus deu o exemplo do descanso na Criação

E, havendo Deus acabado no dia sétimo a obra que fizera, descansou no sétimo dia de toda a sua obra que tinha feito. E abençoou Deus o dia sétimo, e o santificou; porque nele descansou de toda a sua obra que Deus criara e fizera –Génesis 2:2-3.

Quando Deus criou o universo, incluindo a terra e tudo o que ela contém, levou apenas seis dias. Sendo Deus, podemos ter a certeza de que não estava cansado no fim desse trabalho. Ainda assim, apesar disso, tirou um dia de descanso e separou-o dos outros. Fê-lo como exemplo para nós.

Embora a lei do sábado só fosse instituída pelo menos dois mil anos mais tarde, o precedente foi estabelecido na Criação… Descansar um dia por semana.

Deus ordenou o descanso na Lei

Talvez a primeira coisa que nos venha à mente sejam as leis relativas ao dia de sábado, dadas em Êxodo 20:8-11. Foi ordenado especificamente que o povo não trabalhasse no sábado. Além disso, não devia fazer com que outras pessoas trabalhassem.

Outra lei que parecia centrar-se bastante na necessidade de descanso era a do Ano do Jubileu. Em Levítico 25, essa lei determinava que, de sete em sete anos, a terra ficasse em pousio durante todo o ano, os escravos fossem libertados, as terras voltassem a pertencer à família a que originalmente pertenciam e as dívidas fossem canceladas.

As ordens relativas ao Jubileu incluíam certas promessas. Havia a promessa de liberdade — por pior que tivessem sido as coisas nos seis anos anteriores, haveria um recomeço. Havia a promessa de herança — as coisas que tinham sido perdidas e vendidas seriam recuperadas. Havia a promessa de abundância — E, se disserdes: Que comeremos no sétimo ano? Eis que não havemos de semear, nem colher o nosso produto. Então eu mandarei a minha bênção sobre vós no sexto ano, e ela dará fruto por três anos –Levítico 25:20-21. Acima de tudo, havia a promessa de descanso do trabalho — para o povo e para a terra.

Essas ordens não foram impostas ao povo para o afligir. Pelo contrário, Deus deu-as sabendo que, sem elas, o Seu povo não descansaria o suficiente nem dedicaria tempo bastante a concentrar-se n’Ele, o seu Criador.

Todos precisamos de períodos de descanso, mas temos de compreender que guardar o sábado não se resume a abster-se do trabalho. Os nossos esforços para guardar o sábado devem incluir tanto o descanso como a adoração, e devem ser marcados pela presença de Deus na nossa vida, sem distrações.

O Novo Testamento não alterou a necessidade de descanso

Um dos versículos que me vem à mente quando penso no descanso é uma promessa feita por Jesus. Vinde a mim, todos os que estais cansados e oprimidos, e eu vos aliviarei. Tomai sobre vós o meu jugo, e aprendei de mim, que sou manso e humilde de coração; e encontrareis descanso para a vossa alma. Porque o meu jugo é suave e o meu fardo é leve –Mateus 11:28-30.

O livro bíblico de Hebreus também fala da importância do descanso e de entrarmos no descanso de Deus. Portanto, resta ainda um repouso para o povo de Deus. Porque aquele que entrou no seu repouso, ele próprio repousou das suas obras, como Deus das suas. Procuremos, pois, entrar naquele repouso, para que ninguém caia no mesmo exemplo de desobediência –Hebreus 4:9-11.

É importante perceber que o conceito de descanso no Novo Testamento é mais do que simplesmente ter tempo livre do trabalho. A verdadeira paz bíblica está intrinsecamente ligada ao conceito de paz, mesmo no meio de um mundo caótico. Deixo-vos a paz, a minha paz vos dou; não vo-la dou como o mundo a dá. Não se turbe o vosso coração, nem se atemorize –João 14:27. Jesus deu aos Seus seguidores uma paz que lhes permitia descansar, mesmo quando enfrentavam níveis elevados de stress.

Isto é uma bênção, pois não basta simplesmente tirar tempo livre do nosso trabalho habitual. Precisamos de ter a paz e a tranquilidade que a ligação com Jesus oferece. Sem …a paz de Deus, que excede todo o entendimento… –Filipenses 4:7, o nosso tempo livre será tão inquieto como o tempo que passamos a trabalhar.

É evidente que Deus quer que descansemos. Ele sabe que precisamos disso, não apenas por razões espirituais, mas também para a nossa saúde física.

******************************

Os responsáveis pela Revolução Francesa tentaram eliminar todas as instituições do passado. Foi uma iniciativa particularmente ímpia e, entre outras coisas, o novo governo decidiu «reformar» o calendário.

Em 1793, instituíram uma semana de trabalho de dez dias. Cada mês teria três semanas, com um dia de descanso em cada uma dessas semanas de dez dias. Entre outros objetivos, queriam eliminar todos os feriados religiosos e a celebração do domingo como dia de descanso. Acreditavam que se trabalharia mais tendo menos dias de descanso por mês.

Isso criou uma enorme dor de cabeça para os relojoeiros. Precisavam de encontrar uma forma de fabricar relógios que correspondessem aos pormenores desses novos decretos — cada dia teria dez horas, cada hora teria cem minutos e cada minuto teria 100 segundos.

Acabou por ser um desastre. O povo detestou as mudanças e a produtividade caiu consideravelmente em toda a França. Por fim, em 1806, Napoleão aboliu o sistema e voltou ao calendário antigo e ao sistema de descanso aos domingos. Essa «experiência» científica chegou ao fim. Acontece que as pessoas precisam de períodos de descanso e recuperação, e que uma semana de sete dias com um dia de folga para descansar não é apenas um conceito cristão: é algo necessário para a saúde e o bem-estar.

A União Soviética, sob o governo de Josef Stalin, também tentou uma experiência semelhante, eliminando o descanso ao domingo, com resultados semelhantes.

******************************

A semana, tal como Deus a criou (com um dia de descanso em cada sete), é necessária para continuarmos produtivos.

O descanso reduz a inflamação

Parte do problema que as pessoas enfrentam hoje é terem níveis elevados de hormonas do stress, como a adrenalina e o cortisol. Essas hormonas aumentam a pressão arterial e a frequência cardíaca. Também aumentam os níveis de inflamação no nosso corpo.

A inflamação crónica não é saudável, mas, felizmente, o descanso parece ajudar bastante a baixar esses níveis hormonais. Uma boa noite de sono é essencial para a recuperação, precisamente porque reduz essas hormonas e permite a recuperação dos nervos e tecidos sobrecarregados.

As doenças autoimunes e os níveis de dor melhoram quando as pessoas dormem o suficiente. A pressão arterial e as doenças cardíacas também beneficiam quando uma pessoa dorme o suficiente para recuperar.

O descanso permite a recuperação

O exercício é algo bom. Os médicos recomendam a prática regular de exercício cardiovascular porque faz bem ao coração, à mente e ao bem-estar geral.

Não é sensato fazer exercício todos os dias. O exercício também aumenta os níveis das hormonas do stress e não dá ao nosso corpo tempo suficiente para recuperar. As pessoas que se exercitam com demasiada frequência e intensidade têm muito mais probabilidades de acabar com lesões persistentes, dores articulares e musculares e fadiga. Um estudo concluiu que os músculos levam 72 horas a recuperar totalmente depois de um treino com pesos.

Idealmente, as pessoas que fazem exercício precisam de um ou dois dias de descanso por semana para permitir que o corpo recupere da atividade. Quanto mais intensamente treinar, mais precisará desses períodos de descanso. Mesmo alguém que esteja a treinar intensivamente para algo como uma maratona precisa de tirar dias sem correr de vez em quando, ou irá lesionar-se.

O descanso reduz os níveis de dor

Foram realizados muitos estudos que analisaram os relatos das pessoas sobre o sono e aspetos como a dor crónica e as dores de cabeça tensionais. Pelo menos 50 por cento das pessoas com insónia também sofrem de dor crónica. É claro que pode simplesmente acontecer que as pessoas com dor crónica não durmam tão bem como as que não têm esse problema.

Vários estudos analisaram a tolerância à dor das pessoas depois de serem privadas de sono. Concluíram que até mesmo uma única noite sem dormir era suficiente para que as pessoas sentissem a dor de forma mais intensa.

O descanso melhora o nosso sistema imunitário

Vários estudos analisaram o funcionamento de diferentes partes do nosso sistema imunitário e concluíram que funcionam melhor quando os participantes dormem o suficiente. É provável que o facto de os níveis de inflamação serem mais elevados quando não descansamos aumente o risco de infeção.

Quando nos esforçamos demasiado sem descansar, isso sobrecarrega o nosso sistema imunitário. Por outro lado, a melhor forma de recuperar é garantir que descansamos o suficiente.

O descanso faz muitas outras coisas. Ajuda a melhorar o humor. Pode ajudar no desempenho académico e em tarefas que dependem da memória.

Como em tudo, a moderação é fundamental. Alguém que não faça outra coisa senão descansar e dormir não terá um funcionamento melhor do que alguém que dorme bem sete horas por noite, nem será muito produtivo.

Há algumas regras básicas que nos podem ajudar a reservar períodos de descanso.

Descanse regularmente

A mensagem do sábado é que precisamos de reservar regularmente períodos curtos para descansar. Os Anos do Jubileu ensinam-nos que também precisamos de períodos mais longos e menos frequentes para recuperar. É preciso esforço e planeamento para garantir que esses períodos sejam verdadeiramente repousantes.

Talvez seja um pouco como um carro. Só é possível percorrer determinada distância com um depósito de combustível. Se esperar sempre que a luz de aviso acenda para encher o depósito, acabará por acontecer que esteja demasiado longe de uma estação de serviço para o encher antes de ficar sem combustível. Nunca é uma boa altura para ficar sem combustível. Da mesma forma, precisamos de recarregar periodicamente as nossas baterias espirituais, emocionais e físicas. Não há motivo para esperar que apareçam sinais de alerta de que precisamos urgentemente de fazer uma pausa.

O descanso exige preparação

A história do dom do maná em Êxodo 16 ensina-nos que havia maná todos os dias. O povo não podia guardá-lo para o dia seguinte, porque se estragava. No entanto, às sextas-feiras, deviam recolher uma quantidade extra, pois o dia seguinte era de descanso e não havia maná no sábado. Os que não tinham recolhido uma quantidade extra no dia anterior passavam fome.

Da mesma forma, é preciso preparação para ter períodos deste tipo. Não será fácil, mas é importante.

Faça coisas saudáveis durante o descanso

As pessoas tendem a comer coisas pouco saudáveis quando estão sob stress. Quando estão exaustas, normalmente não lhes apetece fazer exercício nem dar passeios. No entanto, são precisamente esse tipo de coisas que podem ajudar-nos a recuperar, tanto física como emocionalmente.

Mais uma vez, isto exige algum esforço, mas escolher opções saudáveis é importante para o nosso bem-estar.

Concentre-se em Deus

Deixei este ponto para o fim, mas é o aspeto mais importante do descanso. O verdadeiro descanso nasce não da medicação, nem mesmo de várias férias, mas de um coração cheio de paz. A paz que excede o entendimento vem de um coração concentrado em Deus.

Os nossos momentos de oração e leitura da Bíblia devem ser momentos de descanso. Se conseguirmos eliminar as distrações e os desafios do trabalho e da vida em casa, e fixar o olhar n’Aquele que mais importa, receberemos uma verdadeira bênção e a renovação de que o nosso espírito precisa.

Receio que muitas pessoas tenham dificuldade em encontrar descanso por não estarem verdadeiramente em paz. Procuremos, pois, entrar naquele repouso, para que ninguém caia no mesmo exemplo de desobediência –Hebreus 4:11. O descanso aqui é aquele que está prometido aos que perseveram e recebem a paz de Deus.

Conclusão

A vida depende do equilíbrio. Há momentos em que precisamos de trabalhar e também há momentos em que devemos descansar. Encontrar esse equilíbrio é o desafio que cada um de nós enfrenta. Uma coisa é certa: cada período de 24 horas estará completamente preenchido quando chegarmos ao seu fim.

Deus vê-nos, vê as nossas limitações e deseja que alcancemos esse equilíbrio entre o trabalho e os períodos de descanso. Se conseguirmos concentrar-nos n’Ele, receberemos orientação para encontrar esse equilíbrio.

Acima de tudo, receberemos uma paz sem preço, que nos permitirá encontrar descanso — mesmo durante uma tempestade.

Greetings of Christian love to each one. Another year has passed us by, and another is spread out before us to navigate. What is our perspective? Do we have hope and joy bubbling up in our hearts or does the future seem full of gloom and doom? Do we see God’s sovereign hand at work in the situations and circumstances around us or does the world seem out of control from our vantage point?

As I interact with folks from around the country there seems to be a common issue that many folks are struggling with—weariness. Weary of mandates. Weary of shutdowns. Weary of all the bickering and fighting that has surrounded the Covid issue. Weary of…

It appears that many people just “Don’t want to think about it”. Why? I’m really not sure what all the reasons are, but I am sure that each person has one. Let’s remember that God wants us to …be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves –Matthew 10:16.

Here, in the United States of America, Christians have had over 60 years (since World War 2) of relative peace and tranquility. For the most part, we have been left alone to raise our families and worship the God of our fathers according to our conscience. We have enjoyed the separation of Church and State that was implemented at the beginning of our country’s existence. We have been able to work with our hands and earn a living. Many of us have lived off the fat of the land.

Maybe we were living in an artificial bubble. Maybe we have been lulled into a false sense of security. What about our counterparts in countries around the world, what is their reality of living as true Christians in their world? Sure, we have been able to use our wealth and freedom of movement to do much good for the rest of the world who have endured much hardship due to following Christ. But at what cost? What have our children learned?

Sometimes, we hear about first generation Christians being “on fire” for their Lord. Sometimes so much so that second and third generation Christians think that first generation Christians are perhaps a little too zealous in their efforts of evangelizing those around them.

What about the next generation? They are learning from someone—about God, themselves, and life. What are they learning? And who are they learning from? We must take stock to ensure that our children are learning life’s lessons in a way that they will be prepared to face the reality of things to come.

And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world? And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many –Matthew 24:3-5.

Remember that this is Jesus Himself speaking to His followers regarding the end of the world. His very first concern is that we would NOT be deceived. He says that deception will be the major issue surrounding the end of time. He says that many will come claiming to be Christ [or His direct spokesperson] in an attempt to gain a listening ear, all in an effort to deceive the hearer and gain a following.

If not before now, we most certainly must be teaching our children certain specific things through word and action. That we are to be strangers and pilgrims as we journey through this life. That if we are friends of this world then God will be our enemy. And that Jesus’ Kingdom is not of this world, therefore, His children must learn to live as ambassadors in a foreign land. Our children need to know that ALL who live godly in Christ Jesus WILL suffer persecution.

Many of the doctrines that have been taught in our churches and para-church functions have severely crippled the next generation of the church. We have been taught that we can have the “power of His resurrection” without needing to be a partaker of the “fellowship of His sufferings”. A suffering Christ with suffering followers has been thrown out in favor of following a Jesus who will not let anything bad happen to you. While there is much emphasis on a Jesus who suffered and died for you, there is very little to NO teaching on the need to “take up your cross daily” and follow Him.

Mental Health and Emotional Stability

Some years ago, I came across the story of a soldier, who, after serving a term of service in Iraq, was struggling to cope with PTSD. Sure, I believe that PTSD is real, and the struggles are real, but as I read this man’s story, I found myself becoming increasingly frustrated with the lack of answers that were being provided to a severely struggling young man. Some of his deepest struggles stemmed from the flashback memories he had of when he had personally killed several of the enemy. No matter how many counseling sessions he went to he just couldn’t come to a place of inner peace and rest. His mind was troubled. He had difficulty sleeping. He had problems getting along with others.

I had to think “If only someone could come alongside this young man and share the Gospel of Jesus Christ with him. If only he could be shown the Truth of God’s Word that to take another human’s life is sin in God’s eyes (even if he is the enemy) and God will not allow him to have peace in his heart until that is taken care of. Also, that the real excitement is that IF he would come to God according to the terms of the Bible and repent of his sin, then he could start walking with God and God could start giving him peace for his troubled soul.”

Over the last number of years, there have been numerous mass shootings here in the United States. Each time the public officials hold news conferences and share their thoughts in an effort to try to make sense out of another seemingly unexplainable tragic event. Usually, it’s not long until someone is talking about mental health and the need to step up public efforts to provide safety nets, screenings, and better and more treatments to curb this senseless violence.

Several weeks ago, there was a terrible, tragic event that took place in another state from where I live. In one of the big cities, a man pushed a woman off of the platform and into the path of an oncoming subway train. She didn’t survive. In the aftermath of such a horrific happening, the public officials made statements to the public in an effort to stem the potential public fear. They concluded that the man must have been emotionally troubled and that they would be stepping up their efforts in trying to provide a safety net for those with mental health issues, so that such things wouldn’t happen again.

Sure, when we look at the issue through the eyes of the world it seems to make sense. But is this the whole of the matter? Have we as Christians become so used to the ways of the world that we forget how far they have strayed from the Truth of God’s Word?

Let’s not point our finger at the world and the elected public officials. Are we, as the church, any better? How well do we know our Bible? How well do we know our Savior? When someone comes to us seeking peace and rest within do we know how to take them to the Scriptures, and lead them to Jesus who can then show them the way to the Father?

Why am I saying all this? If we continue to provide the next generation of the church with artificial answers and temporary solutions to the problems of life, then they will NOT be prepared to …endure unto the end… –Matthew 24:13.

And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24.

Kristna kärlekshälsningar till var och en. Ännu ett år har passerat, och ett nytt ligger framför oss att ta oss igenom. Hur ser vi på det? Bubblar hopp och glädje inom oss, eller verkar framtiden mörk och dyster? Ser vi Guds suveräna hand verka i situationerna och omständigheterna omkring oss, eller verkar världen vara utom kontroll ur vårt perspektiv?

När jag pratar med människor från hela landet verkar det finnas ett gemensamt problem som många brottas med – trötthet. Trötta på restriktioner. Trötta på nedstängningar. Trötta på allt käbbel och alla strider kring covidfrågan. Trötta på …

Det verkar som om många bara ”inte vill tänka på det”. Varför? Jag är verkligen inte säker på alla skälen, men jag är säker på att var och en har ett. Låt oss komma ihåg att Gud vill att vi ska …vara kloka som ormar och oskyldiga som duvor – Matteusevangeliet 10:16.

Här i Amerikas förenta stater har kristna haft över 60 år (sedan andra världskriget) av relativ fred och ro. För det mesta har vi fått vara i fred och uppfostra våra familjer och tillbe våra fäders Gud efter vårt samvete. Vi har åtnjutit åtskillnaden mellan kyrka och stat, som infördes när vårt land grundades. Vi har kunnat arbeta med våra händer och försörja oss. Många av oss har levt i överflöd.

Kanske levde vi i en konstgjord bubbla. Kanske har vi invaggats i en falsk trygghetskänsla. Hur ser verkligheten ut för våra motsvarigheter i länder runt om i världen, när de lever som sanna kristna i sin omvärld? Visst har vi kunnat använda vårt välstånd och vår rörelsefrihet till att göra mycket gott för resten av världen, där människor har fått utstå stora svårigheter för att de följer Kristus. Men till vilket pris? Vad har våra barn fått lära sig?

Ibland hör vi talas om första generationens kristna som är ”brinnande” för sin Herre. Ibland så brinnande att kristna i andra och tredje generationen kanske tycker att första generationens kristna är lite väl ivriga i sina försök att evangelisera människorna omkring sig.

Hur blir det med nästa generation? De lär sig av någon – om Gud, sig själva och livet. Vad lär de sig? Och av vem? Vi måste göra en bedömning för att försäkra oss om att våra barn lär sig livets läxor på ett sätt som gör dem redo att möta verkligheten i det som ska komma.

När han satt på Olivberget kom lärjungarna fram till honom i enrum och frågade: ”Säg oss, när ska detta ske, och vad blir tecknet på din återkomst och tidsålderns slut?” Jesus svarade dem: ”Se till att ingen bedrar er. Många ska komma i mitt namn och säga: Jag är Kristus, och de ska bedra många.” – Matteusevangeliet 24:3–5.

Kom ihåg att det är Jesus själv som talar till sina efterföljare om världens slut. Hans allra första oro är att vi INTE ska bli bedragna. Han säger att bedrägeri kommer att vara den stora frågan kring tidens slut. Han säger att många ska komma och hävda att de är Kristus [eller hans direkta talesperson] för att få människor att lyssna, allt i syfte att bedra den som lyssnar och vinna anhängare.

Om vi inte redan har gjort det, måste vi verkligen lära våra barn vissa saker, både genom ord och handling. Att vi ska vara främlingar och pilgrimer när vi vandrar genom detta liv. Att Gud blir vår fiende om vi är vänner med den här världen. Och att Jesu rike inte är av den här världen; därför måste hans barn lära sig att leva som ambassadörer i ett främmande land. Våra barn behöver veta att ALLA som lever gudfruktigt i Kristus Jesus KOMMER att bli förföljda.

Många av de läror som har förmedlats i våra kyrkor och i verksamheter knutna till kyrkorna har allvarligt hämmat kyrkans nästa generation. Vi har fått lära oss att vi kan ha ”kraften från hans uppståndelse” utan att behöva vara delaktiga i ”gemenskapen i hans lidanden”. En lidande Kristus med lidande efterföljare har kastats åt sidan till förmån för att följa en Jesus som inte låter något ont hända oss. Samtidigt som man lägger stor vikt vid Jesus som led och dog för oss, undervisar man mycket lite, eller INTE ALLS, om behovet av att ”ta sitt kors på sig varje dag” och följa honom.

Psykisk hälsa och känslomässig stabilitet

För några år sedan kom jag över berättelsen om en soldat som efter en tjänstgöringsperiod i Irak kämpade med att hantera posttraumatiskt stressyndrom. Visst tror jag att posttraumatiskt stressyndrom är verkligt och att svårigheterna är verkliga, men när jag läste den här mannens berättelse blev jag alltmer frustrerad över bristen på svar till en ung man som kämpade svårt. En del av hans djupaste svårigheter kom från återblickar till minnen av när han själv hade dödat flera av fienden. Oavsett hur många rådgivningssamtal han gick på kunde han inte finna inre frid och ro. Hans sinne var oroligt. Han hade svårt att sova. Han hade problem med att komma överens med andra.

Jag tänkte: ”Om ändå någon kunde finnas vid den här unge mannens sida och dela Jesu Kristi evangelium med honom. Om han ändå kunde få se sanningen i Guds ord: att ta en annan människas liv är synd i Guds ögon (även om det är fienden), och att Gud inte låter honom få frid i sitt hjärta förrän den saken har blivit uppklarad. Och det verkligt glädjande är att OM han kom till Gud på Bibelns villkor och omvände sig från sin synd, då skulle han kunna börja vandra med Gud, och Gud skulle kunna börja ge frid åt hans oroliga själ.”

Under de senaste åren har det förekommit flera masskjutningar här i USA. Varje gång håller offentliga tjänstemän presskonferenser och delar sina tankar i ett försök att försöka förstå ännu en till synes oförklarlig tragisk händelse. Vanligtvis dröjer det inte länge förrän någon talar om psykisk hälsa och behovet av att öka samhällets insatser för att tillhandahålla skyddsnät, undersökningar och bättre och fler behandlingar för att hejda detta meningslösa våld.

För flera veckor sedan inträffade en fruktansvärd, tragisk händelse i en annan delstat än den där jag bor. I en av de stora städerna knuffade en man ner en kvinna från perrongen och ut framför ett mötande tunnelbanetåg. Hon överlevde inte. Efter en sådan fruktansvärd händelse gjorde offentliga tjänstemän uttalanden till allmänheten i ett försök att dämpa den oro som kunde uppstå. De drog slutsatsen att mannen måste ha varit känslomässigt störd och att de skulle öka sina insatser för att försöka tillhandahålla ett skyddsnät för människor med psykiska problem, så att sådant inte skulle hända igen.

Visst verkar det rimligt när vi ser på frågan genom världens ögon. Men är detta hela saken? Har vi som kristna blivit så vana vid världens sätt att vi glömmer hur långt den har avlägsnat sig från sanningen i Guds ord?

Låt oss inte peka finger åt världen och de folkvalda offentliga tjänstemännen. Är vi som kyrka bättre? Hur väl känner vi vår Bibel? Hur väl känner vi vår Frälsare? När någon kommer till oss och söker frid och ro inom sig, vet vi då hur vi ska föra dem till Skrifterna och leda dem till Jesus, som sedan kan visa dem vägen till Fadern?

Varför säger jag allt detta? Om vi fortsätter att ge kyrkans nästa generation konstgjorda svar och tillfälliga lösningar på livets problem, kommer de INTE att vara redo att …hålla ut till slutet… – Matteusevangeliet 24:13.

Han sade till alla: ”Om någon vill följa mig, ska han förneka sig själv och varje dag ta sitt kors och följa mig. Den som vill rädda sitt liv ska mista det, men den som mister sitt liv för min skull ska rädda det.” – Lukasevangeliet 9:23–24.

Thou hast the dew of thy youth. Psalm 110:3

There are many aspects of youth which are not virtuous. Many youth of our day experience an early season of callused carelessness and casualty. Often decisions that are made in youthful years set the foundation for the rest of their lives. It was a the younger prodigal brother that asked for an early draw on his inheritance then went and wasted it on riotous living. It was a young Dinah who wandered from her father’s house and …went out to see the daughters of the land –Genesis 34:1. There, she was exposed to the heathen young men of the land and occasioned a bloody massacre, leaving Jacob as a stench in the land. Many foolish young people have sown to the wind and reaped the havoc thereof. Those that are void of solid principles and parental authority are at high risk for spiritual shipwreck.

There are particular lusts that inflict youth more so than the aged, and the young are exhorted to flee them. (–see 2 Timothy 2:22) Solomon looked through his window casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding -Proverbs 7:6-7. The young man was in heartfelt pursuit of that which appeared lovely… [Un]Till a dart [struck] through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life –Proverbs 7:23. We could examine the vices from the youthful lives of Rehoboam, Amnon, Nadab and Abihu, and countless others. We also find no lack of modern, folly-filled examples about us fulfilled by frivolous youth.

But youth are not meant to be despised. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. In fact, God generally chooses the youth as the instruments of His propagation. Joseph, of sterling character, was sent by God into Egypt at the age of 17 to preserve life (–see Genesis 45:5). Miriam, at the age of twelve, stood post over the future deliverer of the entire Jewish nation and secured her own mother, Jochebed, to be the nurse of the baby Moses. David, as a youth, was sent to encourage his brethren in the army. He was despised by his brothers: …I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart… –1 Samuel 17:28. He was rejected by Saul: …Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth… –1 Samuel 17:33. He was scorned by Goliath: …Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves… –1 Samuel 17:43. But their contempt was all for naught when he was chosen by God to be king over all Israel.

These noble youthful ambitions were followed by Josiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Mary, and the disciples of the Lord, all who chose to remember their Creator in the days of their youth. But these were not naive specimens seeking to secure their place in life, they were graphic examples of youth who were seeking to imitate the image of their Lord.

We need not gaze long into the character of Christ before we find…

...Thou hast the dew of thy youth

Psalm 110 is perhaps the most referred-to scripture in the Old Testament. This rhetorical portrait of the Messiah reveals a vivid virtue for us to behold. Christ, as the Ancient of days, was described in the Revelation having His head and His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet, here He is depicted as eternally young, as He sits at the right hand of God (–see Psalm 110:1). No weariness of age can enter there, for Christ is the Morning Star. It is perpetual morning around the throne of God. Those saints who are following hard after His likeness will also reflect this virtue, for the light of Jesus is the light of youth.

The psalmist, describing the Messiah, draws from the natural beauty of the morning dew (–see Psalm 110:3). The thought of dew calls us back from the heavens and unveils before us a portrait of this earth on which we dwell. In heaven there is no night, no change of heat and cold, no need of the sun to light up the day and consequently… no dew. The nature of dew belongs to the terrestrial, where everyone who will but stoop to observe it will behold a uniformed regiment of grass sparkling as if embedded with a myriad of diamonds. After a long night of darkness, the dewdrops, like tears, stand in the eyes of the flowers as they weep for joy at the advent of the first morning sunbeam. Those who walk through the lowly vegetation will have their feet washed by a thousand caressing hands of God’s design. Christ is not depicted as the dew of the morning but as the dew of youth, and the imagery is stretched further.

Youth is the season of abounding energy. Some cannot sit still. They are generally interpersonal creatures who love social activity. This is neither a virtue nor a vice. Rather, it is nominal nature. There is a progressive strain in advancing years that tames and tempers the soul. As life progresses, there is a clearer vision and a steadier thought, and we rise to better things. But when the mid-life summit has been crossed and the feet are traveling downward on the slope, that tumultuous rush of bodily energy that plowed through anything becomes enshrined with memories of the past. It is the closest comfort many can find to the bygone days of their strength.

But Christ has not called us to foster a fondness for the past nor a wistful longing for the “DO” of our youth. So many today sadly lament that their ‘get-up-and-go’ has got up and went. These have no vision for higher things and are more energized by a can of Mountain Dew than the Dew of Youth. They are more inspired by a trip down memory lane and reminiscing events of the past than of the hope that lies before them.

Age is no hindrance to securing the dew of youth. The Ancient of Days still rides forth among the golden candlesticks. While John beheld His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet Solomon declares …his locks are bushy, and black as a raven –Song of Solomon 5:11. While age may steal our strength and hearing, …the LORD’S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: –Isaiah 59:1. He has secured the dew of youth and invites us to partake. The problem is not found in our deteriorating body but in a spiritually declining mind. The bane of old age predominately sets in when the mind follows the body.

It is not that life grows poorer as it advances or ceases to be noble when the charm of youth has faded. If we were placed here only to experience joy, the dying out of youthful romance would be terrible. God had a much greater end in view for His children than to just be vibrant ‘doers’. We are sent here to learn. Our allotted years upon earth are all meant to be a schooling, and it is not in the bright romance of youth that we learn the best and most abiding lessons. It is in the dogged doing of our duty, the quiet acceptance of our limitations, the patient carrying of our daily burden, and in the stretching out of a helping hand to our brother. These afford us the true opportunities for Christian culture and are the roots of ethical nobility. Christ labored …not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life… –John 6:27, and He finished His earthly task in 33 years. But the dew of youth did not dissipate as He sat down at the right hand of His Father.

Thus, we conclude that this youthfulness will not be secured by strength, but by…

...Hope

But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. –Hebrews 10:12-13.

How shall we picture this Christ now? Reclining in an easy chair, all worn out from His experience with the stubborn people of this earth? Is He busy putting together a scrap book of precious memories? This is too often the position of the aged and so their mind dies with their bodies.

And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope –Romans 5:3-4. At times, we wonder if this scripture can be true. Anyone with any age on their bones can testify to a poor experience and the subsequent feelings of hopelessness following. As people, we have all faced disappointing experiences with a spouse, a child, or a church relationship after which a nagging cloud of despair settles in. Outside of Christ, a sour experience always tends to pessimism. It was so in the world when Jesus came. It is still so today.

But the dew of youth is incurably hopeful. There is an effervescent expectation that is naturally and magnificently borne in youth and retained in Christ. In every winter, when the fields are bleak, and the cold gust goes whistling through the trees, there lies the hope that the flowers will spring again. In every spring there is the hope of summer. In every summer there is the hope of harvest. It is alive in nature and alive in youth. Those who are blind to it shall reap, at best, a dreary monotone existence. To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all. –Oscar Wilde.

The rest shall be brightly effected with a hope that…

…Heals Our Infirmities

Our bodies are destined for the grave and have no hope for renewal in this life. It is our minds that carry our greatest infirmities. The impotent man of 38 years at Bethesda could only utter a hopeless complaint when Christ asked him, …Wilt thou be made whole? –John 5:6. Upon the wake of his new day, a new remedy was given to him—… Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee –John 5:14. What could be worse than being a cripple for years? A mind that is beset by a doleful indulgence in the sorrows of this world. Age sets in when we have more memories of the past than hope for tomorrow. It is disappointing when folks grow old and have no vision for tomorrow, but it is a disaster to behold youth that are plagued by its crippling effects. Many grope aimlessly through life’s various trials, stupefied by the lack of blessedness. The noonday sun has evaporated the dew of their youth and the only praise that they can muster is culminated from a handful of yesterday’s pleasantries. A new attitude must be birthed by the dew of a new morning.

…Humbles Our Pursuits

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. –John 21:18. When we are young, we can overcome in the strength of our youth. As age takes its course, we will find a different alternative: victory through surrender.

…I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one. –1 John 2:14. The world entices us to selfish living. Youth are often subject to schools of learning that teach them to “be all that you can be”. There is a major focus on self-enhancement and preparation for the future. This may prepare them in a ‘survival of the fittest’ world but will leave them destitute when the strength and prowess of youth has departed.

For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever. –1 John 2:16-17. Overcoming evil with good is the Biblical antidote for channeling youthful energies. Whether it is the lust within or the longing without, hope is conceived by planting a seed of kindness in the life of another. The pursuit of pleasure and lieu of leisure will always disappoint its recipient and leave him in a valley of despair deeper than when he began. It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth … He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope. –Lamentations 3:27-29. We are created to work in God’s vineyard and those who have an appetite for it will reap in hope of its youthful reward.

…Hallows Our Trials

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope... –Romans 8:24. How often we can relate to Job in his pain. But before his pain had received an ounce of retribution, the healing streams began to flow as Job reverenced his Creator. When we can acknowledge that God is perfect in all the trials He allows, we then learn to worship in the temple not made with hands and disregard the frailties of the body. To sit down at the feet of Christ ignites a youthful spark that radiates the spirit within and conceives hope. The dew of youth then becomes our portion as Christ imparts eternal life and eternal youth to us. From the hour of the grave and through eternity we shall be young and bid defiance to weariness and death if we are living in the morning light of Jesus Christ. Heaven is a place of perpetual youth, and just like the light of the sun is reflected on the moon, so likewise the light of Christ is reflected on His bride. She is clean and young, …a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing… –Ephesians 5:27. Blessed is the venerable saint who arrives at the portals of heaven in such a condition.

Tu as la rosée de ta jeunesse. Psaume 110:3

La jeunesse présente de nombreux aspects qui ne sont pas vertueux. Beaucoup de jeunes de notre époque connaissent très tôt une période d’insouciance endurcie et d’imprudence. Souvent, les décisions prises dans la jeunesse posent les fondations du reste de la vie. C’est le jeune frère prodigue qui demanda à recevoir par anticipation sa part d’héritage, puis partit la dissiper dans une vie de débauche. C’est une jeune Dina qui s’éloigna de la maison de son père et …sortit pour voir les filles du pays –Genèse 34:1. Là, elle fut exposée aux jeunes païens du pays et fut à l’origine d’un massacre sanglant, laissant Jacob comme une puanteur dans le pays. Beaucoup de jeunes insensés ont semé le vent et en ont récolté le désastre. Ceux qui sont dépourvus de principes solides et d’autorité parentale courent un grand risque de naufrage spirituel.

Il existe des convoitises particulières qui frappent les jeunes plus que les personnes âgées, et les jeunes sont exhortés à les fuir. (–voir 2 Timothée 2:22) Salomon regarda par le treillis de sa fenêtre, Et je vis parmi les simples, je remarquai parmi les jeunes gens un jeune homme dépourvu de bon sens –Proverbes 7:6-7. Le jeune homme poursuivait de tout son cœur ce qui lui semblait beau… [Jusqu’à ce qu’]une flèche lui transperce le foie ; comme l’oiseau se hâte vers le piège sans savoir que sa vie est en jeu –Proverbes 7:23. Nous pourrions examiner les vices qui marquèrent la jeunesse de Roboam, Amnon, Nadab et Abihu, et d’innombrables autres. Nous ne manquons pas non plus autour de nous d’exemples modernes, remplis de folie et accomplis par des jeunes frivoles.

Mais il ne faut pas mépriser les jeunes. Que personne ne méprise ta jeunesse ; mais sois un modèle pour les croyants, en parole, en conduite, en amour, en esprit, en foi, en pureté –1 Timothée 4:12. En fait, Dieu choisit généralement les jeunes comme instruments pour propager son œuvre. Joseph, d’un caractère irréprochable, fut envoyé par Dieu en Égypte à l’âge de 17 ans pour préserver la vie (–voir Genèse 45:5). Miriam, à l’âge de douze ans, monta la garde auprès de celui qui allait délivrer toute la nation juive et obtint que sa propre mère, Jokébed, soit la nourrice du petit Moïse. David, alors jeune, fut envoyé pour encourager ses frères dans l’armée. Ses frères le méprisèrent : …Je connais ton orgueil et la méchanceté de ton cœur… –1 Samuel 17:28. Saül le rejeta : …Tu ne peux pas aller combattre ce Philistin, car tu n’es qu’un jeune homme… –1 Samuel 17:33. Goliath se moqua de lui : …Suis-je un chien, pour que tu viennes contre moi avec des bâtons… –1 Samuel 17:43. Mais tout leur mépris fut vain lorsque Dieu le choisit pour être roi sur tout Israël.

Ces nobles aspirations de jeunesse furent suivies par Josias, Ésaïe, Jérémie, Daniel, Marie et les disciples du Seigneur, qui tous choisirent de se souvenir de leur Créateur aux jours de leur jeunesse. Mais ils n’étaient pas des êtres naïfs cherchant à s’assurer une place dans la vie ; ils étaient des exemples saisissants de jeunes qui cherchaient à imiter l’image de leur Seigneur.

Il nous suffit de contempler un instant le caractère du Christ pour découvrir…

...Tu as la rosée de ta jeunesse

Le Psaume 110 est peut-être le passage de l’Ancien Testament auquel il est le plus souvent fait référence. Ce portrait rhétorique du Messie nous révèle une vertu éclatante que nous pouvons contempler. Le Christ, en tant qu’Ancien des jours, est décrit dans l’Apocalypse comme ayant la tête et les cheveux… blancs comme la laine, blancs comme la neige… –Apocalypse 1:14 ; pourtant, ici, il est représenté comme éternellement jeune, assis à la droite de Dieu (–voir Psaume 110:1). La lassitude de l’âge ne peut pénétrer là, car le Christ est l’Étoile du matin. Autour du trône de Dieu, c’est un matin perpétuel. Les saints qui s’efforcent de lui ressembler refléteront eux aussi cette vertu, car la lumière de Jésus est la lumière de la jeunesse.

Le psalmiste, décrivant le Messie, s’inspire de la beauté naturelle de la rosée du matin (–voir Psaume 110:3). L’évocation de la rosée nous ramène des cieux et dévoile devant nous un portrait de cette terre où nous vivons. Au ciel, il n’y a ni nuit, ni changement de chaleur et de froid, ni besoin du soleil pour éclairer le jour et, par conséquent… pas de rosée. La rosée appartient au monde terrestre, où quiconque prend la peine de s’arrêter pour l’observer verra un régiment uniforme d’herbe scintiller comme s’il était incrusté de myriades de diamants. Après une longue nuit obscure, les gouttes de rosée, telles des larmes, brillent dans les yeux des fleurs qui pleurent de joie à l’arrivée du premier rayon du soleil matinal. Ceux qui traversent la basse végétation auront les pieds lavés par mille mains caressantes, œuvre de Dieu. Le Christ n’est pas représenté comme la rosée du matin, mais comme la rosée de la jeunesse, et l’image se déploie davantage encore.

La jeunesse est une période d’énergie débordante. Certains ne peuvent rester assis. Ce sont généralement des êtres sociables qui aiment les activités en groupe. Ce n’est ni une vertu ni un vice. C’est plutôt une disposition naturelle. Au fil des ans, une tendance progressive vient apprivoiser et tempérer l’âme. À mesure que la vie avance, la vision s’éclaircit et la pensée devient plus stable, et nous nous élevons vers de meilleures choses. Mais, une fois le sommet de la mi-vie franchi et les pieds engagés dans la descente, cette tumultueuse énergie physique qui fonçait à travers tout se trouve reléguée aux souvenirs du passé. Pour beaucoup, c’est le réconfort le plus proche qu’ils puissent trouver des jours révolus où ils étaient forts.

Mais le Christ ne nous a pas appelés à cultiver la nostalgie du passé ni à regretter avec mélancolie le « dynamisme » de notre jeunesse. Tant de gens déplorent aujourd’hui que leur entrain soit parti sans retour. Ils n’ont aucune vision des choses plus élevées et sont davantage stimulés par une canette de Mountain Dew que par la rosée de la jeunesse. Un voyage dans le passé et l’évocation des événements d’autrefois les inspirent plus que l’espérance qui se trouve devant eux.

L’âge n’empêche pas de recevoir la rosée de la jeunesse. L’Ancien des jours continue de marcher parmi les chandeliers d’or. Tandis que Jean contemplait ses cheveux… blancs comme la laine, blancs comme la neige… –Apocalypse 1:14, Salomon déclare pourtant que …ses boucles sont touffues, noires comme le corbeau –Cantique des cantiques 5:11. L’âge peut nous ôter la force et l’ouïe, mais …la main de l’Éternel n’est pas trop courte pour sauver, et son oreille n’est pas trop dure pour entendre –Ésaïe 59:1. Il nous a acquis la rosée de la jeunesse et nous invite à y prendre part. Le problème ne réside pas dans la détérioration de notre corps, mais dans le déclin spirituel de notre esprit. Le fléau de la vieillesse s’installe principalement lorsque l’esprit suit le corps.

Ce n’est pas que la vie s’appauvrisse en avançant, ni qu’elle cesse d’être noble lorsque le charme de la jeunesse s’est évanoui. Si nous étions placés ici uniquement pour connaître la joie, l’extinction des élans romantiques de la jeunesse serait terrible. Dieu avait pour ses enfants un dessein bien plus grand que celui de n’être que de vigoureux « acteurs ». Nous sommes envoyés ici pour apprendre. Les années qui nous sont accordées sur terre sont toutes destinées à nous instruire, et ce n’est pas dans les brillants élans romantiques de la jeunesse que nous apprenons les leçons les meilleures et les plus durables. C’est dans l’accomplissement tenace de notre devoir, l’acceptation tranquille de nos limites, le port patient de notre fardeau quotidien et le geste de tendre une main secourable à notre frère. Voilà les véritables occasions de nous former chrétiennement et les racines de la noblesse morale. Le Christ a travaillé …non pour la nourriture qui périt, mais pour celle qui subsiste pour la vie éternelle… –Jean 6:27, et il a achevé sa tâche terrestre en 33 ans. Pourtant, la rosée de la jeunesse ne s’est pas dissipée lorsqu’il s’est assis à la droite de son Père.

Ainsi, nous concluons que cette jeunesse ne s’obtient pas par la force, mais par…

...L’espérance

Mais lui, après avoir offert un seul sacrifice pour les péchés, valable pour toujours, s’est assis à la droite de Dieu ; il attend désormais que ses ennemis soient placés comme marchepied sous ses pieds. –Hébreux 10:12-13.

Comment devons-nous nous représenter le Christ aujourd’hui ? Installé dans un fauteuil, épuisé par son expérience auprès du peuple obstiné de cette terre ? Est-il occupé à composer un album de précieux souvenirs ? C’est trop souvent la posture des personnes âgées, et leur esprit meurt ainsi avec leur corps.

Bien plus, nous nous glorifions même dans les tribulations, sachant que la tribulation produit la persévérance, la persévérance l’expérience, et l’expérience l’espérance –Romains 5:3-4. Parfois, nous nous demandons si ce passage peut être vrai. Toute personne qui a vécu assez longtemps peut témoigner d’une expérience pénible et du désespoir qui s’ensuit. En tant qu’êtres humains, nous avons tous connu des expériences décevantes avec un conjoint, un enfant ou dans une relation au sein de l’Église, après lesquelles un nuage tenace de désespoir s’installe. En dehors du Christ, une expérience amère mène toujours au pessimisme. C’était déjà le cas dans le monde lorsque Jésus est venu. C’est encore le cas aujourd’hui.

Mais la rosée de la jeunesse est porteuse d’une espérance incurable. La jeunesse est naturellement et magnifiquement animée d’une attente débordante, que l’on conserve dans le Christ. Chaque hiver, lorsque les champs sont désolés et que le vent froid siffle à travers les arbres, demeure l’espérance que les fleurs refleuriront. Chaque printemps porte l’espérance de l’été. Chaque été porte l’espérance de la moisson. Cette espérance vit dans la nature et dans la jeunesse. Ceux qui ne la voient pas ne récolteront au mieux qu’une existence morne et monotone. Vivre est la chose la plus rare au monde. La plupart des gens existent, c’est tout. –Oscar Wilde.

Les autres seront vivifiés par une espérance qui…

…Guérit nos infirmités

Nos corps sont voués à la tombe et n’ont aucun espoir de renouvellement dans cette vie. Ce sont nos esprits qui portent nos infirmités les plus graves. L’homme impotent depuis 38 ans à Bethesda ne put exprimer qu’une plainte désespérée lorsque le Christ lui demanda : …Veux-tu être guéri ? –Jean 5:6. Au seuil de son jour nouveau, un nouveau remède lui fut donné : …Voici, tu as été guéri ; ne pèche plus, de peur qu’il ne t’arrive quelque chose de pire –Jean 5:14. Qu’est-ce qui pourrait être pire que d’être infirme pendant des années ? Un esprit accablé par une complaisance lugubre dans les chagrins de ce monde. La vieillesse s’installe lorsque nous avons davantage de souvenirs du passé que d’espérance pour demain. Il est décevant de voir des gens vieillir sans avoir de vision pour demain, mais il est désastreux de voir des jeunes frappés par les effets paralysants de cet état. Beaucoup tâtonnent sans but au milieu des diverses épreuves de la vie, engourdis par l’absence de félicité. Le soleil de midi a évaporé la rosée de leur jeunesse, et les seuls éloges qu’ils peuvent formuler se résument à une poignée de plaisirs d’hier. La rosée d’un nouveau matin doit faire naître une attitude nouvelle.

…Rend humbles nos ambitions

En vérité, en vérité, je te le dis, quand tu étais jeune, tu te ceignais toi-même et tu allais où tu voulais ; mais quand tu seras vieux, tu étendras les mains, et un autre te ceindra et te conduira où tu ne voudras pas. –Jean 21:18. Lorsque nous sommes jeunes, nous pouvons triompher grâce à la force de notre jeunesse. Avec l’âge, nous découvrirons une autre voie : la victoire par l’abandon.

…Je vous ai écrit, jeunes gens, parce que vous êtes forts, que la parole de Dieu demeure en vous et que vous avez vaincu le malin. –1 Jean 2:14. Le monde nous attire vers une vie égoïste. Les jeunes sont souvent soumis à des systèmes d’enseignement qui leur apprennent à « être tout ce qu’ils peuvent être ». L’accent est fortement mis sur le développement personnel et la préparation à l’avenir. Cela peut les préparer à un monde où règne la « loi du plus fort », mais les laissera démunis lorsque la force et les prouesses de la jeunesse auront disparu.

Car tout ce qui est dans le monde, la convoitise de la chair, la convoitise des yeux et l’orgueil de la vie, ne vient pas du Père, mais du monde. Et le monde passe, avec ses convoitises ; mais celui qui fait la volonté de Dieu demeure éternellement. –1 Jean 2:16-17. Vaincre le mal par le bien est l’antidote biblique pour canaliser les énergies de la jeunesse. Qu’il s’agisse de la convoitise intérieure ou du désir de ce qui est extérieur, l’espérance naît lorsque l’on sème une graine de bonté dans la vie d’autrui. La recherche du plaisir et la préférence pour les loisirs décevront toujours celui qui s’y livre et le laisseront dans une vallée de désespoir plus profonde qu’au départ. Il est bon pour l’homme de porter le joug dans sa jeunesse… Il met sa bouche dans la poussière : peut-être y a-t-il de l’espérance. –Lamentations 3:27-29. Nous avons été créés pour travailler dans la vigne de Dieu, et ceux qui en ont le désir récolteront dans l’espérance la récompense de cette jeunesse.

…Sanctifie nos épreuves

Car c’est en espérance que nous sommes sauvés ; or l’espérance qu’on voit n’est plus l’espérance… –Romains 8:24. Comme nous pouvons souvent nous reconnaître dans la douleur de Job ! Pourtant, avant même que sa douleur ait reçu la moindre compensation, les flots de guérison commencèrent à couler lorsque Job révéra son Créateur. Lorsque nous reconnaissons que Dieu est parfait dans toutes les épreuves qu’il permet, nous apprenons alors à adorer dans le temple qui n’est pas fait de mains humaines et à ne pas tenir compte des fragilités du corps. S’asseoir aux pieds du Christ allume une étincelle de jeunesse qui rayonne dans l’esprit et fait naître l’espérance. La rosée de la jeunesse devient alors notre part, tandis que le Christ nous communique la vie éternelle et la jeunesse éternelle. Depuis l’heure de la tombe et jusque dans l’éternité, nous serons jeunes et défierons la lassitude et la mort si nous vivons dans la lumière matinale de Jésus-Christ. Le ciel est un lieu de jeunesse perpétuelle et, de même que la lumière du soleil se reflète sur la lune, la lumière du Christ se reflète sur son épouse. Elle est pure et jeune, …une Église glorieuse, sans tache, ni ride, ni rien de semblable… –Éphésiens 5:27. Béni soit le saint vénérable qui arrive aux portes du ciel dans un tel état.

I’ll walk with God—Today—
Tomorrow may not be.
I’ll make the best of TIME—right now—
That God has granted me.

I’ll plan not for a life
That I might live in ease,
But only for today to live
My God alone to please.

Nor dare I think in years
Or move from leaps to bounds;
With God shut out, and self shut in
And selfish aims surround.

There are those who plan their lives,
Who give God little thought;
Who weigh themselves, not with God’s truth,
As every day they ought!

“Boast not thyself,” I’m warned,
“Of what tomorrow brings;
Thy health and wealth—e’en life itself—
May all at once take wings!”

“This night, that soul of thine
May be required of thee:
And dost thou plan the New Year full
There, ‘neath some Christmas tree?”

“Wake up! Take stock, are you prepared?
Your lessons learned alright?
If God, in yet three hours, THIS DAY,
Should close your course TONIGHT?”

","section":"Poem","subtitle":null,"title":"Today"},"source_context":{"byline":{"authors":[{"name":"Marvin L. Fieldhouse"}],"raw":"by Marvin L. Fieldhouse"}},"target_language":"German","terminology_glossary":{},"translation":{"html":"

Ich geh mit Gott – heute –
Morgen vielleicht nicht mehr.
Ich nutze DIE ZEIT – jetzt gleich –
Die Gott mir geschenkt hat.

Ich plane nicht für ein Leben,
In dem ich sorglos leben könnt,
Sondern nur für diesen Tag,
Um allein meinem Gott zu gefallen.

Auch wage ich nicht, in Jahren zu denken
Oder weite Sprünge zu machen;
Gott ausgeschlossen, das eigene Ich eingeschlossen,
Umgeben von selbstsüchtigen Zielen.

Es gibt Menschen, die ihr Leben planen
Und kaum an Gott denken;
Die sich nicht an Gottes Wahrheit messen,
wie sie es jeden Tag tun sollten!

„Rühme dich nicht“, wird mir gesagt,
„dessen, was der Morgen bringt;
deine Gesundheit und dein Wohlstand – ja, selbst dein Leben –
können plötzlich davongeflogen sein!“

„Noch diese Nacht kann deine Seele
von dir gefordert werden:
Und planst du dort, unter einem Weihnachtsbaum,
schon das ganze neue Jahr?“

„Wach auf! Zieh Bilanz: Bist du bereit?
Hast du deine Lektionen gut gelernt?
Wenn Gott in nur drei Stunden, noch an DIESEM TAG,
heute Nacht deinen Lauf beenden sollte?“

The grinding sound of truck tires driving in the gravel lane filled the air as I sat in the house reading an encyclopedia. Leaping to my feet, I peered out the window.

Mom had just returned from the produce auction in Lewisburg with some peaches.

Slamming the door behind me, I raced across the thick green grass and leaped onto the bed of our truck.

On the back of the pickup sat four boxes of peaches. Grinning triumphantly, I reached into a box searching until I found a ripe one. Just before I bit into it, Mom said, “Steven, don’t eat any peaches; it will ruin your supper.” Sadly, I tossed the peach back into the box and then slowly walked away.

Several hours later, Dad called from the veal barn. “Steven, go pick the radishes for our Friday market produce stand.”

After picking, washing, and banding the radishes, I carried them into the old cooler which was inside the red bank barn. The cooler door squeaked as I yanked it open. There along the cooler walls sat the four boxes of the tantalizing peaches. I stared at the peaches, my mouth watering. I quickly set the radishes down. Oh, how good they looked. Surely a little peach wouldn’t ruin a starving ten-year-old’s supper. Mom wouldn’t know if I only took one peach.

Deep in my heart, a battle between right and wrong started to develop. I knew that sneaking was wrong, but those peaches looked way too good.

After devouring the peach, I scanned the dark interior of the barn for a good hiding place to put the peach stone. I looked across the onions, laying on drying racks, to the open hay bale. The only problem was that if I put the stone under the hay someone could find it. Then I spied the holes in the barn siding boards on the west side of the barn. If I pushed the stone through one of those holes it would land beside the road. Then, if someone saw it, they would think that it came from a passing vehicle.

I jammed the stone through the hole, peering out as it fell beside the road. At that split second, I felt a searing pain on my forehead. Frantically, I sprang back. There above the hole hung a yellow jacket nest. Then I saw the culprit as it hovered over me trying to sting me again. I sprinted out the barn door, slamming the door into the yellow jacket’s face.

That evening my forehead swelled like a balloon, making it difficult to look out of my eyes.

A few hours later, everyone else went to bed. I laid on the couch so that Mom could occasionally check up on me during the night. But I just couldn’t fall asleep. My face was inflamed and itchy, but all that I could think about was the guilt and remorse of what I had done.

After several agonizing hours, I gathered the courage to slide off the couch and tiptoed over to my parent’s bedroom. Awakening my parents, I told them the whole story… how I ate the peach, then tried to hide the stone, and how I had gotten stung.

My parents forgave me, deciding that this was one lesson that I wouldn’t soon forget. Walking back to the couch with a light heart, I laid down, and quickly fell into a peaceful sleep.

Det skrapande ljudet av lastbilsdäck som körde på grusvägen fyllde luften medan jag satt i huset och läste ett uppslagsverk. Jag for upp på fötter och kikade ut genom fönstret.

Mamma hade just kommit tillbaka från frukt- och grönsaksauktionen i Lewisburg med några persikor.

Jag slog igen dörren bakom mig, rusade över det täta, gröna gräset och hoppade upp på flaket på vår lastbil.

På pickupens flak stod fyra lådor med persikor. Jag log triumferande och stack handen i en låda, letade tills jag hittade en mogen persika. Precis innan jag bet i den sa mamma: ”Steven, ät inga persikor; då förstör du middagen.” Besviket lade jag tillbaka persikan i lådan och gick sedan långsamt därifrån.

Flera timmar senare ropade pappa från kalvstallet. ”Steven, gå och plocka rädisorna till vårt frukt- och grönsaksstånd på fredagsmarknaden.”

När jag hade plockat, tvättat och buntat rädisorna bar jag in dem i det gamla kylrummet inne i den röda ladugården. Dörren till kylrummet gnisslade när jag ryckte upp den. Där, längs väggarna i kylrummet, stod de fyra lådorna med de frestande persikorna. Jag stirrade på dem och det vattnades i munnen. Jag ställde snabbt ner rädisorna. Åh, så goda de såg ut. En liten persika skulle väl ändå inte förstöra middagen för en utsvulten tioåring. Mamma skulle inte märka något om jag bara tog en persika.

Djupt inom mig började en kamp mellan rätt och fel ta form. Jag visste att det var fel att smyga, men persikorna såg alldeles för goda ut.

När jag hade slukat persikan såg jag mig omkring i ladugårdens mörka inre efter ett bra gömställe för persikokärnan. Jag tittade över lökarna, som låg på torkställningar, mot den öppna höbalen. Problemet var att om jag lade kärnan under höet kunde någon hitta den. Då fick jag syn på hålen i ladugårdens brädvägg på västsidan. Om jag tryckte ut kärnan genom ett av hålen skulle den landa vid vägen. Och om någon såg den skulle de tro att den kom från ett fordon som passerat.

Jag tryckte in kärnan i hålet och kikade ut medan den föll ner vid vägen. Just då kände jag en brännande smärta i pannan. Jag ryggade hastigt tillbaka. Ovanför hålet hängde ett getingbo. Sedan såg jag den skyldiga getingen sväva över mig och försöka sticka mig igen. Jag rusade ut genom ladugårdsdörren och slog igen dörren rakt i ansiktet på getingen.

Den kvällen svullnade min panna upp som en ballong, så att det blev svårt att se.

Några timmar senare gick alla andra och lade sig. Jag låg på soffan så att mamma kunde titta till mig då och då under natten. Men jag kunde bara inte somna. Ansiktet var inflammerat och kliade, men allt jag kunde tänka på var skulden och ångern över det jag hade gjort.

Efter flera plågsamma timmar samlade jag mod till mig, gled ner från soffan och tassade bort till mina föräldrars sovrum. Jag väckte mina föräldrar och berättade hela historien … hur jag hade ätit persikan, sedan försökt gömma kärnan och hur jag hade blivit stucken.

Mina föräldrar förlät mig och bestämde sig för att det här var en läxa som jag inte snart skulle glömma. Med lätt hjärta gick jag tillbaka till soffan, lade mig ner och somnade snabbt i lugn och ro.

Have you ever tried to change the world? I have. As a teenager I dreamed of the daring exploits I was going to do for God. As I set the table in my parent’s house, I waited for the day when I would be able to do greater things—things like setting up house in Africa, speaking strange languages, and leading people to Jesus. The thought of living in a mud hut and dodging venomous snakes seemed thrilling.

And then, part of my dreams came true! I left all I had ever known and had an adrenaline-fueled landing in an African country. I tried to change the small world I was in—that God-forsaken village full of drunkenness, broken marriages, fights, and neglected children. Daily I felt the angst of being so busy with “insignificant,” earthly tasks and wondered how to make a difference. Then suddenly, our labors were abruptly ended by burn-out and a host of government suspicions. None of this was in my dreams.

I still ask the same question, “God, how can I make a difference?” The neighbor calls at the door. The laundry lady needs her pay. Lunch needs to be on the table in 15 minutes. Our fifth grader needs help with multiplying fractions. The sky fills up with dark clouds and the clothesline is full of laundry. I wipe the baby’s nose for the umpteenth time as she sits on top of the table disrupting her brother’s books and papers. I bake bread, make yogurt, and churn butter, and cook 21 meals a week. I fold mountains of laundry and the next week I do it all over again. I sweep the floor that has accumulated an astonishing amount of dirt in only two hours. In many ways, life is more mundane than it ever was before.

I had no ability to change the world as a starry-eyed teen and neither do I have the ability now. God isn’t asking that of me. He only asks me to walk with Him and obey His voice. Slowly I am learning that the spiritual and physical are inseparable—even Jesus taught the gospel of the kingdom while resting, sleeping, and eating. Scrubbing a floor and slicing bread can be acts of worship to my Creator if I will deem them so. It is He who designed that my spiritual walk and the propagation thereof happens as my hands touch the earthly. This is how my spirit is refined. It’s the only way I can express my faith as a living faith. It’s the only way I can touch the hearts of my children and live out a practical gospel for them to imitate. It’s how my faith proves itself to be real to the unbeliever, as they see me struggle through the same things they do, along with my resulting responses.

Slowly I am learning that serving God isn’t about determination or changing the world. It’s about allowing God’s spirit to inhabit me, guide me, and speak to me. I am learning that God is more interested in the person I am becoming instead of everything I want to do for Him. Perhaps I am after all just a smoking flax instead of the one who will change the world. I think Paul could relate to that feeling when he wrote, But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence –1 Corinthians 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot said, “Sometimes the light rises excruciatingly slowly. The Kingdom of God is like leaven and seed, things which work silently, secretly, slowly, but there is in them an incalculable transforming power. Even in the plain soil, even in the dull dough, lies the possibility of transformation.”1

To have my heart set on accomplishments and success is a selfish way to live. When that village and those people were taken from us in a whirl of government issues and misunderstandings, I felt like God couldn’t possibly use this for anyone’s good. He still needed us there, right? The fact is, He didn’t need us there anymore. We were not indispensable. Perhaps God allowed it all in order to learn that His acceptance of me is not based on my accomplishments.

For who hath despised the day of small things… –Zechariah 4:10.

Who am I to judge if a certain work is small or not? Am I restless with my duties, believing God would be more pleased with my perception of ‘great’ duties, seemingly always out of reach? Am I forgetting that serving Christ is not about me and my sense of fulfillment, it is about God and the work He wants to do through me?! Amy Carmichael said, “It is not the place where we are, or the work that we do or cannot do that matters, it is something else. It is the fire within that burns and shines, whatever be our circumstances.”2

The fire that burns and shines within is our secret. That fire can burn while we scrub floors, cook endless meals, and home-school our children. It will touch the laundry lady, the house helper, the struggling girl at church and the neighbors. Sometimes it will happen sub-consciously, sometimes it happens if we decide to reach out instead of taking a nap or something else enjoyable, but always it takes forgetting ourselves, loving others, and noticing the small opportunities.

But beware… we cannot confuse our resignation to the smallness in our lives, with lethargy. Too many Christians do not expect God to use them, so they settle into a lethargic spiritual position. We should expect God to work in amazing ways. God might use us to accomplish those things, but it often happens in ways we least think of or expect.

The widow of Zarephath agreed to give her last handful of flour and the last remaining drops of oil to a stranger. She could have opposed the prophet and demanded he leave immediately, as after all, she was responsible for her son and that little bit of flour was all she had to give him. But no, she chose to give it all. God blessed her willing obedience by miraculously replenishing her flour and oil as long as she needed it.3

God kept culling Gideon’s army until he eventually fought and won the battle with just a few hundred men. Normally, Gideon was accustomed to armies of thousands. and now God was asking him to fight a momentous battle with only a few hundred. In the end, this human impossibility became an opportunity for God to show his power.4

At the beginning of His ministry, Jesus chose only twelve men to disciple, instead of the crowds. In the end, His small band of men deserted Him. He was mocked and killed. To everyone looking on, the remains of Jesus’ work seemed to have died with Him, yet the cosmic plan of redemption was being put into effect—those simple fishermen turned the world upside down with the gospel.5

We see from these examples that God is not looking for the biggest, the strongest, or the best. He doesn’t only use people with specialized skills or impressive gifts. Our strength and resources are often like the few hundred soldiers in Gideon’s army—simply not enough for the need. But when we give what we have with a willing heart, God multiplies our small efforts into a showcase of His grace—a showcase meant for Him, often not visible to others. The simple act of setting a table is an act of faith, of giving, of service, no matter where we are. God has chosen these weak things to be significant in His kingdom.

The secret to a successful life is Jesus in us, not our preconceived ideas of success. With Him working in and through us, His power will burn in our homes and neighborhoods. When He is the reason that we are living, we can trust Him with the outcome. Listening to the voice of Jesus, we can make a difference—one person, one encounter, one small thing at a time.

  1. Elisabeth Elliot, The Savage My Kinsman (revised edition Servant Publications 1981) epilogue pg 147
  2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, pg 218
  3. 1 Kings 17: 11-16
  4. Judges 7
  5. Luke 6:13-16, John 19
