Me di la vuelta en la cama al oír que sonaba mi localizador. No podían haber pasado más de 15 minutos desde que me había metido en la cama después de mi último ingreso. Miré el número que aparecía en el localizador. Sí, era otra vez el Servicio de Urgencias.

Intenté quitarme el sueño de los ojos y despertar mi cerebro, todavía adormecido. Tomé el teléfono y llamé a Urgencias. —Hola —dijo el médico de Urgencias—. Tengo dos ingresos para ti.

—Ah —respondí con voz soñolienta.

—Suena cansado —dijo en tono de broma.

Estaba cansado. Después de graduarse de la facultad de Medicina, los médicos pasan por un período de formación intensiva llamado residencia. Los dos primeros años de esa formación incluían guardias nocturnas en el hospital. No era raro trabajar cien horas en el hospital en una semana.

Incluso cuando no estábamos de guardia, los días empezaban temprano y terminaban tarde. A menudo luchaba contra el sueño mientras conducía de regreso a casa desde el hospital. Sin duda aprendí mucho durante ese tiempo, pero también me alegra que esos días hayan quedado atrás.

La fatiga es parte de la condición humana. Todos hemos pasado por momentos en que nos cuesta vencer el cansancio. Quizá se debiera a un trabajo que había que terminar, a un viaje largo o a noches sin dormir por la llegada de un bebé a la familia; sea cual sea la dificultad, nos esforzamos con determinación para superar esos momentos difíciles.

Desde pequeños nos enseñan que el trabajo es importante. Debemos ser responsables y ocuparnos de las tareas que se nos encomiendan.

El trabajo ha sido ordenado por Dios. En Génesis, capítulo 2, Dios le dio a Adán la tarea de cuidar el huerto del Edén. Más adelante, en Deuteronomio 5:13, se les ordenó a los israelitas que hicieran todo su trabajo en seis días y que descansaran el séptimo.

El Nuevo Testamento ofrece un par de razones más para trabajar. Debemos trabajar para poder mantener a nuestras familias (véase 2 Tesalonicenses 3:10). Además, debemos trabajar para poder dar a quienes tienen necesidad (véase Efesios 4:28).

Dios espera que trabajemos y que lo hagamos de una manera que lo glorifique. Sin embargo, también necesitamos descansar, y Dios dispuso que así fuera.

Dios dio el ejemplo del descanso en la creación

Y acabó Dios en el día séptimo la obra que hizo; y reposó el día séptimo de toda la obra que hizo. Y bendijo Dios al día séptimo, y lo santificó: porque en él reposó de toda la obra que había creado y hecho –Génesis 2:2-3.

Cuando Dios creó el universo, incluida la tierra y todo lo que contiene, lo hizo en solo seis días. Puesto que Dios es Dios, podemos estar seguros de que no estaba cansado al terminar esta obra. Sin embargo, a pesar de eso, se tomó un día de descanso y lo apartó. Lo hizo para darnos ejemplo.

Aunque faltaban al menos dos mil años para que se instituyera la ley del sábado, el precedente quedó establecido en la creación… Descansar un día a la semana.

Dios estableció el descanso en la ley

Quizá lo primero que viene a la mente sean las leyes sobre el día de reposo dadas en Éxodo 20:8-11. Se ordenó específicamente que el pueblo no trabajara en sábado. Además, tampoco debían hacer trabajar a otras personas.

Otra ley que parecía centrarse mucho en la necesidad de descansar era la del año del jubileo. En Levítico 25, esta ley establecía que cada siete años la tierra debía quedar en barbecho durante todo el año, los esclavos debían ser liberados, la tierra debía volver a ser propiedad de la familia a la que originalmente pertenecía y las deudas debían ser canceladas.

Los mandatos del jubileo incluían ciertas promesas. Estaba la promesa de libertad: por muy mal que hubieran sido las cosas durante los seis años anteriores, habría un nuevo comienzo. Era una promesa de herencia: se recuperarían las cosas que se habían perdido y vendido. Era una promesa de abundancia: Y si dijereis: ¿Qué comeremos el año séptimo? he aquí no hemos de sembrar, ni hemos de recoger nuestros frutos: Entonces yo os enviaré mi bendición el sexto año, y ella hará fruto por tres años –Levítico 25:20-21. Pero, sobre todo, era una promesa de descanso del trabajo, para el pueblo y para la tierra.

Estos mandatos no se impusieron al pueblo para afligirlo. Más bien, Dios se los dio porque sabía que, sin ellos, su pueblo no descansaría lo suficiente ni dedicaría suficiente tiempo a centrarse en Él, su Creador.

Cada uno de nosotros necesita momentos de descanso, pero debemos entender que guardar el sábado no consiste simplemente en abstenerse de trabajar. Nuestros esfuerzos por guardar el sábado deben incluir tanto el descanso como la adoración, y debe destacarse la presencia de Dios en nuestra vida, sin distracciones.

El Nuevo Testamento no cambió la necesidad de descansar

Uno de los versículos que me viene a la mente cuando pienso en el descanso es una promesa que dio Jesús. Venid a mí todos los que estáis trabajados y cargados, que yo os haré descansar. Llevad mi yugo sobre vosotros, y aprended de mí, que soy manso y humilde de corazón; y hallaréis descanso para vuestras almas. Porque mi yugo es fácil, y ligera mi carga –Mateo 11:28-30.

El libro bíblico de Hebreos también habla de la importancia del descanso y de entrar en el reposo de Dios. Por tanto, queda un reposo para el pueblo de Dios. Porque el que ha entrado en su reposo, también él ha reposado de sus obras, como Dios de las suyas. Procuremos pues de entrar en aquel reposo; que ninguno caiga en semejante ejemplo de desobediencia –Hebreos 4:9-11.

Es importante ver que el concepto de descanso en el Nuevo Testamento es más que simplemente tomarse un tiempo libre del trabajo. La verdadera paz bíblica está intrínsecamente entrelazada con el concepto de la paz, incluso en medio de un mundo caótico. La paz os dejo, mi paz os doy: no como el mundo la da, yo os la doy. No se turbe vuestro corazón, ni tenga miedo –Juan 14:27. Jesús dio a sus seguidores una paz que les permitía descansar, incluso cuando enfrentaban niveles elevados de estrés.

Esto es una bendición, pues no basta con tomarnos tiempo libre de nuestro trabajo habitual. Necesitamos esa paz y esa calma que ofrece la conexión con Jesús. Sin …la paz de Dios, que sobrepuja todo entendimiento… –Filipenses 4:7, nuestro tiempo libre será tan poco reparador como el tiempo que pasamos trabajando.

Está claro que Dios quiere que descansemos. Él sabe que lo necesitamos, no solo por razones espirituales, sino también por nuestra salud física.

******************************

Los responsables de la Revolución francesa intentaron eliminar todas las instituciones del pasado. Fue una iniciativa particularmente impía y, entre otras cosas, el nuevo gobierno decidió «reformar» el calendario.

En 1793, establecieron una semana laboral de diez días. Cada mes tendría tres semanas, con un día de descanso en cada una de esas semanas de diez días. Entre otros objetivos, querían eliminar todas las fiestas religiosas y la celebración del domingo como día de descanso. Creían que se trabajaría más si había menos días de descanso cada mes.

Esto les causó un gran problema a los relojeros. De alguna manera tenían que fabricar relojes que se ajustaran a los detalles de estos nuevos decretos: cada día duraría diez horas, cada hora tendría cien minutos y cada minuto duraría 100 segundos.

Resultó ser un desastre. A la gente no le gustaron los cambios y la productividad cayó considerablemente en toda Francia. Finalmente, en 1806, Napoleón abolió el sistema y volvió al calendario antiguo y al sistema de descanso dominical. Este «experimento» científico había terminado. Resulta que las personas necesitan períodos de descanso y recuperación, y que una semana de siete días con un día libre para descansar no es solo un concepto cristiano: es algo necesario para la salud y el bienestar.

La Unión Soviética, bajo el mando de Joseph Stalin, también intentó un experimento similar para eliminar el descanso dominical, con resultados parecidos.

******************************

La semana tal como Dios la creó (con un día de descanso de cada siete) es necesaria para que sigamos siendo productivos.

El descanso reduce la inflamación

Parte del problema que enfrentan las personas de hoy es que tienen niveles elevados de hormonas del estrés, como la adrenalina y el cortisol. Estas hormonas aumentan la presión arterial y la frecuencia del pulso. También aumentan los niveles de inflamación en nuestro cuerpo.

La inflamación crónica no es saludable, pero, por fortuna, el descanso parece ayudar mucho a reducir esos niveles hormonales. Dormir bien por la noche es esencial para sanar, precisamente porque reduce estas hormonas y permite que sanen los nervios y tejidos sobreexigidos.

Las enfermedades autoinmunes y los niveles de dolor mejoran cuando las personas duermen lo suficiente. La presión arterial y las afecciones cardíacas también se benefician cuando una persona duerme lo suficiente y obtiene un sueño reparador.

El descanso permite sanar

Hacer ejercicio es bueno. Los médicos recomiendan hacer ejercicio cardiovascular con regularidad porque es saludable para el corazón, la mente y el bienestar general.

No es prudente hacer ejercicio todos los días. También eleva los niveles de hormonas del estrés y no da a nuestro cuerpo tiempo suficiente para sanar. Quienes hacen ejercicio con demasiada frecuencia y demasiada intensidad tienen muchas más probabilidades de acabar con lesiones persistentes, dolores articulares y musculares, y fatiga. Un estudio encontró que los músculos tardan 72 horas en recuperarse por completo después de hacer entrenamiento con pesas.

Lo ideal es que quienes hacen ejercicio descansen uno o dos días a la semana para que el cuerpo se recupere de la actividad. Cuanto más intenso sea el entrenamiento, más se necesitan esos períodos de descanso. Incluso alguien que entrena intensamente para algo como un maratón necesita tomarse días periódicos sin correr, o se lesionará.

El descanso reduce el dolor

Se han realizado muchos estudios que examinaron los informes de las personas sobre el sueño y analizaron aspectos como el dolor crónico y las cefaleas tensionales. Al menos el 50 por ciento de las personas con insomnio también tienen dolor crónico. Por supuesto, es posible que simplemente las personas con dolor crónico no duerman tan bien como quienes no lo padecen.

Varios estudios analizaron la tolerancia al dolor de las personas después de privarlas del sueño. Descubrieron que una sola noche sin dormir bastaba para que las personas sintieran el dolor con mayor intensidad.

El descanso mejora nuestro sistema inmunitario

Varios estudios analizaron el funcionamiento de diferentes partes de nuestro sistema inmunitario y descubrieron que funcionan mejor cuando los participantes duermen lo suficiente. Probablemente, el hecho de que los niveles de inflamación sean más altos cuando no descansamos aumenta el riesgo de infección.

Cuando nos exigimos demasiado sin descansar, nuestro sistema inmunitario se resiente. Por otro lado, la mejor manera de recuperarnos es asegurarnos de descansar lo suficiente.

El descanso tiene muchos otros efectos. Ayuda a mejorar el estado de ánimo. Puede ayudar con el rendimiento académico y las tareas de memoria.

Como con todo, la moderación es clave. Alguien que no hace más que descansar y dormir no funcionará mejor que alguien que duerme bien siete horas por noche, y tampoco será muy productivo.

Hay algunas reglas básicas que pueden ayudarnos a descansar.

Descansar con regularidad

El mensaje del sábado es que necesitamos tomarnos períodos breves y regulares para descansar. Los años del jubileo nos enseñan que también necesitamos períodos más largos y menos frecuentes para recuperarnos. Hace falta esfuerzo y planificación para asegurarnos de que esos momentos sean verdaderamente reparadores.

Quizá sea un poco como un automóvil. Solo puedes conducir cierta distancia con un tanque de gasolina. Si siempre esperas a que se encienda la luz de advertencia para llenar el tanque, tarde o temprano te ocurrirá cuando estés demasiado lejos de una gasolinera para cargar combustible antes de quedarte sin gasolina. Nunca es buen momento para quedarse sin gasolina. Del mismo modo, necesitamos recargar periódicamente nuestras baterías espirituales, emocionales y físicas. No hay razón para esperar a que aparezcan señales de advertencia de que necesitamos desesperadamente tomarnos un descanso.

El descanso requiere preparación

El relato del regalo del maná en Éxodo 16 nos dice que el maná llegaba todos los días. El pueblo no podía guardarlo para el día siguiente porque se echaba a perder. Sin embargo, los viernes debían recoger una cantidad adicional, ya que el día siguiente era de descanso y no caía maná en sábado. Quienes no habían recogido más el día anterior pasaban hambre.

Del mismo modo, hace falta prepararse para tener este tipo de períodos. No será fácil, pero es importante.

Aprovecha el descanso para hacer cosas saludables

Cuando las personas están estresadas, tienden a comer cosas poco saludables. Cuando están agotadas, por lo general no tienen ganas de hacer ejercicio ni de salir a caminar. Sin embargo, esas son precisamente algunas de las cosas que pueden ayudarnos mucho a recargarnos, tanto física como emocionalmente.

Una vez más, esto requiere cierto esfuerzo, pero elegir opciones saludables es importante para nuestro bienestar.

Centrarse en Dios

He dejado esto para el final, pero es el aspecto más importante del descanso. El verdadero descanso no nace de los medicamentos ni siquiera de tomarse varias vacaciones, sino de un corazón lleno de paz. La paz que sobrepasa el entendimiento proviene de un corazón centrado en Dios.

Nuestros momentos de oración y lectura de la Biblia deberían ser momentos de descanso. Si podemos eliminar las distracciones y las preocupaciones de nuestra vida laboral y familiar, y fijar la mirada en Aquel que más importa, recibiremos una verdadera bendición y la renovación que nuestro espíritu necesita.

Me temo que a muchas personas les cuesta encontrar descanso porque no tienen verdadera paz. Procuremos pues de entrar en aquel reposo; que ninguno caiga en semejante ejemplo de desobediencia –Hebreos 4:11. El descanso al que aquí se alude es el que se promete a quienes perseveran y reciben la paz de Dios.

Conclusión

La vida se trata de equilibrio. Hay momentos en que necesitamos trabajar y también hay momentos en que debemos descansar. Encontrar ese equilibrio es el desafío que todos enfrentamos. Lo que sí es seguro es que cada día de 24 horas estará completamente ocupado cuando llegue a su fin.

Dios nos ve, conoce nuestras limitaciones y desea que alcancemos este equilibrio entre el trabajo y nuestros momentos de descanso. Si logramos centrarnos en Él, recibiremos orientación para encontrar ese equilibrio.

Sobre todo, recibiremos una paz que no tiene precio y que nos permitirá descansar, incluso durante una tormenta.

Do you want to have a good life? What is there that you believe you need to experience or accomplish so you can truly enjoy life? Many people’s main goal in life is to seek pleasure and to have fun. Much time and money are spent to achieve this. But do we accomplish it? In our natural mind we think that the circumstances need to be just right to please us. But we all know that circumstances are never ideal all the time. So, we can’t depend on those for our happiness. We need something bigger than that. Or Someone.

Obviously, we know that God alone is never changing and always faithful. Another thing about God is that He is sovereign. In other words, He’s in charge. But we like our independence; we like things to happen in a way that feels good to us. When life doesn’t happen that way, we are brought to a decision. Will we accept all of God—both His unchangeableness and His sovereignty—or will we fight to have our own way in our pursuit of a good life?

The root of joy is with God Himself. This is because He created us for Himself. He created us to bring pleasure to Himself, but we think we need to bring pleasure to ourselves. It started in the garden of Eden when the serpent convinced Eve that pleasing herself was more important than pleasing God. Since then, humans have been at war, both within their own hearts and without, with other folks. All in the effort of trying to find pleasure for themselves, yet not finding it because they were created to please God.

The solution for this war is found in James 4. It’s simple: submit to God. Humble yourselves before Him. This is not too much for Him to ask of us, because He is sovereign. He created us, so He has the say in how we live. If we will truly find enjoyment in life, it will be by putting our own life and desires on the cross and becoming one with God and His original purpose for us. Rather than it being restrictive, this opens up a world of opportunities and possibilities. It doesn’t mean we have to do things because God wants us to. Becoming one with God means that what He wants us to do is also what we want to do.

Worship and Gratitude

When we are one with God, our whole perspective changes. Instead of pining over all the things that aren’t ideal, we begin to see the many things that are true blessings. We can have a heart of worship and gratitude for all the good things that we do experience. We are able to see how unworthy we really are. We didn’t deserve anything good, but God has still given us so many things to enjoy!

Living in the Present

As young ladies, we have a tendency to dream, to live in a future that is idealistic and pleasant. We sometimes struggle to live in the present imperfect reality and find joy in it. But when God’s will becomes our will then true joy happens, because we are fulfilling His purpose for us.

We can learn to experience joy in any circumstance, even in mundane life. We’re afraid of living a boring life. We want it to be exciting. But He wants us to please Him, and when we do, we experience joy no matter the circumstances. However, we are also then available for Him to use in service to His Kingdom, and He may call us to opportunities that are exciting. But we won’t be effective in the exciting missions unless we have learned to be submitted to His will in everyday life.

Relationships

When we are finding joy and contentment in where God has us in the present, we are able to focus on developing solid, upbuilding relationships with those who are in our lives right now. God has created us as social people, and good relationships will bring true enjoyment to us. God is also able to use us in reaching out to other people. When we are one with Him, our focus is no longer on ourselves but on others. The life of God can flow through us and both show others the way to Him and give us joy and fulfillment in doing it.

Emotions

Another tendency we have is to let our emotions control us. And they will run wild if we are looking to our circumstances to give us pleasure. We will end up on a roller coaster of feelings dictated by whatever is happening at the moment. And then we escape to the dream world, which only distorts our view of reality even more. But God is steadfast, and when we are one with Him, He imparts to us stability and rest. And we are able to experience ever present joy—even in ever changing circumstances.

Let us continue to become ever more one with Him. And He will give us heavenly sunlight all of our journey, unchanged by circumstances on earth and realized in full when we see Him face to face. …in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore –Psalm 16:11.

Apakah Anda ingin menjalani hidup yang baik? Apa yang menurut Anda perlu Anda alami atau capai agar benar-benar dapat menikmati hidup? Tujuan utama banyak orang dalam hidup adalah mencari kesenangan dan bersenang-senang. Banyak waktu dan uang dihabiskan untuk mencapainya. Namun, apakah kita berhasil? Dalam pikiran alamiah kita, kita mengira keadaan harus benar-benar tepat agar kita merasa senang. Tetapi kita semua tahu bahwa keadaan tidak pernah ideal setiap saat. Jadi, kita tidak bisa mengandalkannya untuk kebahagiaan kita. Kita membutuhkan sesuatu yang lebih besar dari itu. Atau Seseorang.

Jelas, kita tahu bahwa hanya Allah yang tidak pernah berubah dan selalu setia. Hal lain tentang Allah adalah bahwa Dia berdaulat. Dengan kata lain, Dialah yang berkuasa. Tetapi kita menyukai kemandirian kita; kita suka jika segala sesuatu terjadi dengan cara yang terasa menyenangkan bagi kita. Ketika hidup tidak berjalan demikian, kita dihadapkan pada sebuah pilihan. Akankah kita menerima Allah seutuhnya—baik ketidakberubahan maupun kedaulatan-Nya—atau akankah kita berjuang untuk mendapatkan keinginan kita sendiri dalam upaya mengejar hidup yang baik?

Akar sukacita ada pada Allah sendiri. Sebab Dia menciptakan kita bagi diri-Nya. Dia menciptakan kita untuk menyenangkan diri-Nya, tetapi kita berpikir bahwa kita perlu menyenangkan diri sendiri. Semuanya bermula di taman Eden ketika ular meyakinkan Hawa bahwa menyenangkan dirinya sendiri lebih penting daripada menyenangkan Allah. Sejak saat itu, manusia telah berperang, baik di dalam hati mereka sendiri maupun di luar, dengan orang lain. Semua itu merupakan upaya untuk mencari kesenangan bagi diri mereka sendiri, tetapi mereka tidak menemukannya karena mereka diciptakan untuk menyenangkan Allah.

Solusi untuk perang ini terdapat dalam Yakobus 4. Sederhana saja: tunduklah kepada Allah. Rendahkanlah diri di hadapan-Nya. Ini bukan permintaan yang terlalu berat bagi-Nya untuk diajukan kepada kita, karena Dia berdaulat. Dia menciptakan kita, jadi Dia berhak menentukan bagaimana kita hidup. Jika kita benar-benar ingin menemukan kenikmatan dalam hidup, itu akan terjadi dengan menyalibkan hidup dan keinginan kita sendiri serta menjadi satu dengan Allah dan tujuan semula-Nya bagi kita. Alih-alih membatasi, hal ini membuka dunia penuh kesempatan dan kemungkinan. Ini bukan berarti kita harus melakukan sesuatu hanya karena Allah menghendakinya. Menjadi satu dengan Allah berarti bahwa apa yang Dia ingin kita lakukan juga merupakan apa yang ingin kita lakukan.

Ibadah dan Rasa Syukur

Ketika kita menjadi satu dengan Allah, seluruh sudut pandang kita berubah. Alih-alih meratapi segala sesuatu yang tidak ideal, kita mulai melihat banyak hal yang merupakan berkat sejati. Kita dapat memiliki hati yang menyembah dan bersyukur atas semua hal baik yang kita alami. Kita dapat melihat betapa tidak layaknya kita sebenarnya. Kita tidak pantas mendapatkan hal baik apa pun, tetapi Allah tetap telah memberi kita begitu banyak hal untuk dinikmati!

Hidup di Masa Kini

Sebagai gadis-gadis muda, kita cenderung bermimpi, hidup di masa depan yang idealistis dan menyenangkan. Kadang-kadang kita kesulitan menjalani kenyataan masa kini yang tidak sempurna dan menemukan sukacita di dalamnya. Tetapi ketika kehendak Allah menjadi kehendak kita, sukacita sejati pun terjadi, karena kita sedang memenuhi tujuan-Nya bagi kita.

Kita dapat belajar mengalami sukacita dalam keadaan apa pun, bahkan dalam kehidupan sehari-hari yang biasa-biasa saja. Kita takut menjalani hidup yang membosankan. Kita ingin hidup yang penuh kegembiraan. Tetapi Dia ingin kita menyenangkan-Nya, dan ketika kita melakukannya, kita mengalami sukacita apa pun keadaannya. Namun, dengan demikian kita juga siap dipakai-Nya untuk melayani Kerajaan-Nya, dan Dia mungkin memanggil kita untuk mengambil kesempatan-kesempatan yang menggairahkan. Tetapi kita tidak akan efektif dalam misi-misi yang menggairahkan itu kecuali kita telah belajar tunduk kepada kehendak-Nya dalam kehidupan sehari-hari.

Hubungan

Ketika kita menemukan sukacita dan rasa cukup dalam keadaan yang Allah berikan kepada kita saat ini, kita dapat berfokus mengembangkan hubungan yang kokoh dan saling membangun dengan orang-orang yang ada dalam hidup kita sekarang. Allah menciptakan kita sebagai makhluk sosial, dan hubungan yang baik akan memberi kita kenikmatan sejati. Allah juga dapat memakai kita untuk menjangkau orang lain. Ketika kita menjadi satu dengan-Nya, perhatian kita tidak lagi tertuju pada diri sendiri, melainkan pada orang lain. Hidup Allah dapat mengalir melalui kita, menunjukkan jalan kepada-Nya kepada orang lain sekaligus memberi kita sukacita dan kepuasan saat melakukannya.

Emosi

Kecenderungan lain yang kita miliki adalah membiarkan emosi mengendalikan kita. Emosi akan menjadi tak terkendali jika kita mengandalkan keadaan untuk memberi kita kesenangan. Akibatnya, kita akan terombang-ambing oleh perasaan yang ditentukan oleh apa pun yang sedang terjadi saat itu. Lalu kita melarikan diri ke dunia khayalan, yang hanya semakin menyimpangkan pandangan kita tentang kenyataan. Tetapi Allah teguh, dan ketika kita menjadi satu dengan-Nya, Dia memberi kita kestabilan dan ketenangan. Dan kita mampu mengalami sukacita yang senantiasa ada—bahkan di tengah keadaan yang terus berubah.

Marilah kita terus menjadi semakin satu dengan-Nya. Dan Dia akan memberi kita sinar matahari surgawi sepanjang perjalanan kita, yang tidak berubah oleh keadaan di bumi dan akan kita alami sepenuhnya ketika kita melihat-Nya muka dengan muka. …di hadapan-Mu ada sukacita yang penuh; di tangan kanan-Mu ada nikmat senantiasa –Mazmur 16:11.

Sometimes my heart is heavy,
Weighted with fears and care.
It’s then my Lord calls out to me,
“Come My child, your burden I’ll bear.”

Sometimes questions flood my mind,
The answers seem evasive and trying.
That’s when I lift these eyes to my God,
Claiming His love on me overlying.

Sometimes I feel like quitting,
The way before me seems long and hard.
But I think of the path of my Shepherd,
It was for me He was scarred.

Sometimes my mind is clouded,
I stumble with each step that I take.
Yet out of the fog, I hear a whisper,
“You are Mine, trust Me, a way I will make.”

Sometimes I find my circumstances,
Seemingly harsh, and unfair.
But then my Father whispers,
“Dear one, do not despair.”

Sometimes I feel all alone,
The ache within chokes and burns.
The Master speaks, “My chosen one,
I alone can fulfill, that for which your heart yearns.

Sometimes my eyes are full of tears
My heart feels near to burst.
And then my Savior reminds me,
This path, before me, He traversed.

Sometimes I worry and wonder,
How things will ever turn out right.
Yet the promise remains, all works out well,
For him that in God does delight.

Sometimes the future seems scary,
Not at all like what I had hoped.
Still, I set my eyes on His ultimate goal,
Knowing it’s better than for what I had groped.

Sometimes I feel left behind,
While others lives go on so free.
But, in my Father’s plans I will trust,
And look forward to His eternal jubilee!

Sometimes I find myself dreaming,
Of the future in heaven to come.
Oh what bliss will be the feeling,
To hear those words, “Well done.”

Soms is mijn hart zwaar,
Beladen met angst en zorgen.
Dan roept mijn Heer mij toe:
‘Kom, mijn kind, Ik zal je last dragen.’

Soms overspoelen vragen mijn gedachten,
De antwoorden lijken ontwijkend en moeilijk.
Dan sla ik mijn ogen op naar mijn God,
En vertrouw ik op Zijn liefde die mij omhult.

Soms wil ik het opgeven,
De weg voor mij lijkt lang en zwaar.
Maar ik denk aan het pad van mijn Herder,
Voor mij werd Hij verwond.

Soms is mijn geest beneveld,
Ik struikel bij elke stap die ik zet.
Toch hoor ik vanuit de mist een fluistering:
‘Jij bent van Mij, vertrouw op Mij, Ik zal een weg banen.’

Soms lijken mijn omstandigheden
Hard en oneerlijk.
Maar dan fluistert mijn Vader:
‘Lieve kind, wanhoop niet.’

Soms voel ik me helemaal alleen,
De pijn vanbinnen verstikt en brandt.
De Meester zegt: ‘Mijn uitverkorene,
Ik alleen kan vervullen waarnaar je hart verlangt.

Soms zijn mijn ogen vol tranen,
Mijn hart voelt alsof het bijna barst.
Dan herinnert mijn Heiland mij eraan:
Dit pad voor mij heeft Hij bewandeld.

Soms maak ik me zorgen en vraag ik me af
Hoe alles ooit goed zal komen.
Toch blijft de belofte staan: alles komt goed
Voor wie zich in God verheugt.

Soms lijkt de toekomst beangstigend,
Helemaal niet zoals ik had gehoopt.
Toch richt ik mijn ogen op Zijn uiteindelijke doel,
Wetend dat het beter is dan waar ik naar had gezocht.

Soms voel ik me achtergelaten,
Terwijl het leven van anderen zo vrij doorgaat.
Maar ik zal vertrouwen op de plannen van mijn Vader
En uitzien naar Zijn eeuwige jubel!

Soms droom ik ervan
Dat de toekomst in de hemel aanbreekt.
O, wat een zalig gevoel zal het zijn
Die woorden te horen: ‘Goed gedaan.’

I’ll walk with God—Today—
Tomorrow may not be.
I’ll make the best of TIME—right now—
That God has granted me.

I’ll plan not for a life
That I might live in ease,
But only for today to live
My God alone to please.

Nor dare I think in years
Or move from leaps to bounds;
With God shut out, and self shut in
And selfish aims surround.

There are those who plan their lives,
Who give God little thought;
Who weigh themselves, not with God’s truth,
As every day they ought!

“Boast not thyself,” I’m warned,
“Of what tomorrow brings;
Thy health and wealth—e’en life itself—
May all at once take wings!”

“This night, that soul of thine
May be required of thee:
And dost thou plan the New Year full
There, ‘neath some Christmas tree?”

“Wake up! Take stock, are you prepared?
Your lessons learned alright?
If God, in yet three hours, THIS DAY,
Should close your course TONIGHT?”

Ek sal vandag met God wandel—
Môre bestaan dalk nie.
Ek sal die meeste maak van TYD—nou dadelik—
Wat God my geskenk het.

Ek sal nie beplan vir ’n lewe
Waarin ek gerieflik kan leef nie,
Maar net beplan om vandag te leef
Om alleen my God te behaag.

Ek durf ook nie in jare dink
Of met reusespronge vooruitbeur nie;
Met God uitgesluit en die self ingesluit,
En selfsugtige oogmerke wat my omring.

Daar is dié wat hul lewens beplan,
Wat min aan God dink;
Wat hulself nie aan God se waarheid meet nie,
Soos hulle elke dag behoort te doen!

“Moenie roem nie,” word ek gewaarsku,
“oor wat môre bring;
Jou gesondheid en rykdom—ja, selfs jou lewe—
kan alles skielik wegvlieg!”

“Vanaand kan daardie siel van jou
van jou geëis word:
En beplan jy daar die hele Nuwe Jaar,
onder ’n Kersboom?”

“Word wakker! Maak bestek: is jy gereed?
Het jy jou lesse goed geleer?
As God oor nog drie uur, VANDAG,
jou lewensloop VANAAND sou afsluit?”

1.
God has not promised skies always blue,
Flower-strewn pathways all our lives through;
God has not promised sun without rain,
Joy without sorrow, peace without pain.

Refrain:
But God has promised strength for the day,
Rest for the labor, light for the way,
Grace for the trials, help from above,
Unfailing kindness, undying love.

2.
God has not promised we shall not know
Toil and temptation, trouble and woe;
He has not told us we shall not bear
Many a burden, many a care.

3.
God has not promised smooth roads and wide,
Swift, easy travel, needing no guide;
Never a mountain rocky and steep,
Never a river turbid and deep.

The grinding sound of truck tires driving in the gravel lane filled the air as I sat in the house reading an encyclopedia. Leaping to my feet, I peered out the window.

Mom had just returned from the produce auction in Lewisburg with some peaches.

Slamming the door behind me, I raced across the thick green grass and leaped onto the bed of our truck.

On the back of the pickup sat four boxes of peaches. Grinning triumphantly, I reached into a box searching until I found a ripe one. Just before I bit into it, Mom said, “Steven, don’t eat any peaches; it will ruin your supper.” Sadly, I tossed the peach back into the box and then slowly walked away.

Several hours later, Dad called from the veal barn. “Steven, go pick the radishes for our Friday market produce stand.”

After picking, washing, and banding the radishes, I carried them into the old cooler which was inside the red bank barn. The cooler door squeaked as I yanked it open. There along the cooler walls sat the four boxes of the tantalizing peaches. I stared at the peaches, my mouth watering. I quickly set the radishes down. Oh, how good they looked. Surely a little peach wouldn’t ruin a starving ten-year-old’s supper. Mom wouldn’t know if I only took one peach.

Deep in my heart, a battle between right and wrong started to develop. I knew that sneaking was wrong, but those peaches looked way too good.

After devouring the peach, I scanned the dark interior of the barn for a good hiding place to put the peach stone. I looked across the onions, laying on drying racks, to the open hay bale. The only problem was that if I put the stone under the hay someone could find it. Then I spied the holes in the barn siding boards on the west side of the barn. If I pushed the stone through one of those holes it would land beside the road. Then, if someone saw it, they would think that it came from a passing vehicle.

I jammed the stone through the hole, peering out as it fell beside the road. At that split second, I felt a searing pain on my forehead. Frantically, I sprang back. There above the hole hung a yellow jacket nest. Then I saw the culprit as it hovered over me trying to sting me again. I sprinted out the barn door, slamming the door into the yellow jacket’s face.

That evening my forehead swelled like a balloon, making it difficult to look out of my eyes.

A few hours later, everyone else went to bed. I laid on the couch so that Mom could occasionally check up on me during the night. But I just couldn’t fall asleep. My face was inflamed and itchy, but all that I could think about was the guilt and remorse of what I had done.

After several agonizing hours, I gathered the courage to slide off the couch and tiptoed over to my parent’s bedroom. Awakening my parents, I told them the whole story… how I ate the peach, then tried to hide the stone, and how I had gotten stung.

My parents forgave me, deciding that this was one lesson that I wouldn’t soon forget. Walking back to the couch with a light heart, I laid down, and quickly fell into a peaceful sleep.

जब मैं घर में बैठकर विश्वकोश पढ़ रहा था, तब बजरी वाली गली में चल रहे ट्रक के टायरों की घिसटती आवाज़ से वातावरण भर गया। मैं उछलकर खड़ा हुआ और खिड़की से बाहर झाँका।

माँ अभी-अभी लुईसबर्ग की उपज नीलामी से कुछ आड़ू लेकर लौटी थीं।

अपने पीछे दरवाज़ा ज़ोर से बंद करके, मैं घनी हरी घास पर से दौड़ता हुआ गया और हमारे ट्रक के पीछे चढ़ गया।

पिकअप ट्रक के पिछले हिस्से में आड़ुओं के चार बक्से रखे थे। विजयी मुस्कान के साथ मैंने एक बक्से में हाथ डालकर पका हुआ आड़ू ढूँढ़ा। जैसे ही मैं उसे काटने ही वाला था, माँ ने कहा, “स्टीवन, कोई आड़ू मत खाना; इससे तुम्हारा रात का खाना खराब हो जाएगा।” मैंने दुखी होकर आड़ू वापस बक्से में रख दिया और फिर धीरे-धीरे वहाँ से चला गया।

कई घंटे बाद, पिताजी ने बछड़ों के खलिहान से पुकारा, “स्टीवन, शुक्रवार के बाज़ार में हमारी उपज की दुकान के लिए मूली तोड़ लाओ।”

मूली तोड़ने, धोने और गट्ठर बाँधने के बाद, मैं उन्हें लाल खलिहान के भीतर बने पुराने शीतगृह में ले गया। मैंने ज़ोर से दरवाज़ा खींचकर खोला तो वह चरमराया। शीतगृह की दीवारों के पास वे चारों लुभावने आड़ुओं के बक्से रखे थे। मैं आड़ुओं को देखता रहा और मेरे मुँह में पानी भर आया। मैंने जल्दी से मूली नीचे रख दी। आड़ू कितने अच्छे लग रहे थे! भूखे दस साल के बच्चे का रात का खाना थोड़े-से आड़ू से भला कैसे खराब होता? अगर मैं सिर्फ़ एक आड़ू लेता, तो माँ को पता भी नहीं चलता।

मेरे मन के भीतर सही और ग़लत के बीच संघर्ष शुरू हो गया। मैं जानता था कि चोरी-छिपे खाना ग़लत है, लेकिन वे आड़ू बेहद स्वादिष्ट लग रहे थे।

आड़ू खा चुकने के बाद, मैंने आड़ू की गुठली छिपाने की अच्छी जगह ढूँढ़ने के लिए खलिहान के अँधेरे हिस्से में नज़र दौड़ाई। सूखने के लिए जालीदार तख्तों पर रखे प्याज़ों के पार मेरी नज़र खुले पड़े घास के गट्ठर पर गई। दिक्कत सिर्फ़ यह थी कि अगर मैं गुठली घास के नीचे रखता, तो कोई उसे ढूँढ़ सकता था। फिर मेरी नज़र खलिहान की पश्चिमी तरफ़ की बाहरी तख्तों के छेदों पर पड़ी। अगर मैं गुठली को उन छेदों में से किसी एक में धकेल देता, तो वह सड़क के किनारे जा गिरती। फिर अगर किसी ने उसे देखा, तो वे सोचते कि वह किसी गुज़रते वाहन से गिरी होगी।

मैंने गुठली को छेद में ज़ोर से धकेला और उसे सड़क के किनारे गिरते हुए देखने के लिए बाहर झाँका। उसी पल मेरे माथे में तेज़ जलन वाला दर्द उठा। मैं घबराकर पीछे उछला। छेद के ठीक ऊपर पीली ततैया का घोंसला लटक रहा था। तभी मैंने उस दोषी ततैया को देखा, जो मेरे ऊपर मंडरा रही थी और फिर से डंक मारने की कोशिश कर रही थी। मैं खलिहान के दरवाज़े से बाहर तेज़ी से भागा और दरवाज़ा पीली ततैया के मुँह पर दे मारा।

उस शाम मेरा माथा गुब्बारे की तरह सूज गया, जिससे आँखें खोलकर देखना मुश्किल हो गया।

कुछ घंटे बाद, बाकी सब सोने चले गए। मैं सोफ़े पर लेट गया ताकि माँ रात में कभी-कभी मेरी ख़बर ले सकें। लेकिन मुझे नींद ही नहीं आ रही थी। मेरा चेहरा सूजा हुआ और खुजलीदार था, पर मैं बस अपने किए के अपराधबोध और पछतावे के बारे में ही सोच सकता था।

कई पीड़ादायक घंटों के बाद, मैंने सोफ़े से धीरे से उतरने का साहस जुटाया और दबे पाँव अपने माता-पिता के कमरे तक गया। मैंने उन्हें जगाया और पूरी कहानी बता दी… कि मैंने आड़ू खाया, फिर गुठली छिपाने की कोशिश की, और मुझे डंक भी लगा।

मेरे माता-पिता ने मुझे माफ़ कर दिया और तय किया कि यह ऐसा सबक था जिसे मैं जल्दी नहीं भूलूँगा। मन हल्का किए सोफ़े तक लौटकर, मैं लेट गया और जल्दी ही सुकूनभरी नींद सो गया।

Thou hast the dew of thy youth. Psalm 110:3

There are many aspects of youth which are not virtuous. Many youth of our day experience an early season of callused carelessness and casualty. Often decisions that are made in youthful years set the foundation for the rest of their lives. It was a the younger prodigal brother that asked for an early draw on his inheritance then went and wasted it on riotous living. It was a young Dinah who wandered from her father’s house and …went out to see the daughters of the land –Genesis 34:1. There, she was exposed to the heathen young men of the land and occasioned a bloody massacre, leaving Jacob as a stench in the land. Many foolish young people have sown to the wind and reaped the havoc thereof. Those that are void of solid principles and parental authority are at high risk for spiritual shipwreck.

There are particular lusts that inflict youth more so than the aged, and the young are exhorted to flee them. (–see 2 Timothy 2:22) Solomon looked through his window casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding -Proverbs 7:6-7. The young man was in heartfelt pursuit of that which appeared lovely… [Un]Till a dart [struck] through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life –Proverbs 7:23. We could examine the vices from the youthful lives of Rehoboam, Amnon, Nadab and Abihu, and countless others. We also find no lack of modern, folly-filled examples about us fulfilled by frivolous youth.

But youth are not meant to be despised. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. In fact, God generally chooses the youth as the instruments of His propagation. Joseph, of sterling character, was sent by God into Egypt at the age of 17 to preserve life (–see Genesis 45:5). Miriam, at the age of twelve, stood post over the future deliverer of the entire Jewish nation and secured her own mother, Jochebed, to be the nurse of the baby Moses. David, as a youth, was sent to encourage his brethren in the army. He was despised by his brothers: …I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart… –1 Samuel 17:28. He was rejected by Saul: …Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth… –1 Samuel 17:33. He was scorned by Goliath: …Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves… –1 Samuel 17:43. But their contempt was all for naught when he was chosen by God to be king over all Israel.

These noble youthful ambitions were followed by Josiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Mary, and the disciples of the Lord, all who chose to remember their Creator in the days of their youth. But these were not naive specimens seeking to secure their place in life, they were graphic examples of youth who were seeking to imitate the image of their Lord.

We need not gaze long into the character of Christ before we find…

...Thou hast the dew of thy youth

Psalm 110 is perhaps the most referred-to scripture in the Old Testament. This rhetorical portrait of the Messiah reveals a vivid virtue for us to behold. Christ, as the Ancient of days, was described in the Revelation having His head and His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet, here He is depicted as eternally young, as He sits at the right hand of God (–see Psalm 110:1). No weariness of age can enter there, for Christ is the Morning Star. It is perpetual morning around the throne of God. Those saints who are following hard after His likeness will also reflect this virtue, for the light of Jesus is the light of youth.

The psalmist, describing the Messiah, draws from the natural beauty of the morning dew (–see Psalm 110:3). The thought of dew calls us back from the heavens and unveils before us a portrait of this earth on which we dwell. In heaven there is no night, no change of heat and cold, no need of the sun to light up the day and consequently… no dew. The nature of dew belongs to the terrestrial, where everyone who will but stoop to observe it will behold a uniformed regiment of grass sparkling as if embedded with a myriad of diamonds. After a long night of darkness, the dewdrops, like tears, stand in the eyes of the flowers as they weep for joy at the advent of the first morning sunbeam. Those who walk through the lowly vegetation will have their feet washed by a thousand caressing hands of God’s design. Christ is not depicted as the dew of the morning but as the dew of youth, and the imagery is stretched further.

Youth is the season of abounding energy. Some cannot sit still. They are generally interpersonal creatures who love social activity. This is neither a virtue nor a vice. Rather, it is nominal nature. There is a progressive strain in advancing years that tames and tempers the soul. As life progresses, there is a clearer vision and a steadier thought, and we rise to better things. But when the mid-life summit has been crossed and the feet are traveling downward on the slope, that tumultuous rush of bodily energy that plowed through anything becomes enshrined with memories of the past. It is the closest comfort many can find to the bygone days of their strength.

But Christ has not called us to foster a fondness for the past nor a wistful longing for the “DO” of our youth. So many today sadly lament that their ‘get-up-and-go’ has got up and went. These have no vision for higher things and are more energized by a can of Mountain Dew than the Dew of Youth. They are more inspired by a trip down memory lane and reminiscing events of the past than of the hope that lies before them.

Age is no hindrance to securing the dew of youth. The Ancient of Days still rides forth among the golden candlesticks. While John beheld His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet Solomon declares …his locks are bushy, and black as a raven –Song of Solomon 5:11. While age may steal our strength and hearing, …the LORD’S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: –Isaiah 59:1. He has secured the dew of youth and invites us to partake. The problem is not found in our deteriorating body but in a spiritually declining mind. The bane of old age predominately sets in when the mind follows the body.

It is not that life grows poorer as it advances or ceases to be noble when the charm of youth has faded. If we were placed here only to experience joy, the dying out of youthful romance would be terrible. God had a much greater end in view for His children than to just be vibrant ‘doers’. We are sent here to learn. Our allotted years upon earth are all meant to be a schooling, and it is not in the bright romance of youth that we learn the best and most abiding lessons. It is in the dogged doing of our duty, the quiet acceptance of our limitations, the patient carrying of our daily burden, and in the stretching out of a helping hand to our brother. These afford us the true opportunities for Christian culture and are the roots of ethical nobility. Christ labored …not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life… –John 6:27, and He finished His earthly task in 33 years. But the dew of youth did not dissipate as He sat down at the right hand of His Father.

Thus, we conclude that this youthfulness will not be secured by strength, but by…

...Hope

But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. –Hebrews 10:12-13.

How shall we picture this Christ now? Reclining in an easy chair, all worn out from His experience with the stubborn people of this earth? Is He busy putting together a scrap book of precious memories? This is too often the position of the aged and so their mind dies with their bodies.

And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope –Romans 5:3-4. At times, we wonder if this scripture can be true. Anyone with any age on their bones can testify to a poor experience and the subsequent feelings of hopelessness following. As people, we have all faced disappointing experiences with a spouse, a child, or a church relationship after which a nagging cloud of despair settles in. Outside of Christ, a sour experience always tends to pessimism. It was so in the world when Jesus came. It is still so today.

But the dew of youth is incurably hopeful. There is an effervescent expectation that is naturally and magnificently borne in youth and retained in Christ. In every winter, when the fields are bleak, and the cold gust goes whistling through the trees, there lies the hope that the flowers will spring again. In every spring there is the hope of summer. In every summer there is the hope of harvest. It is alive in nature and alive in youth. Those who are blind to it shall reap, at best, a dreary monotone existence. To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all. –Oscar Wilde.

The rest shall be brightly effected with a hope that…

…Heals Our Infirmities

Our bodies are destined for the grave and have no hope for renewal in this life. It is our minds that carry our greatest infirmities. The impotent man of 38 years at Bethesda could only utter a hopeless complaint when Christ asked him, …Wilt thou be made whole? –John 5:6. Upon the wake of his new day, a new remedy was given to him—… Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee –John 5:14. What could be worse than being a cripple for years? A mind that is beset by a doleful indulgence in the sorrows of this world. Age sets in when we have more memories of the past than hope for tomorrow. It is disappointing when folks grow old and have no vision for tomorrow, but it is a disaster to behold youth that are plagued by its crippling effects. Many grope aimlessly through life’s various trials, stupefied by the lack of blessedness. The noonday sun has evaporated the dew of their youth and the only praise that they can muster is culminated from a handful of yesterday’s pleasantries. A new attitude must be birthed by the dew of a new morning.

…Humbles Our Pursuits

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. –John 21:18. When we are young, we can overcome in the strength of our youth. As age takes its course, we will find a different alternative: victory through surrender.

…I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one. –1 John 2:14. The world entices us to selfish living. Youth are often subject to schools of learning that teach them to “be all that you can be”. There is a major focus on self-enhancement and preparation for the future. This may prepare them in a ‘survival of the fittest’ world but will leave them destitute when the strength and prowess of youth has departed.

For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever. –1 John 2:16-17. Overcoming evil with good is the Biblical antidote for channeling youthful energies. Whether it is the lust within or the longing without, hope is conceived by planting a seed of kindness in the life of another. The pursuit of pleasure and lieu of leisure will always disappoint its recipient and leave him in a valley of despair deeper than when he began. It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth … He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope. –Lamentations 3:27-29. We are created to work in God’s vineyard and those who have an appetite for it will reap in hope of its youthful reward.

…Hallows Our Trials

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope... –Romans 8:24. How often we can relate to Job in his pain. But before his pain had received an ounce of retribution, the healing streams began to flow as Job reverenced his Creator. When we can acknowledge that God is perfect in all the trials He allows, we then learn to worship in the temple not made with hands and disregard the frailties of the body. To sit down at the feet of Christ ignites a youthful spark that radiates the spirit within and conceives hope. The dew of youth then becomes our portion as Christ imparts eternal life and eternal youth to us. From the hour of the grave and through eternity we shall be young and bid defiance to weariness and death if we are living in the morning light of Jesus Christ. Heaven is a place of perpetual youth, and just like the light of the sun is reflected on the moon, so likewise the light of Christ is reflected on His bride. She is clean and young, …a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing… –Ephesians 5:27. Blessed is the venerable saint who arrives at the portals of heaven in such a condition.

你的少年时光如清晨的露水。诗篇 110:3

青春有许多方面并不美德。我们这个时代的许多年轻人，很早就经历了麻木冷漠、鲁莽轻率的时期。年轻时所作的决定，常常为余生奠定基础。那个年轻的小儿子浪子要求提前支取自己的产业，随后便放荡度日，把产业挥霍一空。有个年轻的底拿离开父亲的家，……出去，要看看那地的女子。——创世记 34:1。在那里，她接触到当地的异教青年男子，酿成一场血腥屠杀，使雅各在那地成为臭名昭著的人。许多愚昧的年轻人种下狂风，收获的却是灾祸。那些缺乏坚定原则、又没有父母权柄引导的人，极易遭遇属灵的船难。

有些私欲对年轻人的伤害胜过对年长者，年轻人受劝要逃避这些私欲。（——参见提摩太后书 2:22）所罗门从窗棂向外观看，见愚蒙人内，见少年人中，分明有一个无知的少年人。——箴言 7:6-7。那年轻人一心追求看似美好的事物…………直等箭穿他的肝；他如同雀鸟急入网罗，却不知是自丧己命。——箴言 7:23。我们可以考察罗波安、暗嫩、拿答和亚比户等人的年轻岁月中所犯的恶行，以及无数其他人的例子。我们周围也不乏现代的例子：轻浮的年轻人充满愚行。

但年轻人不该受人轻看。不可叫人小看你年轻；总要在言语、行为、爱心、信心、清洁上，都作信徒的榜样。——提摩太前书 4:12。事实上，神通常拣选年轻人作祂传扬福音的器皿。品格高尚的约瑟，十七岁时蒙神差遣到埃及，为要保全生命（——参见创世记 45:5）。米利暗十二岁时，守在那位将来要拯救整个犹太民族的人身边，并设法让自己的母亲约基别作婴儿摩西的乳母。大卫年轻时被差去鼓励军中的弟兄。他遭兄长轻视：……我知道你的骄傲，和你心里的恶意……——撒母耳记上 17:28。他被扫罗拒绝：……你不能去与那非利士人战斗；因为你年纪太轻……——撒母耳记上 17:33。他被歌利亚嘲笑：……你拿着杖到我这里来，我岂是狗呢？……——撒母耳记上 17:43。然而，当神拣选他作全以色列的王时，他们的轻蔑全都落了空。

约西亚、以赛亚、耶利米、但以理、马利亚，以及主的门徒，都承继了这些高尚的青年志向；他们都选择在年少时记念造他们的主。但他们并非天真地想在人生中谋得一席之地，而是鲜明地显明了年轻人如何寻求效法主的形象。

我们无需长久凝视基督的品格，就会发现……

……你的少年时光如清晨的露水

诗篇 110 可能是旧约中被引用最多的经文。这幅关于弥赛亚的修辞画像，呈现出一个鲜明的美德，供我们瞻仰。基督作为亘古常在者，在《启示录》中被描写为头与发皆白，如白羊毛，如雪……——启示录 1:14；然而这里描绘的祂却永远年轻，坐在神的右边（——参见诗篇 110:1）。那里不会有年老带来的疲倦，因为基督是晨星。神的宝座周围，永远是清晨。那些竭力效法祂的人，也会映照出这美德，因为耶稣的光就是青春之光。

诗篇作者描写弥赛亚时，借用了清晨露水的自然之美（——参见诗篇 110:3）。露水这个意象把我们的目光从天上带回，使我们眼前显出一幅我们居住的地上景象。天上没有黑夜，没有冷热变化，也不需要太阳照亮白昼，因此……没有露水。露水属于大地；凡肯俯身观察的人，都会看见整齐如列队的青草闪闪发光，仿佛嵌满万千颗钻石。经过漫长的黑夜，露珠如泪珠般停留在花朵的眼中；当第一缕晨光到来，花朵欢喜得仿佛流泪。走过低矮草木的人，双脚会被神所造的千百只轻柔之手洗濯。基督所象征的不是清晨的露水，而是青春的露水；这个意象还可以进一步延展。

青春是精力充沛的时期。有些人坐不住。他们通常喜欢与人交往，热爱社交活动。这既不是美德，也不是恶习，而是寻常的天性。随着岁月增长，有一种逐渐发展的力量会磨炼并调和灵魂。人生渐进，我们的眼光更清晰，思想更稳健，也就迈向更美好的事物。然而，当我们越过中年顶峰，双脚沿着斜坡向下走时，那曾经横冲直撞的汹涌体力，便只能珍藏在往事的记忆中。对许多人来说，回忆往日强健的岁月，是他们能找到的最亲切的慰藉。

但基督并未呼召我们留恋过去，也没有要我们忧伤地怀念年轻时的“活力”。今天许多人哀叹自己已经失去了干劲。他们对更高远的事物毫无异象，比起青春的露水，他们喝一罐激浪汽水更能提振精神。他们更受回忆往事、追忆过去事件的鼓舞，而不是前方摆在眼前的盼望。

年岁增长并不妨碍人得着青春的露水。亘古常在者仍在金灯台中间行走。约翰看见祂的头与发……白如羊毛，白如雪……——启示录 1:14，所罗门却说……他的头发厚密，黑如乌鸦。——雅歌 5:11。年岁或许会夺去我们的体力和听力，然而……耶和华的膀臂并非缩短，不能拯救；耳朵并非发沉，不能听见。——以赛亚书 59:1。祂已经为我们保全青春的露水，并邀请我们来领受。问题不在于身体日渐衰败，而在于心灵日渐衰退。年老的祸患主要在于心灵随着身体一同衰退。

人生并不会随着岁月增长而变得贫乏，也不会在青春的魅力消逝时便不再高尚。如果我们来到世上只是为了经历欢乐，那么青春浪漫的消退就会令人痛苦不堪。但神为祂的儿女设定的目标远不止是让他们活力充沛地“做事”。我们被差到世上来学习。我们在世所分得的年日，都是为了受教；我们学到最深刻、最持久的功课，并非来自青春洋溢的浪漫，而是在坚忍地尽本分、平静地接受自身限制、耐心地担起每日的重担，以及向弟兄伸出援手时学到的。这些为我们提供了真正培养基督徒品格的机会，也是道德高尚的根基。基督劳苦，……不要为那必坏的食物劳力，要为那存到永生的食物劳力……——约翰福音 6:27，并在三十三年中完成了祂在世上的使命。但祂坐在父的右边时，青春的露水并未消散。

因此，我们得出结论：这种青春活力不是靠力量得着的，而是……

……盼望

但基督献了一次永远的赎罪祭，就坐在神的右边。从此等候仇敌成了祂的脚凳。——希伯来书 10:12-13。

我们如今该如何想象这位基督？祂会不会疲惫不堪地躺在安乐椅上，仿佛已经受够了世上顽梗的人？祂是否忙着制作一本珍贵回忆剪贴簿？年长者往往就是如此，以至于心灵随着身体一同死去。

不但如此，就是在患难中也是欢欢喜喜的；因为知道患难生忍耐，忍耐生老练，老练生盼望。——罗马书 5:3-4。有时我们会怀疑这段经文是否属实。凡是上了年纪的人，都能作证自己曾有过糟糕的经历，随后感到绝望。我们每个人都曾在配偶、子女或教会关系中经历令人失望的事，之后挥之不去的绝望阴云便笼罩心头。离开基督，令人失望的经历总会使人倾向悲观。耶稣降世时，世上的情形就是如此；今天仍然如此。

但青春的露水带着无法根除的盼望。青春天然地蕴含着一种活泼而美妙的期待；在基督里，这期待得以保留。每逢冬天，田野一片萧瑟，寒风呼啸着穿过树林，心中仍有盼望：花朵会再次绽放。每逢春天，就有对夏天的盼望；每逢夏天，就有对收成的盼望。盼望活在自然中，也活在青春中。对盼望视而不见的人，至多只能收获沉闷单调的人生。活着是世上最稀有的事。大多数人只是存在，仅此而已。——奥斯卡·王尔德。

其余的人则会因盼望而明亮起来，这盼望……

……医治我们的软弱

我们的身体注定归于坟墓，在今生没有更新的盼望。我们最大的软弱在于心思意念。那位在毕士大病了三十八年的瘫子，基督问他……你愿意痊愈吗？——约翰福音 5:6。他只能发出绝望的抱怨。当他迎来新的一天时，基督赐给他新的医治之道——……你已经痊愈了，不要再犯罪，恐怕你遭遇的更加严重。——约翰福音 5:14。有什么会比多年残疾更糟？那就是沉溺于世间哀伤的心。每当我们对过去的记忆多过对明日的盼望，衰老便开始了。人们年老之后对明日毫无异象，令人失望；但看见年轻人也受这种使人瘫痪的影响所困，更是一场灾难。许多人在生命的种种试炼中漫无目的地摸索，因缺乏福乐而麻木。正午的太阳蒸发了他们青春的露水，他们唯一能发出的赞美，也不过是从昨日少许欢愉中拼凑而来。新清晨的露水必须孕育出新的态度。

……使我们的追求谦卑

我实实在在地告诉你，你年少的时候，自己束上带子，随意往来；但年老的时候，你要伸出手来，别人要把你束上，带你到不愿意去的地方。——约翰福音 21:18。年轻时，我们能靠着青春的力量得胜。随着年岁增长，我们会发现另一种途径：借着降服而得胜。

……我写信给你们少年人，因为你们刚强，神的道常存在你们心里，你们也胜了那恶者。——约翰一书 2:14。世界诱惑我们自私地生活。年轻人常常要接受那些教他们“尽你所能做到最好”的学校教育。教育着重于自我提升和为未来作准备。在“适者生存”的世界里，这或许能帮助他们预备自己；但当青春的力量与本领消逝时，他们就会一无所有。

因为凡世界上的事，就像肉体的情欲、眼目的情欲，并今生的骄傲，都不是从父来的，乃是从世界来的。这世界和其上的情欲都要过去；惟独遵行神旨意的，是永远常存。——约翰一书 2:16-17。以善胜恶，是圣经所给的解方，能引导年轻人的活力。无论是内心的私欲，还是外在的渴求，只要在他人的生命中种下仁慈的种子，盼望便会萌生。追逐享乐、贪图闲暇，总会令追求者失望，使他陷入比起初更深的绝望谷底。人在幼年负轭，这原是好的……他当口贴尘埃，或者有指望。——耶利米哀歌 3:27-29。我们受造是要在神的葡萄园里劳作；凡有心投入其中的人，都会怀着盼望，收获青春的奖赏。

……使我们的试炼成圣

我们得救是在乎盼望；只是所见的盼望不是盼望……——罗马书 8:24。我们多么常能体会约伯的痛苦。然而，在他的痛苦尚未得到丝毫补偿之前，疗愈的溪流便已开始流淌，因为约伯敬畏他的造物主。当我们承认神在祂所容许的一切试炼中都是完全的，就学会在非人手所造的圣殿里敬拜，不再看重身体的脆弱。坐在基督脚前，会点燃青春的火花，照亮内里的灵，并孕育盼望。基督将永生和永恒的青春赐给我们，青春的露水便成为我们的分。自坟墓的时刻起，直到永恒，我们都将年轻；若我们活在耶稣基督清晨的光中，就能向疲倦和死亡夸胜。天堂是永恒青春之地；正如太阳的光反映在月亮上，基督的光也照耀在祂的新妇身上。她是圣洁而年轻的，……作个荣耀的教会，毫无玷污、皱纹等类的病……——以弗所书 5:27。有福了，那位德高望重的圣徒如此抵达天堂的门口。

Do you want to have a good life? What is there that you believe you need to experience or accomplish so you can truly enjoy life? Many people’s main goal in life is to seek pleasure and to have fun. Much time and money are spent to achieve this. But do we accomplish it? In our natural mind we think that the circumstances need to be just right to please us. But we all know that circumstances are never ideal all the time. So, we can’t depend on those for our happiness. We need something bigger than that. Or Someone.

Obviously, we know that God alone is never changing and always faithful. Another thing about God is that He is sovereign. In other words, He’s in charge. But we like our independence; we like things to happen in a way that feels good to us. When life doesn’t happen that way, we are brought to a decision. Will we accept all of God—both His unchangeableness and His sovereignty—or will we fight to have our own way in our pursuit of a good life?

The root of joy is with God Himself. This is because He created us for Himself. He created us to bring pleasure to Himself, but we think we need to bring pleasure to ourselves. It started in the garden of Eden when the serpent convinced Eve that pleasing herself was more important than pleasing God. Since then, humans have been at war, both within their own hearts and without, with other folks. All in the effort of trying to find pleasure for themselves, yet not finding it because they were created to please God.

The solution for this war is found in James 4. It’s simple: submit to God. Humble yourselves before Him. This is not too much for Him to ask of us, because He is sovereign. He created us, so He has the say in how we live. If we will truly find enjoyment in life, it will be by putting our own life and desires on the cross and becoming one with God and His original purpose for us. Rather than it being restrictive, this opens up a world of opportunities and possibilities. It doesn’t mean we have to do things because God wants us to. Becoming one with God means that what He wants us to do is also what we want to do.

Worship and Gratitude

When we are one with God, our whole perspective changes. Instead of pining over all the things that aren’t ideal, we begin to see the many things that are true blessings. We can have a heart of worship and gratitude for all the good things that we do experience. We are able to see how unworthy we really are. We didn’t deserve anything good, but God has still given us so many things to enjoy!

Living in the Present

As young ladies, we have a tendency to dream, to live in a future that is idealistic and pleasant. We sometimes struggle to live in the present imperfect reality and find joy in it. But when God’s will becomes our will then true joy happens, because we are fulfilling His purpose for us.

We can learn to experience joy in any circumstance, even in mundane life. We’re afraid of living a boring life. We want it to be exciting. But He wants us to please Him, and when we do, we experience joy no matter the circumstances. However, we are also then available for Him to use in service to His Kingdom, and He may call us to opportunities that are exciting. But we won’t be effective in the exciting missions unless we have learned to be submitted to His will in everyday life.

Relationships

When we are finding joy and contentment in where God has us in the present, we are able to focus on developing solid, upbuilding relationships with those who are in our lives right now. God has created us as social people, and good relationships will bring true enjoyment to us. God is also able to use us in reaching out to other people. When we are one with Him, our focus is no longer on ourselves but on others. The life of God can flow through us and both show others the way to Him and give us joy and fulfillment in doing it.

Emotions

Another tendency we have is to let our emotions control us. And they will run wild if we are looking to our circumstances to give us pleasure. We will end up on a roller coaster of feelings dictated by whatever is happening at the moment. And then we escape to the dream world, which only distorts our view of reality even more. But God is steadfast, and when we are one with Him, He imparts to us stability and rest. And we are able to experience ever present joy—even in ever changing circumstances.

Let us continue to become ever more one with Him. And He will give us heavenly sunlight all of our journey, unchanged by circumstances on earth and realized in full when we see Him face to face. …in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore –Psalm 16:11.

Wil je een goed leven hebben? Wat denk je dat je moet meemaken of bereiken om echt van het leven te kunnen genieten? Voor veel mensen is het belangrijkste doel in het leven om plezier te zoeken en het naar hun zin te hebben. Daar wordt veel tijd en geld aan besteed. Maar bereiken we dat ook? In onze natuurlijke gezindheid denken we dat de omstandigheden precies goed moeten zijn om ons tevreden te stellen. Maar we weten allemaal dat de omstandigheden nooit voortdurend ideaal zijn. Dus kunnen we ons geluk daar niet van laten afhangen. We hebben iets groters nodig dan dat. Of Iemand.

Natuurlijk weten we dat alleen God nooit verandert en altijd trouw is. Nog iets wat God kenmerkt, is dat Hij soeverein is. Met andere woorden: Hij heeft de leiding. Maar wij houden van onze onafhankelijkheid; we willen dat dingen gebeuren op een manier die goed voelt voor ons. Wanneer het leven niet zo verloopt, staan we voor een keuze. Zullen we God in zijn geheel aanvaarden—zowel zijn onveranderlijkheid als zijn soevereiniteit—of zullen we vechten om onze eigen zin te krijgen in ons streven naar een goed leven?

De bron van vreugde ligt bij God Zelf. Dat komt doordat Hij ons voor Zichzelf heeft geschapen. Hij heeft ons geschapen om Hem vreugde te geven, maar wij denken dat we onszelf vreugde moeten geven. Het begon in de hof van Eden, toen de slang Eva ervan overtuigde dat zichzelf behagen belangrijker was dan God behagen. Sindsdien zijn mensen in oorlog, zowel in hun eigen hart als daarbuiten, met andere mensen. Dat alles in een poging om voor zichzelf plezier te vinden, maar ze vinden het niet omdat ze geschapen zijn om God te behagen.

De oplossing voor deze oorlog vinden we in Jakobus 4. Het is eenvoudig: onderwerp je aan God. Verneder jezelf voor Hem. Dat is niet te veel van Hem gevraagd, want Hij is soeverein. Hij heeft ons geschapen, dus bepaalt Hij hoe we leven. Als we werkelijk vreugde in het leven willen vinden, zal dat zijn door ons eigen leven en onze verlangens aan het kruis te nagelen en één te worden met God en zijn oorspronkelijke doel voor ons. In plaats van ons te beperken, opent dit een wereld vol kansen en mogelijkheden. Dat betekent niet dat we dingen moeten doen omdat God dat van ons verlangt. Eén worden met God betekent dat we ook zelf willen doen wat Hij van ons verlangt.

Aanbidding en dankbaarheid

Wanneer we één zijn met God, verandert ons hele perspectief. In plaats van te treuren over alles wat niet ideaal is, beginnen we de vele dingen te zien die ware zegeningen zijn. We kunnen God aanbidden en dankbaar zijn voor alle goede dingen die we meemaken. We kunnen zien hoe onwaardig we werkelijk zijn. We verdienden niets goeds, maar toch heeft God ons zoveel gegeven om van te genieten!

Leven in het heden

Als jonge vrouwen hebben we de neiging om te dromen en te leven in een toekomst die ideaal en aangenaam is. Soms vinden we het moeilijk om te leven in de onvolmaakte werkelijkheid van het heden en daar vreugde in te vinden. Maar wanneer Gods wil onze wil wordt, ontstaat er ware vreugde, omdat we zijn doel voor ons vervullen.

We kunnen leren om in elke omstandigheid vreugde te ervaren, zelfs in het alledaagse leven. We zijn bang voor een saai leven. We willen dat het spannend is. Maar Hij wil dat we Hem behagen, en wanneer we dat doen, ervaren we vreugde, ongeacht de omstandigheden. Tegelijkertijd staan we dan ook klaar om door Hem ingezet te worden in dienst van zijn Koninkrijk, en kan Hij ons roepen voor spannende mogelijkheden. Maar we zullen niet doeltreffend zijn in spannende opdrachten als we niet hebben geleerd ons in het dagelijks leven aan zijn wil te onderwerpen.

Relaties

Wanneer we vreugde en tevredenheid vinden in de plek waar God ons nu heeft, kunnen we ons richten op het opbouwen van hechte, opbouwende relaties met de mensen die op dit moment in ons leven zijn. God heeft ons als sociale mensen geschapen, en goede relaties zullen ons echt vreugde brengen. God kan ons ook gebruiken om anderen te bereiken. Wanneer we één zijn met Hem, zijn we niet langer op onszelf gericht, maar op anderen. Gods leven kan door ons heen stromen, zodat we anderen zowel de weg naar Hem wijzen als zelf vreugde en vervulling ervaren terwijl we dat doen.

Emoties

Een andere neiging die we hebben, is om ons door onze emoties te laten beheersen. En die zullen alle kanten op gaan als we van onze omstandigheden verwachten dat ze ons plezier geven. Uiteindelijk belanden we dan in een emotionele achtbaan, waarbij onze gevoelens worden bepaald door wat er op dat moment gebeurt. Vervolgens vluchten we naar de droomwereld, die ons beeld van de werkelijkheid alleen maar verder vertekent. Maar God is standvastig, en wanneer we één zijn met Hem, schenkt Hij ons stabiliteit en rust. En we kunnen altijd vreugde ervaren—evenals de omstandigheden voortdurend veranderen.

Laten we steeds meer één met Hem worden. En Hij zal ons tijdens onze hele reis hemels zonlicht geven, onveranderd door de omstandigheden op aarde en volledig verwezenlijkt wanneer we Hem van aangezicht tot aangezicht zien. …in uw tegenwoordigheid is overvloed van vreugde; aan uw rechterhand zijn genoegens voor eeuwig –Psalm 16:11.

We can’t afford to win the gain that means another’s loss;
We can’t afford to miss the crown by stumbling at the cross.
We can’t afford the heedless jest that robs us of a friend;
We can’t afford the laugh that finds in bitter tears an end.
We can’t afford the feast today that brings tomorrow’s fast;
We can’t afford the race that comes to tragedy at last.
We can’t afford to play with fire, or tempt a serpent’s bite;
We can’t afford to think that sin brings any true delight.
We can’t afford with serious heed to treat the cynic’s sneer;
We can’t afford to wise men’s words to turn a careless ear.
We can’t afford for hate to give like hatred in return;
We can’t afford to feed a flame and make it fiercer burn.
We can’t afford to lose the soul for this world’s fleeting breath;
We can’t afford to barter life in mad exchange for death.
But blind to good are we apart from THEE, all-seeing Lord;
Oh, grant us light that we may know the things we can’t afford!

Greetings of Christian love to each one. Another year has passed us by, and another is spread out before us to navigate. What is our perspective? Do we have hope and joy bubbling up in our hearts or does the future seem full of gloom and doom? Do we see God’s sovereign hand at work in the situations and circumstances around us or does the world seem out of control from our vantage point?

As I interact with folks from around the country there seems to be a common issue that many folks are struggling with—weariness. Weary of mandates. Weary of shutdowns. Weary of all the bickering and fighting that has surrounded the Covid issue. Weary of…

It appears that many people just “Don’t want to think about it”. Why? I’m really not sure what all the reasons are, but I am sure that each person has one. Let’s remember that God wants us to …be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves –Matthew 10:16.

Here, in the United States of America, Christians have had over 60 years (since World War 2) of relative peace and tranquility. For the most part, we have been left alone to raise our families and worship the God of our fathers according to our conscience. We have enjoyed the separation of Church and State that was implemented at the beginning of our country’s existence. We have been able to work with our hands and earn a living. Many of us have lived off the fat of the land.

Maybe we were living in an artificial bubble. Maybe we have been lulled into a false sense of security. What about our counterparts in countries around the world, what is their reality of living as true Christians in their world? Sure, we have been able to use our wealth and freedom of movement to do much good for the rest of the world who have endured much hardship due to following Christ. But at what cost? What have our children learned?

Sometimes, we hear about first generation Christians being “on fire” for their Lord. Sometimes so much so that second and third generation Christians think that first generation Christians are perhaps a little too zealous in their efforts of evangelizing those around them.

What about the next generation? They are learning from someone—about God, themselves, and life. What are they learning? And who are they learning from? We must take stock to ensure that our children are learning life’s lessons in a way that they will be prepared to face the reality of things to come.

And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world? And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many –Matthew 24:3-5.

Remember that this is Jesus Himself speaking to His followers regarding the end of the world. His very first concern is that we would NOT be deceived. He says that deception will be the major issue surrounding the end of time. He says that many will come claiming to be Christ [or His direct spokesperson] in an attempt to gain a listening ear, all in an effort to deceive the hearer and gain a following.

If not before now, we most certainly must be teaching our children certain specific things through word and action. That we are to be strangers and pilgrims as we journey through this life. That if we are friends of this world then God will be our enemy. And that Jesus’ Kingdom is not of this world, therefore, His children must learn to live as ambassadors in a foreign land. Our children need to know that ALL who live godly in Christ Jesus WILL suffer persecution.

Many of the doctrines that have been taught in our churches and para-church functions have severely crippled the next generation of the church. We have been taught that we can have the “power of His resurrection” without needing to be a partaker of the “fellowship of His sufferings”. A suffering Christ with suffering followers has been thrown out in favor of following a Jesus who will not let anything bad happen to you. While there is much emphasis on a Jesus who suffered and died for you, there is very little to NO teaching on the need to “take up your cross daily” and follow Him.

Mental Health and Emotional Stability

Some years ago, I came across the story of a soldier, who, after serving a term of service in Iraq, was struggling to cope with PTSD. Sure, I believe that PTSD is real, and the struggles are real, but as I read this man’s story, I found myself becoming increasingly frustrated with the lack of answers that were being provided to a severely struggling young man. Some of his deepest struggles stemmed from the flashback memories he had of when he had personally killed several of the enemy. No matter how many counseling sessions he went to he just couldn’t come to a place of inner peace and rest. His mind was troubled. He had difficulty sleeping. He had problems getting along with others.

I had to think “If only someone could come alongside this young man and share the Gospel of Jesus Christ with him. If only he could be shown the Truth of God’s Word that to take another human’s life is sin in God’s eyes (even if he is the enemy) and God will not allow him to have peace in his heart until that is taken care of. Also, that the real excitement is that IF he would come to God according to the terms of the Bible and repent of his sin, then he could start walking with God and God could start giving him peace for his troubled soul.”

Over the last number of years, there have been numerous mass shootings here in the United States. Each time the public officials hold news conferences and share their thoughts in an effort to try to make sense out of another seemingly unexplainable tragic event. Usually, it’s not long until someone is talking about mental health and the need to step up public efforts to provide safety nets, screenings, and better and more treatments to curb this senseless violence.

Several weeks ago, there was a terrible, tragic event that took place in another state from where I live. In one of the big cities, a man pushed a woman off of the platform and into the path of an oncoming subway train. She didn’t survive. In the aftermath of such a horrific happening, the public officials made statements to the public in an effort to stem the potential public fear. They concluded that the man must have been emotionally troubled and that they would be stepping up their efforts in trying to provide a safety net for those with mental health issues, so that such things wouldn’t happen again.

Sure, when we look at the issue through the eyes of the world it seems to make sense. But is this the whole of the matter? Have we as Christians become so used to the ways of the world that we forget how far they have strayed from the Truth of God’s Word?

Let’s not point our finger at the world and the elected public officials. Are we, as the church, any better? How well do we know our Bible? How well do we know our Savior? When someone comes to us seeking peace and rest within do we know how to take them to the Scriptures, and lead them to Jesus who can then show them the way to the Father?

Why am I saying all this? If we continue to provide the next generation of the church with artificial answers and temporary solutions to the problems of life, then they will NOT be prepared to …endure unto the end… –Matthew 24:13.

And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: but whosoever will lose his life for my sake, the same shall save it –Luke 9:23-24.
