Na enkele maanden in Haïti te hebben gewoond, kreeg ik eindelijk de gelegenheid om de plaatselijke medicijnman te bezoeken. Toen ik zijn lange oprijlaan opliep, passeerde ik allerlei standbeelden en satanische symbolen. Het was beslist griezelig. Toen ik de voodootempel naderde die bij zijn huis hoorde, zag ik hem daar staan kijken hoe ik dichterbij kwam. Mijn hart begon sneller te kloppen; ik wist dat hij een machtig man was. Toen begon hij te lachen. Hoe dichterbij ik kwam, hoe harder hij lachte. Ik was enigszins verbaasd, totdat ik besefte dat veel mensen uit het dorp achter mij aan de laan op kwamen. Ze waren erg benieuwd naar wat er zou gebeuren. Ik liep op de man af, zonder te weten wat er vervolgens zou gebeuren.

‘Bent u een predikant?’ vroeg hij.

‘Ja, dat ben ik,’ antwoordde ik. Opnieuw begon hij luid te lachen.

‘Jullie predikanten zijn allemaal hetzelfde,’ verklaarde hij. ‘Jullie willen dat iedereen naar jullie kerken komt, maar jullie kerken hebben geen kracht! Als iemand van jullie ziek wordt, komen ze naar mij. Geen kracht, jullie christenen!’

Een zware last drukte op mij, en ik legde hem uit dat ik het met hem eens was, maar dat de ware kerk van Jezus Christus altijd kracht zou hebben. De Bijbel zegt zelfs dat de poorten van de hel haar niet zullen overweldigen.

Dit was het begin van een zeer bijzondere relatie, maar ik zal die woorden nooit vergeten—woorden die zonder twijfel van de duivel zelf kwamen: ‘Jullie christenen hebben geen kracht!’

Sindsdien heb ik honderden kerken bezocht en moet ik die voodoopriester gelijk geven. Het ontbreekt de christelijke kerken aan kracht. Maar waarom? We weten dat God kracht is. We hebben veel zaken op orde, we zien er goed uit en klinken goed, maar is de kracht van God nog steeds aanwezig in onze kerken?

In het Oude Testament vinden we veel voorbeelden van kracht en van het ontbreken daarvan. We kunnen er ook uit leren hoe we kracht ontvangen en waarom we die verliezen.

In Jozua, hoofdstuk 6, vinden we het bekende verhaal van de Israëlieten en de stad Jericho. God zegt tegen Jozua en alle krijgslieden dat ze om de stad heen moeten trekken en zes dagen lang elke dag één keer eromheen moeten lopen. Op de zevende dag moesten ze niet één keer, maar zeven keer om de stad heen trekken. Nadat ze zeven keer om de stad waren getrokken, moesten de priesters op hun trompetten blazen.

We weten wat er gebeurde toen Jozua elk bevel gehoorzaamde: die dikke, ondoordringbare muren stortten in. God gaf Jozua ook een streng bevel over wat de mannen wel en niet mochten doen. Ze moesten zich verre houden van alles wat God als iets vervloekts had bestempeld; al het zilver, goud en de vaten moesten aan de schatkamer van de HEER worden gewijd; niemand mocht iets van de buit meenemen.

Maar Achan zag mooie dingen die hij graag wilde hebben. Hij stopte ze onder zijn wapenrusting en verborg ze later onder zijn tent, zonder dat iemand iets zag.

Na deze grote overwinning stuurde Jozua verspieders naar de volgende stad, Ai, om te ontdekken hoe goed de stad versterkt was. De mannen keerden terug en zeiden tegen Jozua dat hij niet alle mannen naar Ai moest sturen, want er waren maar weinig verdedigers om de stad te beschermen.

Maar de mannen van Ai versloegen de Israëlieten en joegen hen op de vlucht. Bovendien scheurde Jozua zijn kleren en riep hij tot God. Toen antwoordde God dat er zonde was in het kamp van Israël.

In het Oude Testament zijn de Israëlieten doorgaans een beeld van de kerk van Jezus Christus van vandaag. Kunnen we niet veel leren van dit verhaal? Toen er geen zonde was in het kamp (of in de kerk), behaalden Gods mensen de volledige overwinning; ze verloren er niet één. Ze deden veel wonderbare dingen, vernietigden al hun vijanden rondom hen en leefden in VOLLEDIGE overwinning. Maar zodra de zonde hun midden binnendrong, zelfs een kleine zonde van één man, verloren ze hun kracht. Ze hadden niet langer de overwinning op hun vijanden.

Wat volgt, is een levendige beschrijving van de manier waarop de Israëlieten omgingen met de zonde die het kamp was binnengedrongen. Die werd volledig uitgeroeid.

En Jozua, en heel Israël met hem, nam Achan, de zoon van Zerah, en het zilver, en het kleed, en de goudstaaf, en zijn zonen, en zijn dochters, en zijn runderen, en zijn ezels, en zijn schapen, en zijn tent, en alles wat hij had; en zij brachten hen naar het dal van Achor … En heel Israël stenigde hem met stenen, en verbrandde hen met vuur… –Jozua 7:24-26.

In dit verhaal is duidelijk waarom Gods mensen hun kracht hadden verloren: er was zonde in het kamp. Ook is duidelijk wat ervoor nodig was om de verloren kracht terug te krijgen: de zonde wegdoen.

In hoofdstuk 8 lezen we dat Israël onmiddellijk weer kracht kreeg nadat de zonde was aangepakt. Opnieuw leefden ze in overwinning!

Een andere passage in het Oude Testament die over dit onderwerp spreekt, staat in Leviticus, hoofdstukken 13 en 14. Melaatsheid was een vreemde ziekte. Als iemand melaats werd, verspreidde de ziekte zich gemakkelijk. Daarom waren er strenge richtlijnen nodig voor de aanpak ervan. De priester moest zorgvuldig onderzoeken of de betreffende persoon inderdaad melaats was. Als de priester het niet zeker wist, sloot hij de persoon zeven dagen op en onderzocht hem daarna opnieuw. Als bleek dat de persoon melaats was, werd hij buiten de stad gestuurd.

Wanneer Paulus de kerk in Korinthe aanspreekt, vertelt hij hun dat hij heeft gehoord dat er zonde in de kerk is. Hij lijkt verbaasd dat de kerk daar zo luchtig mee omgaat: …Weet u niet dat een weinig zuurdeeg het hele deeg doorzuurt? Doe daarom het oude zuurdeeg weg, opdat u een nieuw deeg zult zijn, zoals u ongezuurd bent… –1 Korintiërs 5:6-7. Later zegt hij tegen de kerk: …Doe daarom die goddeloze uit uw midden weg –1 Korintiërs 5:13.

Stel dat je hoorde dat melaatsheid opnieuw een probleem was in je dorp. Deze ziekte die het vlees vernietigt, was teruggekeerd en veel mensen uit je dorp waren nu besmet. Dan zit je op zondagochtend in de kerk, gaan de deuren open en komt er een man binnen met huid en vlees die van zijn ledematen hangen. Hij is ernstig besmet, maar lijkt het zelf niet te weten. Wat zou je doen? Wat als hij naast je wilde komen zitten? Wat als hij met je kinderen wilde praten? Ik denk dat we allemaal weten wat we zouden doen; we zouden hem niet in ons midden toelaten. We houden te veel van onze mensen en onze gezinnen om dat te doen.

En hoe zit het met de zonde? Laten we de zonde toe om zich bij ons aan te sluiten? Nemen we het serieus? Wat is erger: besmet raken met een ziekte die het vlees vernietigt, of besmet raken met een zonde die de ziel vernietigt? Bedenk dat het loon van de zonde de dood is—de geestelijke dood; de eeuwige dood. Als we de zonde op dezelfde manier zouden behandelen als die ziekte (en dat zouden we moeten doen), dan zouden onze kerken opnieuw de kracht van de Heilige Geest hebben.

De Bijbel zegt: …u zult kracht ontvangen wanneer de Heilige Geest over u komt; en u zult Mijn getuigen zijn, zowel in Jeruzalem als in heel Judea en Samaria en tot aan het uiterste van de aarde –Handelingen 1:8.

We hebben al gezien hoe de zonde ons scheidt van Gods kracht, en we hebben ook gezien dat God ons kracht wil geven. Hij wil dat we de overwinning behalen op de vijand—de duivel, de wereld en het vlees. Toch lijkt er iets te gebeuren in onze kerken: we laten de zonde binnenkomen. Het is heel gewoon een prediker te horen zeggen: ‘Niemand is volmaakt.’ Of: ‘We zondigen allemaal.’ O, konden we maar beseffen welke schade zulke uitspraken kunnen aanrichten. Jezus kwam om ons te redden van ALLE zonde; van ALLE ongerechtigheid. Als we in onze zonde blijven, wat heeft Jezus dan voor ons gedaan?

Ik hoor over kerken die afglijden naar de wereld. Langzaam laten ze hun overtuigingen los en laten ze nieuwe modes en de praal van de wereld binnen. Ik hoor maar weinig over kerken die uiteenvallen vanwege grove zonde, zoals ontucht of dronkenschap. De vijand van onze ziel wil dat we lauw worden. Hij wil dat de kerk haar kracht verliest en gaat leven als ieder ander. Hier in Haïti zijn overal kerken. Op zondagochtend, vanaf vijf uur, hoor ik de kerken zingen en God aanbidden. Maar waar zijn al die mensen maandagochtend? Ze vermengen zich weer met de wereld waaruit ze afkomstig zijn.

Onlangs sprak ik met een zeer rijke Haïtiaanse man die overal in Haïti resorts en onroerend goed bezat. Ik vroeg hem of hij christen was. (Ik wilde een gesprek beginnen.) Ik kon zien dat hij ja wilde zeggen; in plaats daarvan raakte hij gefrustreerd en zei hij nee. Ik vroeg hem waarom niet. Hij zei precies wat ik dacht dat hij zou zeggen: ‘Ik heb ernaar verlangd christen te worden. Ik ben naar alle kerken hier in de buurt geweest, maar ik heb niet het gevoel dat ze me iets te bieden hebben. Ik heb geld; ik heb materiële zegeningen; maar dat lijkt alles te zijn waar ze naar streven.’

Als onze kerken vandaag de dag niets minder zouden accepteren dan de vervulling, toerusting en leiding van de Heilige Geest, een volle dosis hemelse kracht, dan zouden we de verlorenen om ons heen iets kunnen bieden dat hen aanspreekt. Ik geloof dat dit precies is waar de wereld naar op zoek is; ze zoeken iets beters, iets bovennatuurlijks. Wat als we met niets minder genoegen zouden nemen? Wat als we op onze knieën zouden blijven totdat Gods kracht terugkeerde? Wat als we opnieuw zouden huilen om onze eigen ziel en om de zielen van anderen?

Ik werkte nauw samen met een gewelddadige bendeleider die in het naburige dorp woonde. Hij was hardvochtig, maar God had hem naar mij toe geleid. Zeven lange maanden lang hadden we contact en spraken we met elkaar. Ik wilde dat hij iets van Gods kracht zou zien; ik wilde dat God hem zou redden. Hij werd vaak dronken en dreigde me te vermoorden; ik bleef hem naar de Heiland wijzen. Op een dag kwamen hij en zijn bende langs om een werkproject stil te leggen. Ze zeiden dat het land nu van hen was. Ze zwaaiden met hun geweren en bedreigden iedereen die daar was. Ik legde hem uit dat God de eigenaar van het land was. Hij zei: ‘Dat is prima; zeg tegen God dat Hij hierheen moet komen, dan snijd ik Zijn hoofd eraf.’ Die opmerking verontrustte me en ik vroeg hem of hij begreep hoe machtig de God was die hij zojuist had bedreigd. Op een middag reed ik naar zijn huis en zaten we buiten te praten. God leidde me die dag ertoe hem een krachtige boodschap te prediken: ‘Je moet met dit bendeleven stoppen. God wil je redden en je hart veranderen!’ Hij leek heel nuchter terwijl ik verderging: ‘Je weet nooit wanneer iemand hierheen komt en je vermoordt! Dat heb je niet in de hand, maar mijn vriend, je kunt wel bepalen waar je naartoe gaat nadat je dood bent!’ Daarna herinnerde ik hem aan de verschrikkelijke dingen die hij enkele dagen eerder had gezegd.

Terwijl we nog met elkaar spraken, kwamen twee mannen van een naburige bende op motorfietsen naderbij. Ze waren zwaarbewapend; ze waren precies op dat moment gekomen om hem te doden, maar toen ze mij met hem zagen praten, wachtten ze tot ik weg zou gaan. ‘Je hebt een vrouw en kinderen. Ben je dit leven niet moe? God heeft iets zo veel beters voor je!’ Ik smeekte, ik smeekte om zijn ziel. Het was zijn allerlaatste kans; de dood stond voor de deur. Toen ik vertrok, zei ik dat ik terug zou komen.

Na de schietpartij haastte ik me terug, maar het was voorbij… helemaal voorbij.

Wanneer we leven in de kracht van de opstanding, de kracht van de almachtige God, dan is het dat Hij werkt! Ik heb het gevoel dat er vóór de terugkeer van de Heer nog zoveel werk te doen is, maar Gods mensen hebben het te druk; we hebben geen tijd.

Zijn we bang om over Gods kracht en de Heilige Geest te spreken, alleen omdat de pinksterbeweging verdraaid heeft wat de Bijbel leert? God, help ons.

Wanneer we God om redding aanroepen, doen we dat omdat we weten dat we gered moeten worden; bekeerd moeten worden. We weten ook dat we onszelf niet kunnen redden, dus vragen we God om hulp. En wanneer God ons helpt, kunnen we dingen doen die we eerder niet konden! Boze mensen zijn niet langer boos. Mensen die hun lusten niet konden beheersen, hebben nu zelfbeheersing. Egoïstische mensen beginnen anderen op de eerste plaats te zetten. Verlegen mensen beginnen vrijmoedig te preken. Hebzuchtige mensen beginnen aan anderen te geven. God doet een werk dat hulpverleners en artsen niet kunnen doen: Hij verandert de kern van een mens, en dan wordt alles nieuw. Nu leven we voor iets dat veel beter is dan wat deze wereld te bieden heeft; door Gods kracht stijgen we boven alles uit en laten we deze zieke wereld door de zonde zien dat er een betere weg is!

Door de hele Bijbel heen deden Gods mensen bovennatuurlijke dingen; ze namen geen genoegen met alleen maar een prettig leven. Ze streefden naar iets groters, iets beters. Er is kracht in het bloed van Jezus, maar daarvoor was het kruis nodig. Ook wij hebben een kruis nodig om die kracht te vinden. En Hij zei tegen hen allen: Als iemand achter Mij aan wil komen, moet hij zichzelf verloochenen, dagelijks zijn kruis opnemen en Mij volgen. Want wie zijn leven wil behouden, zal het verliezen, maar wie zijn leven verliest omwille van Mij, die zal het behouden –Lukas 9:23-24. Ja, voor wie verloren gaan lijkt het dwaasheid, maar voor wie geloven is het de kracht van God.

Do you want to have a good life? What is there that you believe you need to experience or accomplish so you can truly enjoy life? Many people’s main goal in life is to seek pleasure and to have fun. Much time and money are spent to achieve this. But do we accomplish it? In our natural mind we think that the circumstances need to be just right to please us. But we all know that circumstances are never ideal all the time. So, we can’t depend on those for our happiness. We need something bigger than that. Or Someone.

Obviously, we know that God alone is never changing and always faithful. Another thing about God is that He is sovereign. In other words, He’s in charge. But we like our independence; we like things to happen in a way that feels good to us. When life doesn’t happen that way, we are brought to a decision. Will we accept all of God—both His unchangeableness and His sovereignty—or will we fight to have our own way in our pursuit of a good life?

The root of joy is with God Himself. This is because He created us for Himself. He created us to bring pleasure to Himself, but we think we need to bring pleasure to ourselves. It started in the garden of Eden when the serpent convinced Eve that pleasing herself was more important than pleasing God. Since then, humans have been at war, both within their own hearts and without, with other folks. All in the effort of trying to find pleasure for themselves, yet not finding it because they were created to please God.

The solution for this war is found in James 4. It’s simple: submit to God. Humble yourselves before Him. This is not too much for Him to ask of us, because He is sovereign. He created us, so He has the say in how we live. If we will truly find enjoyment in life, it will be by putting our own life and desires on the cross and becoming one with God and His original purpose for us. Rather than it being restrictive, this opens up a world of opportunities and possibilities. It doesn’t mean we have to do things because God wants us to. Becoming one with God means that what He wants us to do is also what we want to do.

Worship and Gratitude

When we are one with God, our whole perspective changes. Instead of pining over all the things that aren’t ideal, we begin to see the many things that are true blessings. We can have a heart of worship and gratitude for all the good things that we do experience. We are able to see how unworthy we really are. We didn’t deserve anything good, but God has still given us so many things to enjoy!

Living in the Present

As young ladies, we have a tendency to dream, to live in a future that is idealistic and pleasant. We sometimes struggle to live in the present imperfect reality and find joy in it. But when God’s will becomes our will then true joy happens, because we are fulfilling His purpose for us.

We can learn to experience joy in any circumstance, even in mundane life. We’re afraid of living a boring life. We want it to be exciting. But He wants us to please Him, and when we do, we experience joy no matter the circumstances. However, we are also then available for Him to use in service to His Kingdom, and He may call us to opportunities that are exciting. But we won’t be effective in the exciting missions unless we have learned to be submitted to His will in everyday life.

Relationships

When we are finding joy and contentment in where God has us in the present, we are able to focus on developing solid, upbuilding relationships with those who are in our lives right now. God has created us as social people, and good relationships will bring true enjoyment to us. God is also able to use us in reaching out to other people. When we are one with Him, our focus is no longer on ourselves but on others. The life of God can flow through us and both show others the way to Him and give us joy and fulfillment in doing it.

Emotions

Another tendency we have is to let our emotions control us. And they will run wild if we are looking to our circumstances to give us pleasure. We will end up on a roller coaster of feelings dictated by whatever is happening at the moment. And then we escape to the dream world, which only distorts our view of reality even more. But God is steadfast, and when we are one with Him, He imparts to us stability and rest. And we are able to experience ever present joy—even in ever changing circumstances.

Let us continue to become ever more one with Him. And He will give us heavenly sunlight all of our journey, unchanged by circumstances on earth and realized in full when we see Him face to face. …in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore –Psalm 16:11.

Voulez-vous avoir une vie heureuse ? Que pensez-vous devoir vivre ou accomplir pour vraiment profiter de la vie ? Pour beaucoup, le principal objectif dans la vie est de rechercher le plaisir et de s’amuser. On dépense beaucoup de temps et d’argent pour y parvenir. Mais y arrivons-nous ? Dans notre raisonnement naturel, nous pensons que les circonstances doivent être idéales pour nous satisfaire. Pourtant, nous savons tous que les circonstances ne sont jamais idéales en permanence. Nous ne pouvons donc pas compter sur elles pour être heureux. Il nous faut quelque chose de plus grand. Ou quelqu’un.

Évidemment, nous savons que Dieu seul ne change jamais et qu’il est toujours fidèle. Une autre caractéristique de Dieu est qu’il est souverain. Autrement dit, c’est lui qui dirige. Mais nous aimons notre indépendance ; nous aimons que les choses se passent d’une manière qui nous convient. Lorsque la vie ne se déroule pas ainsi, nous devons prendre une décision. Accepterons-nous Dieu tout entier — son immuabilité comme sa souveraineté — ou lutterons-nous pour faire comme bon nous semble dans notre quête d’une vie heureuse ?

La source de la joie se trouve en Dieu lui-même. En effet, il nous a créés pour lui. Il nous a créés pour lui faire plaisir, mais nous pensons devoir nous faire plaisir à nous-mêmes. Tout a commencé dans le jardin d’Éden, lorsque le serpent a convaincu Ève qu’il était plus important de se faire plaisir que de plaire à Dieu. Depuis lors, les êtres humains sont en guerre, à la fois au fond de leur cœur et avec les autres. Tout cela dans le but de trouver du plaisir pour eux-mêmes, sans y parvenir, car ils ont été créés pour plaire à Dieu.

La solution à cette guerre se trouve dans Jacques 4. Elle est simple : soumettez-vous à Dieu. Humiliez-vous devant lui. Ce n’est pas trop lui demander, car il est souverain. Il nous a créés ; c’est donc lui qui décide de la manière dont nous devons vivre. Si nous voulons vraiment trouver du plaisir dans la vie, il nous faudra mettre notre vie et nos désirs sur la croix, et ne faire qu’un avec Dieu et son dessein initial pour nous. Loin d’être une restriction, cela ouvre un monde d’occasions et de possibilités. Cela ne signifie pas que nous devons faire les choses simplement parce que Dieu le veut. Ne faire qu’un avec Dieu signifie que ce qu’il veut que nous fassions est aussi ce que nous voulons faire.

Adoration et gratitude

Lorsque nous ne faisons qu’un avec Dieu, notre perspective tout entière change. Au lieu de nous lamenter sur tout ce qui n’est pas idéal, nous commençons à voir les nombreuses choses qui sont de véritables bénédictions. Nous pouvons avoir un cœur rempli d’adoration et de gratitude pour toutes les bonnes choses dont nous faisons l’expérience. Nous sommes capables de voir combien nous sommes réellement indignes. Nous ne méritions rien de bon, et pourtant Dieu nous a donné tant de choses dont nous pouvons profiter !

Vivre dans le présent

En tant que jeunes femmes, nous avons tendance à rêver, à vivre dans un avenir idéaliste et agréable. Nous avons parfois du mal à vivre dans la réalité imparfaite du présent et à y trouver de la joie. Mais lorsque la volonté de Dieu devient la nôtre, la vraie joie naît, car nous accomplissons son dessein pour nous.

Nous pouvons apprendre à éprouver de la joie quelles que soient les circonstances, même dans la vie quotidienne ordinaire. Nous avons peur d’avoir une vie ennuyeuse. Nous voulons qu’elle soit passionnante. Mais Dieu veut que nous lui plaisions, et lorsque nous le faisons, nous éprouvons de la joie quelles que soient les circonstances. Nous sommes alors aussi disponibles pour le servir dans son Royaume, et il peut nous appeler à saisir des occasions passionnantes. Mais nous ne serons pas efficaces dans ces missions exaltantes si nous n’avons pas appris à nous soumettre à sa volonté dans la vie de tous les jours.

Relations

Lorsque nous trouvons joie et contentement dans la situation où Dieu nous place dans le présent, nous pouvons nous concentrer sur l’établissement de relations solides et édifiantes avec les personnes qui font partie de notre vie aujourd’hui. Dieu nous a créés pour vivre en société, et de bonnes relations nous procurent un véritable plaisir. Dieu peut aussi se servir de nous pour aller vers les autres. Lorsque nous ne faisons qu’un avec lui, nous ne sommes plus centrés sur nous-mêmes, mais sur les autres. La vie de Dieu peut couler à travers nous, nous permettant à la fois de montrer aux autres le chemin vers lui et de trouver de la joie et de l’épanouissement en le faisant.

Émotions

Nous avons aussi tendance à laisser nos émotions nous dominer. Et elles s’emballeront si nous comptons sur les circonstances pour nous procurer du plaisir. Nous finirons par vivre des montagnes russes émotionnelles, au gré de ce qui se passe sur le moment. Puis nous nous évaderons dans le monde du rêve, ce qui ne fera que déformer davantage notre vision de la réalité. Mais Dieu est inébranlable et, lorsque nous ne faisons qu’un avec lui, il nous donne stabilité et repos. Nous pouvons alors éprouver une joie toujours présente, même au milieu de circonstances qui changent sans cesse.

Continuons à ne faire toujours davantage qu’un avec lui. Et il nous donnera la lumière du soleil céleste tout au long de notre parcours, lumière que les circonstances terrestres ne peuvent altérer et dont nous jouirons pleinement lorsque nous le verrons face à face. …il y a abondance de joie en ta présence, des délices éternelles à ta droite –Psaume 16:11.

Have you ever tried to change the world? I have. As a teenager I dreamed of the daring exploits I was going to do for God. As I set the table in my parent’s house, I waited for the day when I would be able to do greater things—things like setting up house in Africa, speaking strange languages, and leading people to Jesus. The thought of living in a mud hut and dodging venomous snakes seemed thrilling.

And then, part of my dreams came true! I left all I had ever known and had an adrenaline-fueled landing in an African country. I tried to change the small world I was in—that God-forsaken village full of drunkenness, broken marriages, fights, and neglected children. Daily I felt the angst of being so busy with “insignificant,” earthly tasks and wondered how to make a difference. Then suddenly, our labors were abruptly ended by burn-out and a host of government suspicions. None of this was in my dreams.

I still ask the same question, “God, how can I make a difference?” The neighbor calls at the door. The laundry lady needs her pay. Lunch needs to be on the table in 15 minutes. Our fifth grader needs help with multiplying fractions. The sky fills up with dark clouds and the clothesline is full of laundry. I wipe the baby’s nose for the umpteenth time as she sits on top of the table disrupting her brother’s books and papers. I bake bread, make yogurt, and churn butter, and cook 21 meals a week. I fold mountains of laundry and the next week I do it all over again. I sweep the floor that has accumulated an astonishing amount of dirt in only two hours. In many ways, life is more mundane than it ever was before.

I had no ability to change the world as a starry-eyed teen and neither do I have the ability now. God isn’t asking that of me. He only asks me to walk with Him and obey His voice. Slowly I am learning that the spiritual and physical are inseparable—even Jesus taught the gospel of the kingdom while resting, sleeping, and eating. Scrubbing a floor and slicing bread can be acts of worship to my Creator if I will deem them so. It is He who designed that my spiritual walk and the propagation thereof happens as my hands touch the earthly. This is how my spirit is refined. It’s the only way I can express my faith as a living faith. It’s the only way I can touch the hearts of my children and live out a practical gospel for them to imitate. It’s how my faith proves itself to be real to the unbeliever, as they see me struggle through the same things they do, along with my resulting responses.

Slowly I am learning that serving God isn’t about determination or changing the world. It’s about allowing God’s spirit to inhabit me, guide me, and speak to me. I am learning that God is more interested in the person I am becoming instead of everything I want to do for Him. Perhaps I am after all just a smoking flax instead of the one who will change the world. I think Paul could relate to that feeling when he wrote, But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence –1 Corinthians 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot said, “Sometimes the light rises excruciatingly slowly. The Kingdom of God is like leaven and seed, things which work silently, secretly, slowly, but there is in them an incalculable transforming power. Even in the plain soil, even in the dull dough, lies the possibility of transformation.”1

To have my heart set on accomplishments and success is a selfish way to live. When that village and those people were taken from us in a whirl of government issues and misunderstandings, I felt like God couldn’t possibly use this for anyone’s good. He still needed us there, right? The fact is, He didn’t need us there anymore. We were not indispensable. Perhaps God allowed it all in order to learn that His acceptance of me is not based on my accomplishments.

For who hath despised the day of small things… –Zechariah 4:10.

Who am I to judge if a certain work is small or not? Am I restless with my duties, believing God would be more pleased with my perception of ‘great’ duties, seemingly always out of reach? Am I forgetting that serving Christ is not about me and my sense of fulfillment, it is about God and the work He wants to do through me?! Amy Carmichael said, “It is not the place where we are, or the work that we do or cannot do that matters, it is something else. It is the fire within that burns and shines, whatever be our circumstances.”2

The fire that burns and shines within is our secret. That fire can burn while we scrub floors, cook endless meals, and home-school our children. It will touch the laundry lady, the house helper, the struggling girl at church and the neighbors. Sometimes it will happen sub-consciously, sometimes it happens if we decide to reach out instead of taking a nap or something else enjoyable, but always it takes forgetting ourselves, loving others, and noticing the small opportunities.

But beware… we cannot confuse our resignation to the smallness in our lives, with lethargy. Too many Christians do not expect God to use them, so they settle into a lethargic spiritual position. We should expect God to work in amazing ways. God might use us to accomplish those things, but it often happens in ways we least think of or expect.

The widow of Zarephath agreed to give her last handful of flour and the last remaining drops of oil to a stranger. She could have opposed the prophet and demanded he leave immediately, as after all, she was responsible for her son and that little bit of flour was all she had to give him. But no, she chose to give it all. God blessed her willing obedience by miraculously replenishing her flour and oil as long as she needed it.3

God kept culling Gideon’s army until he eventually fought and won the battle with just a few hundred men. Normally, Gideon was accustomed to armies of thousands. and now God was asking him to fight a momentous battle with only a few hundred. In the end, this human impossibility became an opportunity for God to show his power.4

At the beginning of His ministry, Jesus chose only twelve men to disciple, instead of the crowds. In the end, His small band of men deserted Him. He was mocked and killed. To everyone looking on, the remains of Jesus’ work seemed to have died with Him, yet the cosmic plan of redemption was being put into effect—those simple fishermen turned the world upside down with the gospel.5

We see from these examples that God is not looking for the biggest, the strongest, or the best. He doesn’t only use people with specialized skills or impressive gifts. Our strength and resources are often like the few hundred soldiers in Gideon’s army—simply not enough for the need. But when we give what we have with a willing heart, God multiplies our small efforts into a showcase of His grace—a showcase meant for Him, often not visible to others. The simple act of setting a table is an act of faith, of giving, of service, no matter where we are. God has chosen these weak things to be significant in His kingdom.

The secret to a successful life is Jesus in us, not our preconceived ideas of success. With Him working in and through us, His power will burn in our homes and neighborhoods. When He is the reason that we are living, we can trust Him with the outcome. Listening to the voice of Jesus, we can make a difference—one person, one encounter, one small thing at a time.

  1. Elisabeth Elliot, The Savage My Kinsman (revised edition Servant Publications 1981) epilogue pg 147
  2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, pg 218
  3. 1 Kings 17: 11-16
  4. Judges 7
  5. Luke 6:13-16, John 19

Você já tentou mudar o mundo? Eu já. Na adolescência, sonhava com as façanhas ousadas que faria por Deus. Enquanto arrumava a mesa na casa dos meus pais, esperava pelo dia em que poderia realizar coisas maiores — coisas como estabelecer-me na África, falar línguas estranhas e conduzir pessoas a Jesus. A ideia de viver numa cabana de barro e desviar-me de cobras venenosas parecia emocionante.

E então, parte dos meus sonhos se tornou realidade! Deixei para trás tudo o que conhecia e cheguei a um país africano tomada pela adrenalina. Tentei mudar o pequeno mundo em que estava — aquele vilarejo esquecido por Deus, cheio de embriaguez, casamentos desfeitos, brigas e crianças negligenciadas. Todos os dias sentia a angústia de estar tão ocupada com tarefas terrenas “insignificantes” e me perguntava como poderia fazer a diferença. Então, de repente, nosso trabalho foi interrompido abruptamente pelo esgotamento e por uma série de suspeitas do governo. Nada disso fazia parte dos meus sonhos.

Ainda faço a mesma pergunta: “Deus, como posso fazer a diferença?” A vizinha bate à porta. A mulher que lava a roupa precisa receber. O almoço precisa estar na mesa em 15 minutos. Nosso filho do quinto ano precisa de ajuda para multiplicar frações. O céu se enche de nuvens escuras, e o varal está cheio de roupa. Limpo o nariz do bebê pela enésima vez enquanto ela se senta em cima da mesa, espalhando os livros e papéis do irmão. Faço pão, preparo iogurte, bato manteiga e cozinho 21 refeições por semana. Dobro montanhas de roupa, e na semana seguinte faço tudo de novo. Varro o chão, que acumulou uma quantidade espantosa de sujeira em apenas duas horas. Em muitos aspectos, a vida é mais rotineira do que jamais foi.

Eu não tinha capacidade para mudar o mundo quando era uma adolescente sonhadora, e tampouco tenho essa capacidade agora. Deus não me pede isso. Ele só me pede que caminhe com Ele e obedeça à sua voz. Aos poucos, estou aprendendo que o espiritual e o físico são inseparáveis — até Jesus ensinava o evangelho do Reino enquanto descansava, dormia e comia. Esfregar o chão e cortar pão podem ser atos de adoração ao meu Criador, se eu assim os considerar. Foi Ele quem planejou que minha caminhada espiritual e sua propagação acontecessem quando minhas mãos tocam o que é terreno. É assim que meu espírito é aperfeiçoado. É a única maneira de eu expressar minha fé como uma fé viva. É a única maneira de tocar o coração dos meus filhos e viver diante deles um evangelho prático que possam imitar. É assim que minha fé se mostra real aos que não creem, quando me veem enfrentar as mesmas coisas que eles enfrentam e observam minhas reações a elas.

Aos poucos, estou aprendendo que servir a Deus não tem a ver com determinação nem com mudar o mundo. Tem a ver com permitir que o Espírito de Deus habite em mim, me guie e fale comigo. Estou aprendendo que Deus se interessa mais pela pessoa que estou me tornando do que por tudo o que quero fazer por Ele. Talvez, afinal, eu seja apenas um pavio fumegante, em vez de alguém que mudará o mundo. Acho que Paulo poderia compreender esse sentimento quando escreveu: Mas Deus escolheu as coisas loucas do mundo para envergonhar as sábias; e Deus escolheu as coisas fracas do mundo para envergonhar as fortes; e Deus escolheu as coisas humildes do mundo, e as desprezadas, e aquelas que não são, para reduzir a nada as que são, a fim de que ninguém se glorie na presença dele –1 Coríntios 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot disse: “Às vezes, a luz surge com uma lentidão excruciante. O Reino de Deus é como o fermento e a semente, coisas que agem em silêncio, secretamente, devagar, mas que contêm um poder transformador incalculável. Até no solo simples, até na massa sem graça, existe a possibilidade de transformação.”1

Viver com o coração voltado para realizações e sucesso é uma maneira egoísta de viver. Quando aquele vilarejo e aquelas pessoas nos foram tirados em meio a uma onda de problemas e mal-entendidos com o governo, senti que Deus não poderia, de modo algum, usar aquilo para o bem de alguém. Ele ainda precisava de nós lá, não é? A verdade é que Ele já não precisava de nós lá. Não éramos indispensáveis. Talvez Deus tenha permitido tudo aquilo para que eu aprendesse que a aceitação dele não se baseia nas minhas realizações.

Pois quem despreza o dia das coisas pequenas… –Zacarias 4:10.

Quem sou eu para julgar se determinada obra é pequena ou não? Fico inquieta com minhas responsabilidades, acreditando que Deus se agradaria mais da minha ideia de responsabilidades “grandiosas”, que parecem estar sempre fora do meu alcance? Estou me esquecendo de que servir a Cristo não diz respeito a mim e à minha sensação de realização; diz respeito a Deus e à obra que Ele quer realizar por meu intermédio?! Amy Carmichael disse: “Não importa o lugar onde estamos, nem o trabalho que fazemos ou não podemos fazer; importa outra coisa. É o fogo interior que arde e brilha, sejam quais forem as nossas circunstâncias.”2

O fogo que arde e brilha dentro de nós é o nosso segredo. Esse fogo pode arder enquanto esfregamos o chão, preparamos refeições sem fim e ensinamos nossos filhos em casa. Ele tocará a mulher que lava a roupa, a ajudante doméstica, a jovem que enfrenta dificuldades na igreja e os vizinhos. Às vezes isso acontecerá sem que percebamos; outras vezes, acontecerá se decidirmos estender a mão em vez de tirar uma soneca ou fazer outra coisa agradável. Mas sempre exige que nos esqueçamos de nós mesmos, amemos os outros e percebamos as pequenas oportunidades.

Mas cuidado… não podemos confundir a aceitação da pequenez em nossa vida com a apatia. Muitos cristãos não esperam que Deus os use e, por isso, acomodam-se numa posição de apatia espiritual. Devemos esperar que Deus opere de maneiras extraordinárias. Deus pode nos usar para realizar essas coisas, mas isso muitas vezes acontece de maneiras que menos imaginamos ou esperamos.

A viúva de Sarepta concordou em dar seu último punhado de farinha e as últimas gotas de azeite que lhe restavam a um desconhecido. Ela poderia ter se oposto ao profeta e exigido que ele fosse embora imediatamente, pois, afinal, era responsável por seu filho, e aquele pouquinho de farinha era tudo o que tinha para lhe dar. Mas não: ela escolheu dar tudo. Deus abençoou sua obediência voluntária, repondo milagrosamente a farinha e o azeite enquanto ela precisou deles.3

Deus foi reduzindo o exército de Gideão até que, por fim, ele lutou e venceu a batalha com apenas algumas centenas de homens. Normalmente, Gideão estava acostumado a exércitos de milhares; agora, porém, Deus lhe pedia que travasse uma batalha monumental com apenas algumas centenas. No fim, essa impossibilidade humana tornou-se uma oportunidade para Deus mostrar seu poder.4

No início de seu ministério, Jesus escolheu apenas doze homens para discipular, em vez de escolher as multidões. No fim, aquele pequeno grupo de homens o abandonou. Ele foi escarnecido e morto. Para todos os que observavam, parecia que o que restava da obra de Jesus havia morrido com Ele; no entanto, o plano cósmico da redenção estava sendo posto em ação — aqueles simples pescadores viraram o mundo de cabeça para baixo com o evangelho.5

Vemos por esses exemplos que Deus não está à procura dos maiores, dos mais fortes ou dos melhores. Ele não usa somente pessoas com habilidades especializadas ou dons impressionantes. Nossa força e nossos recursos muitas vezes se parecem com os poucos soldados do exército de Gideão — simplesmente não são suficientes para a necessidade. Mas, quando oferecemos o que temos com disposição, Deus multiplica nossos pequenos esforços e os transforma numa demonstração da sua graça — uma demonstração destinada a Ele, muitas vezes invisível aos outros. O simples ato de arrumar a mesa é um ato de fé, de generosidade e de serviço, onde quer que estejamos. Deus escolheu essas coisas fracas para que fossem significativas em seu Reino.

O segredo de uma vida bem-sucedida é Jesus em nós, não nossas ideias preconcebidas de sucesso. Com Ele operando em nós e por nosso intermédio, seu poder arderá em nossos lares e bairros. Quando Ele é a razão pela qual vivemos, podemos confiar a Ele o resultado. Ao ouvir a voz de Jesus, podemos fazer a diferença — uma pessoa, um encontro, uma pequena coisa de cada vez.

  2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, p. 218
  3. 1 Reis 17: 11-16
  4. Juízes 7
  5. Lucas 6:13-16, João 19

Thou hast the dew of thy youth. Psalm 110:3

There are many aspects of youth which are not virtuous. Many youth of our day experience an early season of callused carelessness and casualty. Often decisions that are made in youthful years set the foundation for the rest of their lives. It was a the younger prodigal brother that asked for an early draw on his inheritance then went and wasted it on riotous living. It was a young Dinah who wandered from her father’s house and …went out to see the daughters of the land –Genesis 34:1. There, she was exposed to the heathen young men of the land and occasioned a bloody massacre, leaving Jacob as a stench in the land. Many foolish young people have sown to the wind and reaped the havoc thereof. Those that are void of solid principles and parental authority are at high risk for spiritual shipwreck.

There are particular lusts that inflict youth more so than the aged, and the young are exhorted to flee them. (–see 2 Timothy 2:22) Solomon looked through his window casement, And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding -Proverbs 7:6-7. The young man was in heartfelt pursuit of that which appeared lovely… [Un]Till a dart [struck] through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life –Proverbs 7:23. We could examine the vices from the youthful lives of Rehoboam, Amnon, Nadab and Abihu, and countless others. We also find no lack of modern, folly-filled examples about us fulfilled by frivolous youth.

But youth are not meant to be despised. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity –1 Timothy 4:12. In fact, God generally chooses the youth as the instruments of His propagation. Joseph, of sterling character, was sent by God into Egypt at the age of 17 to preserve life (–see Genesis 45:5). Miriam, at the age of twelve, stood post over the future deliverer of the entire Jewish nation and secured her own mother, Jochebed, to be the nurse of the baby Moses. David, as a youth, was sent to encourage his brethren in the army. He was despised by his brothers: …I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart… –1 Samuel 17:28. He was rejected by Saul: …Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth… –1 Samuel 17:33. He was scorned by Goliath: …Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves… –1 Samuel 17:43. But their contempt was all for naught when he was chosen by God to be king over all Israel.

These noble youthful ambitions were followed by Josiah, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Mary, and the disciples of the Lord, all who chose to remember their Creator in the days of their youth. But these were not naive specimens seeking to secure their place in life, they were graphic examples of youth who were seeking to imitate the image of their Lord.

We need not gaze long into the character of Christ before we find…

...Thou hast the dew of thy youth

Psalm 110 is perhaps the most referred-to scripture in the Old Testament. This rhetorical portrait of the Messiah reveals a vivid virtue for us to behold. Christ, as the Ancient of days, was described in the Revelation having His head and His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet, here He is depicted as eternally young, as He sits at the right hand of God (–see Psalm 110:1). No weariness of age can enter there, for Christ is the Morning Star. It is perpetual morning around the throne of God. Those saints who are following hard after His likeness will also reflect this virtue, for the light of Jesus is the light of youth.

The psalmist, describing the Messiah, draws from the natural beauty of the morning dew (–see Psalm 110:3). The thought of dew calls us back from the heavens and unveils before us a portrait of this earth on which we dwell. In heaven there is no night, no change of heat and cold, no need of the sun to light up the day and consequently… no dew. The nature of dew belongs to the terrestrial, where everyone who will but stoop to observe it will behold a uniformed regiment of grass sparkling as if embedded with a myriad of diamonds. After a long night of darkness, the dewdrops, like tears, stand in the eyes of the flowers as they weep for joy at the advent of the first morning sunbeam. Those who walk through the lowly vegetation will have their feet washed by a thousand caressing hands of God’s design. Christ is not depicted as the dew of the morning but as the dew of youth, and the imagery is stretched further.

Youth is the season of abounding energy. Some cannot sit still. They are generally interpersonal creatures who love social activity. This is neither a virtue nor a vice. Rather, it is nominal nature. There is a progressive strain in advancing years that tames and tempers the soul. As life progresses, there is a clearer vision and a steadier thought, and we rise to better things. But when the mid-life summit has been crossed and the feet are traveling downward on the slope, that tumultuous rush of bodily energy that plowed through anything becomes enshrined with memories of the past. It is the closest comfort many can find to the bygone days of their strength.

But Christ has not called us to foster a fondness for the past nor a wistful longing for the “DO” of our youth. So many today sadly lament that their ‘get-up-and-go’ has got up and went. These have no vision for higher things and are more energized by a can of Mountain Dew than the Dew of Youth. They are more inspired by a trip down memory lane and reminiscing events of the past than of the hope that lies before them.

Age is no hindrance to securing the dew of youth. The Ancient of Days still rides forth among the golden candlesticks. While John beheld His hairs ... white like wool, as white as snow… –Revelation 1:14, yet Solomon declares …his locks are bushy, and black as a raven –Song of Solomon 5:11. While age may steal our strength and hearing, …the LORD’S hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: –Isaiah 59:1. He has secured the dew of youth and invites us to partake. The problem is not found in our deteriorating body but in a spiritually declining mind. The bane of old age predominately sets in when the mind follows the body.

It is not that life grows poorer as it advances or ceases to be noble when the charm of youth has faded. If we were placed here only to experience joy, the dying out of youthful romance would be terrible. God had a much greater end in view for His children than to just be vibrant ‘doers’. We are sent here to learn. Our allotted years upon earth are all meant to be a schooling, and it is not in the bright romance of youth that we learn the best and most abiding lessons. It is in the dogged doing of our duty, the quiet acceptance of our limitations, the patient carrying of our daily burden, and in the stretching out of a helping hand to our brother. These afford us the true opportunities for Christian culture and are the roots of ethical nobility. Christ labored …not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life… –John 6:27, and He finished His earthly task in 33 years. But the dew of youth did not dissipate as He sat down at the right hand of His Father.

Thus, we conclude that this youthfulness will not be secured by strength, but by…

...Hope

But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God; From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool. –Hebrews 10:12-13.

How shall we picture this Christ now? Reclining in an easy chair, all worn out from His experience with the stubborn people of this earth? Is He busy putting together a scrap book of precious memories? This is too often the position of the aged and so their mind dies with their bodies.

And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope –Romans 5:3-4. At times, we wonder if this scripture can be true. Anyone with any age on their bones can testify to a poor experience and the subsequent feelings of hopelessness following. As people, we have all faced disappointing experiences with a spouse, a child, or a church relationship after which a nagging cloud of despair settles in. Outside of Christ, a sour experience always tends to pessimism. It was so in the world when Jesus came. It is still so today.

But the dew of youth is incurably hopeful. There is an effervescent expectation that is naturally and magnificently borne in youth and retained in Christ. In every winter, when the fields are bleak, and the cold gust goes whistling through the trees, there lies the hope that the flowers will spring again. In every spring there is the hope of summer. In every summer there is the hope of harvest. It is alive in nature and alive in youth. Those who are blind to it shall reap, at best, a dreary monotone existence. To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all. –Oscar Wilde.

The rest shall be brightly effected with a hope that…

…Heals Our Infirmities

Our bodies are destined for the grave and have no hope for renewal in this life. It is our minds that carry our greatest infirmities. The impotent man of 38 years at Bethesda could only utter a hopeless complaint when Christ asked him, …Wilt thou be made whole? –John 5:6. Upon the wake of his new day, a new remedy was given to him—… Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee –John 5:14. What could be worse than being a cripple for years? A mind that is beset by a doleful indulgence in the sorrows of this world. Age sets in when we have more memories of the past than hope for tomorrow. It is disappointing when folks grow old and have no vision for tomorrow, but it is a disaster to behold youth that are plagued by its crippling effects. Many grope aimlessly through life’s various trials, stupefied by the lack of blessedness. The noonday sun has evaporated the dew of their youth and the only praise that they can muster is culminated from a handful of yesterday’s pleasantries. A new attitude must be birthed by the dew of a new morning.

…Humbles Our Pursuits

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. –John 21:18. When we are young, we can overcome in the strength of our youth. As age takes its course, we will find a different alternative: victory through surrender.

…I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one. –1 John 2:14. The world entices us to selfish living. Youth are often subject to schools of learning that teach them to “be all that you can be”. There is a major focus on self-enhancement and preparation for the future. This may prepare them in a ‘survival of the fittest’ world but will leave them destitute when the strength and prowess of youth has departed.

For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world. And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever. –1 John 2:16-17. Overcoming evil with good is the Biblical antidote for channeling youthful energies. Whether it is the lust within or the longing without, hope is conceived by planting a seed of kindness in the life of another. The pursuit of pleasure and lieu of leisure will always disappoint its recipient and leave him in a valley of despair deeper than when he began. It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth … He putteth his mouth in the dust; if so be there may be hope. –Lamentations 3:27-29. We are created to work in God’s vineyard and those who have an appetite for it will reap in hope of its youthful reward.

…Hallows Our Trials

For we are saved by hope: but hope that is seen is not hope... –Romans 8:24. How often we can relate to Job in his pain. But before his pain had received an ounce of retribution, the healing streams began to flow as Job reverenced his Creator. When we can acknowledge that God is perfect in all the trials He allows, we then learn to worship in the temple not made with hands and disregard the frailties of the body. To sit down at the feet of Christ ignites a youthful spark that radiates the spirit within and conceives hope. The dew of youth then becomes our portion as Christ imparts eternal life and eternal youth to us. From the hour of the grave and through eternity we shall be young and bid defiance to weariness and death if we are living in the morning light of Jesus Christ. Heaven is a place of perpetual youth, and just like the light of the sun is reflected on the moon, so likewise the light of Christ is reflected on His bride. She is clean and young, …a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing… –Ephesians 5:27. Blessed is the venerable saint who arrives at the portals of heaven in such a condition.

لك ندى شبابك. مزمور 110:3

ثمة جوانب كثيرة من الشباب لا تتسم بالفضيلة. فكثير من شباب أيامنا يمرون في مطلع حياتهم بمرحلة من اللامبالاة المتصلبة والتهور. وغالبًا ما ترسي القرارات التي تُتخذ في سنوات الشباب أساسًا لبقية الحياة. وكان الأخ الأصغر، الابن الضال، هو من طلب أن ينال مبكرًا نصيبه من الميراث، ثم مضى فبدده في عيش مسرف. وكانت دينة شابة حين خرجت من بيت أبيها، «لتنظر بنات الأرض» – التكوين 34:1. وهناك تعرضت لشبان الأرض الوثنيين، وتسببت في مذبحة دامية، حتى صار يعقوب نتنًا في الأرض. لقد زرع كثير من الشبان الحمقى للريح، فحصدوا خرابها. والذين يفتقرون إلى المبادئ الراسخة وسلطة الوالدين معرضون بشدة للغرق الروحي.

هناك شهوات بعينها تصيب الشباب أكثر مما تصيب المسنين، ولذلك يُحث الشبان على الهرب منها. (انظر 2 تيموثاوس 2:22) نظر سليمان من كوة نافذته، «فرأيت بين الجهال، ولاحظت بين الفتيان، غلامًا عديم الفهم» – الأمثال 7:6-7. كان الشاب يسعى من كل قلبه وراء ما بدا جميلًا… «حتى اخترق سهم كبده؛ وكما يسرع الطائر إلى الفخ، ولا يعلم أنه لنفسه» – الأمثال 7:23. يمكننا أن نتأمل الرذائل في حياة رحبعام وأمنون وناداب وأبيهو، وغيرهم كثيرين. كما أننا لا نفتقر إلى أمثلة معاصرة كثيرة على الحماقة، يحققها شباب طائشون من حولنا.

لكن ليس المقصود أن يُحتقر الشباب. «لا يستهن أحد بحداثتك، بل كن قدوة للمؤمنين في الكلام، في التصرف، في المحبة، في الروح، في الإيمان، في الطهارة» – 1 تيموثاوس 4:12. بل إن الله يختار الشباب عمومًا ليكونوا أدوات لنشر رسالته. أرسل الله يوسف، ذا الخلق الرفيع، إلى مصر في سن السابعة عشرة ليحفظ الحياة (انظر التكوين 45:5). ووقفت مريم، وهي في الثانية عشرة من عمرها، حارسةً لمخلّص الأمة اليهودية كلها في المستقبل، وضمنت لأمها يوكابد أن تكون مرضعة الطفل موسى. وأُرسل داود، وهو فتى، ليشجع إخوته في الجيش. فاحتقره إخوته: «أنا عارف كبرياءك وشر قلبك…» – 1 صموئيل 17:28. ورفضه شاول: «لا تستطيع أن تذهب إلى هذا الفلسطيني لتحاربه، لأنك غلام…» – 1 صموئيل 17:33. وسخر منه جليات: «ألعلي كلب حتى إنك تأتي إلي بعصي؟…» – 1 صموئيل 17:43. لكن احتقارهم كله ذهب سدى حين اختاره الله ملكًا على إسرائيل كلها.

وتبع هذه الطموحات النبيلة لدى الشباب يوشيا وإشعياء وإرميا ودانيال ومريم وتلاميذ الرب؛ فقد اختاروا جميعًا أن يذكروا خالقهم في أيام شبابهم. لكنهم لم يكونوا نماذج ساذجة تسعى إلى تأمين مكانتها في الحياة، بل كانوا أمثلة جلية لشباب سعوا إلى التشبه بصورة ربهم.

ولا نحتاج إلى التعمق طويلًا في شخصية المسيح حتى نجد…

...لك ندى شبابك

ربما يكون المزمور 110 أكثر نصوص العهد القديم استشهادًا. وهذه الصورة البلاغية للمسيح تكشف فضيلة ساطعة نتأملها. فقد وُصف المسيح، باعتباره قديم الأيام، في سفر الرؤيا بأن «رأسه وشعره أبيضان كالصوف الأبيض كالثلج…» – رؤيا 1:14، ومع ذلك يُصوَّر هنا شابًا إلى الأبد، وهو جالس عن يمين الله (انظر مزمور 110:1). فلا يصل إلى هناك أي تعب من جراء التقدم في السن، لأن المسيح هو كوكب الصبح. فالصباح دائم حول عرش الله. والقديسون الذين يتبعون صورته بكل اجتهاد سيعكسون هم أيضًا هذه الفضيلة، لأن نور يسوع هو نور الشباب.

ويستلهم صاحب المزمور، وهو يصف المسيح، من جمال ندى الصباح الطبيعي (انظر مزمور 110:3). وفكرة الندى تعيدنا من السماوات وتكشف أمامنا صورة لهذه الأرض التي نسكنها. ففي السماء لا ليل، ولا تغير في الحرارة والبرودة، ولا حاجة إلى الشمس لتضيء النهار، وبالتالي… لا ندى. فالندى من طبيعة الأرض، حيث كل من ينحني ليتأمله يرى صفوفًا متراصة من العشب تتلألأ كأنها مرصعة بعدد لا يُحصى من الألماس. وبعد ليل طويل من الظلام، تقف قطرات الندى، كالدموع، في عيون الأزهار وهي تبكي فرحًا بمجيء أول شعاع من شمس الصباح. والذين يمشون بين النباتات الواطئة تغسل أقدامهم ألف يد حانية من صنع الله. لا يُصوَّر المسيح على أنه ندى الصباح، بل ندى الشباب، وتمضي الصورة أبعد من ذلك.

الشباب موسم وفرة الطاقة. فبعضهم لا يستطيع الجلوس ساكنًا. وهم عمومًا اجتماعيون يحبون النشاط مع الآخرين. وهذا ليس فضيلة ولا رذيلة، بل هو طبيعة عادية. ومع التقدم في العمر يبدأ مسار تدريجي يروّض النفس ويهذبها. ومع تقدم الحياة تتضح الرؤية ويزداد الفكر ثباتًا، ونرتقي إلى أمور أفضل. لكن حين نعبر قمة منتصف العمر وتبدأ أقدامنا في الهبوط على المنحدر، يصبح ذلك الاندفاع الصاخب للطاقة الجسدية، الذي كان يشق طريقه عبر كل شيء، حبيس ذكريات الماضي. وهذا أقرب عزاء يجده كثيرون لأيام قوتهم الغابرة.

لكن المسيح لم يدعنا إلى تنمية الحنين إلى الماضي، ولا إلى التوق الحزين إلى «الاندفاع» الذي عرفناه في شبابنا. فكثيرون اليوم يأسفون لأن «حيويتهم قد خمدت ورحلت». ليس لهؤلاء تطلع إلى أمور أسمى، وهم يستمدون طاقة أكبر من علبة مشروب ماونتن ديو الغازي من ندى الشباب. ويستوحون من جولة في أروقة الذكريات واستعادة أحداث الماضي أكثر مما يستوحون من الرجاء الذي أمامهم.

السن لا يحول دون نيل ندى الشباب. فما زال قديم الأيام يجول بين المنائر الذهبية. وبينما رأى يوحنا «رأسه وشعره أبيضان كالصوف الأبيض كالثلج…» – رؤيا 1:14، يعلن سليمان: «…خصلاته مسترسلة، سوداء كالغراب» – نشيد الأنشاد 5:11. قد يسلبنا العمر قوتنا وسمعنا، لكن «يد الرب لم تقصر عن أن تخلّص، ولم تثقل أذنه عن أن تسمع» – إشعياء 59:1. لقد هيأ لنا ندى الشباب ويدعونا إلى أن ننال منه. فالمشكلة ليست في أجسادنا المتدهورة، بل في عقل يتراجع روحيًا. وغالبًا ما يبدأ بلاء الشيخوخة حين يتبع العقل الجسد في تدهوره.

ليس معنى ذلك أن الحياة تزداد فقرًا كلما تقدمت، أو أنها تفقد نبلها حين يخبو سحر الشباب. لو كنا هنا لمجرد اختبار الفرح، لكان انطفاء غرام الشباب أمرًا فظيعًا. لكن لله غاية أسمى بكثير لأبنائه من أن يكونوا مجرد «فاعلين» مفعمين بالحيوية. لقد أُرسلنا إلى هنا لنتعلم. فجميع سنواتنا المخصصة لنا على الأرض مقصود بها أن تكون مدرسة، ولسنا نتعلم أفضل الدروس وأبقاها في غرام الشباب المتألق. بل نتعلمها في المثابرة على أداء واجبنا، وقبول حدودنا بهدوء، وحمل أعبائنا اليومية بصبر، ومد يد العون إلى أخينا. وهذه تتيح لنا فرصًا حقيقية للنمو المسيحي، وهي جذور النبل الأخلاقي. عمل المسيح «لا للطعام البائد، بل للطعام الباقي للحياة الأبدية…» – يوحنا 6:27، وأنهى مهمته الأرضية في ثلاثة وثلاثين عامًا. لكن ندى الشباب لم يتبدد حين جلس عن يمين أبيه.

وهكذا نستنتج أن هذا الشباب لا يُنال بالقوة، بل بـ…

...الرجاء

«وأما هذا فبعدما قدم عن الخطايا ذبيحة واحدة إلى الأبد، جلس في يمين الله، منتظرًا بعد ذلك حتى توضع أعداؤه موطئًا لقدميه» – عبرانيين 10:12-13.

كيف نتصور المسيح الآن؟ هل يستلقي على كرسي مريح، وقد أنهكته خبرته مع شعب هذه الأرض العنيد؟ هل يشغل نفسه بإعداد سجل قصاصات للذكريات الثمينة؟ كثيرًا ما تكون هذه حال المسنين، ولذلك يموت عقلهم مع أجسادهم.

«وليس ذلك فقط، بل نفتخر أيضًا في الضيقات، عالمين أن الضيق ينشئ صبرًا، والصبر تزكية، والتزكية رجاء» – رومية 5:3-4. أحيانًا نتساءل إن كان هذا النص صحيحًا. فكل من تقدم به العمر يستطيع أن يشهد بتجربة سيئة، وبما أعقبها من مشاعر اليأس. وقد اختبرنا جميعًا، نحن البشر، خيبات في علاقتنا بزوج أو طفل أو كنيسة، أعقبها استقرار غيمة مزعجة من القنوط. وخارج المسيح، تميل التجربة المريرة دائمًا إلى التشاؤم. هكذا كان العالم حين جاء يسوع، وما زال كذلك اليوم.

لكن ندى الشباب لا ينفك عن الرجاء. فهناك توقع متألق يولد طبيعيًا وبروعة في الشباب، ويظل قائمًا في المسيح. في كل شتاء، حين تبدو الحقول كئيبة وتهب الرياح الباردة صفيرًا بين الأشجار، يبقى الرجاء بأن الأزهار ستتفتح من جديد. وفي كل ربيع رجاء بالصيف. وفي كل صيف رجاء بالحصاد. إنه حي في الطبيعة وحي في الشباب. والذين يعمون عنه لن يحصدوا، في أحسن الأحوال، سوى حياة رتيبة كئيبة. «أن تحيا هو أندر شيء في العالم. فمعظم الناس موجودون فحسب، وهذا كل شيء» – أوسكار وايلد.

أما الباقون فسيكونون مشرقين برجاء…

…يشفي عاهاتنا

أجسادنا مصيرها القبر، ولا رجاء لها بالتجدد في هذه الحياة. أما أكبر عاهاتنا فتحملها عقولنا. ولم يستطع الرجل العاجز منذ ثمانية وثلاثين عامًا عند بيت حسدا إلا أن يطلق شكوى يائسة حين سأله المسيح: «أتريد أن تبرأ؟» – يوحنا 5:6. ومع إشراقة يومه الجديد، أُعطي علاجًا جديدًا: «ها أنت قد برئت، فلا تخطئ أيضًا، لئلا يكون لك أشر» – يوحنا 5:14. ما الذي يمكن أن يكون أسوأ من أن يكون المرء مقعدًا لسنوات؟ عقلٌ تستولي عليه الاستطابة الكئيبة لأحزان هذا العالم. ويبدأ التقدم في السن حين تكون لدينا ذكريات عن الماضي أكثر من الرجاء في الغد. من المحبط أن يكبر الناس من دون تطلع إلى الغد، لكن من المفزع أن نرى الشباب يعانون آثارًا تشلهم. فكثيرون يتلمسون طريقهم بلا هدف وسط محن الحياة المختلفة، وقد خدرهم افتقارهم إلى البركة. لقد بخرت شمس الظهيرة ندى شبابهم، ولم يعد مدحهم الممكن إلا خلاصة حفنة من مباهج الأمس. لا بد أن يولد موقف جديد من ندى صباح جديد.

…يخضع مساعينا

«الحق الحق أقول لك: لما كنت أكثر حداثة كنت تمنطق ذاتك وتمشي حيث تشاء، ولكن متى شخت فإنك تمد يديك وآخر يمنطقك ويحملك حيث لا تشاء» – يوحنا 21:18. حين نكون شبابًا، نستطيع أن ننتصر بقوة شبابنا. أما مع تقدم العمر، فسنجد سبيلًا مختلفًا: الانتصار بالتسليم.

«قد كتبت إليكم أيها الأحداث لأنكم أقوياء، وكلمة الله ثابتة فيكم، وقد غلبتم الشرير» – 1 يوحنا 2:14. يغري العالمُنا بالعيش لأنفسنا. وكثيرًا ما يتعرض الشباب لتعليم في المدارس يحثهم على أن «يكونوا كل ما يستطيعون أن يكونوه». وينصب التركيز كثيرًا على تطوير الذات والاستعداد للمستقبل. وقد يهيئهم ذلك لعالم تحكمه قاعدة «البقاء للأقوى»، لكنه سيتركهم معدمين حين ترحل عنهم قوة الشباب وبأسه.

«لأن كل ما في العالم: شهوة الجسد، وشهوة العيون، وتعظم المعيشة، ليس من الآب بل من العالم. والعالم يمضي وشهوته، وأما الذي يصنع مشيئة الله فيثبت إلى الأبد» – 1 يوحنا 2:16-17. إن غلبة الشر بالخير هي الترياق الكتابي لتوجيه طاقات الشباب. سواء أكانت الشهوة في الداخل أم التوق في الخارج، يُولد الرجاء بزرع بذرة لطف في حياة شخص آخر. والسعي وراء اللذة بدلًا من الراحة سيخيب دائمًا من يناله، ويتركه في وادي يأس أعمق من الوادي الذي بدأ منه. «جيد للرجل أن يحمل النير في صباه… ويجعل فمه في التراب، لعله يوجد رجاء» – مراثي إرميا 3:27-29. لقد خُلقنا لنعمل في كرم الله، والذين لديهم رغبة في ذلك سيحصدون على رجاء ثمره الشبابي.

…يقدّس محننا

«لأننا بالرجاء خلصنا. ولكن الرجاء المنظور ليس رجاء…» – رومية 8:24. كثيرًا ما نستطيع أن نتفهم ألم أيوب. لكن قبل أن ينال ألمه أي قدر من القصاص، بدأت أنهار الشفاء تتدفق حين وقّر أيوب خالقه. وحين نقر بأن الله كامل في جميع التجارب التي يسمح بها، نتعلم عندئذ أن نعبد في الهيكل غير المصنوع بالأيدي، وأن نتغاضى عن ضعف الجسد. والجلوس عند قدمي المسيح يشعل شرارة شباب تبث إشراقها في الروح الكامنة فينا، وتولد الرجاء. عندئذ يصبح ندى الشباب نصيبنا، إذ يمنحنا المسيح الحياة الأبدية والشباب الأبدي. فمن ساعة القبر وإلى الأبد سنبقى شبابًا ونتحدى التعب والموت، إن كنا نعيش في نور صباح يسوع المسيح. السماء موضع شباب دائم، وكما ينعكس نور الشمس على القمر، ينعكس نور المسيح على عروسه. إنها طاهرة وشابة، «كنيسة مجيدة لا دنس فيها ولا غضن أو شيء من مثل ذلك…» – أفسس 5:27. طوبى للقديس الوقور الذي يبلغ أبواب السماء وهو على هذه الحال.
